children.text:
śrī-rājānakānandavardhanācārya-viracito
dhvany-ālokaḥ[*2]
[*2] Also known as Sahṛdayālokaḥ.
children.translated_text: The <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> (Light on Suggestion), composed by the revered master <s>Rājānaka Ānandavardhana</s>. [Also known as <s>Sahṛdayāloka</s> (Light for the Connoisseur).]

children.text: // prathamoddyotaḥ //
children.translated_text: // First <s>Uddyota</s> (Illumination) //

children.text: svecchā-kesariṇaḥ svaccha-svacchāyāyāsitendavaḥ /
children.translated_text: May the nails of <s>Madhusūdana</s> (the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>, i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s>), which act freely like lions, which are moons darkened by their own clear reflection,

children.text: trāyantāṃ vo madhuripoḥ prapannārti-cchido nakhāḥ //
children.translated_text: and which cut short the suffering of those who take refuge [in him], protect you.
DhvK 1.1:

children.text: kāvyasyātmā dhvanir iti budhair yaḥ samāmnāta-pūrvas tasyābhāvaṃ jagadur apare bhāktam āhus tam anye /
children.translated_text: That which the wise have traditionally called '<s>dhvani</s>' (suggestion) as the soul of poetry—some have denied its existence; others have called it figurative (<s>bhākta</s>);

children.text: kecid vācām sthitam aviṣaye tattvam ūcus tadīyaṃ tena brūmaḥ sahṛdaya-manaḥ-prītaye tat-svarūpam // DhvK_1.1 //
children.translated_text: some have declared that its reality lies beyond the reach of words. Therefore, we shall describe its true nature for the delight of the minds of connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). // DhvK_1.1 //

children.text: budhaiḥ kāvya-tattva-vidbhiḥ kāvyasyātmā dhvanir iti saṃjñitaḥ, paramparayā yaḥ samāmnāta-pūrvaḥ samyak āsamantāt mnātaḥ prakaṭitaḥ / tasya sahṛdaya-jana-manaḥ-prakāśamānasyāpy abhāvam anye jagaduḥ / tad-abhāva-vādināṃ cāmī vikalpāḥ sambhavanti /
children.translated_text: By the wise—those who know the essence of poetry—the soul of poetry has been designated as '<s>dhvani</s>' (suggestion), which has been well and fully transmitted—that is, made manifest—through tradition. Yet others have denied the existence of this [<s>dhvani</s>], which shines [clearly] in the minds of connoisseurs. And for those who deny its existence, these alternatives are possible:

children.text:
tatra kecid ācakṣīran-śabdārtha-śarīraṃ tāvat kāvyam / tatra ca śabda-gatāś cārutva-hetavo 'nuprāsādayaḥ prasiddhā eva / artha-gatāś copamādayaḥ / varṇa-saṅghaṭanādharmāś ca ye mādhuryādayas te 'pi pratīyante / tad-anatirikta-vṛttayo vṛttayo 'pi yāḥ kaiścid upanāgarikādyāḥ prakāśitāḥ, tā api gatāḥ śravaṇa-gocaram / rītayaś ca vaidarbhī-prabhṛtayaḥ /
tad-vyatiriktaḥ ko 'yam dhvanir nāmeti /
children.translated_text: There, some would say: Poetry is, to begin with, a body of words and meanings. And among word-based causes of beauty, <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) and the like are well known. And among meaning-based [figures], <s>upamā</s> (simile) and the like. And those qualities of phonetic arrangement such as <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) and the like are also perceived. And the styles (<s>vṛtti</s>)—such as the <s>upanāgarikā</s> and others that have been described by some as not exceeding [the scope of] those—they too have come within the range of hearing. And the modes (<s>rīti</s>) such as <s>Vaidarbhī</s> and the rest [are also known]. So what is this thing called '<s>dhvani</s>' that is different from all these?

children.text: anye brūyuḥ-nāsty eva dhvaniḥ / prasiddha-prasthāna-vyatirekiṇaḥ kāvya-prakārasya kāvyatva-hāneḥ sahṛdaya-hṛdayāhlādi-śabdārtha-mayatvam eva kāvya-lakṣaṇam / na cokta-prasthānātirekiṇo mārgasya tat sambhavati / na ca tat-samatāntaḥ-pātinaḥ sahṛdayān kāṃścit parikalpya tat-prasiddhyā dhvanau kāvya-vyapadeśaḥ pravartito 'pi sakala-vidvan-mano-grāhitām avalambate /
children.translated_text: Others would say: <s>Dhvani</s> simply does not exist. Since a type of poetry that differs from the well-known traditions would forfeit its status as poetry, the very definition of poetry is that it consists of words and meanings that delight the hearts of connoisseurs. And this cannot belong to a path that exceeds the established traditions. Nor, even if some connoisseurs are imagined as falling within those [traditions], and the term '<s>dhvani</s>' is applied to poetry through their familiarity [with it], does this command the assent of all the learned.

children.text:
punar apare tasyābhāvam anyathā kathayeyuḥ-na sambhavaty eva dhvanir nāmāpūrvaḥ kaścit / kāmanīyakam anati-vartamānasya tasyokteṣv eva cārutva-hetuṣv antar-bhāvāt /
teṣām anyatamasyaiva vā apūrva-samākhyā-mātra-karaṇe yat kiṃcana kathanaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Yet others would describe its non-existence differently: There simply cannot exist any unprecedented thing called '<s>dhvani</s>,' since [what is claimed as such], not exceeding the bounds of charm, is subsumed within the already-stated causes of beauty. Or, if merely a new name is given to one of those very [causes], that is a trivial matter.

children.text:
kiṃ ca vāg-vikalpānām ānantyāt sambhavaty api vā kasmiṃścit kāvya-lakṣaṇa-vidhāyibhiḥ prasiddhair apradarśite prakāra-leśe dhvanir dhvanir iti yad etad alīka-sahṛdayatva-bhāvanā-mukulita-locanair nṛtyate, tatra hetuṃ na vidmaḥ / sahasraśo hi mahātmabhir anyair alaṅkāra-prakārāḥ prakāśitāḥ prakāśyante ca / na ca teṣām eṣā daśā śrūyate / tasmāt pravāda-mātraṃ dhvaniḥ / na tv asya kṣoda-kṣamam tattvam kiṃcid api prakāśayituṃ śakyam /
tathā cānyena kṛta evātra ślokaḥ-
children.translated_text: Moreover, since the varieties of verbal expression are infinite, even if there is some trace of a mode not demonstrated by the well-known authorities on poetic definition, we do not know the reason why those whose eyes are closed by a meditation on false connoisseurship dance about [chanting] '<s>dhvani</s>, <s>dhvani</s>!' For thousands of types of figures have been illuminated—and continue to be illuminated—by other great authorities. And this condition [of dancing about] is not heard of in their case. Therefore, <s>dhvani</s> is merely a rumor. No substantial reality of it can be demonstrated that would withstand scrutiny. And thus a verse has been composed by another on this very subject:

children.text: yasminn asti na vastu kiṃcana manaḥ-prahlādi sālaṃkṛti
children.translated_text: In which there is nothing whatsoever that delights the mind, nor is it a well-ornamented [composition],

children.text: vyutpannai racitaṃ ca naiva vacanair vakrokti-śūnyaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: and what is composed by the learned is not even devoid of indirect expression (<s>vakrokti</s>)—

children.text: kāvyaṃ tad-dhvaninā samanvitam iti prītyā praśaṃsañ jaḍo
children.translated_text: a dullard who, with delight, praises such poetry as 'endowed with <s>dhvani</s>'—

children.text: no vidmo 'bhidadhāti kiṃ sumatinā pṛṣṭaḥ svarūpaṃ dhvaneḥ //
children.translated_text: we do not know what he says when asked by an intelligent person about the true nature of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: bhāktam āhus tam anye / anye taṃ dhvani-saṃjñitam kāvyātmānaṃ guṇa-vṛttir ity āhuḥ / yady api ca dhvani-śabda-saṃkīrtanena kāvya-lakṣaṇa-vidhāyibhir guṇa-vṛttir anyo vā na kaścit prakāraḥ prakāśitaḥ, tathāpi amukhya-vṛttyā kāvyeṣu vyavahāraṃ darśayatā dhvani-mārgo manāk spṛṣṭo 'pi na lakṣita iti parikalpyaivam uktam-"bhāktam āhus tam anye" iti /
children.translated_text: 'Others have called it figurative (<s>bhākta</s>).' Others call this soul of poetry designated as '<s>dhvani</s>' a [mere] function of <s>guṇa</s> (quality) [and] <s>vṛtti</s> (style). Although no mode other than <s>guṇa-vṛtti</s> or any other has been illuminated by the authorities on poetic definition through the use of the word '<s>dhvani</s>,' nevertheless, by showing non-primary usage in poetry, the path of <s>dhvani</s> was slightly touched upon but not [explicitly] recognized—and so this statement has been formulated thus: 'Others have called it figurative.'

children.text: kecit punar lakṣaṇa-karaṇa-śālīna-buddhayo dhvanes tattvaṃ girām agocaram sahṛdaya-hṛdaya-saṃvedyam eva samākhyātavantaḥ / tenaivaṃ-vidhāsu vimatiṣu sthitāsu sahṛdaya-manaḥ-prītaye tat-svarūpaṃ brūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Still others, whose intellects are modest when it comes to formulating definitions, have declared that the reality of <s>dhvani</s> is beyond the reach of words, perceivable only by the hearts of connoisseurs. Therefore, in the midst of such disagreements, we shall describe its true nature for the delight of the minds of connoisseurs.

children.text: tasya hi dhvaneḥ svarūpaṃ sakala-sat-kavi-kāvyopaniṣad-bhūtam atiramaṇīyam aṇīyasībhir api cirantana-kāvya-lakṣaṇa-vidhāyināṃ buddhibhir anunmīlita-pūrvam, atha ca rāmāyaṇa-mahābhārata-prabhṛtini lakṣye sarvatra prasiddha-vyavahāraṃ lakṣayatāṃ sahṛdayānām ānando manasi labhatāṃ pratiṣṭhām iti prakāśyate || DhvA_1.1 ||
children.translated_text: For the true nature of this <s>dhvani</s>, which constitutes the secret doctrine (<s>upaniṣad</s>) of all fine poetry by all true poets, which is supremely beautiful, and which has never before been fully revealed even by the subtlest intellects of the ancient authorities on poetic definition—and yet which has a well-established usage everywhere in the visible [works] beginning with the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> and <s>Mahābhārata</s>—is now being illuminated so that it may find a place in the minds of those connoisseurs who [already] perceive it [intuitively] and experience delight. // DhvA_1.1 //

children.text: tatra dhvaner eva lakṣayitum ārabdhasya bhūmikāṃ racayitum idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: There, in order to lay out the ground for <s>dhvani</s>, which has been begun to be defined, this is stated:
DhvK 1.2:

children.text: yo 'rthaḥ sahṛdaya-ślāghyaḥ kāvyātmeti vyavasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: That meaning which is praiseworthy to connoisseurs and which is established as the soul of poetry—

children.text: vācya-pratīyamānākhyau tasya bhedāv ubhau smṛtau // DhvK_1.2 //
children.translated_text: its two divisions are called the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) and the suggested (<s>pratīyamāna</s>). // DhvK_1.2 //

children.text: kāvyasya hi lalitocita-sanniveśa-cāruṇaḥ śarīrasyevātmā sāra-rūpatayā sthitaḥ sahṛdaya-ślāghyo yo 'rthas tasya vācyaḥ pratīyamānaś ceti dvau bhedau /
children.translated_text: For the meaning that is praiseworthy to connoisseurs, which stands as the essence—like the soul of a body whose arrangement is beautiful and befitting graceful [expression]—has two divisions: the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) and the suggested (<s>pratīyamāna</s>).
DhvK 1.3:

children.text: tatra vācyaḥ prasiddho yaḥ prakārair upamādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: There, the expressed meaning, which is well known, [has been analyzed]

children.text: bahudhā vyākṛtaḥ so 'nyaiḥ kāvyalakṣma-vidhāyibhiḥ // DhvK_1.3 //
children.translated_text: in many ways through the modes of <s>upamā</s> (simile) and the like, and has been variously elaborated by others who formulate poetic definitions. // DhvK_1.3 //

children.text: tato neha pratanyate kevalam anūdyate punar yathopayogam iti || DhvA_1.3 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it is not expanded upon here; it is merely recalled as occasion requires. // DhvA_1.3 //
DhvK 1.4:

children.text: pratīyamānaṃ punar anyad eva vastv asti vāṇīṣu mahā-kavīnām /
children.translated_text: But the suggested [meaning] is indeed something else—a [distinct] reality—in the speech of the great poets,

children.text: yat tat prasiddhāvayavātiriktaṃ vibhāti lāvaṇyam ivāṅganāsu // DhvK_1.4 //
children.translated_text: which, being different from the well-known constituents, shines forth like <s>lāvaṇya</s> (grace/beauty) in women. // DhvK_1.4 //

children.text: pratīyamānaṃ punar anyad eva vācyād vastv asti vāṇīṣu mahā-kavīnām / yat tat sahṛdaya-suprasiddhaṃ prasiddhebhyo 'laṅkṛtebhyaḥ pratītebhyo vāvayavebhyo vyatiriktatvena prakāśate lāvaṇyam ivāṅganāsu / yathā hy aṅganāsu lāvaṇyaṃ pṛthaṅ-nirvarṇyamānaṃ nikhilāvayava-vyatireki kim apy anyad eva sahṛdaya-locanāmṛtaṃ tattvāntaraṃ tadvad eva so 'rthaḥ / sa hy artho vācya-sāmarthyākṣiptam vastu-mātram alaṅkāra-rasādayaś cety aneka prabheda-prabhinnau darśayiṣyate / sarveṣu ca teṣu prakāreṣu tasya vācyād anyatvam / tathā hy ādyas tāvat prabhedo vācyād dūram vibhedavān / sa hi kadācid vācye vidhi-rūpe pratiṣedha-rūpaḥ / yathā-
children.translated_text: But the suggested [meaning] is indeed a distinct reality, other than the expressed, in the speech of the great poets. It is well-known to connoisseurs and shines as something different from the well-known, ornamented, and perceived constituent parts—just as <s>lāvaṇya</s> (grace) in women. For just as <s>lāvaṇya</s> in women, when each part is examined separately, is something other than all the individual parts—a distinct reality that is nectar to the eyes of connoisseurs—so too is that meaning. For that meaning will be shown to be of many divisions: mere subject matter implied by the power of the expressed meaning, and [the figures of] <s>alaṅkāra</s>, <s>rasa</s>, and so forth. And in all those modes, its difference from the expressed meaning [will be demonstrated]. For the first division, to begin with, differs markedly from the expressed. For sometimes, where the expressed is in the form of a positive injunction, [the suggested is] in the form of a prohibition. As in:

children.text: bhama dhammia vīsattho so suṇao ajja mārio deṇa /
children.translated_text: 'Wander freely, O righteous one! That dog has today been killed by him—

children.text: golā-ṇaī-kaccha-kuḍaṅga-bāsiṇā daria-sīheṇa //[*3]
children.translated_text: by the proud lion dwelling in the thicket of creepers on the bank of the <s>Godāvarī</s> river.'
Gāthā 2.75, Cited in <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> 138.

children.text: Gāthā 2.75, Cited, Kāvya-prakāśa 138.
[bhrama dhārmika visrabdhaḥ sa śunako 'dya māritas tena /
children.translated_text: ['Wander freely, O righteous one! That dog has today been killed by him—

children.text: godā-nadī-kūla-latā-kuñja-vāsinā dṛpta-siṃhena //]
children.translated_text: by the proud lion dwelling in the thicket of creepers on the bank of the <s>Godā</s> river.']

children.text: kvacid vācye pratiṣedha-rūpe vidhi-rūpo yathā-
children.translated_text: Sometimes, where the expressed is in the form of a prohibition, [the suggested is] in the form of an injunction. As in:

children.text: attā ettha ṇimajjai ettha ahaṃ diasaaṃ paloehi /
children.translated_text: 'My mother-in-law is drowning here; here I am—look for me while it is daylight!

children.text: mā pahia rattiandhia sejjāe maha ṇimajjahisi //[*4]
children.translated_text: O traveler, blinded by the night, do not sink [with me] upon my bed!'
Gāthā 1.4. Cited in <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> 136, <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 1.2.

children.text: Gāthā 1.4. Cited, Kāvya-prakāśa 136, Sāhitya-darpaṇa 1.2.
(śvaśrūr atra nimajjati, atrāhaṃ divasa eva pralokaya /
children.translated_text: ('My mother-in-law is drowning here; here I am—look [for me] while it is still daylight!

children.text: mā pathika rātryandha śayyāyāṃ mama nimaṅkṣyasi //)
children.translated_text: O traveler, blinded by the night, do not sink upon my bed!')

children.text: kvacid vācye vidhi-rūpe 'nubhaya-rūpo yathā-
children.translated_text: Sometimes, where the expressed is in the form of an injunction, [the suggested is] in a form that is neither [injunction nor prohibition]. As in:

children.text: vacca maha bbia ekkei hontu ṇīsāsaroiabbāiṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Go, my child—let mine alone be the sighing and weeping!

children.text: mā tujja bi tīa biṇā dakkhiṇa-haassa jāantu //[*5]
children.translated_text: May they not arise for you too, deprived of her, [you] whose courtesy is your undoing!'
Gāthā 938.

children.text: Gāthā 938.
[vraja mamaivaikasyā bhavantu niḥśvāsa-roditavyāni /
children.translated_text: ['Go, my child—let mine alone be the sighing and weeping!

children.text: mā tavāpi tayā vinā dākṣiṇya-hatasya janiṣata //]
children.translated_text: May they not arise for you too, deprived of her, [you] whose courtesy is your undoing!']

children.text: kvacid vācye pratiṣedha-rūpe 'nubhaya-rūpo yathā-
children.translated_text: Sometimes, where the expressed is in the form of a prohibition, [the suggested is] in a form that is neither [injunction nor prohibition]. As in:

children.text: deā pasia ṇivattassu muha-sasi-johṇā-vilutta-tama-ṇivahe /
children.translated_text: 'O lady, seeing [you] by chance—by [you] whose face-moonlight has swept away the flood of darkness—turn back!

children.text: ahisāriāṇaṃ vigghaṃ karosi aṇṇāṇaṃ bi haāse //[*6]
children.translated_text: You create an obstacle for the <s>abhisārikās</s> (women going to their lovers), and even for the hopeless others, you [create] laughter.'
Gāthā 962.

children.text: Gāthā 962.
[daivād dṛṣṭvā nitānta-su mukha-śaśi-jyotsnā-vilupta-tamo-nivahe /
children.translated_text: ['Having seen [you] by chance, O [lady] whose face-moon's radiance has swept away the flood of darkness—

children.text: abhisārikāṇāṃ vighnaṃ karoṣy anyāsām api hatāśe //]
children.translated_text: you create an obstacle for the <s>abhisārikās</s>, and even for the hopeless others, you [create] laughter!']

children.text: kvacid vācyād vibhinna-viṣayatvena vyavasthāpito yathā-
children.translated_text: Sometimes, [the suggested] is established as having a subject matter different from the expressed. As in:

children.text: kassa ba ṇa hoi roso daṭṭhūṇa piyāe sa-bbaṇaṃ aharaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Who would not be angry upon seeing the wounded lip of his beloved—

children.text: sa-bhamara-pa{u}ma-gghāiṇi vāria-vāme sahasu ehṇiṃ //[*7]
children.translated_text: [she] whose habit is to smell lotuses with bees, [she] who had been forbidden [but was] willful—now look at her suddenly!'
Gāthā 880. Cited in <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> 135.

children.text: Gāthā 880. Cited Kāvya-prakāśa 135.
[kasya vā na bhavati roṣo dṛṣṭvā priyāyāḥ sa-vraṇam adharam /
children.translated_text: ['Who would not be angry upon seeing the wounded lip of his beloved—

children.text: sa-bhramara-padmāghrāṇa-śīle vārita-vāme sahasvedānīm //]
children.translated_text: [she] whose habit is to smell lotuses with bees, [she] who had been forbidden [but was] willful—now look at her suddenly!']

children.text: anye caivaṃ-prakārā vācyād vibhedinaḥ pratīyamāna-bhedāḥ saṃbhavanti / teṣāṃ diṅ-mātram etat pradarśitam /
children.translated_text: Other such divisions of the suggested that differ from the expressed are possible. Only a brief indication of them has been shown here.

children.text: dvitīyo 'pi prabhedo vācyād vibhinnaḥ sa-prapañcam agre darśayiṣyate /
children.translated_text: The second division too, which differs from the expressed, will be shown in detail further on.

children.text: tṛtīyas tu rasādi-lakṣaṇaḥ prabhedo vācya-sāmarthyākṣiptaḥ prakāśate, na tu sākṣāc-chabda-vyāpāra-viṣaya iti vācyād vibhinna eva / tathā hi vācyatvaṃ tasya sva-śabda-niveditatvena vā syāt / vibhāvādi-pratipādana-mukhena vā / purvasmin pakṣe sva-śabda-niveditatvābhāve rasādīnām apratīti-prasaṅgaḥ / na ca sarvatra teṣāṃ sva-śabda-niveditatvam / yatrāpy asti tat, tatrāpi viśiśṭa-vibhāvādi-pratipādana-mukhenaivaiṣāṃ pratītiḥ /
children.translated_text: The third division, characterized by <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and the like, is implied by the power of the expressed meaning—it shines forth, but is not directly the object of verbal function—and is thus indeed different from the expressed. For the expressedness of <s>rasa</s> would either have to be through its own [specific] word, or through the medium of presenting the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and the like. In the first case, since <s>rasa</s> and the like are not always denoted by their own [specific] words, there would be the unwanted consequence that they would not be perceived [in cases lacking such words]. And even where such [direct naming] exists, the perception of <s>rasa</s> occurs only through the medium of presenting the specific <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like.

children.text: svaśabdena sā kevalamanūdyate, na tu tatkṛtā viṣayāntare tathā tasyā adarśanāt / na hi kevala-śṛṅgārādi-śabda-mātra-bhāji vibhāvādi-pratipādana-rahite kāvye manāg api rasavattva-pratītir asti / yataś ca svābhidhānam antareṇa kevalebhyo 'pi vibhāvādibhyo viśiśṭebhyo rasādīnāṃ pratītiḥ / kevalāc ca svābhidhānād apratītiḥ / tasmād anvaya-vyatirekābhyām abhidheya-sāmarthyākṣiptatvam eva rasādīnām / na tv abhidheyatvaṃ kathaṃcit, iti tṛtīyo 'pi prabhedo vācyād vibhinna eveti sthitam / vācyena tv asya saheva pratītir ity agre darśayiṣyate || DhvA_1.4 ||
children.translated_text: The direct naming merely restates [the <s>rasa</s>]; it does not create the perception, since such [perception through naming alone] is not observed in other contexts. For in poetry that consists merely of the bare words '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' and the like, devoid of the presentation of <s>vibhāvas</s> and so forth, there is not even the slightest perception of <s>rasa</s>. And since the perception of <s>rasa</s> arises even from the specific <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like alone, without direct naming; and since non-perception [results] from direct naming alone—therefore, by the positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), <s>rasa</s> and the like are indeed implied by the power of the expressed meaning, not expressed in any manner. Thus the third division too is established as indeed different from the expressed. But its perception occurs together with the expressed—this will be shown further on. // DhvA_1.4 //
DhvK 1.5:

children.text: kāvyasyātmā sa evārthas tathā cādikaveḥ purā /
children.translated_text: That very meaning is the soul of poetry. And thus, in ancient times, of the first poet (<s>ādikavi</s>),

children.text: krauñca-dvandva-viyogotthaḥ śokaḥ ślokatvam āgataḥ // DhvK_1.5 //
children.translated_text: the grief born from the separation of the <s>krauñca</s> (curlew) pair took the form of verse (<s>śloka</s>). // DhvK_1.5 //

children.text:
vividha-vācya-vācaka-racanā-prapañca-cāruṇaḥ kāvyasya sa evārthaḥ sāra-bhūtaḥ /
cādikaver vālmīkeḥ nihata-sahacarī-viraha-kātara-krauñcākranda-janitaḥ śoka eva ślokatayā pariṇataḥ / śoko hi karuṇa-sthāyi-bhāvaḥ / pratīyamānasya cānya-bheda-darśane 'pi rasa-bhāva-mukhenaivopalakṣaṇaṃ prādhānyāt || DhvA_1.5 ||
children.translated_text: That very meaning is the essential element of poetry, which is beautiful through the elaborate arrangement of diverse expressed meanings and their verbal expression. And of the first poet, <s>Vālmīki</s>, the grief born from the anguished cry of the <s>krauñca</s> bird distressed by the separation from its killed mate transformed into verse (<s>śloka</s>). For grief is the stable emotion (<s>sthāyibhāva</s>) of the compassionate <s>rasa</s> (<s>karuṇa</s>). And even in showing the other divisions of the suggested, the exemplification is primarily through <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), because of their primacy. // DhvA_1.5 //
DhvK 1.6:

children.text: sarasvatī svādu tad-artha-vastu niḥṣyandamānā mahatāṃ kavīnām /
children.translated_text: The sweet speech (<s>Sarasvatī</s>) of the great poets, pouring forth that reality of meaning,

children.text: aloka-sāmānyam abhivyanakti parisphurantam pratibhā-viśeṣam // DhvK_1.6 //
children.translated_text: manifests the extraordinary flash of genius (<s>pratibhā-viśeṣa</s>), which is not common to [the rest of] the world. // DhvK_1.6 //

children.text: tat vastu-tattvaṃ niḥṣyandamānā mahatāṃ kavīnāṃ bhāratī aloka-sāmānyaṃ pratibhā-viśeṣaṃ parisphurantam abhivyanakti / yenāsminn ativicitra-kavi-paramparā-vāhini saṃsāre kālidāsa-prabhṛtayo dvitrāḥ pañcaṣā vā mahā-kavaya iti gaṇyante || DhvA_1.6 ||
children.translated_text: Pouring forth that reality of meaning, the speech of the great poets manifests the extraordinary, brilliantly flashing genius that is uncommon to the [ordinary] world. It is for this reason that in this world, which bears the succession of endlessly diverse poets, only two or three, or five or six, such as <s>Kālidāsa</s> and the like, are counted as great poets. // DhvA_1.6 //

children.text: idaṃ cāparaṃ pratīyamānasyārthasya sad-bhāva-sādhanaṃ pramāṇam-
children.translated_text: And this is another proof (<s>pramāṇa</s>) establishing the existence of the suggested meaning (<s>pratīyamāna artha</s>):
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 1.7:

children.text: śabdārtha-śāsana-jñāna-mātreṇaiva na vedyate /
children.translated_text: It is not apprehended merely by knowledge of the science of word and meaning;

children.text: vedyate sa tu kāvyārtha-tattvajñair eva kevalam // DhvK_1.7 //
children.translated_text: It is apprehended only by those who know the true nature of poetic meaning. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 1.7 //

children.text: so 'rtho yasmāt kevalaṃ kāvyārtha-tattva-jñair eva jñāyate / yadi ca vācya-rūpa evāsāv arthaḥ syāt tad-vācya-vācaka-rūpa-parijñānād eva tat-pratītiḥ syāt / atha ca vācya-vācaka-lakṣaṇa-mātra-kṛta-śramāṇāṃ kāvya-tattvārtha-bhāvanā-vimukhānāṃ svara-śruty-ādi-lakṣaṇam ivāpragītānāṃ gāndharva-lakṣaṇa-vidām agocara evāsāv arthaḥ || DhvA_1.7 ||
children.translated_text: That meaning, since it is known only by those who know the true nature of poetic meaning—if it were merely of the nature of the expressed (<s>vācya</s>), then from the full knowledge of the relationship of word and meaning alone, its cognition would arise. But that meaning is beyond the reach of those whose labor has been confined merely to the characteristics of word and meaning, who are averse to the cultivation of the true nature of poetic meaning—just as the characteristics of <s>gāndharva</s> (music) are beyond the reach of those versed in the characteristics of pitch (<s>svara</s>), <s>śruti</s> (microtone), and the like, who have never actually performed [music].

children.text: evaṃ vācya-vyatirekiṇo vyaṅgyasya sad-bhāvaṃ pratipādya prādhānyaṃ tasyaiveti darśayati-
children.translated_text: Having thus established the existence of the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) as distinct from the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>), he shows that it is precisely this [suggested meaning] that holds primacy:
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 1.8:

children.text: so 'rthas tad-vyakti-sāmarthya-yogī śabdaś ca kaścana /
children.translated_text: That meaning, and a certain word endowed with the power to manifest it—

children.text: yatnataḥ pratyabhijñeyau tau śabdārthau mahākaveḥ // DhvK_1.8 //
children.translated_text: Those two—word and meaning—of the great poet should be carefully recognized. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 1.8 //

children.text: vyaṅgyo 'rthas tad-vyakti-sāmarthya-yogī śabdaś ca kaścana, na śabda-mātram / tāv eva śabdārthau mahākaveḥ pratyabhijñeyau /vyaṅgya-vyañjakābhyām eva suprayuktābhyāṃ mahākavitva-lābho mahā-kavīnāṃ, na vācya-vācaka-racanā-mātreṇa || DhvA_1.8 ||
children.translated_text: The suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya artha</s>), and a certain word endowed with the power to manifest it—not mere word [alone]. Those two alone—word and meaning—of the great poet should be recognized. The attainment of great poethood by great poets is through the suggested and the suggestor (<s>vyaṅgya-vyañjaka</s>) alone, both well-employed; not through mere arrangement of expressed meaning and its expression (<s>vācya-vācaka</s>).

children.text: idānīṃ vyaṅgya-vyañjakayoḥ prādhānye 'pi yad-vācya-vācakāv eva prathamam upādadate kavayas tad api yuktam evetyāha-
children.translated_text: Now, even though the suggested and the suggestor hold primacy, the fact that poets first employ the expressed meaning and its expression is also fitting—he says:
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 1.9:

children.text: ālokārthī yathā dīpa-śikhāyāṃ yatnavāñ janaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a person desiring light makes effort regarding the lamp-flame,

children.text: tad-upāyatayā tadvad arthe vācye tad-ādṛtaḥ // DhvK_1.9 //
children.translated_text: So too, intent on that [suggested meaning], one is attentive to the expressed meaning as its means. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 1.9 //

children.text: yathā hy ālokārthī sann api dīpa-śikhāyāṃ yatnavāñ jano bhavati tad-upāyatayā / na hi dīpa-śikhām antareṇālokaḥ sambhavati / tad vyaṅgyam arthaṃ pratyādṛto jano vācye 'rthe yatnavān bhavati / anena pratipādakasya kaver vyaṅgyam arthaṃ prati vyāpāro darśitaḥ || DhvA_1.9 ||
children.translated_text: Just as a person, even though desiring light, makes effort regarding the lamp-flame because it is the means [to light]—for light is not possible without the lamp-flame—so too a person intent on the suggested meaning makes effort regarding the expressed meaning. By this, the activity of the communicating poet directed toward the suggested meaning is demonstrated.

children.text: pratipādyasyāpi taṃ darśayitum āha-
children.translated_text: To show this also for the audience being communicated to, he says:
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 1.10:

children.text: yathā padārtha-dvāreṇa vākyārthaḥ sampratīyate /
children.translated_text: Just as sentence-meaning is apprehended through the gateway of word-meanings,

children.text: vācyārtha-pūrvikā tadvat pratipattasya vastunaḥ // DhvK_1.10 //
children.translated_text: So too, the cognition of the [suggested] matter is preceded by [cognition of] the expressed meaning. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 1.10 //

children.text: yathā hi padārtha-dvāreṇa vākyārthāvagamas tathā vācyārtha-pratīti-pūrvikā vyaṅgyasyārthasya pratipattiḥ || DhvA_1.10 ||
children.translated_text: Just as the understanding of sentence-meaning [comes] through the gateway of word-meanings, so the apprehension of the suggested meaning is preceded by the cognition of the expressed meaning.

children.text: idānīṃ vācyārtha-pratīti-pūrvakatve 'pi tat-pratīter vyaṅgyasyārthasya prādhānyaṃ yathā na vyālupyate tathā darśayati-
children.translated_text: Now, he shows how, even though preceded by the cognition of the expressed meaning, the primacy of the suggested meaning is not thereby diminished:
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 1.11:

children.text: sva-sāmarthya-vaśenaiva vākyārthaṃ pratipādayan /
children.translated_text: Just as the word-meaning, while communicating the sentence-meaning by its own power alone,

children.text: yathā vyāpāra-niṣpattau padārtho na vibhāvyate // DhvK_1.11 //
children.translated_text: Is not perceived as a separate [entity] when the [communicative] operation is completed— // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 1.11 //

children.text: yathā sva-sāmarthya-vaśenaiva vākyārthaṃ prakāśayann api padārtho vyāpāra-niṣpattau na bhāvyate vibhaktatayā || DhvA_1.11 ||
children.translated_text: Just as the word-meaning, while illuminating the sentence-meaning by the force of its own power alone, is not apprehended separately when the [communicative] operation is completed—
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 1.12:

children.text: tadvat sa-cetasāṃ so 'rtho vācyārtha-vimukhātmanām /
children.translated_text: So too, for sensitive minds (<s>sahṛdaya</s>), that meaning, [belonging to those] whose minds are turned away from the expressed meaning,

children.text: buddhau tattvārtha-darśinyāṃ jhaṭity evāvabhāsate // DhvK_1.12 //
children.translated_text: Flashes instantly in an intellect that discerns the true meaning. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 1.12 //

children.text: evaṃ vācya-vyatirekiṇo vyaṅgyasyārthasya sad-bhāvaṃ pratipādya prakṛta upayojayann āha-
children.translated_text: Having thus established the existence of the suggested meaning as distinct from the expressed, he applies it to the matter at hand and says:
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 1.13:

children.text: yatrārthaḥ śabdo vā tam artham upasarjanīkṛta-svārthau /
children.translated_text: Where a meaning or a word, having subordinated its own [primary] meaning,

children.text: vyaṅktaḥ kāvya-viśeṣaḥ sa dhvanir iti sūribhiḥ kathitaḥ // DhvK_1.13 //
children.translated_text: Suggests another meaning—that variety of poetry has been called <s>dhvani</s> (resonance) by the wise. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 1.13 //

children.text: yatrārtho vācya-viśeṣaḥ vācaka-viśeṣaḥ śabdo vā tam arthaṃ vyaṅktaḥ, sa kāvya-viśeṣo dhvanir iti / anena vācya-vācaka-cārutva-hetubhya upamādibhyo 'nuprāsādibhyaś ca vibhakta eva dhvaner viṣaya iti darśitam /
children.translated_text: Where a particular expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) or a particular word (<s>vācaka</s>) suggests another meaning, that variety of poetry is <s>dhvani</s>. By this it is shown that the domain of <s>dhvani</s> is entirely distinct from figures of speech (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) such as simile (<s>upamā</s>) and the like, and from phonetic figures (<s>anuprāsa</s>) and the like, which are causes of the charm of expressed meaning and expression.

children.text: yad apy uktam-"prasiddha-prasthānātikramiṇo mārgasya kāvya-hāner dhvanir nāsti" iti, tad apy ayuktam / yato lakṣaṇa-kṛtām eva sa kevalaṃ na prasiddhaḥ, lakṣye tu parīkṣyamāṇe sa eva sahṛdaya-hṛdayāhlāda-kāri kāvya-tattvam / tato 'nyac citram evety agre darśayiṣyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: As for what was said—'Since this path transgresses the well-established approaches, there is no <s>dhvani</s> [as it would entail] the loss of poetry'—this too is improper. For it is merely not well-known to the makers of definitions; but when examined in actual poetic instances (<s>lakṣya</s>), it alone is the true nature of poetry that delights the hearts of sensitive readers (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). That anything other than this is merely 'striking' (<s>citra</s>)—we shall demonstrate later.

children.text: yad apy uktam-"kāmanīyakam anativartamānasya tasyoktālaṅkārādi-prakāreṣv antar-bhāvaḥ" iti, tad apy asamīcīnam; vācya-vācaka-mātrāśrayiṇi prasthāne vyaṅgya-vyañjaka-samāśrayeṇa vyavasthitasya dhvaneḥ katham antar-bhāvaḥ, vācya-vācaka-cārutva-hetavo hi tasyāṅga-bhūtāḥ, sa tv aṅgi-rūpa eveti pratipādayiṣyamāṇatvāt /
children.translated_text: As for what was said—'Since it does not exceed charm (<s>kāmanīyaka</s>), it is subsumed within the stated categories of ornament (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) and the like'—this too is incorrect. How can <s>dhvani</s>, which is established by depending on both the suggested and the suggestor, be subsumed within an approach that rests only on the expressed and the expression? For the causes of charm in the expressed and the expression are subsidiary parts (<s>aṅga</s>) of it, while it [<s>dhvani</s>] itself is the principal body (<s>aṅgin</s>)—this will be demonstrated.

children.text: parikara-ślokāś cātra-
children.translated_text: The supporting verses here are:

children.text: vyaṅgya-vyañjaka-sambandha-nibandhanatayā dhvaneḥ /
children.translated_text: Since <s>dhvani</s> is grounded in the relationship of the suggested and the suggestor,

children.text: vācya-vācaka-cārutva-hetv-antaḥ-pātitā kutaḥ //
children.translated_text: How can it be subsumed within the causes of charm of the expressed and the expression?

children.text: nanu yatra pratīyamānasyārthasya vaiśadyenāpratītiḥ sa nāma mā bhūd dhvaner viṣayaḥ / yatra tu pratītir asti, yathā-samāsoktyākṣepānukta-nimitta-viśeṣokti-paryāyoktāpahnuti-dīpaka-saṅkarālaṅkārādau , tatra dhvaner antar-bhāvo bhaviṣyatīty ādi nirākartum abhihitam-"upasarjanī-kṛta-svārthau" iti /
children.translated_text: Now, [the objection:] 'Where there is no clear cognition of the suggested meaning, let that indeed not be the domain of <s>dhvani</s>; but where there is cognition, as in <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), <s>ākṣepa</s> (apparent denial), the unnamed-cause (<s>anukta-nimitta</s>), <s>viśeṣokti</s> (specific statement), <s>paryāyokta</s> (circumlocution), <s>apahnuti</s> (denial), <s>dīpaka</s> (illuminator), <s>saṅkara</s> (conflation), and other figures—there <s>dhvani</s> would be subsumed [within them].' To refute such [objections], it was stated: 'having subordinated its own [primary] meaning.'

children.text:
artho guṇīkṛtātmā, guṇīkṛtābhidheyaḥ śabdo vā yatrārthāntaram abhivyanakti sa dhvanir iti / teṣu kathaṃ tasyāntar-bhāvaḥ / vyaṅgya-prādhānye hi dhvaniḥ / na caitat samāsoktyādiṣv asti /
samāsoktau tāvat-
upoḍha-rāgeṇa vilola-tārakaṃ
children.translated_text: With intensified passion, with trembling stars [i.e., eyes],

children.text: tathā gṛhītaṃ śaśinā niśā-mukham /
children.translated_text: Thus was the face of the night seized by the moon,

children.text: yathā samastaṃ timirāṃśukaṃ tayā
children.translated_text: So that the entire veil of darkness—

children.text: puro 'pi rāgād galitaṃ na lakṣitam //
children.translated_text: Though slipped off before [him] due to passion—was not even noticed.

Where a meaning—one whose own expressed content has been rendered subsidiary—or a word whose own denotation has been rendered subsidiary, manifests another meaning, that is <s>dhvani</s>. How then can it be subsumed within them [those figures]? For <s>dhvani</s> obtains when the suggested is primary; and this [primacy of the suggested] does not exist in <s>samāsokti</s> and the like.
In <s>samāsokti</s>, for instance:

children.text: ity ādau vyaṅgyenānugataṃ vācyam eva prādhānyena pratīyate samāropita-nāyikā-nāyaka-vyavahārayor niśā-śaśinor eva vākyārthatvāt /
children.translated_text: In such [verses], it is the expressed meaning alone, accompanied by the suggested, that is apprehended primarily, since the sentence-meaning pertains to the night and the moon, upon which the behavior of heroine and hero has been superimposed.

children.text: ākṣepe 'pi vyaṅgya-viśeṣākṣepiṇo 'pi vācyasyaiva cārutvaṃ prādhānyena vākyārtha ākṣepokti-sāmarthyād eva jñāyate / tathā hi-tatra śabdopārūḍho viśeṣābhidhānecchayā pratiṣedha-rūpo ya ākṣepaḥ sa eva vyaṅgya-viśeṣam ākṣipan mukhyaṃ kāvya-śarīram /
children.translated_text: In <s>ākṣepa</s> (apparent denial) too, the charm of the expressed meaning—which itself negates a particular suggested [element]—is primarily the sentence-meaning, known by the very power of the negating utterance. For there, the negation that is verbally expressed, in the form of a denial made with the intention of expressing something specific, is itself, while negating the specific suggested [element], the principal body of the poem.

children.text: cārutvotkarṣa-nibandhanā hi vācya-vyaṅgyayoḥ prādhānya-vivakṣā / yathā-
children.translated_text: For the intention of primacy between the expressed and the suggested is grounded in the excellence of charm. For example:

children.text: anurāgavatī sandhyā divasas tat-puraḥsaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The twilight is full of passion (<s>anurāga</s>); the day goes before her;

children.text: aho daiva-gatiḥ kīdṛk tathāpi na samāgamaḥ //
children.translated_text: Alas, how strange is the course of fate—yet still there is no union!

children.text: atra satyām api vyaṅgya-pratītau vācyasyaiva cārutvam utkarṣavad iti tasyaiva prādhānya-vivakṣā /
children.translated_text: Here, even though there is cognition of the suggested meaning, it is the charm of the expressed meaning alone that is eminent; hence the expressed meaning alone is intended as primary.

children.text: yathā ca dīpakāpahnuty-ādau vyaṅgyatvenopamāyāḥ pratītāv api prādhānyenāvivakṣitatvān na tayā vyapadeśas tadvad atrāpi draṣṭavyam / anukta-nimittāyām api viśeṣoktau-
children.translated_text: And just as in <s>dīpaka</s>, <s>apahnuti</s>, and the like, even though simile (<s>upamā</s>) is cognized as suggested, it is not designated by it because it is intentionally non-primary—the same should be seen here. In <s>viśeṣokti</s> (specific statement) with an unnamed cause too:

children.text: āhūto 'pi sahāyair om ity uktvā vimukta-nidro 'pi /
children.translated_text: Though called by his companions, though he has said 'yes,' though freed from sleep,

children.text: gantu-manā api pathikaḥ saṅkocaṃ naiva śithilayati //
children.translated_text: Though wishing to depart—the traveler does not at all loosen his embrace.

children.text: ity ādau vyaṅgyasya prakaraṇa-sāmarthyāt pratīti-mātraṃ na tu tat-pratīti-nimittā kācic cārutva-niṣpattir iti na prādhānyam / paryāyokte 'pi yadi prādhānyena vyaṅgyatvaṃ tad bhavatu nāma tasya dhvanāv antar-bhāvaḥ / na tu dhvanes tatrāntar-bhāvaḥ / tasya mahā-viṣayatvenāṅgitvena ca pratipādayiṣyamāṇatvāt / na punaḥ paryāyo bhāmahodāhṛta-sadṛśe vyaṅgyasyaiva prādhānyam / vācyasya tatropasarjanābhāvenāvivakṣitatvāt /
children.translated_text: In such [verses], there is merely the cognition of the suggested through the power of the context, but no production of charm occasioned by that cognition; hence there is no primacy [of the suggested]. In <s>paryāyokta</s> (circumlocution) too, if the suggested primarily has the status of being suggested, then let that be subsumed within <s>dhvani</s>—but <s>dhvani</s> is not subsumed within it, since [<s>dhvani</s>] will be demonstrated as having a vast domain and as being the principal [element]. However, in a <s>paryāyokta</s> similar to the one cited by <s>Bhāmaha</s>, it is the suggested alone that holds primacy, since the expressed is unintended due to its being entirely subsidiary.

children.text: apahnuti-dīpakayoḥ punar-vācyasya prādhānyaṃ vyaṅgyasya cānuyāyitvaṃ prasiddham eva /
children.translated_text: In <s>apahnuti</s> (denial) and <s>dīpaka</s> (illuminator), moreover, the primacy of the expressed and the subsidiary status of the suggested are well-established.

children.text: saṅkarālaṅkāre 'pi yadālaṅkāro 'laṅkārāntara-cchāyām anugṛhṇāti, tadā vyaṅgyasya prādhānyenāvivakṣitatvān na dhvani-viṣayatvam / alaṅkāra-dvaya-sambhāvanāyāṃ tu vācya-vyaṅgyayoḥ samaṃ prādhānyam / atha vācyopasarjanī-bhāvena vyaṅgyasya tatrāvasthānaṃ tadā so 'pi dhvani-viṣayo 'stu, na tu sa eva dhvanir iti vaktuṃ śakyam / paryāyokta-nirdiṣṭa-nyāyāt / api ca saṅkarālaṅkāre 'pi ca kvacit saṅkaroktir eva dhvani-sambhāvanāṃ nirākaroti /
children.translated_text: In <s>saṅkara</s> (conflation of figures) too, when one figure takes on the coloring of another figure, the suggested is intentionally non-primary, so it is not the domain of <s>dhvani</s>. When both figures are equally present, the expressed and the suggested have equal primacy. But when the expressed becomes subsidiary and the suggested takes its stand [as primary], then let that too be the domain of <s>dhvani</s>; but one cannot say it is <s>dhvani</s> itself—by the principle stated regarding <s>paryāyokta</s>. Moreover, even in <s>saṅkara</s>, in some cases the conflated expression itself rules out the possibility of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: aprastuta-praśaṃsāyām api yadā sāmānya-viśeṣa-bhāvān nimitta-nimitti-bhāvād vā abhidhīyamānasyāprastutasya pratīyamānena prastutenābhisambandhas tadābhidhīyamāna-pratīyamānayoḥ samam eva prādhānyam / yadā tāvat sāmānyasyāprastutasyābhidhīyamānasya prākaraṇikena viśeṣeṇa pratīyamānena sambandhas tadā viśeṣa-pratītau satyām api prādhānyena tat-sāmānyenāvinābhāvāt sāmānyasyāpi prādhānyam / yadāpi viśeṣasya sāmānya-niṣṭhatvaṃ tadāpi sāmānyasya prādhānye sāmānye sarva-viśeṣāṇām antar-bhāvād viśeṣasyāpi prādhānyam / nimitta-nimitti-bhāve cāyam eva nyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) too, when the connection of the stated irrelevant [topic] with the understood relevant [topic] is through the relation of universal-to-particular or cause-to-effect, the stated and the understood have equal primacy. When the universal that is stated as irrelevant is connected with the relevant particular that is understood, even though the particular is cognized, since it cannot exist without its universal, the universal too has primacy due to the primary status of the particular. And when the particular depends on the universal, even though the universal holds primacy, since all particulars are included within the universal, the particular too has primacy. The same principle applies in the cause-to-effect relation.

children.text: yadā tu sārūpya-mātra-vaśenāprastuta-praśaṃsāyām aprakṛta-prakṛtayoḥ sambandhas tadāpy aprastutasya sarūpasyābhidhīyamānasya prādhānyenāvivakṣāyāṃ dhvanāv evāntaḥ-pātaḥ / itarathā tv alaṅkārāntaram eva / tad ayam atra saṅkṣepaḥ-
vyaṅgyasya yatrāprādhānyaṃ vācya-mātrānuyāyinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where the suggested is non-primary, merely following the expressed meaning—

children.text: samāsoktyādayas tatra vācyālaṅkṛtayaḥ sphuṭāḥ //
children.translated_text: There <s>samāsokti</s> and the like are clearly figures of expressed meaning (<s>vācyālaṅkṛti</s>).

But when in <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>, the connection between the irrelevant and the relevant is based merely on resemblance, then too, when the stated irrelevant counterpart is intentionally non-primary, it falls within <s>dhvani</s> itself. Otherwise, it is simply another figure. Here then is the summary:

children.text: vyaṅgyasya pratibhā-mātre vācyārthānugame 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: Where the suggested is only a flash of insight, or follows the expressed meaning,

children.text: na dhvanir yatra vā tasya prādhānyaṃ na pratīyate //
children.translated_text: Or where its primacy is not perceived—there is no <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: tat-parāv eva śabdārthau yatra vyaṅgyaṃ prati sthitau /
children.translated_text: Where word and meaning are oriented precisely toward the suggested [as primary],

children.text: dhvaneḥ sa eva viṣayo mantavyaḥ saṅkarojjhitaḥ //
children.translated_text: That alone should be considered the domain of <s>dhvani</s>, free from conflation.

children.text: tasmān na dhvaner anyatrāntar-bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>dhvani</s> is not subsumed within anything else.

children.text: itaś ca nāntar-bhāvaḥ ; yataḥ kāvya-viśeṣo 'ṅgī dhvanir iti kathitaḥ / tasya punar aṅgāni-alaṅkārā guṇā vṛttayaś ceti pratipādayiṣyante / na cāvayava eva pṛthag-bhūto 'vayavīti prasiddhaḥ / apṛthag-bhāve tu tad-aṅgatvaṃ tasya / na tu tattvam eva / yatrāpi vā tattvaṃ tatrāpi dhvaner mahā-viṣayatvān na tan-niṣṭhatvam eva /
children.translated_text: And for this further reason there is no subsumption: because <s>dhvani</s> has been declared to be a variety of poetry that is the principal body (<s>aṅgin</s>). Its subsidiary parts (<s>aṅga</s>)—figures of speech (<s>alaṅkāra</s>), qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), and styles (<s>vṛtti</s>)—will be demonstrated. And a part taken separately is not known as the whole. If they are not separate, then their being parts of it [<s>dhvani</s>] is [established], but not their being identical with it. Even where there is identity, because <s>dhvani</s> has a vast domain, it is not restricted to being solely that [one figure].

children.text: "sūribhiḥ kathita" iti vidvad-upajñeya-muktiḥ, na tu yathā-kathañcit-pravṛtteti pratipādyate / prathame hi vidvāṃso vaiyākaraṇāḥ, vyākaraṇa-mūlatvāt sarva-vidyānām / te ca śrūyamāṇeṣu varṇeṣu dhvanir iti vyavaharanti / tathaivānyais tan-matānusāribhiḥ sūribhiḥ kāvya-tattvārtha-darśibhir vācya-vācaka-sammiśraḥ śabdātmā kāvyam iti vyapadeśyo vyañjakatva-sāmyād dhvanir ity uktaḥ / na caivaṃ-vidhasya dhvaner vakṣyamāṇa-prabheda-tad-bheda-saṃkalanayā mahā-viṣayasya yat-prakāśanaṃ tad-aprasiddhālaṅkāra-viśeṣa-mātra-pratipādanena tulyam iti tad-bhāvita-cetasāṃ yukta eva saṃrambhaḥ / na ca teṣu kathañcid īrṣyayā kaluṣita-śemuṣī-katvam āviṣkaraṇīyam / tad evaṃ dhvanes tāvad abhāva-vādinaḥ pratyuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Declared by the wise' (<s>sūribhiḥ kathitaḥ</s>)—this indicates that it is to be understood on the authority of the learned, not that it proceeds in any haphazard manner. For the first [among the] wise are the grammarians, since all sciences are rooted in grammar. They use the term <s>dhvani</s> for the sounds that are heard. In the same way, by other wise ones who follow their view and who discern the true nature of poetry, [the term <s>dhvani</s>] has been applied to poetry whose nature is verbal (<s>śabdātmā</s>), mixed with expressed meaning and expression, because of the similarity in the function of suggestion (<s>vyañjakatva</s>). And the elucidation of such <s>dhvani</s>—which has a vast domain when its forthcoming divisions and sub-divisions are compiled—is not equivalent to the mere exposition of some unfamiliar minor type of figure; therefore the enthusiasm of those whose minds are steeped in this [subject] is entirely justified. Nor should one display toward them a talent polluted by jealousy. Thus, those who deny the existence of <s>dhvani</s> have been answered.

children.text: asti dhvaniḥ / sa cāsāv avivakṣita-vācyo vivakṣitāny apara-vācyaś ceti dvividhaḥ sāmānyena / tatrādyasyodāharaṇam-
children.translated_text: <s>Dhvani</s> (suggestion) exists. And that [<s>dhvani</s>] is generally of two types: <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> (where the literal meaning is not intended) and <s>vivakṣitānya-para-vācya</s> (where another meaning is intended as primary). An example of the first [type] is—

children.text: suvarṇa-puṣpāṃ pṛthivīṃ cinvanti puruṣās trayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Three [kinds of] men gather [from] the earth whose flowers are gold:

children.text: śūraś ca kṛta-vidyaś ca yaś ca jānāti sevitum //
children.translated_text: the hero, the learned, and he who knows how to serve.

children.text: dvitīyasyāpi-
śikhariṇi kva nu nāma kiyac ciraṃ
children.translated_text: O mountain-dwelling girl, where indeed, for how long,

children.text: kim abhidhānam asāv akarot tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: of what name did that one perform austerity?

children.text: taruṇi yena tavādhara-pāṭalaṃ
children.translated_text: O young woman, by which [austerity] the redness of your lip—

children.text: daśati bimba-phalaṃ śukaśāvakaḥ || DhvA_1.13 ||
children.translated_text: a young parrot bites the <s>bimba</s> fruit [that resembles it].
Of the second [type] also—

children.text: yad apy uktaṃ bhaktir dhvanir iti, tat pratisamādhīyate-
children.translated_text: As to what has been said—'Figurative usage (<s>bhakti</s>) is <s>dhvani</s>'—that is now refuted:

children.text: Dhv_1.14a:
children.translated_text: [Verse] 1.14a:

children.text: bhaktyā bibharti naikatvam rūpa-bhedād ayaṃ dhvaniḥ // DhvK_1.14a //
children.translated_text: This <s>dhvani</s>, through figurative usage (<s>bhakti</s>), does not maintain unity, because of the difference in forms.

children.text: ayam ukta-prakāro dhvanir bhaktyā naikatvaṃ bibharti bhinna-rūpatvāt / vācya-vyatiriktasyārthasya vācya-vācakābhyāṃ tātparyeṇa prakāśanaṃ yatra vyaṅgya-prādhānye sa dhvaniḥ / upacāra-mātraṃ tu bhaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: This <s>dhvani</s> of the described type does not maintain unity through figurative usage, because of the diversity of forms. Where the meaning beyond the literal is revealed through the literal meaning and its expression with the intention [of suggestion], and where the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) predominates—that is <s>dhvani</s>. Mere figurative transfer, however, is <s>bhakti</s>.

children.text: mā caitat syād bhaktir lakṣaṇaṃ dhvaner ity āha-
children.translated_text: Lest one think that <s>bhakti</s> is the defining characteristic of <s>dhvani</s>, he says—

children.text: Dhv_1.14b:
children.translated_text: [Verse] 1.14b:

children.text: ativyāpter athāvyāpter na cāsau lakṣyate tayā // DhvK_1.14b //
children.translated_text: Due to over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) and under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>), <s>dhvani</s> is not defined by it [<s>bhakti</s>].

children.text: naiva bhaktyā dhvanir lakṣyate / katham ? ativyāpter avyāpteś ca / tatrātivyāptir dhvani-vyatirikte 'pi viṣaye bhakteḥ sambhavāt / yatra hi, vyaṅgya-kṛtaṃ mahat-sauṣṭhavaṃ nāsti tatrāpy upacarita-śabda-vṛttyā prasiddhy-anurodha-pravartita-vyavahārāḥ kavayo dṛśyante / yathā [ratnāvalī 2.12]-
children.translated_text: <s>Dhvani</s> is indeed not defined by <s>bhakti</s>. How so? Because of over-extension and under-extension. Therein, the over-extension [arises] because <s>bhakti</s> is possible even in domains other than <s>dhvani</s>. For even where there is no great beauty produced by suggestion, poets are seen to employ figurative word-usage driven by conventional association. For example [from <s>Ratnāvalī</s> 2.12]—

children.text: parimlānaṃ pīna-stana-jaghana-saṅgād ubhayatas
children.translated_text: Wilted on both sides from contact with full breasts and hips,

children.text: tanor madhyasyāntaḥ parimalanam aprāpya haritam /
children.translated_text: its interior not having attained the green color of the middle of [her] body,

children.text: idaṃ vyasta-nyāsaṃ ślatha-bhuja-latākṣepa-valanaiḥ
children.translated_text: this [lotus-leaf bed], [its leaves] laid out separately, [disheveled] by the tossing and turning of languid vine-like arms,

children.text: kṛśāṅgyāḥ santāpaṃ vadati visinī-patra-śayanam //[*8]
children.translated_text: tells of the anguish of the slender-limbed woman—[such is] the lotus-leaf bed.
Reference note: <s>Subhāṣita-ratna-kośa</s> 709, <s>Rasārṇava</s> 1.441.

children.text: Srk 709, Rasārṇava 1.441.
tathā-
children.translated_text: Similarly—

children.text: cumbajja{i} saahuttaṃ avarundhijja{i} sahassa-huttaṃ bi /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] She is kissed a hundred times, embraced a thousand times;

children.text: ramia puṇo bi ramijja{i} pie jaṇe ṇatthi puṇaruttaṃ //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] having paused, she is enjoyed again—with a beloved person, there is no repetition.

children.text: [cumbyate śata-kṛtvo 'varudhyate sahasra-kṛtvaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] She is kissed a hundred times, embraced a thousand times;

children.text: viramya punā ramyate priyo jano nāsti punaruktam //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] having paused, she is enjoyed again—with a beloved person, there is no repetition.

children.text: tathā-
children.translated_text: Similarly—

children.text: kubiāo pasaṇnāo oraṇṇa-muhīo vihasamāṇāo /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] Angry or pleased, with tear-stained faces or laughing—

children.text: jaha gahiā taha hiaaṃ haranti ucchinta-mahilāo //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] however grasped, they steal the heart—[such are] wanton women.

children.text: [kupitāḥ prasannā avarudita-vadanā vihasantyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] Angry or pleased, with tear-stained faces or laughing—

children.text: yathā gṛhītās tathā hṛdayaṃ haranti svairiṇyo mahilāḥ //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] however grasped, they steal the heart—[such are] wanton women.

children.text: tathā-
children.translated_text: Similarly—

children.text: ajjāe pahāro ṇavala-dāe diṇṇo pieṇa thaṇa-baṭṭe /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] The blow given by the beloved with a fresh vine on the wife's breast—

children.text: mi{u}o bi dūsaho bbia jāo hiae savattīṇaṃ //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] though gentle, it became as if unbearable in the hearts of the co-wives.

children.text: [bhāryāyāḥ prahāro nava-latayā dattaḥ priyeṇa stana-pṛṣṭhe /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] The blow given by the beloved with a fresh vine on the wife's breast—

children.text: mṛduko 'pi duḥsaha iva jāto hṛdaye sapatnīnām //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] though gentle, it became as if unbearable in the hearts of the co-wives.

children.text: tathā-
parārthe yaḥ pīḍām anubhavati bhaṅge 'pi madhuro
children.translated_text: whose transformation is indeed desired by all—

children.text: yadīyaḥ sarveṣām iha khalu vikāro 'py abhimataḥ /
children.translated_text: whose transformation is indeed desired by all here,

children.text: na samprāpto vṛddhiṃ yadi sa bhṛśam akṣetra-patitaḥ
children.translated_text: if he has not attained growth, being fallen on barren soil,

children.text: kim ikṣor doṣo 'sau na punar aguṇāyā maru-bhuvaḥ //
children.translated_text: is that the fault of sugarcane, or rather of the unmeritorious desert land?
He who experiences suffering for the sake of others, who is sweet even when broken,

children.text: ity atrekṣu-pakṣe 'nubhavati śabdaḥ / na caivaṃ-vidhaḥ kadācid api dhvaner viṣayaḥ / yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Here, taking sugarcane as the subject, the word 'experiences' [is used figuratively]. And such [figurative usage] is never the domain of <s>dhvani</s>. Because—
[Verse] 1.15:

children.text: ukty-antareṇāśakyaṃ yat tac cārutvaṃ prakāśayan /
children.translated_text: A word that reveals that beauty which cannot [be expressed] by any other utterance,

children.text: śabdo vyañjakatāṃ bibhrad dhvany-ukter viṣayībhavet // DhvK_1.15 //
children.translated_text: bearing suggestive power (<s>vyañjakatva</s>), becomes the domain of <s>dhvani</s>-expression.

children.text: atra codāhṛte viṣaye nokty-antarā-śakya-cārutva-vyakti-hetuḥ śabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the domain illustrated above, the word is not the cause of manifesting a beauty inexpressible by other utterance.

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover—
[Verse] 1.16:

children.text: rūḍhā ye viṣaye 'nyatra śabdāḥ sva-viṣayād api /
children.translated_text: Words like 'grace' (<s>lāvaṇya</s>) and the like, conventionally established in a domain other than their own,

children.text: lāvaṇyādyāḥ prayuktās te na bhavanti padaṃ dhvaneḥ // DhvK_1.16 //
children.translated_text: when employed [figuratively], do not become the locus of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: teṣu copacarita-śabda-vṛttir astīti / tathā-vidhe ca viṣaye kvacit sambhavann api dhvani-vyavahāraḥ prakārāntareṇa pravartate / na tathā-vidha-śabda-mukhena /
children.translated_text: And in these [cases], there is [merely] figurative word-usage. Even if <s>dhvani</s>-usage sometimes occurs in such a domain, it operates through another mode, not through such a word directly.

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore—
[Verse] 1.17:

children.text: mukhyāṃ vṛttiṃ parityajya guṇa-vṛttyārtha-darśanam /
children.translated_text: Abandoning the primary function and perceiving meaning through secondary function (<s>guṇa-vṛtti</s>)—

children.text: yad uddiśya phalaṃ tatra śabdo naiva skhalad-gatiḥ // DhvK_1.17 //
children.translated_text: the word, aiming at a purpose there, does not stumble in its course.

children.text: tatra hi cārutvātiśaya-viśiṣṭārtha-prakāśana-lakṣaṇe prayojane kartavye yadi śabdasyāmukhyatā tadā tasya prayoge duṣṭataiva syāt / na caivam ; tasmāt-
children.translated_text: For if, when the purpose is to reveal a meaning distinguished by extraordinary beauty, there were a departure from the primary [function] of the word, then its employment would indeed be faulty. But that is not the case; therefore—
[Verse] 1.18:

children.text: vācakatvāśrayeṇaiva guṇa-vṛttir vyavasthitā /
children.translated_text: Secondary function (<s>guṇa-vṛtti</s>) is established solely on the basis of denotative power (<s>vācakatva</s>);

children.text: vyañjakatvaika-mūlasya dhvaneḥ syāl lakṣaṇaṃ katham // DhvK_1.18 //
children.translated_text: how then could it be the defining characteristic of <s>dhvani</s>, which is rooted solely in suggestive power (<s>vyañjakatva</s>)?

children.text: tasmād anyo dhvanir anyā ca guṇa-vṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>dhvani</s> is one thing, and secondary function (<s>guṇa-vṛtti</s>) is another.

children.text: avyāptir apy asya lakṣaṇasya / na hi dhvani-prabhedo vivakṣitānya-para-vācya-lakṣaṇaḥ / anye ca bahavaḥ prakārā bhaktyā vyāpyantaḥ ; tasmād bhaktir alakṣaṇam || DhvA_1.18 ||
children.translated_text: There is also under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) of this definition. For the variety of <s>dhvani</s> characterized as <s>vivakṣitānya-para-vācya</s> (where another meaning is intended as primary) [is not covered by <s>bhakti</s>]. And many other types are encompassed by <s>bhakti</s>; therefore <s>bhakti</s> is not a valid definition.

children.text: Dhv_1.19a:
children.translated_text: [Verse] 1.19a:

children.text: kasyacid dhvani-bhedasya sā tu syād upalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhakti</s>] may, however, serve as an indicative mark (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) of some [particular] variety of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: sā punar bhaktir vakṣyamāṇa-prabheda-madhyād anyatamasya bhedasya yadi nāmopalakṣaṇatayā sambhāvyeta ; yadi ca guṇa-vṛttyaiva dhvanir lakṣyata ity ucyate tad-abhidhā-vyāpāreṇa tad-itaro 'laṅkāra-vargaḥ samagra eva lakṣyata iti pratyekam alaṅkārāṇāṃ lakṣaṇa-karaṇa-vaiyarthya-prasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, that <s>bhakti</s> might be accepted as an indicative mark of some one among the varieties to be described [later]. But if it is said that <s>dhvani</s> is defined by secondary function (<s>guṇa-vṛtti</s>) alone, then by the operation of denotation, the entire class of other ornaments (<s>alaṅkāras</s>) would also be defined [in the same way], resulting in the futility of defining each ornament individually.

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover—

children.text: Dhv_1.19b:
children.translated_text: [Verse] 1.19b:

children.text: lakṣaṇe 'nyaiḥ kṛte cāsya pakṣa-saṃsiddhir eva naḥ // DhvK_1.19a //
children.translated_text: Even if the definition of this [<s>dhvani</s>] is made by others, our thesis is thereby only established.

children.text: kṛte 'pi vā pūrvam evānyair dhvani-lakṣaṇe pakṣa-saṃsiddhir eva naḥ ; yasmād dhvanir astīti naḥ pakṣaḥ / sa ca prāg eva saṃsiddha ity ayatna-sampanna-samīhitārthāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ smaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if the definition of <s>dhvani</s> has already been made by others, our thesis is only established; for our position is that <s>dhvani</s> exists. And since that has already been established, we have become those whose desired goal is accomplished without effort.

children.text: ye 'pi sahṛdaya-hṛdaya-saṃvedyam anākhyeyam eva dhvaner ātmānam āmnāsiṣus te 'pi na parīkṣya vādinaḥ / yata uktayā nītyā vakṣyamāṇayā ca dhvaneḥ sāmānya-viśeṣa-lakṣaṇe pratipādite 'pi yady anākhyeyatvaṃ tat sarveṣām eva vastūnāṃ tat-prasaktam / yadi punar dhvaner atiśayoktyānayā kāvyāntarātiśāyi taiḥ svarūpam ākhyāyate tat te 'pi yuktābhidhāyina eva //
children.translated_text: Even those who have declared that the essence of <s>dhvani</s> is simply inexpressible, perceptible only to the hearts of sensitive readers (<s>sahṛdayas</s>)—they too are not speakers after [careful] examination. For if, even though the general and specific definitions of <s>dhvani</s> have been established by the methods stated and to be stated, [they still maintain] inexpressibility, then that [inexpressibility] would follow for all things whatsoever. But if by this [claim of] hyperbole they describe the nature of <s>dhvani</s> as surpassing other poetry, then they too are indeed speaking aptly.

children.text: iti śrī-rājānakānandavardhanācārya-viracite dhvany-āloke prathama uddyotaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the First <s>Uddyota</s> (Illumination) in the <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> composed by the venerable master <s>Rājānaka Ānandavardhana</s>.

children.text: // dvitīyoddyotaḥ //
children.translated_text: The Second <s>Uddyota</s> (Illumination)

children.text:
evam avivakṣita-vācya-vivakṣitānya-para-vācyatvena dhvanir dvi-prakāraḥ prakāśitaḥ /
tatrāvivakṣita-vācyasya prabheda-pratipādanāyedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Thus <s>dhvani</s> has been shown to be of two types: <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> (where the literal meaning is not intended) and <s>vivakṣitānya-para-vācya</s> (where another meaning is intended as primary). Now, to establish the sub-varieties of the <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> type, this is said—
[Verse] 2.1:

children.text: arthāntare saṅkramitam atyantaṃ vā tiraskṛtam /
children.translated_text: The literal meaning of <s>dhvani</s> of the <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> type is considered to be of two kinds:

children.text: avivakṣita-vācyasya dhvaner vācyaṃ dvidhā matam // DhvK_2.1 //
children.translated_text: either transferred to another meaning (<s>arthāntara-saṅkramita</s>), or completely concealed (<s>atyanta-tiraskṛta</s>).

children.text: tathāvidhābhyāṃ ca tābhyāṃ vyañgyasyaiva viśeṣaḥ / tatrārthāntara-saṅkramita-vācyo yathā-
snigdha-śyāmala-kānti-lipta-viyato vellad-balākā ghanā
children.translated_text: The sky smeared with a lustrous dark glow, the clouds with undulating cranes,

children.text: vātāḥ śīkariṇaḥ payoda-suhṛdām ānanda-kekāḥ kalāḥ /
children.translated_text: the winds carrying spray, the peacocks—friends of the clouds—crying their joyful notes—

children.text: kāmaṃ santu dṛḍhaṃ kaṭhora-hṛdayo rāmo 'smi sarvaṃ sahe
children.translated_text: let them be! Firmly hard-hearted <s>Rāma</s> I am; I shall endure all.

children.text: vaidehī tu katham bhaviṣyati hahā hā devi dhīrā bhava //[*9]
children.translated_text: But how will <s>Vaidehī</s> fare? Alas, alas! O queen, be brave!
Reference note: <s>Sad-ukti-karṇāmṛta</s> 978, <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 2.17.

children.text: Sad-ukti-karṇāmṛta 978, Sāh.D. 2.17.

children.translated_text: And by those two [kinds], the distinction is of the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) alone. An example of the <s>arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācya</s> (meaning transferred to another sense) type is—

children.text: ity atra rāma-śabdaḥ / anena hi vyaṅgya-dharmāntara-pariṇataḥ saṃjñī pratyāyyate, na saṃjñi-mātram / yathā ca mamaiva viṣama-bāṇa-līlāyām-
children.translated_text: Here, [the key word is] '<s>Rāma</s>.' For by this, the named person is conveyed as transformed by the properties of the suggested meaning, not merely as the bearer of the name. And as in my own [work] <s>Viṣama-bāṇa-līlā</s>—

children.text: tālā jāanti guṇā jālā de sahiaehiṃ gheppanti /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] Then virtues arise, when they are grasped by the sensitive (<s>sahṛdayas</s>);

children.text: ra{i}-kiraṇānuggahīāiṃ honti kamalāiṃ kamalāiṃ //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] blessed by the rays of the sun, lotuses become [true] lotuses.

children.text: [tadā jāyante guṇā yadā te sahṛdayair gṛhyante /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] Then virtues arise, when they are grasped by the sensitive;

children.text: ravi-kiraṇānugṛhītāni bhavanti kamalāni kamalāni //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] blessed by the rays of the sun, lotuses become [true] lotuses.

children.text: ity atra dvitīyaḥ kamala-śabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, [the key word is] the second [occurrence of] the word '<s>kamala</s>' (lotus).

children.text: atyanta-tiraskṛta-vācyo yathādi-kaver vālmīkeḥ-
children.translated_text: An example of the <s>atyanta-tiraskṛta-vācya</s> (meaning completely concealed) type, from the original poet <s>Vālmīki</s>—

children.text:
ravi-saṅkrānta-saubhāgyas tuṣārāvṛta-maṇḍalaḥ /
niḥśvāsāndha ivādarśaś candramā na prakāśate //iti /
children.translated_text: Its beauty having passed to the sun, its disc covered with frost, the moon does not shine—like a mirror dimmed by breath.

children.text: atrāndha-śabdaḥ / yathā ca-
children.translated_text: Here, [the key word is] 'dimmed' (<s>andha</s>). And similarly—

children.text: gaanaṃ ca matta-mehaṃ dhārāluli-ajjunāiṃ a baṇāiṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] The sky with intoxicated clouds, the forests with trees [whose <s>arjuna</s> bark is] drenched by torrents—

children.text: ṇirahaṅkāra-miaṅkā haranti ṇīlāo nisāo //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] the dark nights with an egoless moon steal [the heart].

children.text: [gaganaṃ ca matta-meghaṃ dhārā-lulitārjunāni ca vanāni /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] The sky with intoxicated clouds, the forests with trees drenched by torrents—

children.text: nirahaṅkāra-mṛgāṅkā haranti nīlā api niśāḥ //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] the dark nights with an egoless moon steal [the heart].

children.text: atra matta-nirahaṅkāra-śabdau || DhvA_2.1 ||
children.translated_text: Here, [the key words are] 'intoxicated' (<s>matta</s>) and 'egoless' (<s>nirahaṅkāra</s>).
[Verse] 2.2:

children.text: asaṃlakṣya-kramoddyotaḥ krameṇa dyotitaḥ paraḥ /
children.translated_text: One [type] illuminated in an imperceptible sequence, and the other manifested in [discernible] sequence—

children.text: vivakṣitābhidheyasya dhvaner ātmā dvidhā mataḥ // DhvK_2.2 //
children.translated_text: the essence of <s>dhvani</s> of the <s>vivakṣitābhidheya</s> (where the expressed meaning is intended) type is considered to be of two kinds.

children.text: mukhyatayā prakāśamāno vyaṅgyo 'rtho dhvaner ātmā / sa ca vācyārthāpekṣayā kaścid alakṣya-kramatayā prakāśate, kaścit krameṇeti dvidhā mataḥ || DhvA_2.2 ||
children.translated_text: The suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya artha</s>) that shines forth as primary is the essence of <s>dhvani</s>. And that [essence], in relation to the expressed meaning, is considered twofold: some manifests in an imperceptible sequence, and some in [discernible] sequence.

children.text: tatra-
children.translated_text: Of these—
[Verse] 2.3:

children.text: rasa-bhāva-tad-ābhāsa-tat-praśānty-ādir akramaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), <s>bhāva</s> (transient emotion), their semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>), their tranquility (<s>praśānti</s>), and so forth—these, of the imperceptible-sequence [type],

children.text: dhvaner ātmāṅgi-bhāvena bhāsamāno vyavasthitaḥ // DhvK_2.3 //
children.translated_text: shining in the [role of] the dominant element (<s>aṅgin</s>), are established as the essence of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: rasādir artho hi saheva vācyenāvabhāsate / sa cāṅgitvenāvabhāsamāno dhvaner ātmā /
children.translated_text: For the meaning consisting of <s>rasa</s> and the rest manifests simultaneously with the expressed meaning. And that [meaning], manifesting as the dominant element, is the essence of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: idānīṃ rasavad-alaṅkārād alakṣya-krama-dyotanātmano dhvaner vibhakto viṣaya iti pradarśyate-
children.translated_text: Now it is demonstrated that the domain of <s>dhvani</s> whose nature is imperceptible-sequence illumination is distinct from the ornament called <s>rasavat</s>—
[Verse] 2.4:

children.text: vācya-vācaka-cārutva-hetūnāṃ vividhātmanām /
children.translated_text: Where the various causes of beauty in the expressed meaning and its expression

children.text: rasādi-paratā yatra sa dhvaner viṣayo mataḥ // DhvK_2.4 //
children.translated_text: are subordinate to <s>rasa</s> and the rest—that is considered the domain of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: rasa-bhāvatad-ābhāsa-tat-praśama-lakṣaṇaṃ mukhyam artham anuvartamānā śabdārthālaṅkārā guṇāś ca parasparaṃ dhvany-apekṣayā vibhinna-rūpā vyavasthitās tatra kāvye dhvanir iti vyapadeśaḥ || DhvA_2.4 ||
children.translated_text: The ornaments of word, meaning, and [poetic] qualities (<s>guṇas</s>), following the primary meaning characterized by <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, their semblance, and their tranquility, are mutually established in distinct forms with respect to <s>dhvani</s>. In such poetry, the designation '<s>dhvani</s>' [applies].
[Verse] 2.5:

children.text: pradhānye 'nyatra vākyārthe yatrāṅgaṃ tu rasādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: In poetry where [some] other sentence-meaning is primary and <s>rasa</s> and the rest are subordinate elements (<s>aṅga</s>)—

children.text: kāvye tasminn alaṅkāro rasādir iti me matiḥ // DhvK_2.5 //
children.translated_text: in my view, <s>rasa</s> and the rest [function as] ornament (<s>alaṅkāra</s>).

children.text: yady api rasavad-alaṅkārasyānyair darśito viṣayas tathāpi yasmin kāvye pradhānatayānyo 'rtho vākyārthī-bhūtas tasya cāṅga-bhūtā ye rasādayas te rasāder alaṅkārasya viṣayā iti māmakīnaḥ pakṣaḥ / tad yathā cāṭuṣu preyo 'laṅkārasya vākyārthatve 'pi rasādayo 'ṅgabhūtā dṛśyante / sa ca rasādir alaṅkāraḥ śuddhaḥ saṅkīrṇo vā /
children.translated_text: Even though the domain of the <s>rasavat</s> ornament has been shown by others [in a different way], nevertheless, in my view, in poetry where another meaning has become primary as the sentence-meaning and <s>rasa</s> and the rest are subordinate to it—those are the domain of the ornament consisting of <s>rasa</s> and the rest. For example, in love-verses (<s>cāṭu</s>), even when [<s>rasa</s> and the rest] become the sentence-meaning, they are seen as subordinate elements of the <s>preyas</s> ornament. And that ornament consisting of <s>rasa</s> and the rest is either pure or mixed.

children.text: tatrādyo yathā-
children.translated_text: An example of the first [pure] type—

children.text: kiṃ hāsyena na me prayāsyasi punaḥ prāptaś cirād darśanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Why do you laugh? Will you not stay for me? Having obtained your sight after so long—

children.text: keyam niṣkaruṇa pravāsa-rucitā kenāsi dūrikṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: what is this, O merciless one? This fondness for travel—by whom have you been sent away?'

children.text: svapnānteṣv iti te vadan priyatama-vyāsakta-kaṇṭha-graho
children.translated_text: Speaking thus [in her dream], clutching the neck of her beloved,

children.text: buddhā roditi rikta-bāhu-valayas tāraṃ ripu-strī-janaḥ //
children.translated_text: awakened, the enemy's womenfolk weep loudly, their arms' bangles [now] empty.

children.text: ity atra karuṇa-rasasya śuddhasyāṅga-bhāvāt spaṣṭam eva rasavad-alaṅkāratvam / evam evaṃ-vidhe viṣaye rasāntarāṇāṃ spaṣṭa evāṅgabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, because the pure <s>karuṇa-rasa</s> (pathetic sentiment) is in a subordinate role, it is clearly an instance of the <s>rasavat</s> ornament. Similarly, in such domains, the subordinate status of other <s>rasas</s> is evident.

children.text: saṅkīrṇo rasādir aṅga-bhūto yatha-
children.translated_text: An example of [<s>rasa</s> and the rest as] subordinate elements in a mixed [form]—

children.text: kṣipto hastāvalagnaḥ prasabham abhihato 'py ādadāno 'ṃśukāntaṃ
children.translated_text: Thrown [aside yet] clinging to the hand, forcibly struck yet grasping the edge of the garment,

children.text: gṛhṇan keśeṣv apāstaś caraṇa-nipatito nekṣitaḥ sambhrameṇa /
children.translated_text: seized by the hair yet cast away, fallen at the feet yet not looked at—[all done] with agitation—

children.text: āliṅgan yo 'vadhūtas tripura-yuvatibhiḥ sāśru-netrotpalābhiḥ
children.translated_text: embracing yet rejected by the <s>Tripura</s> maidens whose lotus-eyes brimmed with tears—

children.text: kāmīvārdrāparādhaḥ sa dahatu duritaṃ śāmbhavo vaḥ śarāgniḥ //
children.translated_text: like a lover guilty of a tender offense—may that fire of <s>Śambhu</s>'s arrow burn away your sin!

children.text: ity atra tripura-ripu-prabhāvātiśayasya vākyārthatve īrṣyā-vipralambhasya śleṣa-sahitasyāṅga-bhāva iti, evaṃ-vidha eva rasavad-ādy-alaṅkārasya nyāyyo viṣayaḥ / ata eva cerṣyā-vipralambha-karuṇayor aṅgatvena vyavasthānāt samāveśo na doṣaḥ / yatra hi rasasya vākyārthī-bhāvas tatra katham alaṅkāratvam ? alaṅkāro hi cārutva-hetuḥ prasiddhaḥ ; na tv asāv ātmaivātmanaś cārutva-hetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus here, when the extraordinary power of the enemy of <s>Tripura</s> [i.e., <s>Śiva</s>] constitutes the sentence-meaning, the jealousy-in-separation (<s>īrṣyā-vipralambha</s>) combined with double-meaning (<s>śleṣa</s>) has the status of a subordinate element (<s>aṅga</s>). In this way alone is the proper domain of <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures) such as <s>rasavat</s> (that which contains rasa). And precisely for this reason, since jealousy-in-separation and the pathetic sentiment (<s>karuṇa</s>) are established as subordinate elements, their co-presence is not a fault. For where <s>rasa</s> constitutes the sentence-meaning, how can it be an <s>alaṅkāra</s>? For an <s>alaṅkāra</s> is well-known as a cause of beauty; but the self is not itself the cause of its own beauty.

children.text: tathā cāyam atra saṃkṣepaḥ-
children.translated_text: And thus the summary here is:

children.text: rasa-bhāvādi-tātparyam āśritya viniveśanam /
children.translated_text: The placement [of figures] depending upon the predominance of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc.,

children.text: alaṅkṛtīnāṃ sarvāsām alaṅkāratva-sādhanam //
children.translated_text: Is what establishes the <s>alaṅkāra</s>-nature (ornamental character) of all ornaments.

children.text: tasmād yatra rasādayo vākyārthī-bhūtāḥ sa sarvo na rasāder alaṅkārasya viṣayaḥ ; sa dhvaneḥ prabhedaḥ, tasyopamādayo 'laṅkārāḥ / yatra tu prādhānyenārthāntarasya vākyārthī-bhāve rasādibhiś cārutva-niṣpattiḥ kriyate, sa rasāder alaṅkāratāyā viṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, wherever <s>rasa</s> etc. constitute the sentence-meaning, that entire [passage] is not the domain of <s>alaṅkāras</s> such as <s>rasavat</s>; it is a variety of <s>dhvani</s>, and <s>upamā</s> (simile) and the like are its <s>alaṅkāras</s>. But where, with another meaning principally constituting the sentence-meaning, beauty is produced through <s>rasa</s> etc., that is the domain of <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status for <s>rasa</s> etc.

children.text: evaṃ dhvaner upamādīnāṃ rasavad-alaṅkārasya ca vibhakta-viṣayatā bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus <s>dhvani</s>, [figures like] <s>upamā</s> etc., and the <s>rasavat alaṅkāra</s> have distinct domains.

children.text: yadi tu cetanānāṃ vākyārthī-bhāvo rasādy-alaṅkārasya viṣaya ity ucyate tarhy upamādīnāṃ pravirala-viṣayatā nirviṣayatā vābhihitā syāt / yasmād acetana-vastu-vṛtte vākyārthī-bhūte punaś cetana-vastu-vṛttānta-yojanayā yathā-kathañcid bhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: But if it is said that the sentence-meaning involving sentient beings is the domain of <s>rasavat alaṅkāra</s>, then <s>upamā</s> and the like would have an extremely limited domain, or no domain at all. For when a narrative involving inanimate objects constitutes the sentence-meaning, there must somehow be an attribution of the narrative of sentient beings.

children.text:
atha satyām api tasyāṃ yatrācetanānāṃ vākyārthī-bhāvo nāsau rasavad-alaṅkārasya viṣaya ity ucyate / tan mahataḥ kāvya-prabandhasya rasanidhānabhūtasya nīrasatvamabhihitaṃ syāt /
yathā-
children.translated_text: Now, if it is said that even when such [attribution] exists, wherever inanimate objects constitute the sentence-meaning, that is not the domain of <s>rasavat alaṅkāra</s> — then that would amount to declaring a great poetic composition, which is a repository of <s>rasa</s>, to be devoid of <s>rasa</s>. For example:

children.text: taraṅga-bhrū-bhaṅgā kṣubhita-vihaga-śreṇi-raśanā
children.translated_text: With waves as furrowed brows, with rows of agitated birds as her girdle,

children.text: vikarṣantī phenaṃ vasanam iva saṃrambha-śithilam /
children.translated_text: Dragging foam like a garment loosened in agitation,

children.text: yathā-viddhaṃ yāti skhalitam abhisandhāya bahuśo
children.translated_text: Going as if wounded, stumbling and regaining composure repeatedly —

children.text: nadī-rūpeṇeyaṃ dhruvam asahanā sā pariṇatā //
children.translated_text: In the form of a river, she, the intolerant one, has surely been transformed.

children.text: yathā vā-
tanvī megha-jalārdra-pallavatayā dhautādhar evāśrubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Slender, with her lower lip as if washed by tears through having sprouts moistened by cloud-water,

children.text: śūnyevābharaṇaiḥ svakāla-virahād viśrānta-puṣpodgamā /
children.translated_text: As if bereft of ornaments, her flowering ceased due to separation from her proper season,

children.text: cintā maunam ivāśritā madhu-kṛtāṃ śabdair vinā lakṣyate
children.translated_text: Seeming to have taken to the silence of thought, perceived without the sounds of bees —

children.text: caṇḍī mām avadhūya pāda-patitaṃ jātānutāpeva sā //
children.translated_text: She, the fierce one, as if filled with remorse after having rejected me who fell at her feet.
Or as [in the following]:

children.text: yathā vā-
teṣāṃ gopa-vadhū-vilāsa-suhṛdāṃ rādhā-rahaḥ-sākṣiṇāṃ
children.translated_text: Are those bower-houses on the bank of the daughter of Mount <s>Kalinda</s> [i.e., the <s>Yamunā</s>] doing well, dear friend —

children.text: kṣemaṃ bhadra kalinda-śaila-tanayā-tīre latā-veśmanāṃ /
children.translated_text: Those that were companions of the dalliances of the cowherd-women, witnesses to <s>Rādhā</s>'s secrets?
