children.text: vicchinne smara-talpa-kalpana-mṛd-ucchedopayoge 'dhunā
children.translated_text: Now that their use for gathering earth to fashion love-beds has ceased,

children.text: te jāne jaraṭhī-bhavanti vigalan nīla-tviṣaḥ pallavāḥ //[*10]
children.translated_text: I know their sprouts, with fading blue luster, are growing old.
Reference: Srk 808 (vidyāyāḥ); Svm 87.8 (kasyāpi)

children.text: Srk 808 (vidyāyāḥ); Svm 87.8 (kasyāpi)

children.translated_text: Or as [in the following]:

children.text: ity evam ādau viṣaye 'cetanānāṃ vākyārthī-bhāve 'pi cetana-vastu-vṛttānta-yojanāsty eva / atha yatra cetana-vastu-vṛttānta-yojanāsti tatra rasādir alaṅkāraḥ / tad evaṃ saty upamādayo nirviṣayāḥ pravirala-viṣayā vā syuḥ / yasmān nāsty evāsāv acetana-vastu-vṛttānto yatra cetana-vastu-vṛttānta-yojanā nāsty antato vibhāvatvena / tasmād aṅgatvena ca rasādīnām alaṅkāratā /
yaḥ punar aṅgī raso bhāvo vā sarvākāram alaṅkāryaḥ sa dhvaner ātmeti || DhvA_2.5 ||
children.translated_text: But the predominant (<s>aṅgin</s>) <s>rasa</s> or <s>bhāva</s>, which is in every way the thing to be adorned (<s>alaṅkārya</s>) — that is the soul of <s>dhvani</s>. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.5]

Thus, in cases such as these, even when inanimate objects constitute the sentence-meaning, there is indeed an attribution of the narrative of sentient beings. Now, if wherever there is an attribution of a sentient narrative, there <s>rasa</s> etc. are <s>alaṅkāras</s> — then, this being the case, <s>upamā</s> and the like would have no domain, or an extremely limited one. For there is indeed no narrative of inanimate objects in which there is not, at the very least, an attribution of sentient narrative by way of being a <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant). Therefore, <s>rasa</s> etc. have <s>alaṅkāra</s>-status [only] in their subordinate (<s>aṅga</s>) capacity.

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.6:]

children.text: tam artham avalambante ye 'ṅginaṃ te guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those [qualities of style] that support that predominant meaning are called <s>guṇas</s> (qualities);

children.text: aṅgāśritās tv alaṅkārā mantavyāḥ kaṭakādivat // DhvK_2.6 //
children.translated_text: But those dependent on the subordinate elements should be regarded as <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments), like bracelets and the like. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.6]

children.text: ye tam arthaṃ rasādi-lakṣaṇam aṅginaṃ santam avalambate te guṇāḥ śauryādivat / vācya-vācaka-lakṣaṇāny aṅgāni ye punas tad-āśritās te 'laṅkārā mantavyāḥ kaṭakādivat || DhvA_2.6 ||
children.translated_text: Those that support that meaning which is predominant, characterized by <s>rasa</s> etc. — they are <s>guṇas</s>, like valor and the like [in a hero]. But those that are dependent on the subordinate elements — namely the expressed meaning and expression — they should be regarded as <s>alaṅkāras</s>, like bracelets and the like. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.6]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And thus:
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.7:]

children.text: śṛṅgāra eva madhuraḥ paraḥ prahlādano rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) alone is the supremely sweet, delightful <s>rasa</s>;

children.text: tan-mayaṃ kāvyam āśritya mādhuryaṃ pratitiṣṭhati // DhvK_2.7 //
children.translated_text: Depending on poetry pervaded by it, <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) is established. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.7]

children.text: śṛṅgāra eva rasāntarāpekṣayā madhuraḥ prahlāda-hetutvāt / tat-prakāśana-para-śabdārthatayā kāvyasya sa mādhurya-lakṣaṇo guṇaḥ / śravyatvaṃ punar ojaso 'pi sādhāraṇam iti || DhvA_2.7 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> alone, in comparison with other <s>rasas</s>, is sweet, because it is the cause of delight. The <s>guṇa</s> characterized as <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) belongs to poetry whose words and meanings are devoted to manifesting that [<s>rasa</s>]. Agreeableness to the ear, however, is common to <s>ojas</s> (vigor) as well. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.7]
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.8:]

children.text: śṛṅgāre vipralambhākhye karuṇe ca prakarṣavat /
children.translated_text: In <s>śṛṅgāra</s> known as <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) and in <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic), preeminently,

children.text: mādhuryam ārdratāṃ yāti yatas tatrādhikaṃ manaḥ // DhvK_2.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness) reaches the state of <s>ārdratā</s> (tenderness), because the mind is more [engaged] there. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.8]

children.text: vipralambha-śṛṅgāra-karuṇayos tu mādhuryam eva prakarṣavat / sahṛdaya-hṛdayāvarjanātiśaya-nimittatvād iti || DhvA_2.8 ||
children.translated_text: In <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic love-in-separation) and <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic), <s>mādhurya</s> is preeminent, because it is the cause of the surpassing captivation of the hearts of the sensitive (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.8]
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.9:]

children.text: raudrādayo rasā dīptyā lakṣyante kāvya-vartinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>raudra</s> (furious) and other <s>rasas</s> present in poetry are characterized by <s>dīpti</s> (brilliance);

children.text: tad-vyakti-hetū śabdārthāv āśrityaujo vyavasthitam // DhvK_2.9 //
children.translated_text: Based on the word and meaning that are the causes of their manifestation, <s>ojas</s> (vigor) is established. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.9]

children.text:
raudrādayo hi rasāḥ parāṃ dīptim ujjvalatāṃ janayantīti lakṣaṇayā ta eva dīptir ity ucyate /
tat-prakāśana-paraḥ śabdo dīrgha-samāsa-racanālaṅkṛtaṃ vākyam / yathā-
children.translated_text: For the <s>raudra</s> and other <s>rasas</s> generate supreme brilliance and radiance; by metonymy, they themselves are called <s>dīpti</s> (brilliance). The word devoted to manifesting them is a sentence adorned with long compound constructions. For example:

children.text: cañcad-bhuja-bhramita-caṇḍa-gadābhighāta-
children.translated_text: With whirling arms swinging the fierce mace, whose blows

children.text: sañcūrṇitoru-yugalasya suyodhanasya /
children.translated_text: Have shattered the pair of thighs of <s>Suyodhana</s>,

children.text: styānāvabaddha-ghana-śoṇita-śoṇa-pāṇir
children.translated_text: His hand reddened with thick blood clotted and congealed —

children.text: uttaṃsayiṣyati kacāṃs tava devi bhīmaḥ //(veṇi 1.21)
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīma</s> shall adorn your hair, O queen! [<s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 1.21]

children.text: tat-prakāśana-paraś cārtho 'napekṣita-dīrgha-samāsa-racanaḥ prasanna-vācakābhidheyaḥ / yathā-
yo yaḥ śastraṃ bibharti sva-bhuja-guru-madaḥ pāṇḍavīnāṃ camūnāṃ
children.translated_text: Whoever bears a weapon, intoxicated by the strength of his own arms, among the armies of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>,

children.text: yo yaḥ pāñcāla-gotre śiśur adhika-vayā garbha-śayyāṃ gato vā /
children.translated_text: Whoever in the <s>Pāñcāla</s> clan, whether a child, one advanced in age, or still in the womb,

children.text: yo yas tat-karma-sākṣī carati mayi raṇe yaś ca yaś ca pratīpaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever goes about as a witness of those deeds, and whoever is hostile to me in battle —

children.text: krodhāndhas tasya tasya svayam api jagatām antakasyāntako 'ham //(veṇi 3.32)
children.translated_text: Blinded by fury, I myself am the destroyer of the destroyer of worlds (<s>Antaka</s>) for each and every one of them. [<s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 3.32]
And the meaning devoted to manifesting that [rasa], not requiring long compound constructions, expressed through lucid words, is as follows:

children.text: ity ādau dvayor ojastvam || DhvA_2.9 ||
children.translated_text: In both of the above, there is the quality of <s>ojas</s> (vigor). [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.9]
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.10:]

children.text: samarpakatvaṃ kāvyasya yat tu sarva-rasān prati /
children.translated_text: That quality of poetry which delivers [it] with respect to all <s>rasas</s> —

children.text: sa prasādo guṇo jñeyaḥ sarva-sādhāraṇa-kriyaḥ // DhvK_2.10 //
children.translated_text: That should be known as the <s>guṇa</s> (quality) of <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity), which functions universally. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.10]

children.text: prasādas tu svacchatā śabdārthayoḥ / sa ca sarva-rasa-sādhāraṇo guṇaḥ sarva-racanā-sādhāraṇaś ca vyaṅgyārthāpekṣayaiva mukhyatayā vyavasthito mantavyaḥ || DhvA_2.10 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prasāda</s> is the lucidity of word and meaning. It is a <s>guṇa</s> common to all <s>rasas</s> and common to all [types of] composition, and should be understood as primarily established with reference to the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgyārtha</s>). [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.10]
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.11:]

children.text: śruti-duṣṭādayo doṣā anityā ye ca darśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those faults such as being harsh to the ear (<s>śruti-duṣṭa</s>) and others that have been shown to be non-permanent —

children.text: dhvany-ātmany eva śṛṅgāre te heyā ity udāhṛtāḥ // DhvK_2.11 //
children.translated_text: They are to be avoided only in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> that is the soul of <s>dhvani</s>, so it is declared. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.11]

children.text: anityā doṣāś ca ye śruti-duṣṭādayaḥ sūcitās te 'pi na vācye artha-mātre, na ca vyaṅgye śṛṅgāre vā dhvaner anātma-bhūte / kiṃ tarhi ? dhvanyātmany eva śṛṅgāre 'ṅgitayā vyaṅgye te heyā ity udāhṛtāḥ / anyathā hi teṣām anitya-doṣataiva na syāt / evam ayam asaṃlakṣya-krama-dyoto dhvaner ātmā pradarśitaḥ sāmānyena || DhvA_2.11 ||
children.translated_text: The non-permanent faults such as being harsh to the ear that have been indicated — they are [to be avoided] not in the expressed meaning alone, nor in the suggested <s>śṛṅgāra</s> when it is not the soul of <s>dhvani</s>. Rather, they are to be avoided only in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> that is the soul of <s>dhvani</s>, suggested as the predominant element. For otherwise, their status as non-permanent faults would not hold. Thus, this soul of <s>dhvani</s>, whose sequence of manifestation is imperceptible (<s>asaṃlakṣya-krama-dyota</s>), has been shown in general terms. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.11]
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.12:]

children.text: tasyāṅgānāṃ prabhedā ye prabhedāḥ svagatāś ca ye /
children.translated_text: The varieties of its subordinate elements, and the internal varieties [of those] —

children.text: teṣāmānantyamanyonyasambandhaparikalpane // DhvK_2.12 //
children.translated_text: Their infinity [arises] when their mutual interrelationships are imagined. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.12]

children.text: aṅgitayā vyaṅgyo rasādir vivakṣitāny apara-vācyasya dhvaner eka ātmā ya uktas tasyāṅgānāṃ vācya vācakānupātinām alaṅkārāṇāṃ ye prabhedā niravadhayo ye ca svagatās tasyāṅgino 'rthasya rasa-bhāva-tad-ābhāsa-tat-praśama-lakṣaṇā vibhāvānubhāva-vyabhicāri-pratipādana-sahitā anantāḥ svāśrayāpekṣayā niḥsīmāno viśeṣās teṣām anyonya-sambandha-parikalpane kriyamāṇe kasyacid anyatamasyāpi rasasya prakārāḥ parisaṅkhyātuṃ na śakyante kim uta sarveṣām /
children.translated_text: The <s>rasa</s> etc. suggested as the predominant element — this has been said to be one soul of <s>dhvani</s> where the expressed meaning is intended as secondary. The varieties of its subordinate elements — the <s>alaṅkāras</s> that follow the expressed word and meaning — are limitless; and the internal varieties of that predominant meaning itself, characterized as <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, their semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>), and their subsidence (<s>praśama</s>), together with the presentation of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions), are infinite, with boundless distinctions relative to their own substrates. When the mutual interrelationships among these are imagined, the varieties of even a single <s>rasa</s> cannot be enumerated — how much less those of all of them!

children.text:
tathā hi śṛṅgārasyāṅginas tāvad ādyau dvau bhedau-sambhogo vipralambhaś ca / sambhogasya ca paraspara-prema-darśana-surata-viharaṇādi-lakṣaṇāḥ prakārāḥ /
vipralambhasyāpy abhilāṣerṣyā-viraha-pravāsa-vipralambhādayaḥ / teṣāṃ ca pratyekaṃ vibhāvānubhāva-vyabhicāri-bhedaḥ / teṣāṃ ca deśa-kālādy-āśrayāvasthā-bheda iti svagata-bhedāpekṣayaikasya tasyāparimeyatvaṃ, kiṃ punar aṅga-prabheda-kalpanāyām / te hy aṅga-prabhedāḥ pratyekam aṅgi-prabheda-sambandha-parikalpane kriyamāṇe satyānantyam evopayānti || DhvA_2.12 ||
children.translated_text: For instance, the predominant <s>śṛṅgāra</s> first has two varieties — <s>sambhoga</s> (union) and <s>vipralambha</s> (separation). <s>Sambhoga</s> has varieties characterized by the display of mutual love, lovemaking, amorous play, and so forth. <s>Vipralambha</s> too has [sub-varieties such as] longing (<s>abhilāṣa</s>), jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), physical separation (<s>viraha</s>), separation due to travel (<s>pravāsa</s>), and others. Each of these again has distinctions according to <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s>. And these further differ according to distinctions of place, time, etc., and the states of their substrates. Thus, with respect to internal varieties alone, a single [<s>rasa</s>] is immeasurable — how much more so when the varieties of subordinate elements are considered! For those varieties of subordinate elements, when their mutual interrelation with the varieties of the predominant element is imagined, truly approach infinity. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.12]
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.13:]

children.text: diṅ-mātraṃ tūcyate yena vyutpannānāṃ sa-cetasām /
children.translated_text: Only a general direction is stated, by which the intellect of the learned and sensitive (<s>sahṛdaya</s>),

children.text: buddhir āsāditālokā sarvatraiva bhaviṣyati // DhvK_2.13 //
children.translated_text: Having gained illumination, will [be able to discern] everywhere. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.13]

children.text: diṅ-mātra-kathanena hi vyutpannānāṃ sahṛdayānām ekatrāpi rasa-bhede sahālaṅkārair aṅgāṅgi-bhāva-parijñānād āsāditālokā buddhiḥ sarvatraiva bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: For by the statement of merely a general direction, the intellect of the learned <s>sahṛdayas</s>, having gained illumination through understanding the relationship of predominant and subordinate elements together with <s>alaṅkāras</s> in even a single variety of <s>rasa</s>, will [be able to discern] everywhere.

children.text: tatra-
children.translated_text: On this point:
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.14:]

children.text: śṛṅgārasyāṅgino yatnād eka-rūpānubandhavān /
children.translated_text: When <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is the predominant [<s>rasa</s>], alliteration (<s>anuprāsa</s>) with deliberate uniform continuity

children.text: sarveṣv eva prabhedeṣu nānuprāsaḥ prakāśakaḥ // DhvK_2.14 //
children.translated_text: Is not expressive in all its varieties. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.14]

children.text: aṅgino hi śṛṅgārasya ye uktāḥ prabhedās teṣu sarveṣv eka-prakārānubandhitayā prabandhena pravṛtto 'nuprāso na vyañjakaḥ / aṅgina ity anenāṅga-bhūtasya śṛṅgārasyaika-rūpānubandhy-anuprāsa-nibandhane kāma-cāram āha //2.14 //
children.translated_text: Of the predominant <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, the varieties that have been mentioned — in all of them, <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) employed in continuous succession with uniform pattern is not a revealer [of <s>rasa</s>]. By [the word] 'predominant' (<s>aṅginaḥ</s>), he declares freedom of choice in the employment of uniform alliteration when <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is [merely] a subordinate element. [End of 2.14]
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.15:]

children.text: dhvanyātma-bhūte śṛṅgāre yamakādi-nibandhanam /
children.translated_text: When <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is the soul of <s>dhvani</s>, the employment of <s>yamaka</s> (rhyming repetition) and the like,

children.text: śaktāv api pramāditvaṃ vipralambhe viśeṣataḥ // DhvK_2.15 //
children.translated_text: Even when one is capable of it, is negligence — especially in <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation). [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.15]

children.text: dhvaner ātma-bhūtaḥ śṛṅgāras tātparyeṇa vācya-vācakābhyāṃ prakāśyamānas tasmin yamakādīnāṃ yamaka-prakārāṇāṃ nibandhanaṃ duṣkara-śabda-bhaṅga-śleṣādīnāṃ śaktāv api pramāditvaṃ / "pramāditvam" ity anenaitad darśyate-kāka-tālīyena kadācit kasyacid ekasya yamakāder niṣpattāv api bhūmnālaṅkārāntaravad rasāṅgatvena nibandho na kartavya iti / "vipralambhe viśeṣata" ity anena vipralambhe saukumāryātiśayaḥ khyāpyate / tasmin dyotye yamakāder aṅgasya nibandho niyamān na kartavya iti || DhvA_2.15 ||
children.translated_text: When <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, as the soul of <s>dhvani</s>, is being manifested through the expressed word and meaning as its primary purpose — in that case, the employment of <s>yamaka</s> and the like, including varieties of <s>yamaka</s>, difficult word-patterns (<s>duṣkara-śabda-bhaṅga</s>), <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), etc., even when one is capable of it, constitutes negligence. By 'negligence,' this is shown: even if, by coincidence, a single instance of <s>yamaka</s> or the like happens to occur, it should not be deliberately employed in abundance as a subordinate element of <s>rasa</s>, as other <s>alaṅkāras</s> are. By 'especially in <s>vipralambha</s>,' the extreme delicacy of <s>vipralambha</s> is made known: in that [<s>rasa</s>] to be suggested, the employment of <s>yamaka</s> and the like as subordinate elements must certainly not be made. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.15]

children.text: atra yuktir abhidhīyate-
children.translated_text: Here the rationale is stated:
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.16:]

children.text: rasākṣiptatayā yasya bandhaḥ śakya-kriyo bhavet /
children.translated_text: That <s>alaṅkāra</s> whose composition can be accomplished as if drawn forth by the <s>rasa</s> [itself],

children.text: apṛthag-yatna-nirvatyaḥ so 'laṅkāro dhvanau mataḥ // DhvK_2.16 //
children.translated_text: Achievable without separate effort — that is considered [proper] <s>alaṅkāra</s> in <s>dhvani</s>. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.16]

children.text: niṣpattāv āścarya-bhūto 'pi yasyālaṅkārasya rasākṣiptatayaiva bandhaḥ śakya-kriyo bhavet so 'sminn alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgye dhvanāv alaṅkāro mataḥ / tasyaiva rasāṅgatvaṃ mukhyam ity arthaḥ / yathā-
children.translated_text: Even if wondrous in its achievement, that <s>alaṅkāra</s> whose composition can be accomplished only as drawn forth by the <s>rasa</s> — that is considered an <s>alaṅkāra</s> in this <s>dhvani</s> where the sequence [of manifestation] is imperceptible. Its being a subordinate element of <s>rasa</s> is primary — that is the meaning. For example:

children.text: kapole pattrālī karatala-nirodhena mṛditā
children.translated_text: The leaf-ornament on the cheek has been crushed by the pressure of [his] palm;

children.text: nipīto niḥśvāsair ayam amṛta-hṛdyo 'dhara-rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: This nectar-sweet lip-juice has been drunk in by [his] sighs;

children.text: muhuḥ kaṇṭhe lagnas taralayati bāṣpa-stana-taṭīṃ
children.translated_text: Clinging repeatedly to the neck, he agitates the breast-slope with tears —

children.text: priyo manyur jātas tava niranurodhe na tu vayam //[*11]
children.translated_text: O darling, anger has arisen at your indifference, not at us.
Reference: Amaru 67; Srk 664, Skm 720, Skv 489, Sv 1627

children.text: Amaru 67; Srk 664, Skm 720, Skv 489, Sv 1627

rasāṅgatve ca tasya lakṣaṇam apṛthag-yatna-nirvartyatvam iti yo rasaṃ bandhu-madhya-vasitasya kaver alaṅkāras tāṃ vāsanām atyūhya yatnāntaram āsthitasya niṣpadyate sa na rasāṅgam iti / yamake ca prabandhena buddhi-pūrvakaṃ kriyamāṇe niyamenaiva yatnāntara-parigraha āpatati śabda-viśeṣānveṣaṇa-rūpaḥ / alaṅkārāntareṣv api tat-tulyam iti cet-naivam; alaṅkārāntarāṇi hi nirūpyamāṇa-durghaṭanāny api rasa-samāhita-cetasaḥ pratibhānavataḥ kaver aham-pūrvikayā parāpatanti / yathā kādambaryāṃ kādambarī-darśanāvasare / yathā ca māyā-rāma-śiro-darśanena vihvalāyāṃ sīta-devyāṃ setau / yuktaṃ caitat, yato rasā vācya-viśeṣair evākṣeptavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the criterion for [an <s>alaṅkāra</s>'s] being a subordinate of <s>rasa</s> is that it is produced without separate effort. Thus, for a poet who dwells within the family of <s>rasa</s>, the <s>alaṅkāra</s> [arises naturally]; but one that is produced by abandoning that natural tendency (<s>vāsanā</s>) and resorting to a separate effort is not a subordinate of <s>rasa</s>. And in the case of <s>yamaka</s> (paronomasia) composed deliberately in a sustained manner, the resort to a separate effort—in the form of searching for specific words—invariably arises. [Objection:] The same is true of other <s>alaṅkāras</s> as well. [Reply:] Not so; for other <s>alaṅkāras</s>, even though difficult to achieve when examined, come rushing forward spontaneously to the genius-endowed poet whose mind is absorbed in <s>rasa</s>. As in the <s>Kādambarī</s>, at the occasion of seeing <s>Kādambarī</s>. And as on the bridge [to <s>Laṅkā</s>], when queen <s>Sītā</s> was distraught upon seeing the illusory head of <s>Rāma</s>. And this is fitting, since <s>rasas</s> are to be evoked precisely through specific expressed meanings.

children.text: asyaivārthasya saṅgraha-ślokāḥ-
children.translated_text: Summary verses of this very subject:

children.text: rasavanti hi vastūni sālaṅkārāṇi kānicit /
children.translated_text: Some things endowed with <s>rasa</s> and possessing <s>alaṅkāras</s>

children.text: ekenaiva prayatnena nirvartyante mahā-kaveḥ //
children.translated_text: are produced by a great poet through a single effort alone.

children.text: yamakādi-nibandhe tu pṛthag-yatno 'sya jāyate /
children.translated_text: But in the composition of <s>yamaka</s> and the like, a separate effort arises for him.

children.text: śaktasyāpi rase 'ṅgatvaṃ tasmād eṣāṃ na vidyate //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the status of being subordinate to <s>rasa</s> does not exist for these.

children.text: rasābhāsāṅga-bhāvas tu yamakāder na vāryate /
children.translated_text: But the status of being subordinate to <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>) is not precluded for <s>yamaka</s> and the like.

children.text: dhvany-ātma-bhūte śṛṅgāre tv aṅgatā nopapadyate || DhvA_2.16 ||
children.translated_text: However, subordination [to <s>rasa</s>] is not possible when <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) constitutes the essence of <s>dhvani</s>. // DhvA_2.16 //

children.text: idānīṃ dhvany-ātma-bhūtasya śṛṅgārasya vyañjako 'laṅkāra-varga ākhyāyate-
children.translated_text: Now, the class of <s>alaṅkāras</s> that serves as the suggestor of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> as the essence of <s>dhvani</s> is described:
DhvK 2.17:

children.text: dhvany-ātma-bhūte śṛṅgāre samīkṣya viniveśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: When, in [a composition where] <s>śṛṅgāra</s> constitutes the essence of <s>dhvani</s>, the class of <s>alaṅkāras</s> beginning with <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) is deployed with deliberation,

children.text: rūpakādir alaṅkāra-varga eti yathārthatām // DhvK_2.17 //
children.translated_text: it achieves its true purpose [of being an <s>alaṅkāra</s>, i.e., an 'ornament']. // DhvK_2.17 //

children.text:
alaṅkāro hi bāhyālaṅkārasāmyādaṅginaścārutva-heturucyate /
vācyālaṅkāravargaś ca rūpakādiryāvānukto vakṣyate ca kaiścit, alaṅkārāṇāmanantatvāt ///
children.translated_text: For an <s>alaṅkāra</s> is called a cause of beauty for its bearer, by analogy with external ornamentation. And the class of expressed <s>alaṅkāras</s> beginning with <s>rūpaka</s>, however many have been described and will be described by various [authorities], is infinite in its varieties.

children.text: sa sarvo 'pi yadi samīkṣya viniveśyate tada-lakṣyakramavyaṅgyasya dhvaner aṅginaḥ sarvasyaiva cārutvaheturniṣpadyate || DhvA_2.17 ||
children.translated_text: If all of these are deployed with deliberation, they all become causes of beauty for <s>dhvani</s>—the bearer—whose suggestion occurs in the <s>alakṣyakrama</s> (imperceptibly sequenced) mode. // DhvA_2.17 //

children.text: eṣā cāsya viniveśane samīkṣā-
children.translated_text: And this is the deliberation in their deployment:

children.text: vivakṣā tatparatvena nāṅgitvena kadācana /
children.translated_text: The intention [should be] directed toward it [<s>rasa</s>] as primary—never toward the <s>alaṅkāra</s> as the principal element.

children.text: kāle ca grahaṇa-tyāgau nātinirvahaṇaiṣitā // DhvK_2.18 //
children.translated_text: And [there should be] adoption and abandonment at the right time; [the poet] should not be excessively eager to carry [the <s>alaṅkāra</s>] through. // DhvK_2.18 //

children.text: nirvyūḍhāv api cāṅgatve yatnena pratyavekṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: And even when [an <s>alaṅkāra</s>] has been carried through, its subordination should be carefully examined.

children.text: rūpakādir alaṅkāra-vargasyāṅgatva-sādhanam // DhvK_2.19 //
children.translated_text: [These are] the means of establishing the subordination of the class of <s>alaṅkāras</s> beginning with <s>rūpaka</s>. // DhvK_2.19 //

children.text: rasa-bandheṣv atyādṛta-manāḥ kavir yam alaṅkāraṃ tad aṅgatayā vivakṣati / yathā [śaku. 1.20]-
children.translated_text: The poet whose mind is greatly devoted to the composition of <s>rasa</s> intends an <s>alaṅkāra</s> as subordinate to it. As in [<s>Śakuntalā</s> 1.20]:

children.text: calāpāṅgāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ spṛśasi nava-gopa-sudṛśāṃ
children.translated_text: You touch the restless sidelong glance of the beautiful young cowherdesses,

children.text: rahasyākhyāyīva mṛśasi mṛdu karṇāntika-caraḥ /
children.translated_text: and, wandering near the ear, you brush [against it] gently, as if whispering a secret.

children.text: karaṃ vyādhunvatyāḥ pibasi rati-sarvasvam adharaṃ
children.translated_text: You drink the lower lip—the very essence of love—of her whose hand is waving [you away].

children.text: vayaṃ tattvānveṣān madhukara hatās tvaṃ khalu kṛtī //[*12]
children.translated_text: We, through the pursuit of truth, are destroyed, O bee—but you indeed are the successful one!
<s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 515

children.text: Srk 515

atra hi bhramara-svabhāvoktir alaṅkāro rasānuguṇaḥ / "nāṅgitvena" iti na prādhānyena /
kadācid rasādi-tātparyeṇa vivakṣito 'pi hy alaṅkāraḥ kaścid aṅgitvena vivakṣito dṛśyate / yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, the description of the bee's natural behavior is the <s>alaṅkāra</s>, which is in conformity with <s>rasa</s>. 'Not as the principal element' means: not as the primary [intention]. For sometimes an <s>alaṅkāra</s>, even though intended with the purport of <s>rasa</s> and the like, is seen to be intended as the principal element. As in:

children.text: cakrābhighāta-prasabhājñayaiva cakāra yo rāhu-vadhū-janasya /
children.translated_text: He who, by the sheer force of his command through the striking of his discus, turned the body of the conqueror of <s>Bali</s> (<s>Indra</s>) into a woman,

children.text: āliṅganoddāma-vilāsa-vandhyaṃ ratotsavaṃ cumbana-mātra-śeṣam //
children.translated_text: and made the love-festival of the wives of <s>Rāhu</s> barren of the passionate play of embracing, reduced to mere kissing—

children.text: atra hi paryāyoktasyāṅgitvena vivakṣā rasādi-tātparye saty apīti / aṅgatvena vivakṣitam api yam avasare gṛhṇāti nānavasare /
children.translated_text: here, the <s>paryāyokti</s> (periphrasis) is intended as the principal element, even though the purport is toward <s>rasa</s> and the like. An [<s>alaṅkāra</s>] intended as subordinate, which one adopts at the right occasion and not at the wrong occasion:

children.text: avasare gṛhītir, yathā (ratnāvalyāṃ 2.4)-
children.translated_text: An example of adoption at the right occasion, as in [<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 2.4]:

children.text: uddāmotkalikāṃ vipāṇḍura-rucaṃ prārabdha-jṛmbhāṃ kṣaṇād āyāsaṃ śvasanodgamair aviratair ātanvatīm ātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: With its bud-bursts opening wildly, its color pale, its yawning begun in a moment,

children.text: adyodyānalatām imāṃ samadanāṃ nārīm ivānyāṃ dhruvaṃ paśyan kopa-vipāṭala-dyuti mukhaṃ devyāḥ kariṣyāmy aham //[*13]
children.translated_text: spreading its own fatigue through ceaseless gusts of breath—seeing this garden-creeper today, like another passionate woman, I shall surely make the queen's face redden with the glow of anger!
<s>Rasārṇavasudhākara</s> 2.26.

children.text: Rasārṇava-sudhākara 2.26.
ity atra upamā śleṣasya / gṛhītam api ca yam avasare tyajati tad-rasānuguṇa-tayālaṅkārāntarāpekṣayā / yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>upamā</s> (simile) [is subordinate] to the <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning). And [an <s>alaṅkāra</s>] that has been adopted but which one abandons at the right occasion—that [abandonment is] in view of another <s>alaṅkāra</s> more conducive to that <s>rasa</s>. As in:

children.text: raktas tvaṃ nava-pallavair aham api ślāghyaiḥ priyāyā guṇais
children.translated_text: You are enamored of fresh sprouts; I too [am enamored] of the praiseworthy qualities of my beloved.

children.text: tvām āyānti śilīmukhāḥ smara-dhanur-muktās tathā mām api /
children.translated_text: The bee-arrows released from the bow of <s>Kāma</s> (Love) assail you—and me as well.

children.text: kāntāpāda-talāhatis tava mude tadvan mamāpy āvayoḥ
children.translated_text: The kick of the beloved's foot is your delight—and mine as well. Of the two of us,

children.text: sarvaṃ tulyam aśoka kevalam ahaṃ dhātrā sa-śokaḥ kṛtaḥ //[*14]
children.translated_text: everything is the same, O <s>Aśoka</s> tree—except that the Creator has made me one 'with sorrow' (<s>sa-śoka</s>)!
<s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 770.

children.text: Srk 770.

atra hi prabandha-pravṛtto 'pi śleṣo vyatireka-vivakṣayā tyajyamāno rasa-viśeṣam puṣṇāti /
nātrālaṅkāra-dvaya-sannipātaḥ, kiṃ tarhi ? alaṅkārāntaram eva śleṣa-vyatireka-lakṣaṇaṃ narasiṃhavad iti cet-na, tasya prakārāntareṇa vyavasthāpanāt / yatra hi śleṣa-viṣaya eva śabde prakārāntareṇa vyatireka-pratītir jāyate sa tasya viṣayaḥ / yathā-"sa harir nāmnā devaḥ sa-harir vara-turaga-nivahena" ity ādau /
children.translated_text: Here, although the <s>śleṣa</s> (pun) was in progress throughout, its abandonment through the intention of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) nourishes the particular <s>rasa</s>. Nor should it be said that this is a conjunction of two <s>alaṅkāras</s>, but rather that it is simply another <s>alaṅkāra</s> characterized by the <s>śleṣa-vyatireka</s>, like <s>Narasiṃha</s> [being both man and lion]—no, because that [<s>vyatireka</s>] is established through a different mode. For where the perception of <s>vyatireka</s> arises through a different mode in the very word that is the domain of <s>śleṣa</s>—that is its [proper] domain. As in: '<s>Sa hariḥ</s> by name the god, <s>sa-hariḥ</s> (with horses) by his excellent troop of steeds,' and so forth.

children.text: atra hy anya eva śabdaḥ śleṣasya viṣayo 'nyaś ca vyatirekasya / yadi caivaṃ-vidhe viṣaye 'laṅkārāntaratva-kalpanā kriyate tat-saṃsṛṣṭer viṣayāpahāra eva syāt / śleṣa-mukhenaivātra vyatirekasyātma-lābha iti nāyaṃ saṃsṛṣṭer viṣaya iti cet-na ; vyatirekasya prakārāntareṇāpi darśanāt / yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, one word is the domain of <s>śleṣa</s> and another of <s>vyatireka</s>. And if the classification as a different <s>alaṅkāra</s> is made in such a domain, it would amount to a usurpation of the domain of <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination). [Objection:] The <s>vyatireka</s> here achieves its existence only through the medium of <s>śleṣa</s>, and therefore this is not the domain of <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>. [Reply:] No, because <s>vyatireka</s> is also observed in another mode. As in:

children.text: no kalpāpāya-vāyor adaya-raya-dalat-kṣmādharasyāpi śamyā
children.translated_text: Not extinguished even by the merciless blast of the wind at the dissolution of the age that splits the horizon,

children.text: gāḍhodgīrṇojjvala-śrīr ahani na rahitā no tamaḥ-kajjalena /
children.translated_text: with its tightly [held] brilliance radiant and full, not deprived even in the day, not [smeared] with the collyrium of darkness,

children.text: prāptotpattiḥ pataṅgān na punar upagatā moṣa-muṣṇa-tviṣo vo
children.translated_text: not having attained [fresh] production of moths, nor again having acquired the brightness of a jewel that steals [its appearance]—

children.text: vartiḥ saivānya-rūpā sukhayatu nikhila-dvīpa-dīpasya dīptiḥ //
children.translated_text: may that very same wick, though in another form, that light of the lamp of the entire world, bring you happiness!

children.text:
atra hi sāmya-prapañca-pratipādanaṃ vinaiva vyatireko darśitaḥ / nātra śleṣa-mātrāc cārutva-pratītir astīti śleṣasya vyatirekāṅgatvenaiva vivakṣitatvāt na svato 'laṅkāratety api na vācyam /
yata evaṃ-vidhe viṣaye sāmya-mātrād api supratipāditāc cārutvaṃ dṛśyata eva / yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) has been shown without any elaborate display of similarity. Nor should it be said that here the perception of beauty comes from <s>śleṣa</s> alone and therefore <s>śleṣa</s> has been intended as subordinate to <s>vyatireka</s> and is not an <s>alaṅkāra</s> in its own right—because in such a domain, beauty is seen even from well-established similarity alone. As in:

children.text:
ākrandāḥ stanitair vilocana-jalānya-śrānta-dhārāmbudhis
tad-viccheda-bhuvaś ca śoka-śikhinas tulyās taḍid-vibhramaiḥ /
antar me dayitā-mukhaṃ tava śaśī vṛttiḥ samaivāvayos
tat kiṃ mām aniśaṃ sakhe jala-dhara tvaṃ dagdhum evodyataḥ //[*15] ity ādau /
children.translated_text: Within me is the face of my beloved; in you is the moon—our way of being is the same. Then why, O friend cloud, are you constantly intent on burning me?' And so on.
<s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 240, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 993, by <s>Yaśodharman</s>, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 43.33.

children.text: Srk 240, Skm 993, yaśodharmaṇaḥ, Smv 43.33.

children.translated_text: 'My cries are [like] your thunders; my tears are [like] your unwearied streams of rain; and the flames of my grief are comparable to your flashes of lightning.

children.text: rasa-nirvahaṇaika-tāna-hṛdayo yaṃ ca nātyantaṃ nirvoḍhum icchati / yathā-
children.translated_text: And an [<s>alaṅkāra</s>] that one whose heart is single-mindedly devoted to the completion of <s>rasa</s> does not wish to carry through excessively. As in:

children.text: kopāt komala-lola-bāhu-latikā-pāśena baddhā dṛḍhaṃ
children.translated_text: Firmly bound in anger by the noose of soft, trembling arm-creepers,

children.text: nītvā vāsa-niketanaṃ dayitayā sāyaṃ sakhīnāṃ puraḥ /
children.translated_text: led to the dwelling-place by the beloved, in the evening, before her friends—

children.text: bhūyo naivam iti skhalat-kala-girā saṃsūcya duśceṣṭitaṃ
children.translated_text: and then, indicating the misdeed with faltering sweet words, 'Never again like this!'—

children.text: dhanyo hanyata eva nihnuti-paraḥ preyān rudatyā hasan //
children.translated_text: blessed is the lover who, intent on denial, is struck by [his beloved who is] weeping yet laughing!

children.text: atra hi rūpakam ākṣiptam anirvyūḍhaṃ ca paraṃ rasa-puṣṭaye / nirvoḍhum iṣṭam api yaṃ yatnād aṅgatvena pratyavekṣate yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) was evoked and left unelaborated—for the enrichment of <s>rasa</s>. And an [<s>alaṅkāra</s>] that, even when one wishes to carry it through, one carefully examines for its subordination [to <s>rasa</s>]. As in:

children.text:
śyāmāsvaṅgaṃ cakita-hariṇī-prekṣaṇe dṛṣṭi-pātaṃ
gaṇḍa-cchāyāṃ śaśini śikhināṃ barha-bhāreṣu keśān /
utpaśyāmi pratanuṣu nadī-vīciṣu bhrū-vilāsān
hantaika-sthaṃ kvacid api na te bhīru sādṛśyam asti //ity ādau /
children.translated_text: 'In the dark-complexioned [women] I see your limbs; in the glance of a startled doe, the fall of your gaze; in the moon, the luster of your cheek; in the peacocks' heavy plumes, your hair; in the slender waves of the river, the play of your brows. Alas, O timid one, nowhere at all is there an [exact] likeness of you gathered in one place!' And so on.

children.text: sa evam upanibadhyamāno 'laṅkāro rasābhivyakti-hetuḥ kaver bhavati / ukta-prakārātikrame tu niyamenaiva rasa-bhaṅga-hetuḥ saṃpadyate / lakṣyaṃ ca tathāvidhaṃ mahā-kavi-prabandheṣv api dṛśyate bahuśaḥ / tat tu sūkti-sahasra-dyotitātmanāṃ mahātmanāṃ doṣodghoṣaṇam ātmana eva dūṣaṇaṃ bhavatīti na vibhajya darśitam / kiṃ tu rūpakāder alaṅkāra-vargasya yeyaṃ vyañjakatve rasādi-viṣaye lakṣaṇa-dig-darśitā tām anusaran svayaṃ cānyal lakṣaṇam utprekṣamāṇo yady alakṣya-krama-pratibham anantaroktam enaṃ dhvaner ātmānam upanibadhnāti sukaviḥ samāhita-cetās tadā tasyātma-lābho bhavati mahīyān iti || DhvA_2.18-19 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>alaṅkāra</s> thus composed becomes the cause of the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> for the poet. But when the prescribed method is transgressed, it invariably becomes the cause of the destruction of <s>rasa</s>. And such instances are seen abundantly even in the works of great poets. But to proclaim the faults of great souls whose selves have been illuminated by thousands of fine sayings would be a blemish upon oneself—therefore [such instances] have not been shown in detail. But if the true poet, with concentrated mind, following this direction that has been indicated regarding the definition of the suggestive function of the class of <s>alaṅkāras</s> beginning with <s>rūpaka</s> in the domain of <s>rasa</s>, and also devising further definitions on his own, composes this soul of <s>dhvani</s> that is imperceptibly sequenced and genius-born as described above—then a magnificent realization [of <s>dhvani</s>] comes about. // DhvA_2.18-19 //
DhvK 2.20:

children.text: krameṇa pratibhāty ātmā yo 'syānusvāna-sannibhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The soul [of <s>dhvani</s>] that shines forth sequentially, which resembles a reverberation (<s>anusvāna</s>)—

children.text: śabdārtha-śakti-mūlatvāt so 'pi dvedhā vyavasthitaḥ // DhvK_2.20 //
children.translated_text: since it is rooted in the power of word and meaning, it too is established as twofold. // DhvK_2.20 //

children.text: asya vivakṣitāny apara-vācyasya dhvaneḥ saṃlakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyatvād anuraṇana-prakhyo ya ātmā so 'pi śabda-śakti-mūlo 'rtha-śakti-mūlaś ceti dvi-prakāraḥ || DhvA_2.20 ||
children.translated_text: Of this <s>dhvani</s> whose expressed meaning is intended as something other [than the suggested], the soul that is of the <s>saṃlakṣyakrama</s> (perceptibly sequenced) type of suggestion—resembling a reverberation—is also of two kinds: rooted in the power of the word, and rooted in the power of meaning. // DhvA_2.20 //

children.text: nanu śabda-śaktyā yatrārthāntaraṃ prakāśate sa yadi dhvaneḥ prakāra ucyate tad idānīṃ śleṣasya viṣaya evāpahṛtaḥ syāt, nāpahṛta ity āha-
children.translated_text: Objection: If [<s>dhvani</s>] where another meaning shines forth through the power of the word is called a type of <s>dhvani</s>, then the domain of <s>śleṣa</s> (punning) would be usurped. [Reply:] It is not usurped, he says:
DhvK 2.21:

children.text: ākṣipta evālaṅkāraḥ śabda-śaktyā prakāśate /
children.translated_text: Where an <s>alaṅkāra</s> that is merely implied shines forth through the power of the word,

children.text: yasminn anuktaḥ śabdena śabda-śakty-udbhavo hi saḥ // DhvK_2.21 //
children.translated_text: and is not stated by the word—that is born of the power of the word [as <s>dhvani</s>]. // DhvK_2.21 //

children.text: yasmād alaṅkāro na vastu-mātraṃ yasmin kāvye śabda-śaktyā prakāśate sa śabda-śakty-udbhavo dhvanir ity asmākaṃ vivakṣitam / vastu-dvaye ca śabda-śaktyā prakāśamāne śleṣaḥ / yathā-
children.translated_text: Since what we intend [as <s>dhvani</s>] is the case where an <s>alaṅkāra</s>—not a mere thing (<s>vastu</s>)—shines forth through the power of the word: that is the word-power-born <s>dhvani</s>. But where two things (<s>vastu</s>) shine forth through the power of the word, that is <s>śleṣa</s>. As in:

children.text: yena dhvasta-manobhavena balijit-kāyaḥ purāstrī-kṛto
children.translated_text: He by whom, having vanquished the god of love (<s>Manobhava</s>), the body of the conqueror of <s>Bali</s> (<s>Indra</s>) was turned into a woman;

children.text: yaś codvṛtta-bhujaṅga-hāra-valayo gaṅgāṃ ca yo 'dhārayat /
children.translated_text: and he whose arms are adorned with upraised serpent-garlands, and who bore the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;

children.text: yasyāhuḥ śaśimac chiro hara iti stutyaṃ ca nāmāmarāḥ
children.translated_text: he whose head, they say, bears the moon—'O <s>Hara</s>!'—and whose name the immortals praise—

children.text: pāyāt sa svayam andhaka-kṣaya-karas tvāṃ sarvado mādhavaḥ //
children.translated_text: may that <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>/<s>Śiva</s>), the destroyer of <s>Andhaka</s>, the all-giver, protect you himself!

children.text: nanv alaṅkārāntara-pratibhāyām api śleṣa-vyapadeśo bhavatīti darśitaṃ bhaṭṭodbhaṭena, tat punar api śabda-śakti-mūlo dhvanir niravakāśa ity āśaṅkyedam uktam "ākṣipta" iti / tad ayam arthaḥ-yatra śabda-śaktyā sākṣād alaṅkārāntaraṃ vācyaṃ sat pratibhāsate sa sarvaḥ śleṣa-viṣayaḥ / yatra tu śabda-śaktyā sāmarthyākṣiptaṃ vācya-vyatiriktaṃ vyaṅgyam evālaṅkārāntaraṃ prakāśate sa dhvaner viṣayaḥ / śabda-śaktyā sākṣād-alaṅkārāntara-pratibhā yathā-
children.translated_text: Objection: But [the rhetorician] <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s> has shown that even where another <s>alaṅkāra</s> [merely] shines forth, the designation of <s>śleṣa</s> applies. Therefore, the word-power-born <s>dhvani</s> is again left without scope. Anticipating this objection, [the author] has said 'merely implied.' The meaning is this: Where another <s>alaṅkāra</s> directly appears as something expressed through the power of the word—all of that is the domain of <s>śleṣa</s>. But where, through the power of the word, an implied (<s>sāmarthyākṣipta</s>) <s>alaṅkāra</s>—which is distinct from the expressed and is the suggested [meaning] alone—shines forth, that is the domain of <s>dhvani</s>. An example of an <s>alaṅkāra</s> directly appearing through the power of the word:

children.text: tasyā vināpi hāreṇa nisargād eva hāriṇau /
children.translated_text: Even without a necklace, her breasts, which by nature were captivating (<s>hāriṇau</s>),

children.text: janayāmāsatuḥ kasya vismayaṃ na payodharau //
children.translated_text: produced astonishment in whom did they not?

children.text: atra śṛṅgāra-vyabhicārī vismayākhyo bhāvaḥ sākṣād-virodhālaṅkāraś ca pratibhāsata iti virodha-cchāyānugrāhiṇaḥ śleṣasyāyaṃ viṣayaḥ / na tv anusvānopama-vyaṅgyasya dhvaneḥ / alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyasya tu dhvaner vācyena śleṣeṇa virodher na vā vyañjitasya viṣaya eva /
children.translated_text: Here, the emotion called wonder (<s>vismaya</s>), which is a transient state of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, and the <s>alaṅkāra</s> of <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) directly appear—therefore this is the domain of <s>śleṣa</s>, which supports the shadow of <s>virodha</s>. It is not, however, the domain of <s>dhvani</s> of the reverberation-like suggested type. But it is indeed the domain of <s>dhvani</s> of the imperceptibly-sequenced suggested type, [where] <s>virodha</s> is suggested by the expressed <s>śleṣa</s>.

children.text: tasyā vināpi hāreṇa nisargād eva hāriṇau /
children.translated_text: Even without a necklace, her breasts, which by nature were captivating (<s>hāriṇau</s>),

children.text: janayāmāsatuḥ kasya vismayaṃ na payodharau //
children.translated_text: produced astonishment in whom did they not?

children.text: atra śṛṅgāra-vyabhicārī vismayākhyo bhāvaḥ sākṣād-virodhālaṅkāraś ca pratibhāsata iti virodha-cchāyānugrāhiṇaḥ śleṣasyāyaṃ viṣayaḥ / na tv anusvānopama-vyaṅgyasya dhvaneḥ / alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyasya tu dhvaner vācyena śleṣeṇa virodher na vā vyañjitasya viṣaya eva /
children.translated_text: Here, the emotion called wonder (<s>vismaya</s>), which is a transient state of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, and the <s>alaṅkāra</s> of <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) directly appear—therefore this is the domain of <s>śleṣa</s>, which supports the shadow of <s>virodha</s>. It is not, however, the domain of <s>dhvani</s> of the reverberation-like suggested type. But it is indeed the domain of <s>dhvani</s> of the imperceptibly-sequenced suggested type, [where] <s>virodha</s> is suggested by the expressed <s>śleṣa</s>.

children.text: yathā mamaiva-
children.translated_text: As in [a verse] of my own:

children.text: ślāghyāśeṣa-tanuṃ sudarśana-karaḥ sarvāṅga-līlājita-
children.translated_text: He of praiseworthy body in every limb, [the wielder of the] <s>Sudarśana</s> in his hand, who by the grace of every limb has conquered

children.text: trailokyāṃ caraṇāravinda-lalitenākrānta-loko hariḥ /
children.translated_text: the three worlds, who with the loveliness of his lotus-feet has pervaded all the worlds—<s>Hari</s>!

children.text: bibhrāṇāṃ mukham indu-sundara-rucaṃ candrātma-cakṣur dadhat
children.translated_text: Bearing a face radiant as the beautiful moon, possessing eyes that are the very essence of the moon,

children.text: sthāne yāṃ svatanor apaśyad adhikāṃ sā rukmiṇī vo 'vatāt //
children.translated_text: She whom He rightly beheld as surpassing His own body—may that <s>Rukmiṇī</s> protect you! //

children.text: atra vācyatayaiva vyatireka-cchāyānugrāhī śleṣaḥ pratīyate / yathā ca-
children.translated_text: Here, <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) that supports the semblance of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) is perceived as expressed meaning itself. And as [another example]—

children.text: bhramim aratim alasa-hṛdayatāṃ
children.translated_text: Bewilderment, restlessness, languor of heart,

children.text: pralayaṃ mūrcchāṃ tamaḥ śarīra-sārdam /
children.translated_text: dissolution, swooning, darkness together with the body,

children.text: maraṇaṃ ca jalada-bhuja-gajaṃ
children.translated_text: and death—like a cloud-armed elephant,

children.text: prasahya kurute viṣaṃ viyoginīnām //
children.translated_text: poison forcibly inflicts [all these] upon women in separation. //

children.text: yathā vā-
children.translated_text: Or as [in this example]—

children.text: camahia-māṇasa-kañcaṇa-paṅka-aṇi mmahia-parimalā jassa /
children.translated_text: He whose mind-born golden lotuses are crushed, whose fragrance is churned,

children.text: akhaṇḍia-dāṇa-pasārā bāhu-ppalihā ccia ga{i}ndā //
children.translated_text: whose unbroken streams of <s>dāna</s> (ichor) [flow], whose arms are like iron bars—[such are his] elephants. //

children.text: [khaṇḍita-mānasa-kāñcana-paṅkajanir mathita-parimalā yasya /
children.translated_text: [He whose mind-born golden lotuses are crushed, whose fragrance is churned,

children.text: akhaṇḍita-dāna-prasarā bāhu-parighā iva gajendrāḥ //]
children.translated_text: whose unbroken streams of <s>dāna</s> (ichor) [flow], whose arms are like iron bars—[such are his] lordly elephants. //]

children.text: atra rūpaka-cchāyānugrāhī śleṣo vācyatayaivāvabhāsate / sa cākṣipto 'laṅkāro yatra punaḥ śabdāntareṇābhihita-svarūpas tatra na śabda-śakty-udbhavānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgya-dhvani-vyavahāraḥ / tatra vakrokty-ādi-vācyālaṅkāra-vyavahāra eva / yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) that supports the semblance of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) manifests as expressed meaning itself. And where a figure [of speech] is merely hinted at (<s>ākṣipta</s>), but whose true form is conveyed by a different word—there is no application of the term <s>dhvani</s> as suggestion born from the power of words in the form of resonance (<s>anuranana</s>). In such cases, only the designation of expressed figures like <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique speech) etc. applies. As [in this example]—

children.text: dṛṣṭyā keśava gopa-rāga-hṛtayā kiṃcin na dṛṣṭaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: "With a gaze stolen by love for the cowherd, O <s>Keśava</s>, nothing was seen by me;

children.text: tenaiva skhalitāsmi nātha patitāṃ kiṃ nāma nālambase /
children.translated_text: thereby I stumbled—O Lord, why do you not support me who have fallen?

children.text: ekas tvaṃ viṣameṣu khinna-manasāṃ sarvābalānāṃ gatir
children.translated_text: You alone are the refuge of all helpless women whose minds are distressed in adversity."

children.text: gopyaivaṃ gaditaḥ sa-leśam avatād goṣṭhe harir vaś ciram //
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the <s>gopī</s> with double meaning—may <s>Hari</s> in the cowpen protect you long! //

children.text: evaṃ-jātīyakaḥ sarva eva bhavatu kāmaṃ vācya-śleṣasya viṣayaḥ / yatra tu sāmarthyākṣiptaṃ sad-alaṅkārāntaraṃ śabda-śaktyā prakāśate sa sarva eva dhvaner viṣayaḥ / yathā-"atrāntare kusuma-samaya-yugam upasaṃharann ajṛmbhata grīṣmābhidhānaḥ phulla-mallikā-dhavalāṭṭa-hāso mahā-kālaḥ" /
children.translated_text: Let the entire domain of expressed <s>śleṣa</s> be of this kind, as one wishes. But where a different figure, implied by contextual capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>), is manifested through the power of words—all of that is the domain of <s>dhvani</s>. As [in this example]: "In the interval, the one called <s>Grīṣma</s> (Summer) expanded, withdrawing the pair of flower-seasons—the great <s>Kāla</s> (Time/Death) whose laughter is the white <s>mallikā</s> blossoms in full bloom."

children.text: yathā ca-
children.translated_text: And as [in this example]—

children.text: unnataḥ prollasad-dhāraḥ kālāgarumalīmasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Elevated, with overflowing streams, dark with <s>kālāgaru</s> (black aloe),

children.text: payodharabharastanvyāḥ kaṃ na cakre 'bhilāṣiṇam //
children.translated_text: the weight of [her] breasts—whom did it not make desirous? //

children.text: yathā vā-
dattānandāḥ prajānāṃ samucita-samayākṛṣṭa-sṛṣṭaiḥ payobhiḥ
children.translated_text: Having given delight to the people with waters drawn forth and released at the appropriate time,

children.text: pūrvāhṇe viprakīrṇā diśi diśi viramaty ahni saṃhāra-bhājaḥ /
children.translated_text: scattered in every direction in the forenoon, subject to withdrawal when the day ceases,

children.text: dīptāṃśor dīrgha-duḥkha-prabhava-bhava-bhayodanvad-uttāra-nāvo
children.translated_text: boats for crossing the ocean of the fear of existence that arises from the long suffering [caused by] the blazing-rayed [sun]—

children.text: gāvo vaḥ pāvanānāṃ parama-parimitāṃ prītim utpādayantu //
children.translated_text: may the cows produce in you the supreme and most excellent joy of the purified! //
Or as [in this example]—

children.text: eṣūdāharaṇeṣu śabda-śaktyā prakāśamāne satya-prākaraṇike 'rthāntare vākyasyāsambaddhārthābhidhāyitvaṃ mā prasāṅkṣīd ity aprākaraṇika-prākaraṇikārthayor upamānopameya-bhāvaḥ kalpayitavyaḥ sāmarthyād ity arthākṣipto 'yaṃ śleṣo na śabdopārūḍha iti vibhinna eva śleṣād anusvānopama-vyaṅgyasya dhvaner viṣayaḥ / anye 'pi cālaṅkārāḥ śabda-śakti-mūlānusvāna-rūpa-vyaṅgye dhvanau sambhavanty eva / tathā hi virodho 'pi śabda-śakti-mūlānusvāna-rūpo dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: In these examples, when the contextually relevant secondary meaning is manifested through the power of words, lest the sentence appear to convey an incoherent meaning, one must construe—by contextual capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>)—a relation of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) between the contextually relevant and non-contextually relevant meanings. Thus this <s>śleṣa</s> is implied by meaning (<s>arthākṣipta</s>), not mounted upon the word itself—and hence the domain of <s>dhvani</s> as suggestion in the form of resonance is entirely distinct from [expressed] <s>śleṣa</s>. Other figures too are possible in <s>dhvani</s> as suggestion in the form of resonance rooted in word-power. For indeed, <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) too is seen as having the form of resonance rooted in word-power.

children.text: yathā sthāṇvīśvarākhya-janapada-varṇane bhaṭṭa-bāṇasya-
children.translated_text: As in <s>Bhaṭṭa Bāṇa</s>'s description of the <s>Sthāṇvīśvara</s> region—

children.text: yatra ca mātaṅga-gāminyaḥ śīlavatyaś ca gauryo vibhava-ratāś ca śyāmāḥ padma-rāgiṇyaś ca dhavala-dvija-śuci-vadanā madirāmodiśvasanāś ca pramadāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Where there are women who walk with the gait of elephants and are virtuous, who are fair and devoted to wealth, who are dark-complexioned and passionate for lotus-gems, who have faces pure as white teeth, and whose breath is fragrant with wine."

children.text:
atra hi vācyo virodhas tac-chāyānugrāhī vā śleṣo 'yam iti na śakyaṃ vaktum / sākṣāc-chabdena virodhālaṅkārasyāprakāśitatvāt / yatra hi sākṣāc-chabdāvedito virodhālaṅkāras tatra hi śliṣṭoktau vācyālaṅkārasya virodhasya śleṣasya vā viṣayatvam / yathā tatraiva-
"samavāya iva virodhināṃ padārthānām / tathā hi-sannihita-bālāndhakārāpi bhāsvan-mūrtiḥ" ity ādau /
children.translated_text: Here it cannot be said that the expressed [figure] is <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) or that this is <s>śleṣa</s> supporting its semblance—because the figure of contradiction is not directly manifested by the words. For where the figure of contradiction is directly conveyed by words, there in <s>śliṣṭa</s> (equivocal) expression, either the expressed figure of contradiction or <s>śleṣa</s> is the subject. As in that very [work]: "A co-inherence, as it were, of contradictory entities. For example: 'though proximate darkness is present, [there is] a luminous form'"—and so on.

children.text: yathā vā mamaiva-
children.translated_text: Or as in my own [verse]—

children.text: sarvaika-śaraṇam akṣayam adhīśam īśaṃ dhiyāṃ hariṃ kṛṣṇam /
children.translated_text: The sole refuge of all, imperishable, supreme lord, lord of minds, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: caturātmānaṃ niṣkriyam ari-mathanaṃ namata cakra-dharam //
children.translated_text: the four-souled one, actionless, destroyer of enemies—bow to the bearer of the discus! //

children.text: atra hi śabda-śakti-mūlānusvāna-rūpo virodhaḥ sphuṭam eva pratīyate / evaṃ-vidho vyatireko 'pi dṛśyate / yathā mamaiva-
children.translated_text: Here, <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) in the form of resonance rooted in word-power is clearly perceived. <s>Vyatireka</s> (contrast) of this kind is also seen. As in my own [verse]—

children.text: khaṃ ye 'tyujjvalayanti lūna-tamaso ye vā nakhodbhāsino
children.translated_text: Those who illuminate the sky most brilliantly, who dispel darkness, who shine forth from nails,

children.text: ye puṣṇanti saroruha-śriyam api kṣiptābja-bhāsaś ca ye /
children.translated_text: who nourish the beauty of lotuses, and who cast forth lotus-radiance,

children.text: ye mūrdhasv avabhāsinaḥ kṣiti-bhṛtāṃ ye cāmarāṇāṃ śirāṃ-
children.translated_text: who shine upon the peaks of mountains, and who mount upon the heads of the immortals—

children.text: syākrāmanty ubhaye 'pi te dina-pateḥ pādāḥ śriye santu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: both of these—the feet of the lord of day—may they be for your prosperity! //

children.text: evam anye 'pi śabda-śakti-mūlānusvāna-rūpa-vyaṅgya-dhvani-prakārāḥ santi te sahṛdayaiḥ svayam anusartavyāḥ / iha tu grantha-vistara-bhayān na tat-prapañcaḥ kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus there are other varieties of <s>dhvani</s> as suggestion in the form of resonance rooted in word-power; these should be pursued independently by sensitive readers (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). Here, however, their elaboration has not been undertaken for fear of excessive length of the treatise.
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.22:

children.text: artha-śakty-udbhavas tv anyo yatrārthaḥ sa prakāśate /
children.translated_text: But another [type], born from the power of meaning, where that meaning manifests—

children.text: yas tātparyeṇa vastv anyad vyanakty uktiṃ vinā svataḥ // DhvK_2.22 //
children.translated_text: which, through purport (<s>tātparya</s>), suggests another thing without [explicit] utterance, by itself. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.22 //

children.text: yatrārthaḥ sva-sāmarthyād arthāntaram abhivyanakti śabda-vyāpāraṃ vinaiva so 'rtha-śakty-udbhavo nāmānusvānopama-vyaṅgyo dhvaniḥ /
children.translated_text: Where a meaning, by its own capacity, suggests another meaning without the operation of words—that is called <s>dhvani</s> as suggestion in the form of resonance born from the power of meaning (<s>artha-śakty-udbhava</s>).

children.text: yathā [ku.saṃ. 6.84]-
children.translated_text: As [in <s>Kumārasambhava</s> 6.84]—

children.text: evaṃ vādini devarṣau pārśve pitur adhomukhī /
children.translated_text: While the divine sage (<s>Devarṣi</s>) was thus speaking, [she], with face cast down, at her father's side,

children.text: līlā-kamala-patrāṇi gaṇayāmāsa pārvatī //
children.translated_text: <s>Pārvatī</s> counted the petals of a play-lotus. //

children.text: atra hi līlā-kamala-patra-gaṇanam upasarjanīkṛta-svarūpaṃ śabda-vyāpāraṃ vinaivārthāntaraṃ vyabhicāri-bhāva-lakṣaṇaṃ prakāśayati / na cāyam alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyasyaiva dhvaner viṣayaḥ / yato yatra sākṣac-chabda-niveditebhyo vibhāvānubhāva-vyabhicāribhyo rasādīnāṃ pratītiḥ, sa tasya kevalasya mārgaḥ / yathā kumāra-sambhave madhu-prasaṅge vasanta-puṣpābharaṇaṃ vahantyā devyā āgamanādi-varṇanaṃ manobhava-śara-sandhāna-paryantaṃ śambhoś ca parivṛtta-dhairyasya ceṣṭā-viśeṣa-varṇanādi sākṣac-chabda-niveditam / tasmād ayam anyo dhvaneḥ prakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the counting of play-lotus petals, its own form being subordinated, manifests a different meaning—namely, a <s>vyabhicāri-bhāva</s> (transitory emotion)—without the operation of words. And this is not the domain of <s>dhvani</s> whose sequence is imperceptible (<s>alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgya</s>) alone. Because where <s>rasa</s> and the like are cognized from <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> directly conveyed by words—that is the path of that [other type] alone. As in the <s>Kumārasambhava</s>, in the context of spring: the description of the goddess arriving bearing the ornament of spring flowers, up to the stringing of <s>Manobhava</s>'s (Kāma's) arrows, and the description of the particular gestures of <s>Śambhu</s> whose composure has been shaken—all this is directly conveyed by words. Therefore this is another variety of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: yatra ca śabda-vyāpāra-sahāyo 'rtho 'rthāntarasya vyañjakatvenopādīyate sa nāsya dhvaner viṣayaḥ / yathā-
children.translated_text: And where a meaning, assisted by the operation of words, is employed as suggestive of another meaning—that is not the domain of this [type of] <s>dhvani</s>. As [in this example]—

children.text: saṅketa-kāla-manasaṃ viṭaṃ jñātvā vidagdhayā /
children.translated_text: Knowing the gallant (<s>viṭa</s>) to be thinking of the appointed time, the clever woman

children.text: hasan-netrārpitākūtaṃ līlā-padmaṃ nimīlitam //
children.translated_text: closed her play-lotus, with her intention cast through a laughing glance. //

children.text: atra līlā-kamala-nimīlanasya vyañjakatvam uktyaiva niveditam || DhvA_2.22 ||
children.translated_text: Here, the suggestive function of closing the play-lotus is conveyed by the utterance itself. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Commentary 2.22 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And thus—
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.23:

children.text: śabdārtha-śaktyā kṣipto 'pi vyaṅgyo 'rthaḥ kavinā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when a suggested meaning is implied by the power of word, meaning, or both,

children.text: yatrāviṣkriyate svoktyā sānyaivālaṅkṛtir dhvaneḥ // DhvK_2.23 //
children.translated_text: where [the poet] reveals it through his own utterance—that is a different figure from <s>dhvani</s>. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.23 //

children.text:
śabda-śaktyārtha-śaktyā śabdārtha-śaktyā vākṣipto 'pi vyaṅgyo 'rthaḥ kavinā punaryatra svoktyā prakāśī-kriyate so 'smād anusvānopama-vyaṅgyād dhvaner anya evālaṅkāraḥ /
alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyasya vā dhvaneḥ sati sambhave sa tādṛg anyo 'laṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when a suggested meaning is implied by the power of word, the power of meaning, or by both together—where [the poet] makes it manifest through his own utterance—that is entirely a different figure from this <s>dhvani</s> as resonance-like suggestion. Or rather, when there is the possibility of <s>dhvani</s> whose sequence is imperceptible, such a different figure [may obtain].

children.text: tatra śabda-śaktyā yathā-
children.translated_text: In the case of word-power, as [in this example]—

children.text: vatse mā gā viṣādaṃ śvasanam urujavaṃ santyajordhva-pravṛttaṃ
children.translated_text: "Child, do not despair! Abandon this breath rushing violently upward!

children.text: kampaḥ ko vā gurus te bhavatu balabhidā jṛmbhitenātra yāhi /
children.translated_text: What is this trembling? Let your heaviness be [dispelled]—go [forth] with the yawning of <s>Balabhid</s> (Indra)!

children.text: pratyākhyānaṃ surāṇām iti bhaya-śamana-cchadmanā kārayitvā
children.translated_text: The rejection of the gods!"—having thus caused [him to act] under the pretext of allaying fear,

children.text: yasmai lakṣmī-madād vaḥ sa dahatu duritaṃ mantha-mūḍhāṃ payodhiḥ //
children.translated_text: may that ocean, bewildered by the churning, burn away your sins—he to whom <s>Lakṣmī</s> was given out of pride! //

children.text: artha-śaktyā yathā-
ambā śete 'tra vṛddhā pariṇata-vayasām agraṇīr atra tāto
children.translated_text: "Mother sleeps here, aged; here is father, foremost among those of advanced years;

children.text: niḥśeṣāgāra-karma-śrama-śithila-tanuḥ kumbha-dāsī tathātra /
children.translated_text: here too is the maid-servant <s>Kumbhadāsī</s>, her body weakened by the exhaustion of all household chores.

children.text: asmin pāpāham ekā katipaya-divasa-proṣita-prāṇanāthā
children.translated_text: In this [house], I alone am sinful—my husband having departed for but a few days."

children.text: pānthāyetthaṃ taruṇyā kathitam avasara-vyāhṛti-vyāja-pūrvam //
children.translated_text: Thus was it told by the young woman to the traveler, with words ostensibly about the occasion. //
In the case of meaning-power, as [in this example]—

children.text: ubhaya-śaktyā, yathā-"dṛṣṭyā keśava-gopa-rāga-hṛtayā" ity ādau || DhvA_2.23 ||
children.translated_text: In the case of both powers [combined], as in "With a gaze stolen by love for the cowherd, O <s>Keśava</s>"—and so on. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Commentary 2.23 //
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.24:

children.text: prauḍhokti-mātra-niṣpanna-śarīraḥ sambhavī svataḥ /
children.translated_text: That whose body is produced merely by the bold utterance of the poet, and that which arises by itself—

children.text: artho 'pi dvividho jñeyo vastuno 'nyasya dīpakaḥ // DhvK_2.24 //
children.translated_text: the suggested meaning too should be known as twofold: [one that is] an illuminator of another thing. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.24 //

children.text: artha-śakty-udbhavānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgye dhvanau yo vyañjako 'rtha uktas tasyāpi dvau prakārau-kaveḥ kavi-nibaddhasya vā vaktuḥ prauḍhokti-mātra-niṣpanna-śarīra ekaḥ, svataḥ-sambhavī ca dvitīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>dhvani</s> as suggestion in the form of resonance born from meaning-power, the suggestive meaning that has been described also has two varieties: one whose body is produced merely by the bold utterance (<s>prauḍhokti</s>) of the poet or of a speaker created by the poet, and a second that arises by itself (<s>svataḥ-sambhavī</s>).

children.text: kavi-prauḍhokti-mātra-niṣpanna-śarīro yathā-
children.translated_text: An example of [suggestion] whose body is produced merely by the bold utterance of the poet—

children.text: sajjehi surahi-māso ṇa dāva
children.translated_text: The fragrant spring month does not yet

children.text: appei juva{i}-jaṇa-lakkha-suhe /
children.translated_text: bestow the delights sought by the young women;

children.text: ahiṇava-sahaāra-muhe
children.translated_text: [rather, it bestows] fresh mango-blossoms

children.text: ṇava-pattale aṇaṅgassa sare //
children.translated_text: as new-leafed arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless Love-god). //

children.text: (sajjayati surabhi-māso na tāvad
children.translated_text: (The fragrant spring month does not yet

children.text: arpayati yuvati-jana-lakṣya-sahān /
children.translated_text: bestow the delights sought by the young women;

children.text: abhinava-sahakāra-mukhān
children.translated_text: [rather, it bestows] fresh mango-blossoms

children.text: nava-patralān anaṅgasya śarān //)
children.translated_text: as new-leafed arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s>. //)

children.text: kavi-nibaddha-vaktṛ-prauḍhokti-mātra-niṣpanna-śarīro yathodāhṛtam eva-"śikhariṇi" ity ādi / yathā vā-
children.translated_text: An example of [suggestion] whose body is produced merely by the bold utterance of a speaker created by the poet is the one already cited—"On the <s>Śikharinī</s> [mountain]..." etc. Or as [in this example]—

children.text: sādara-vitīrṇa-yauvana-hastālambaṃ samunnamadbhyām /
children.translated_text: By your two breasts, which are rising upward

children.text: abhyutthānam iva manmathasya dattaṃ tava stanābhyām //
children.translated_text: as if offering a respectfully extended hand-support to [your newly attained] youth—it is as though a rising-up has been given to <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of Love). //

children.text: svataḥ sambhavī ya aucityena bahir api sambhāvyamāna-sad-bhāvo na kevalaṃ bhaṇiti-vaśenaivābhiniṣpanna-śarīraḥ / yathodāhṛtam "evaṃ-vādini" ity ādi / yathā vā-
children.translated_text: That which arises by itself (<s>svataḥ-sambhavī</s>) is that whose existence is plausibly conceived even externally, through propriety (<s>aucitya</s>)—not one whose body is produced solely by the poet's utterance. The example already cited is "While [the sage] was thus speaking..." etc. Or as [in this example]—

children.text: śikhi-piccha-karṇa-pūrā jāyā vyādhasya garviṇī bhramati /
children.translated_text: The hunter's wife, wearing peacock-feather ear-ornaments, walks proudly

children.text: muktā-phala-racita-prasādhanānāṃ madhye sapatnīnām || DhvA_2.24 ||
children.translated_text: among her co-wives who are adorned with pearl ornaments. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Commentary 2.24 //
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.25:

children.text: artha-śakter alaṅkāro yatrāpy anyaḥ pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Where yet another figure is perceived through the power of meaning—

children.text: anusvānopama-vyaṅgyaḥ sa prakāro 'paro dhvaneḥ // DhvK_2.25 //
children.translated_text: that is another variety of <s>dhvani</s> as resonance-like suggestion. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.25 //

children.text: vācyālaṅkāra-vyatirikto yatrānyo 'laṅkāro 'rtha-sāmarthyāt pratīyamāno 'vabhāsate so 'rtha-śakty-udbhavo nāmānusvāna-rūpa-vyaṅgyo 'nyo dhvaniḥ || DhvA_2.25 ||
children.translated_text: Where another figure, distinct from the expressed figure, manifests as perceived through the capacity of meaning—that is another [type of] <s>dhvani</s> as suggestion in the form of resonance born from meaning-power. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Commentary 2.25 //

children.text: tasya pravirala-viṣayatvam āśaṅkyedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Apprehending that this [type] might have only rare instances, it is said—
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.26:

children.text: rūpakādir alaṅkāra-vargo yo vācyatāṃ śritaḥ /
children.translated_text: The group of figures such as <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and others, which has resorted to expressed status [in one place],

children.text: sa sarvo gamyamānatvaṃ bibhrad bhūmnā pradarśitaḥ // DhvK_2.26 //
children.translated_text: has been abundantly demonstrated as also having the status of being suggested [elsewhere]. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.26 //

children.text: anyatra vācyatvena prasiddho yo rūpakādir alaṅkāraḥ so 'nyatra pratīyamānatayā bāhulyena pradarśitas tatrabhavadbhir bhaṭṭodbhaṭādibhiḥ / tathā ca sa-sandehādiṣūpamā-rūpakātiśayoktīnāṃ prakāśamānatvaṃ pradarśitam ity alaṅkārāntarasyālaṅkārāntare vyaṅgyatvaṃ na yatna-pratipādyam || DhvA_2.26 ||
children.translated_text: The figures such as <s>rūpaka</s> and others, well-known elsewhere as expressed, have been abundantly demonstrated by the revered masters such as <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s> and others as having the status of being suggested elsewhere. Thus the manifestation of <s>upamā</s> (simile), <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), and <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) in [contexts like] doubt (<s>saṃdeha</s>) etc. has been shown—therefore the suggestibility of one figure within another is not something requiring [further] effort to establish. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Commentary 2.26 //

children.text: iyat punar ucyata eva-
children.translated_text: This much, however, must be stated—
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.27:

children.text: alaṅkārāntarasyāpi pratītau yatra bhāsate /
children.translated_text: Where, even when another figure is perceived,

children.text: tat-paratvaṃ na vācyasya nāsau mārgo dhvaner mataḥ // DhvK_2.27 //
children.translated_text: the primacy does not belong to the expressed [meaning]—that is not considered the path of <s>dhvani</s>. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.27 //

children.text: alaṅkārāntareṣu tv anuraṇana-rūpālaṅkāra-pratītau satyām api yatra vācyasya vyaṅgya-pratipādanaunmukhyena cārutvaṃ na prakāśate nāsau dhvaner mārgaḥ / tathā ca dīpakādāv alaṅkāre upamāyā gamyamānatve 'pi tatparatvena cārutvasyāvyavasthānān na dhvani-vyapadeśaḥ / yathā-
children.translated_text: But among other figures, even when there is cognition of a figure in the form of resonance, where the charm of the expressed [meaning] does not shine forth through its orientation toward conveying the suggested—that is not the path of <s>dhvani</s>. Thus in figures like <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) and others, even though <s>upamā</s> (simile) is perceived [as suggested], since charm is not established through primacy of that [suggestion], the designation '<s>dhvani</s>' does not apply. As [in this example]—

children.text: canda-maūehiṃ ṇimā ṇalinī kamalehiṃ kusuma-gucchehiṃ laā /
children.translated_text: Night [is made beautiful] by moonbeams, the lotus-pond by lotuses, the vine by clusters of flowers,

children.text: haṃsehiṃ saraa-sohā kavva-kahā sajjanehiṃ kara{i} garuī //
children.translated_text: the autumn splendor by swans, and a poetic tale is made weighty by good people. //

children.text: [candra-mayūkhair niśā nalinī kamalaiḥ kusuma-gucchair latā /
children.translated_text: [Night is made beautiful by moonbeams, the lotus-pond by lotuses, the vine by clusters of flowers,

children.text: haṃsaiḥ śārada-śobhā kāvya-kathā sajjanaiḥ kriyate gurvī //]
children.translated_text: the autumn splendor by swans, and a poetic tale is made weighty by good people. //]

children.text: ity ādiṣūpamā-garbhatve 'pi sati vācyālaṅkāra-mukhenaiva cārutvaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate na vyaṅgyālaṅkāra-tātparyeṇa / tasmāt tatra vācyālaṅkāra-mukhenaiva kāvya-vyapadeśo nyāyyaḥ / yatra tu vyaṅgya-paratvenaiva vācyasya vyavasthānaṃ tatra vyaṅgya-mukhenaiva vyapadeśo yuktaḥ / yathā-
children.translated_text: In such [verses], even though simile (<s>upamā</s>) is embedded [within the figure], the charm is established through the expressed figure (<s>vācyālaṅkāra</s>) alone, not with the intent of a suggested figure (<s>vyaṅgyālaṅkāra</s>). Therefore, in such cases, the designation of poetry is justified through the expressed figure alone. But where the expressed meaning is established precisely through the primacy of the suggested, there the designation of poetry is justified through the suggested alone—

children.text: prāpta-śrīr eṣa kasmāt punar api mayi taṃ mantha-khedaṃ vidadhyān
children.translated_text: Having already attained glory, why should he again inflict upon me that churning-fatigue?

children.text: nidrām apy asya pūrvām anala-manaso naiva sambhāvayāmi /
children.translated_text: I cannot even imagine that this fire-minded one would have had any prior sleep;

children.text: setuṃ badhnāti bhūyaḥ kim iti ca sakala-dvīpa-nāthānuyātas
children.translated_text: 'Why does he again build a bridge?'—and accompanied by the lords of all islands,

children.text: tvayy āyāte vitarkāniti dadhata ivābhāti kampaḥ payodheḥ //
children.translated_text: Upon your arrival, as if harboring such apprehensions—thus appears the trembling of the ocean.

children.text: yathā vā mamaiva-
children.translated_text: Or, as in my own [verse]:

children.text: lāvaṇya-kānti-paripūrita-diṅ-mukhe 'smin
children.translated_text: When this [face], filling the directions with the radiance of loveliness—

children.text: smere 'dhunā tava mukhe taralāyatākṣi /
children.translated_text: Now, O woman of tremulous wide eyes, when your face is smiling—

children.text: kṣobhaṃ yadeti na manāg api tena manye
children.translated_text: That it does not become even slightly agitated—by this I think

children.text: suvyaktam eva jala-rāśir ayaṃ payodhiḥ //
children.translated_text: It is quite evident that this ocean is merely a mass of water.

children.text: ity evaṃ-vidhe viṣaye 'nuraṇana-rūpa-rūpakāśrayeṇa kāvya-cārutva-vyavasthānād rūpaka-dhvanir iti vyapadeśo nyāyyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In such a case, since the charm of poetry is established through a metaphor (<s>rūpaka</s>) in the form of reverberation (<s>anuraṇana</s>), the designation '<s>rūpaka-dhvani</s>' (metaphor-suggestion) is justified.

children.text: upamā-dhvanir, yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Upamā-dhvani</s> (simile-suggestion), as in:

children.text: vīrāṇaṃ rama{i} ghusiṇāruṇammi ṇa tahā piā-thaṇucchaṅge /
children.translated_text: The gaze of heroes does not delight as much in the bosom of the beloved, reddened with saffron,

children.text: diṭṭhī riu-gaa-kumbha-tthalammi jaha bahala-sindūre //
children.translated_text: As it does on the frontal globes of enemy elephants, thickly smeared with vermilion.

children.text: [vīrāṇāṃ ramate ghusṛṇāruṇe na tathā priyā-stanotsaṅge /
children.translated_text: [The gaze of heroes does not delight as much in the bosom of the beloved, reddened with saffron,

children.text: dṛṣṭī ripu-gaja-kumbha-sthale yathā bahala-sindūre //]
children.translated_text: As it does on the frontal globes of enemy elephants, thickly smeared with vermilion.]

children.text: yathā vā mamaiva viṣama-bāṇa-līlāyām asura-parākramaṇe kāmadevasya-
children.translated_text: Or, as in my own [work], the <s>Viṣama-bāṇa-līlā</s> (Sport of the Crooked-Arrowed One), in the section on the attack of the demons against <s>Kāmadeva</s>:

children.text: taṃ tāṇaṃ siri-sahoara-raaṇāharaṇammi hiaam ekka-rasam /
children.translated_text: In the act of seizing those gems, sisters of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), their hearts were single-mindedly [fixed]—

children.text: bimbāhare piāṇaṃ nivesiaṃ kusuma-bāṇena //[*16]
children.translated_text: [But] by the Flower-arrowed One (<s>Kusuma-bāṇa</s>, i.e., <s>Kāmadeva</s>), [their hearts] were lodged on the <s>bimba</s>-fruit-like lips of their beloveds.
Supplement 982 to the <s>Gāhā-sattasaī</s>.

children.text: Supplement 982 to Gāhā-sattasāi.
[tat teṣāṃ śrī-sahodara-ratnāharaṇe hṛdayam eka-rasam /
children.translated_text: [The hearts of those [demons] were single-mindedly [fixed] in seizing those gems, sisters of <s>Śrī</s>—

children.text: bimbādhare priyāṇāṃ niveśitaṃ kusuma-bāṇena //]
children.translated_text: [But] by the Flower-arrowed One (<s>Kāmadeva</s>), [they] were lodged on the <s>bimba</s>-fruit-like lips of their beloveds.]

children.text: ākṣepa-dhvanir, yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Ākṣepa-dhvani</s> (suggestion through apparent denial), as in:

children.text: sa vaktum akhilāñ śakto hayagrīvāśritān guṇān /
children.translated_text: He alone is capable of describing all the virtues possessed by <s>Hayagrīva</s>,

children.text: yo 'mbu-kumbhaiḥ paricchedaṃ jñātuṃ śakto mahodadheḥ //
children.translated_text: Who is capable of knowing the measure of the great ocean by means of water-pots.

children.text: atrātiśayoktyā hayagrīva-guṇānām avarṇanīyatā-pratipādana-rūpasyāsādhāraṇa-tad-viśeṣa-prakāśana-parasyākṣepasya prakāśanam /
children.translated_text: Here, through hyperbole (<s>atiśayokti</s>), what is manifested is an <s>ākṣepa</s> (apparent denial) whose purpose is to establish the indescribability of <s>Hayagrīva</s>'s virtues—uniquely suited to illuminating his special distinction.

children.text: arthāntaranyāsa-dhvaniḥ śabda-śakti-mūlānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgyo 'rtha-śakti-mūlānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgyaś ca sambhavati / tatrādyasyodāharaṇam-
children.translated_text: <s>Arthāntaranyāsa-dhvani</s> (suggestion through corroboration) can have the suggested element in the form of reverberation based on word-power (<s>śabda-śakti</s>) or in the form of reverberation based on meaning-power (<s>artha-śakti</s>). An example of the first:

children.text: devāettammi phale kiṃ kīra{i} ettiaṃ puṇā bhaṇimo /
children.translated_text: 'When the fruit is in the hands of fate, what can be done? This much, however, we say:

children.text: kaṅkilla-pallavāḥ pallavāṇaṃ aṇṇāṇaṃ ṇa saricchā //
children.translated_text: The shoots of the <s>Aśoka</s> tree are unlike other shoots.'

children.text: [daivāyatte phale kiṃ kriyatām etāvat punar bhaṇāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: ['When the fruit is in the hands of fate, what can be done? This much, however, we say:

children.text: raktāśoka-pallavāḥ pallavānām anyeṣāṃ na sadṛśāḥ //]
children.translated_text: The shoots of the <s>Raktāśoka</s> (red <s>Aśoka</s>) are unlike other shoots.']

children.text: pada-prakāśaś cāyaṃ dhvanir iti vākyasyārthāntara-tātparye 'pi sati na virodhaḥ / dvitīyasyodāharaṇaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: And this <s>dhvani</s> is of the word-illuminating (<s>pada-prakāśa</s>) type, so there is no contradiction even though the sentence as a whole has the intent of [establishing] another meaning (<s>arthāntara</s>). An example of the second [type]:

children.text: hiaa-ṭṭhābia-maṇṇuṃ abaruṇṇa-muhaṃ hi maṃ pasāanta /
children.translated_text: 'Even while appeasing me, though I keep my anger lodged in my heart and show no displeasure on my face—

children.text: abaraddhassa bi ṇa hu de bahu-jāṇaa rosiuṃ sakkaṃ //
children.translated_text: Even for one who has offended, O man of many stratagems, it is truly not possible to be angered by you.'

children.text: [hṛdaya-sthāpita-manyum aparoṣa-mukhīm api māṃ prasādayan /
children.translated_text: ['Even while appeasing me, whose anger has been stored in the heart and whose face shows no ire—

children.text: aparāddhasyāpi na khalu te bahujña roṣitum śakyam //]
children.translated_text: Even for one who has offended, O man of many stratagems, it is truly not possible to be angered by you.']

children.text: atra hi vācya-viśeṣeṇa sāparādhasyāpi bahujñasya kopaḥ kartum aśakya iti samarthakaṃ sāmānyam anvitam anyat tātparyeṇa prakāśate /
children.translated_text: Here, through the specific expressed meaning, a general principle—that even an offender possessed of many wiles cannot be made the object of anger—is manifested as a corroborating universal, conjoined with another [meaning] as its intent.

children.text: vyatireka-dhvanir apy ubhaya-rūpaḥ sambhavati / tatrādyasyodāharaṇaṃ prāk-pradarśitam eva / dvitīyasyodāharaṇaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Vyatireka-dhvani</s> (suggestion through contrast) too is possible in both forms. An example of the first has already been shown earlier. An example of the second:

children.text: jāejja vanuddese khujja bbia pāabo gaḍia-batto /
children.translated_text: 'Let him be born in a forest region, a crooked tree with fallen leaves—

children.text: mā mānusammi loe tāekka-raso dariddo a //
children.translated_text: But not in the human world, devoted solely to generosity yet destitute!'

children.text: [jāyeya vanoddeśe kubja eva pādapo galita-patraḥ /
children.translated_text: ['Let him be born in a forest region, a crooked tree with fallen leaves—

children.text: mā mānuṣe loke tyāgaika-raso daridraś ca //]
