children.translated_text: But not in the human world, devoted solely to generosity yet destitute!']

children.text: atra hi tyāgaika-rasasya daridrasya janmānabhinandanaṃ truṭita-patra-kubja-pādapa-janmābhinandanaṃ ca sākṣāc-chabda-vācyam / tathāvidhād api pādapāt tādṛśasya puṃsa upamānopameyatva-pratīti-pūrvakaṃ śocyatāyām ādhikyaṃ tātparyeṇa prakāśayati /
children.translated_text: Here, the not-welcoming of the birth of one devoted solely to generosity yet destitute, and the welcoming of the birth of a crooked, leaf-shorn tree, are directly expressed by the words. Through the prior cognition of the relation of standard-of-comparison and object-of-comparison between such a tree and such a man, the greater pitiableness [of the man] is manifested as the intent.

children.text: utprekṣā-dhvanir yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Utprekṣā-dhvani</s> (suggestion through poetic fancy), as in:

children.text: candanāsakta-bhujaga-niḥśvāsānila-mūrcchitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Infused with the breeze of the exhalations of serpents clinging to sandal trees—

children.text: mūrcchayaty eṣa pathikān madhau malaya-mārutaḥ //
children.translated_text: This <s>Malaya</s> breeze, in spring, causes travelers to swoon.

children.text:
atra hi madhau malaya-mārutasya pathika-mūrcchākāritvaṃ manmathonmātha-dāyitvenaiva /
tat tu candanāsakta-bhujaga-niḥśvāsānila-mūrcchitatvenotprekṣitam ity utprekṣā sākṣād anuktāpi vākyārtha-sāmarthyād anuraṇana-rūpā lakṣyate / na caivaṃ-vidhe viṣaye ivādi-śabda-prayogam antareṇāsaṃbaddhataiveti śakyate vaktum / gamakatvād anyatrāpi tad-aprayoge tad-arthāvagati-darśanāt / yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>Malaya</s> breeze's causing travelers to swoon in spring is precisely through its power to arouse desire (<s>manmatha</s>). But that [swooning] is poetically fancied (<s>utprekṣita</s>) as being caused by the breath of serpents clinging to sandal trees; thus the poetic fancy (<s>utprekṣā</s>), though not directly stated, is perceived through the force of the sentence-meaning in the form of reverberation. And in such a case [it is dhvani]—

children.text: īsā-kalusassa bi tuha muhassa ṇaṃ esa puṇṇimā-cando /
children.translated_text: 'Even with your face clouded by jealousy, indeed this full moon—

children.text: ajja sarisattaṇaṃ pābiūṇa aṅge bia ṇa māi //
children.translated_text: Having today attained equality [with your face], alas, does not shine!'

children.text: īrṣyā-kaluṣasyāpi tava mukhasya nanv eṣa pūrṇimā-candraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Even with your face clouded by jealousy, indeed this full moon—

children.text: adya sadṛśatvaṃ prāpyāṅga eva na māti //
children.translated_text: Having today attained equality [with your face], alas, does not shine!'

children.text: yathā vā-
trāsākulaḥ paripatan parito niketān
children.translated_text: Trembling with fear, running about in all directions seeking shelter—

children.text: puṃbhir na kaiścid api dhanvibhir anvabandhi /
children.translated_text: By no bowmen at all was he pursued;

children.text: tasthau tathāpi na mṛgaḥ kvacid aṅga-nābhir
children.translated_text: Yet the musk deer did not stand still anywhere, O friend—

children.text: ākarṇa-pūrṇa-nayaneṣu-hatekṣaṇa-śrīḥ //
children.translated_text: Its beauty of gaze destroyed, as if struck by arrows [drawn] from eyes filled to the ears [i.e., by the wide-eyed glances of women].
Or, as in:

children.text: śabdārtha-vyavahāre ca prasiddhir eva pramāṇam /
children.translated_text: And in the usage of words and meanings, common convention (<s>prasiddhi</s>) alone is the authority.

children.text: śleṣa-dhvanir yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa-dhvani</s> (suggestion through paronomasia), as in:

children.text: ramyā iti prāptavatīḥ patākāḥ rāgaṃ viviktā iti vardhayantīḥ /
children.translated_text: 'They are lovely'—thinking thus, they acquired banners; 'they are secluded'—thinking thus, they increased their passion;

children.text: yasyām asevanta namad-valīkāḥ samaṃ vadhūbhir valabhīr yuvānaḥ //
children.translated_text: In that [city], young men with bowing creepers [or: supple waists] frequented the balconies along with the young women.

children.text: atra vadhūbhiḥ saha valabhīrasevanteti vākyārtha-pratīter anantaraṃ vadhva iva valabhya iti śleṣa-pratītir aśabdāpy artha-sāmarthyān mukhyatvena vartate /
children.translated_text: Here, after the cognition of the sentence-meaning 'young men frequented the balconies along with the brides,' the paronomastic cognition that 'the balconies are like the brides' arises through meaning-power, even though not verbally expressed, and functions as primary.

children.text: yathā-saṅkhya-dhvanir yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Yathā-saṅkhya-dhvani</s> (suggestion through enumeration), as in:

children.text: aṅkuritaḥ pallavitaḥ korakitaḥ puṣpitaś ca sahakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>sahakāra</s> (mango) tree has sprouted, put forth shoots, budded, and blossomed;

children.text: aṅkuritaḥ pallavitaḥ korakitaḥ puṣpitaś ca hṛdi madanaḥ //
children.translated_text: And love (<s>Madana</s>) in the heart has sprouted, put forth shoots, budded, and blossomed.

children.text: atra hi yathoddeśam anūddeśe yac cārutvam anuraṇana-rūpaṃ madana-viśeṣaṇa-bhūtāṅkuritādi-śabda-gataṃ tan-madana-sahakārayos tulya-yogitā-samuccaya-lakṣaṇād vācyād atiricyamānam ālakṣyate / evam anye 'py alaṅkārā yathāyogaṃ yojanīyāḥ || DhvA_2.27 ||
children.translated_text: Here, the charm that resides in the reverberation-form—the words 'sprouted' and so forth applied as qualifiers of <s>Madana</s> (love), corresponding term-by-term to those applied to the <s>sahakāra</s> tree—is perceived as exceeding the expressed meaning, which is merely the co-occurrence (<s>tulya-yogitā-samuccaya</s>) of <s>Madana</s> and the <s>sahakāra</s>. In the same way, other figures too should be applied as appropriate.

children.text: evam alaṅkāra-dhvani-mārgaṃ vyutpādya tasya prayojanavattāṃ khyāpayitum idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Having thus expounded the path of <s>alaṅkāra-dhvani</s> (suggestion through figures of speech), to declare its purposefulness, this is said:
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.28:

children.text: śarīrīkaraṇaṃ yeṣāṃ vācyatve na vyavasthitam /
children.translated_text: Those [figures] whose embodiment (<s>śarīrīkaraṇa</s>) is not established in the [mere] expressed—

children.text: te 'laṅkārāḥ parāṃ chāyāṃ yānti dhvanyaṅgatāṃ gataḥ // DhvK_2.28 //
children.translated_text: Those figures of speech attain their highest splendor when they become subsidiary to <s>dhvani</s>. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.28 //

children.text: dhvany-aṅgatā cobhābhyāṃ prakārābhyāṃ vyañjakatvena vyaṅgyatvena ca / tatreha prakaraṇād vyaṅgyatvenety avagantavyam / vyaṅgyatve 'py alaṅkārāṇāṃ prādhānya-vivakṣāyām eva satyāṃ dhvanāv antaḥ-pātaḥ / itarathā tu guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyatvaṃ pratipādayiṣyate || DhvA_2.28 ||
children.translated_text: Being a subsidiary of <s>dhvani</s> (<s>dhvany-aṅgatā</s>) is of two kinds: as the suggestor (<s>vyañjaka</s>) and as the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). Here, from the context, it should be understood as 'being the suggested.' Even as suggested, figures of speech fall within <s>dhvani</s> only when there is an intention of their primacy. Otherwise, the status of being suggested-yet-subordinate (<s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>) will be demonstrated—

children.text: aṅgitvena vyaṅgyatāyām api / alaṅkārāṇāṃ dvayī gatiḥ-kadācid vastu-mātreṇa vyajyante, kadācid alaṅkāreṇa / tatra-
children.translated_text: Even when the suggested has the status of being the principal body (<s>aṅgin</s>). The figures of speech have a twofold course: sometimes they are suggested by mere content (<s>vastu-mātra</s>), sometimes by [another] figure (<s>alaṅkāra</s>). In that regard:
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.29:

children.text:
vyajyante vastumātreṇa yadālaṅkṛtayastayā /
dhruvaṃ dhvanyaṅgatā tāsāṃ . . . . . . . .
children.translated_text: When those embellishments are suggested by mere content, their status as subsidiary to <s>dhvani</s> is certain . . .

children.text: atra hetuḥ-
. . . . . . . . kāvya-vṛttis tad-āśrayā // DhvK_2.29 //
children.translated_text: . . . [for] the poetic function (<s>kāvya-vṛtti</s>) depends on that [suggested figure]. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.29 //
Here is the reason:

children.text: yasmāt tatra tathāvidha-vyaṅgyālaṅkāra-paratvenaiva kāvyaṃ pravṛttam / anyathā tu tad-vākya-mātram eva syāt || DhvA_2.29 ||
children.translated_text: Because in such cases, the poetry operates precisely through the primacy of such a suggested figure; otherwise, it would be a mere sentence.

children.text: tāsām evālaṅkṛtīnām-
children.translated_text: Of those same embellishments—
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.30:

children.text: alaṅkārāntara-vyaṅgya-bhāve . . . . . . . .
children.translated_text: When there is the state of being suggested by another figure . . .

children.text: punaḥ,
children.translated_text: Again,

children.text: . . . . . . . . dhvany-aṅgatā bhavet /
children.translated_text: . . . there would be the status of being subsidiary to <s>dhvani</s>,

children.text: cārutvotkarṣato vyaṅgya-prādhānyaṃ yadi lakṣyate // DhvK_2.30 //
children.translated_text: If the primacy of the suggested is perceived through the excellence of charm. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.30 //

children.text:
uktaṃ hy etat-"cārutvotkarṣa-nibandhanā vācya-vyaṅgyayoḥ prādhānya-vivakṣā" iti /
vastu mātra-vyaṅgyatve cālaṅkārāṇām anantaropadarśitebhya evodāharaṇebhyo viṣaya unneyaḥ / tad evam artha-mātreṇālaṅkāra-viśeṣa-rūpeṇa vārthenārthāntarasyālaṅkārasya vā prakāśane cārutvotkarṣa-nibandhane sati prādhānye 'rtha-śakty-udbhavānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgyo niravagantavyaḥ || DhvA_2.30 ||
children.translated_text: For it has been stated: 'The intention of primacy between the expressed and the suggested is grounded in the excellence of charm.' And in the case of figures suggested by mere content, the scope should be inferred from the very examples shown immediately before. Thus, whether by content alone—in the form of a particular meaning—or by a meaning [constituting] another figure, [the suggested alaṅkāra falls within dhvani].

children.text: evaṃ dhvaneḥ prabhedān pratipādya tad-ābhāsa-vivekaṃ kartum ucyate-
children.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the varieties of <s>dhvani</s>, to make the discrimination from its semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>), it is said:
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.31:

children.text: yatra pratīyamāno 'rthaḥ pramliṣṭatvena bhāsate /
children.translated_text: Where the suggested meaning appears in an indistinct manner (<s>pramliṣṭatva</s>),

children.text: vācyasyāṅgatayā vāpi nāsyāsau gocaro dhvaneḥ // DhvK_2.31 //
children.translated_text: Or as subsidiary to the expressed—that is not the domain of this <s>dhvani</s>. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.31 //

children.text: dvividho 'pi pratīyamānaḥ sphuṭo 'sphuṭaś ca / tatra ya eva sphuṭaḥ śabda-śaktyārtha-śaktyā vā prakāśate sa eva dhvaner mārgo netaraḥ / sphuṭo 'pi yo 'bhidheyasyāṅgatvena pratīyamāno 'vabhāsate so 'syānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgyasya dhvaner agocaraḥ / yathā-
children.translated_text: The suggested meaning, even though of two kinds—clear and unclear: only what is clearly manifested, whether through word-power (<s>śabda-śakti</s>) or meaning-power (<s>artha-śakti</s>), is the path of <s>dhvani</s>, not the other. Even what is clear, if it appears as subsidiary to the expressed, is not the domain of this reverberation-form (<s>anuraṇana-rūpa</s>) <s>dhvani</s>. For example:

children.text: kamalāarā ṇa maliā haṃsā uḍḍābiā ṇa a piucchā /
children.translated_text: 'The lotus-pond has not been muddied, the geese have not been made to fly away, nor [has anything happened to] the father's sister—

children.text: keṇa bi gāma-taḍāe abbhaṃ uttāṇaaṃ phaliham //
children.translated_text: [Yet] by someone, a cloud has been overturned [and thrown] into the village tank!'

children.text: [kamalākarā na malitā haṃsā uḍḍāyitā na ca pitṛ-śvasaḥ /
children.translated_text: ['The lotus-pond has not been muddied, the geese have not been made to fly away, nor the father's sister [disturbed]—

children.text: kenāpi grāma-taṭāke 'bhram uttānitaṃ kṣiptam //]
children.translated_text: [Yet] by someone, a cloud has been overturned [and thrown] into the village tank!']

children.text:
atra hi pratīyamānasya mugdha-vadhvā jaladhara-pratibimba-darśanasya vācyāṅgatvam eva /
evaṃ-vidhe viṣaye 'nyatrāpi yatra vyaṅgyāpekṣayā vācyasya cārutvotkarṣa-pratītyā prādhānyam avasīyate, tatra vyaṅgyasyāṅgatvena pratīter dhvaner aviṣayatvam / yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, the suggested element—namely the naive young bride's [wonder at] seeing the cloud's reflection—is merely subsidiary to the expressed meaning. In such cases, and elsewhere too where the primacy of the expressed is determined through the cognition of its superior charm relative to the suggested, the suggested is [merely] subsidiary; hence [such cases] are not the domain of <s>dhvani</s>. For example:

children.text: vāṇari-kuḍaṅgoḍḍīṇa-sa{u}ni-kolāhalaṃ suṇantīe /
children.translated_text: Hearing the clamor of birds flying up from the thicket of cane-creepers,

children.text: ghara-kamma-vāvaḍāe bahue sīanti aṅgāiṃ //[*17]
children.translated_text: The limbs of the bride, engaged in household work, languish.
Supplement 868 to the <s>Gāhā-sattasaī</s>.

children.text: Supplement 868 to Gāhā-sattasāi.
[vetasa-latā-gahanoḍḍīna-śakuni-kolāhalaṃ śṛṇvatyāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Hearing the clamor of birds flying up from the thicket of cane-creepers,

children.text: gṛha-karma-vyāpṛtāyā vadhvāḥ sīdanty aṅgāni //]
children.translated_text: The limbs of the bride, engaged in household work, languish.]

children.text: evaṃ-vidho hi viṣayaḥ prāyeṇa guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyasyodāharaṇatvena nirdekṣyate / yatra tu prakaraṇādi-pratipattyā nirdhārita-viśeṣo vācyo 'rthaḥ punaḥ pratīyamānāṅga-tvenaivāvabhāsate so 'syaivānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgyasya dhvaner mārgaḥ / yathā-
children.translated_text: Such a case will generally be cited as an example of <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> (suggested-yet-subordinate). But where the expressed meaning, its specific reference determined through context and the like, appears precisely as subsidiary to the suggested element, that is the path of this reverberation-form (<s>anuraṇana-rūpa</s>) <s>dhvani</s>. For example:

children.text: uccinasu paḍiaṃ kusumaṃ mā dhuṇa sehāliaṃ halia-suhṇe /
children.translated_text: 'Pick up the fallen flower; do not shake the <s>Śephālikā</s> tree, O farmer's daughter-in-law!

children.text: aha de visama-virāvo sasureṇa suo valaa-saddo //
children.translated_text: This is your terrible consequence—the sound of your bangles has been heard by your father-in-law.'

children.text: [uccinu patitaṃ kusumaṃ mā dhunīhi śephālikāṃ hālika-snuṣe /
children.translated_text: ['Pick up the fallen flower; do not shake the <s>Śephālikā</s> tree, O farmer's daughter-in-law!

children.text: eṣa te viṣama-vipākaḥ śvasureṇa śruto valaya-śabdaḥ //]
children.translated_text: This is your terrible consequence—the sound of your bangles has been heard by your father-in-law.']

children.text: atra hy avinaya-patinā saha ramamāṇā sakhī bahiḥ-śruta-valaya-kala-kalayā sakhyā pratibodhyate / etad apekṣaṇīyaṃ vācyārtha-pratipattaye / pratipanne ca vācye 'rthe tasyāvinaya-pracchādana-tātparyeṇābhidhīyamānatvāt punar vyaṅgyāṅgatvam evety asminn anuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgya-dhvanāvantar-bhāvaḥ || DhvA_2.31 ||
children.translated_text: Here, a woman secretly dallying with her mischievous husband is alerted by her friend through the externally heard tinkling of her bangles. This [surface meaning] must be grasped for the comprehension of the expressed meaning. But once the expressed meaning is comprehended, since it is uttered with the intent of concealing the impropriety, it again takes on the status of being subsidiary to the suggested—and thus in this [case it is genuine dhvani].

children.text: evaṃ vivakṣita-vācyasya dhvanes tad-ābhāsa-viveke prastute satya-vivakṣita-vācyasyāpi taṃ kartum āha-
children.translated_text: Having thus presented the discrimination of <s>dhvani</s> with intended expressed meaning (<s>vivakṣita-vācya</s>) from its semblance, in order to make the same [discrimination] for <s>dhvani</s> with unintended expressed meaning (<s>avivakṣita-vācya</s>) as well, he says:
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.32:

children.text: avyutpatter aśakter vā nibandho yaḥ skhalad-gateḥ /
children.translated_text: The employment of a word that stumbles in its course, due to either lack of etymological fitness or lack of power,

children.text: śabdasya sa ca na jñeyaḥ sūribhir viṣayo dhvaneḥ // DhvK_2.32 //
children.translated_text: Should not be regarded by the learned as the domain of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion). // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.32 //

children.text: skhalad-gater upacaritasya śabdasyāvyutpatter aśakter vā nibandho yaḥ sa ca na dhvaner viṣayaḥ / yataḥ-
children.translated_text: The employment of a word that stumbles in its course as a figurative usage, due to either lack of etymological fitness or lack of power — that is not the domain of <s>dhvani</s>. Because—
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.33:

children.text: sarveṣv eva prabhedeṣu sphuṭatvenāvabhāsanam /
children.translated_text: In all the varieties [of <s>dhvani</s>], the clear manifestation

children.text: yad vyaṅgyasyāṅgi-bhūtasya tat pūrṇaṃ dhvani-lakṣaṇam // DhvK_2.33 //
children.translated_text: Of the suggested meaning as the principal element — that is the complete definition of <s>dhvani</s>. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 2.33 //

children.text: tac codāhṛta-viṣayam eva || DhvA_2.33 ||
children.translated_text: And this has been [demonstrated] with respect to the very examples already cited. || <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Autocommentary 2.33 ||

children.text: iti śrī-rājānakānanda-vardhanācārya-viracite dhvany-āloke dvitīya uddyotaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the Second <s>Uddyota</s> (Illumination) in the <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> composed by the revered master <s>Rājānaka Ānandavardhana</s>.

children.text:
(3)
tṛtīyiddyotaḥ
children.translated_text: (3) Third <s>Uddyota</s> (Illumination)
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.1:

children.text: evaṃ vyaṅgya-mukhenaiva dhvaneḥ pradarśite sa-prabhede svarūpe punar vyañjaka-mukhenaitat prakāśyate-
children.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the nature of <s>dhvani</s> together with its varieties through the gateway of the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), the same is now elucidated through the gateway of the suggestor (<s>vyañjaka</s>)—

children.text: avivakṣita-vācyasya pada-vākya-prakāśatā /
children.translated_text: The manifestation through word and sentence of [<s>dhvani</s>] whose expressed meaning is unintended (<s>avivakṣita-vācya</s>),

children.text: tad-anyasyānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgyasya ca dhvaneḥ // DhvK_3.1 //
children.translated_text: And of [<s>dhvani</s>] whose suggested meaning takes the form of a reverberating echo (<s>anuraṇana</s>) of something other [than the expressed]. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.1 //

children.text: avivakṣita-vācyasyātyanta-tiraskṛta-vācye prabhede pada-prakāśatā yathā maharṣer vyāsasya-saptaitāḥ samidhaḥ śriyaḥ / yathā vā kālidāsasya-kaḥ sannaddhe viraha-vidhurāṃ tvayy upekṣeta jāyām / yathā vā-kim iva hi madhurāṇāṃ maṇḍanaṃ nākṛtīnām / eṣūdāharaṇeṣu "samidha" iti, "sannaddha" iti, "madhurāṇām" iti ca padāni vyañjakatvābhiprāyeṇaiva kṛtāni /
children.translated_text: Of [<s>dhvani</s>] whose expressed meaning is unintended, in the variety where the expressed meaning is completely set aside (<s>atyanta-tiraskṛta-vācya</s>), the word-level manifestation (<s>pada-prakāśatā</s>) [is illustrated] as in the great sage <s>Vyāsa</s>'s [verse]: 'These seven pieces of firewood are glories (<s>śrī</s>)'; or as in <s>Kālidāsa</s>'s: 'Who, when you are armed [for battle], would neglect a wife distressed by separation?'; or as in: 'What indeed does not serve as an ornament for beautiful forms?' In these examples, the words 'firewood,' 'armed,' and 'beautiful' have been employed precisely with the intention of being suggestive.

children.text: tasyaivārthāntara-saṅkramita-vācye yathā-rāmeṇa priya-jīvitena tu kṛtaṃ premṇaḥ priye nocitam / atra rāmeṇety etat-padaṃ samasāhasaika-rasatvādi-vyaṅgyābhisaṅkramita-vācyaṃ vyañjakam /
children.translated_text: Of that same [type], in the variety where the expressed meaning is transferred to another sense (<s>arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācya</s>), [the illustration is] as in: '<s>Rāma</s>, for whom life was dear, yet acted [thus]; but what was fitting for one's beloved, that was not done [by him] out of love.' Here the word '<s>Rāma</s>' is the suggestor whose expressed meaning has been transferred to suggest reckless rashness as the dominant mood and the like.

children.text: yathā vā-
children.translated_text: Or as in—

children.text: emea jaṇo tissā deu kabolopamāi sasi-bimbaṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'People give the moon-orb as a comparison for her cheek;'

children.text: paramattha-viāre uṇa cando cando bia varāo //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'But upon careful examination, the moon is [merely] a moon — the poor thing!'

children.text: [evam eva janas tasyā dadāti kapolopamāyāṃ śaśi-bimbam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'People give the moon-orb as a comparison for her cheek;'

children.text: paramārtha-vicāre punaś candraś candra iva varākaḥ //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'But upon careful examination, the moon is [merely] a moon — the poor thing!'

children.text: atra dvitīyaś candra-śabdo 'rthāntara-saṅkramita-vācyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the second occurrence of the word 'moon' has its expressed meaning transferred to another sense.

children.text: avivakṣita-vācyasyātyanta-tiraskṛta-vācye prabhede vākya-prakāśatā yathā-
children.translated_text: Of [<s>dhvani</s>] whose expressed meaning is unintended, in the variety where the expressed meaning is completely set aside, the sentence-level manifestation (<s>vākya-prakāśatā</s>) [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: yā niśā sarva-bhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī /
children.translated_text: 'What is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one is awake;

children.text: yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ //
children.translated_text: That in which beings are awake is the night for the seeing sage.'

children.text: anena hi vākyena niśārtho na ca jāgaraṇārthaḥ kaścid vivakṣitaḥ / kiṃ tarhi ? tattva-jñānāvahitatvam atattva-parāṅmukhatvaṃ ca muneḥ pratipādyata iti tiraskṛta-vācyasyāsya vyañjakatvam /
children.translated_text: For by this sentence, neither the meaning of 'night' nor the meaning of 'wakefulness' is intended literally. What then? The sage's absorption in the knowledge of reality and his turning away from non-reality are conveyed — thus this [sentence] whose expressed meaning is set aside functions as a suggestor.

children.text: tasyaivārthāntara-saṅkramita-vācyasya vākya-prakāśatā yathā-
children.translated_text: Of that same [type], where the expressed meaning is transferred to another sense, the sentence-level manifestation [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: visama{i}o ccia kāṇa bi kāṇa bi bolei amiaṇimmāo /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Time moves unevenly — for some it rains nectar-like sweetness;'

children.text: kāṇa bi bisāmiamao kāṇa bi abisāmao kālo //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'For some it is a mixture of poison and nectar; for some it is neither poison nor nectar.'

children.text: [viṣam ayitaḥ keṣām api keṣām api prayāty amṛta-nirmāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'Time moves unevenly — for some it issues nectar-like sweetness;'

children.text: keṣām api viṣāmṛta-mayaḥ keṣām apy aviṣāmṛtaḥ kālaḥ //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'For some it is a mixture of poison and nectar; for some it is neither poison nor nectar.'

children.text: atra hi vākye viṣāmṛta-śabdābhyāṃ duḥkha-sukha-rūpa-saṅkramita-vācyābhyāṃ vyavahāra ity arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācyasya vyañjakatvam /
children.translated_text: Here indeed, in this sentence, the words 'poison' and 'nectar,' whose expressed meanings have been transferred to the senses of 'suffering' and 'happiness,' function as suggestors in the context of worldly experience — thus this is the suggestive function of [a sentence] whose expressed meaning has been transferred to another sense.

children.text: vivakṣitābhidheyasyānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgyasya śabda-śakty-udbhave prabhede pada-prakāśatā yathā-
children.translated_text: Of [<s>dhvani</s>] whose expressed meaning is intended (<s>vivakṣitābhidheya</s>), [where] the suggested takes the form of reverberating echo (<s>anuraṇana</s>), in the variety where [the suggestion] arises from the power of the word (<s>śabda-śakty-udbhava</s>), the word-level manifestation [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: prātuṃ dhanair arthi-janasya vāñchāṃ
children.translated_text: 'If I was not created by fate to fulfill

children.text: daivena sṛṣṭo yadi nāma nāsmi /
children.translated_text: The desires of the needy with wealth,

children.text: pathi prasannāmbudharas taḍāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Then why was I not made a lake with clear water on the path,

children.text: kūpo 'thavā kiṃ na jaḍaḥ kṛto 'ham //
children.translated_text: Or a well — why was I not made inert [instead]?'

children.text: atra hi jaḍa iti padaṃ nirviṇṇena vakrātma-samānādhikaraṇatayā prayuktam anuraṇana-rūpatayā kūpa-samānādhikaraṇatāṃ sva-śaktyā pratipadyate / tasyaiva vākya-prakāśatā yathā harṣa-carite siṃha-nāda-vākyeṣu-"vṛtte 'smin mahā-pralaye dharaṇī-dhāraṇāyādhunā tvaṃ śeṣaḥ" / etad dhi vākyam anuraṇana-rūpam arthāntaraṃ śabda-śaktyā sphuṭam eva prakāśayati /
children.translated_text: Here, the word 'inert' (<s>jaḍa</s>), employed by one who is despondent in co-referentiality with himself (<s>vakrātman</s>), through its reverberating-echo nature, attains co-referentiality with 'well' through its own [inherent] power. Of this same [type], the sentence-level manifestation [is illustrated] as in the <s>Harṣacarita</s>, in the lion's-roar passages: 'After this great dissolution has occurred, you are now <s>Śeṣa</s> (the Remainder/the cosmic serpent) for the task of bearing the earth.' For this sentence, through the reverberating-echo form, clearly manifests another meaning through the power of the word.

children.text: asyaiva kavi-prauḍhokti-mātra-niṣpanna-śarīrasyārtha-śakty-udbhave prabhede pada-prakāśatayā, yathā hari-vijaye-
children.translated_text: Of this same [type], whose body is produced solely by the poet's bold expression (<s>kavi-prauḍhokti</s>), in the variety where [the suggestion] arises from the power of the meaning (<s>artha-śakty-udbhava</s>), at the word-level, as in the <s>Harivijaya</s>—

children.text: cūaṃkurābaaṃsaṃ chaṇa-pasara-
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Adorned with mango-shoot ear-ornaments, with the momentary wafting

children.text: mahagghaṇa-maṇa-hara-surāmoaṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] of costly, captivating fragrance of wine,'

children.text: asamappiaṃ pi gahiaṃ kusuma-
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Though not offered, [the face of spring] was seized

children.text: sareṇa mahu-māsa-lacchi-muhaṃ //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] by the flower-arrowed one — the face of the beauty of the spring month.'

children.text: [cūtāṅkurāvataṃsaṃ kṣaṇa-prasara-
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'Adorned with mango-shoot ear-ornaments, with the momentary wafting

children.text: mahārgha-manohara-surāmodam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] of costly, captivating fragrance of wine,'

children.text: asamarpitam api gṛhītaṃ kusuma-
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'Though not offered, [the face] was seized

children.text: śareṇa madhu-māsa-lakṣmī-mukham //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] by the flower-arrowed one — the face of the beauty of the spring month.'

children.text: atra hy asamarpitam api kusuma-śareṇa madhu-māsa-lakṣmyā mukhaṃ gṛhītam ity asamarpitam apīty etad avasthābhidhāyi-padam artha-śaktyā kusumaśarasya balāt-kāraṃ prakāśayati /
children.translated_text: Here, the face of the beauty of the spring month, though not offered, was seized by the flower-arrowed one (<s>Kusuma-śara</s>, i.e., <s>Kāmadeva</s>). The word 'though not offered' (<s>asamarpitam api</s>), being a word that denotes a state, through the power of the meaning reveals <s>Kāmadeva</s>'s forcible seizure.

children.text:
atraiva prabhede vākya-prakāśatā yathodāhṛtaṃ prāk "sajjayati surabhimāso" ity ādi /
atra sajjayati surabhi-māso na tāvad arpayaty anaṅgāya śarān ity ayaṃ vākyārthaḥ kavi-prauḍhokti-mātra-niṣpanna-śarīro manmathonmātha-kadanāvasthāṃ vasanta-samayasya sūcayati /
children.translated_text: In this same variety, the sentence-level manifestation [is illustrated] as previously cited: 'The fragrant spring month ensnares...' and so forth. Here, 'The fragrant spring month does not indeed hand arrows to <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One)' — this sentence-meaning, whose body is produced solely by the poet's bold expression, indicates the state of being tormented and afflicted by the agitation of <s>Kāmadeva</s> during the spring season.

children.text: svataḥ-sambhavi-śarīrārtha-śakty-udbhave prabhede pada-prakāśatā yathā-
children.translated_text: In the variety where [the suggestion] arises from the power of the meaning whose body is naturally possible (<s>svataḥ-sambhavi</s>), the word-level manifestation [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: vāṇiaa hatthi-dantā kutto amhāṇaṃ bāgha-kittī a /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'O merchant, from where would we get ivory

children.text: jāva luliālaa-muhī gharammi parisakkae suṇhā //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] and tiger-skins, as long as the daughter-in-law, with disheveled locks about her face, embraces [her husband] in the house?'

children.text: [vāṇijaka hasti-dantāḥ kuto 'smākaṃ vyāghra-kṛttayaś ca /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'O merchant, from where would we get ivory

children.text: yāval lulitālaka-mukhī gṛhe pariṣvakkate snuṣā //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] and tiger-skins, as long as the daughter-in-law, with disheveled locks about her face, embraces [her husband] in the house?'

children.text: atra lulitālaka-mukhīty etat-padaṃ vyādha-vadhvāḥ svataḥ-sambhāvita-śarīrārtha-śaktyā surata-krīḍāsaktiṃ sūcayaṃs tadīyasya bhartuḥ satata-sambhoga-kṣāmatāṃ prakāśayati /
children.translated_text: Here, the word 'with disheveled locks about her face' (<s>lulitālaka-mukhī</s>), through the power of the naturally possible meaning regarding the hunter's wife, while indicating [her] addiction to amorous sport, reveals her husband's capacity for constant love-making.

children.text: tasyaiva vākya-prakāśatā, yathā-
children.translated_text: Of this same [type], the sentence-level manifestation, as in—

children.text: sihi-piccha-kaṇṇa-ūrā bahuā bāhassa gabbirī bhama{i} /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'The wife of the hunter, with peacock-feather ear-ornaments, roams proudly'

children.text: muttā-phala-ra{i}a-pasāhaṇāṇaṃ majjhe sabattīṇaṃ //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Among her co-wives who are adorned with pearl ornaments.'

children.text: [śikhi-piccha-karṇa-pūrā jāyā vyādhasya garviṇī bhramati /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'The wife of the hunter, with peacock-feather ear-ornaments, roams proudly'

children.text: muktā-phala-racita-prasādhanānāṃ madhye sapatnīnām //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'Among her co-wives who are adorned with pearl ornaments.'

children.text: anenāpi vākyena vyādha-vadhvāḥ śikhi-picchi-karṇa-pūrāyā nava-pariṇītāyāḥ kasyāścit saubhāgyātiśayaḥ prakāśyate / tat-sambhogaika-rato mayūra-mātra-māraṇa-samarthaḥ patir jāta ity artha-prakāśanāt tad anyāsāṃ cira-pariṇītānāṃ muktā-phala-racita-prasādhanānāṃ daurbhāgyātiśayaḥ khyāpyate / tat sa-sambhoga-kāle sa eva vyādhaḥ kari-vara-vadhavyāpāra-samartha āsīd ity artha-prakāśanāt /
children.translated_text: By this sentence too, the surpassing good fortune of the hunter's wife — newly married, wearing peacock-feather ear-ornaments — is revealed. Since her husband, devoted solely to her love-making, has become capable of killing only peacocks, [this is manifested] through the revelation of that meaning. And thereby the surpassing misfortune of the other wives, long married, adorned with pearl ornaments, is proclaimed — through the revelation that during their time of love-making, that same hunter was capable of slaying the finest elephants.

children.text: nanu kāvya-viśeṣo dhvanir ity uktaṃ tat kathaṃ tasya pada-prakāśatā ? kāvya-viśeṣo hi viśiṣtārtha-pratipatti-hetuḥ śabda-sandarbha-viśeṣaḥ / tad-bhāvaś ca pada-prakāśatve nopapadyate, padānāṃ smārakatvenāvācakatvāt / ucyate-"syād eṣa doṣaḥ yadi vācakatvaṃ prayojakaṃ dhvani-vyavahāre syāt /" na tv evam ; tasya vyañjakatvena vyavasthānāt / kiṃ ca kāvyānāṃ śarīrāṇām iva saṃsthāna-viśeṣāvacchinna-samudāya-sādhyāpi cārutva-pratītir anvaya-vyatirekābhyāṃ bhāgeṣu kalpyata iti padānām api vyañjakatva-mukhena vyavasthito dhvani-vyavahāro na virodhī /
children.translated_text: Now, [the objection:] 'It was said that <s>dhvani</s> is a special kind of poetry; then how can it have word-level manifestation? For a special kind of poetry is a particular arrangement of words (<s>śabda-sandarbha-viśeṣa</s>) that causes the apprehension of a distinguished meaning. And word-level manifestation would not accord with that, since individual words are reminders (<s>smāraka</s>) and not denotators.' The reply is: 'This would be a defect if denotation (<s>vācakatva</s>) were the operative factor in the functioning of <s>dhvani</s>.' But that is not the case, since <s>dhvani</s> is established through suggestive power (<s>vyañjakatva</s>). Moreover, just as with physical bodies, the apprehension of beauty, though accomplished through the particular configuration of the whole, is attributed through positive and negative concomitance to the parts — so too the functioning of <s>dhvani</s>, established through the suggestive power of individual words, is not contradictory.

children.text: aniṣṭasya śrutir yadvad āpādayati duṣṭatām /
children.translated_text: Just as hearing something unpleasant brings about a fault [in poetry],

children.text: śruti-duṣṭādiṣu vyaktaṃ tadvad iṣṭa-smṛtir guṇam //
children.translated_text: So clearly, in cases of phonetic harshness and the like, the remembrance of something pleasing [through a word] brings about a quality.

children.text: padānāṃ smārakatve 'pi pada-mātrāvabhāsinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though words [merely] remind, in all the varieties

children.text: tena dhvaneḥ prabhedeṣu sarveṣv evāsti ramyatā //
children.translated_text: Of <s>dhvani</s> that manifest through words alone, there is charm.

children.text: vicchitti-śobhinaikena bhūṣaṇeneva kāminī /
children.translated_text: Just as a beautiful woman shines with a single ornament that radiates grace (<s>vicchitti</s>),

children.text: pada-dyotyena sukaver dhvaninā bhāti bhāratī //
children.translated_text: So the speech of a good poet shines with <s>dhvani</s> manifested through a word.

children.text: iti parikara-ślokāḥ || DhvA_3.1 ||
children.translated_text: Thus [end] the supporting verses. || <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Autocommentary 3.1 ||
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.2:

children.text: yas tv alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyo dhvanir varṇa-padādiṣu /
children.translated_text: That <s>dhvani</s>, moreover, whose suggestion proceeds by imperceptible sequence (<s>alakṣya-krama</s>), [manifested] in phonemes, words, and the like,

children.text: vākye saṅghaṭanāyāṃ ca sa prabandhe 'pi dīpyate // DhvK_3.2 //
children.translated_text: And in sentences and in composition (<s>saṅghaṭanā</s>) — it shines forth in extended works (<s>prabandha</s>) as well. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.2 //

children.text: tatra varṇānām anarthakatvād dyotakatvam asambhavīty āśaṅkyedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Now, since phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) are devoid of meaning, their suggestive function would be impossible — to counter such a doubt, this is stated:
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.3-4:

children.text: śaṣau sa-repha-saṃyogo ḍhakāraś cāpi bhūyasā /
children.translated_text: The sibilants <s>śa</s> and <s>ṣa</s>, conjuncts with <s>r</s>, and the letter <s>ḍha</s>, when occurring frequently,

children.text: virodhinaḥ syuḥ śṛṅgāre te na varṇā rasa-cyutaḥ // DhvK_3.3 //
children.translated_text: Are antagonistic to the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) <s>rasa</s> — those phonemes do not cause the loss of <s>rasa</s> [in themselves]. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.3 //

children.text: ta eva tu niveśyante bībhatsādau rase yadā /
children.translated_text: But when those very [phonemes] are placed in the <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting) and other <s>rasas</s>,

children.text: tadā taṃ dīpayanty eva te na varṇā rasa-cyutaḥ // DhvK_3.4 //
children.translated_text: Then they illuminate that [<s>rasa</s>] — those phonemes do not cause the loss of <s>rasa</s> [in themselves]. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.4 //

children.text: śloka-dvayenānvaya-vyatirekābhyāṃ varṇānāṃ dyotakatvaṃ darśitaṃ bhavati / pade cālakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyasya dyotanaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: By these two verses, the suggestive power of phonemes has been shown through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>). The manifestation of [<s>dhvani</s>] with imperceptible-sequence suggestion at the word-level [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: utkampinī bhaya-pariskhalitāṃśukāntā
children.translated_text: 'Trembling, with the edge of her garment slipping due to fear,

children.text: te locane pratidiśaṃ vidhure kṣipantī /
children.translated_text: Casting her distressed eyes in every direction,

children.text: krūreṇa dāruṇatayā sahasaiva dagdhā
children.translated_text: You were not seen [by us] — [you who were] suddenly burned

children.text: dhūmāndhitena dahanena na vīkṣitāsi //
children.translated_text: By the cruel and merciless fire, blinding with smoke!'

children.text: atra hi te ity etat padaṃ rasamayatvena sphuṭam evāvabhāsate sahṛdayānām / yathā vā-
children.translated_text: Here indeed, the word 'your' (<s>te</s>) manifests itself as saturated with <s>rasa</s> clearly to sensitive readers (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). Or as in—

children.text: jhagiti kanaka-citre tatra dṛṣṭe kuraṅge
children.translated_text: 'Suddenly, when that golden-painted deer was seen there,

children.text: rabhasa-vilasitās te dṛṣṭi-pātāḥ priyāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those impetuous, playful glances of your beloved —

children.text: pavana-vilulitānām utpalānāṃ palāśa-
children.translated_text: Scattering, as it were, a shower of petals

children.text: prakaram iva kirantaḥ smaryamāṇā dahanti //[*18]
children.translated_text: Of lotuses tossed by the wind — when remembered, they burn.'
Note: Not found in all editions.

children.text: Not found in all editions.
padāvayavena dyotanaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: The manifestation through a sub-component of a word (<s>padāvayava</s>) [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: vrīḍā-yogān nata-vadanayā sannidhāne gurūṇāṃ
children.translated_text: 'With downcast face due to modesty, in the presence of the elders,

children.text: baddhotkampaṃ kuca-kalaśayor manyum antar nigṛhya /
children.translated_text: Suppressing her anger with trembling agitation of her pitcher-like breasts,

children.text: tiṣṭhety uktaṃ kim iva na tayā yat samutsṛjya bāṣpaṃ
children.translated_text: Why did she, when told "Stay!" — not — having let fall her tears —

children.text: mayy āsaktaś cakita-hariṇī-hāri-netra-tribhāgaḥ //
children.translated_text: [Cast upon me] a third-portion of her glance, charming as a startled doe's eyes?'

children.text: ity atra tribhāga-śabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, [the suggestive sub-component] is the word 'third-portion' (<s>tribhāga</s>).

children.text:
vākya-rūpaś cālakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyo dhvaniḥ śuddho 'laṅkāra-saṅkīrṇaś ceti dvidhā mataḥ /
tatra śuddhasyodāharaṇaṃ yathā rāmābhyudaye-"kṛtaka-kupitaiḥ" ity ādi ślokaḥ /
etad dhi vākyaṃ parasparānurāgaṃ paripoṣa-prāptaṃ pradarśayat sarvata eva paraṃ rasa-tattvaṃ prakāśayati /
children.translated_text: Sentence-level <s>dhvani</s> with imperceptible-sequence suggestion is regarded as twofold: pure (<s>śuddha</s>) and mixed with figures (<s>alaṅkāra-saṅkīrṇa</s>). Of these, the illustration of the pure [type] is as in the <s>Rāmābhyudaya</s>: the verse beginning 'With feigned anger...' and so forth. For this sentence, while depicting mutual love that has reached its fullness, manifests from every angle the supreme essence of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: alaṅkārāntara-saṅkīrṇo, yathā-"smara-nava-nadī-pūreṇoḍhāḥ" ity ādi-ślokaḥ / atra hi rūpakeṇa yathokta-vyañjaka-lakṣaṇānugatena prasādhito rasaḥ sutarām abhivyajyate || DhvA_3.3-4 ||
children.translated_text: [The type] mixed with another figure [is illustrated] as in the verse beginning 'Swept away by the fresh flood of the river of <s>Smara</s> (Love)...' and so forth. Here, the <s>rasa</s>, adorned by a metaphor (<s>rūpaka</s>) that conforms to the aforementioned characteristics of suggestors, is manifested all the more vividly. || <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Autocommentary 3.3-4 ||

children.text: alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyaḥ saṅghaṭanāyāṃ bhāsate dhvanir ity uktaṃ tatra saṅghaṭanā-svarūpam eva tāvan nirūpyate-
children.translated_text: It was stated that <s>dhvani</s> with imperceptible-sequence suggestion shines forth in composition (<s>saṅghaṭanā</s>). Now, the very nature of composition is first examined—
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.5:

children.text: asamāsā samāsena madhyamena ca bhūṣitā /
children.translated_text: Without compounds, adorned with moderate compounds,

children.text: tathā dīrgha-samāseti tridhā saṅghaṭanoditā // DhvK_3.5 //
children.translated_text: And with long compounds — thus composition is declared to be threefold. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.5 //

children.text: kaiścit /
children.translated_text: By some [authorities].

children.text: tāṃ kevalam anūdyedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Having merely restated that, the following is said—

children.text: Dhv_3.6a:
children.translated_text: <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.6a:

children.text: guṇān āśritya tiṣṭhantī mādhuryādīn vyanakti sā /
children.translated_text: Depending on the qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) such as sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>) and the like, the composition reveals [them];
The <s>rasas</s> . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.6a //

children.text:
sā saṅghaṭanā rasādīn vyanakti guṇānāśritya tiṣṭhantīti / atra ca vikalpyam guṇānāṃ saṅghaṭanāyāścaikyaṃ vyatireko vā / vyatireke 'pi dvayī gatiḥ / guṇāśrayā saṅghaṭanā, saṅghaṭanāśrayā vā guṇā iti / tatraikya-pakṣe saṅghaṭanāśraya-guṇa-pakṣe ca guṇānātma-bhūtānādheya-bhūtān vāśritya tiṣṭhantī saṅghaṭanā rasādīn vyanaktīty ayam arthaḥ / yadā tu nānātva-pakṣe guṇāśraya-saṅghaṭanā-pakṣaḥ tadā guṇān āśritya tiṣṭhantī guṇa-paratantra-svabhāvā na tu guṇa-rūpaivety arthaḥ / kiṃ punar evaṃ vikalpanasya prayojanam iti ?
abhidhīyate-yadi guṇāḥ saṅghaṭanā cetyekaṃ tattvaṃ saṅghaṭanāśrayā vā guṇāḥ, tadā saṅghaṭanāyā iva guṇānām aniyata-viṣayatva-prasaṅgaḥ / guṇānāṃ hi mādhurya-prasāda-prakarṣaḥ karuṇa-vipralambha-śṛṅgāra-viṣaya eva / raudrādbhutādi-viṣayam ojaḥ /
mādhuryaprasādau rasa-bhāvatad-ābhāsa-viṣayāveveti viṣayaniyamo vyavasthitaḥ, saṅghaṭanāyās tu sa vighaṭate / tathā hi śṛṅgāre 'pi dīrgha-samāsā dṛśyate raudrādiṣv asamāsā ceti /
children.translated_text: That <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> (composition) manifests <s>rasa</s> etc. while resting upon <s>guṇas</s>. Here one must consider: is there identity or difference between <s>guṇas</s> and <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>? If different, there are two possibilities: either <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> rests upon <s>guṇas</s>, or <s>guṇas</s> rest upon <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>. In the identity view and in the view that <s>guṇas</s> rest upon <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>, the meaning is: <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>, resting upon <s>guṇas</s> that are its own essence or its foundation, manifests <s>rasa</s> etc. But when, in the difference view, it is the view that <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> rests upon <s>guṇas</s>, the meaning is: [<s>saṅghaṭanā</s>] resting upon <s>guṇas</s> is dependent on <s>guṇas</s> in its nature, but is not itself of the form of <s>guṇas</s>. Now, what is the purpose of this analysis? It is stated: If <s>guṇas</s> and <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> are one reality, or if <s>guṇas</s> rest upon <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>, then the problem arises that <s>guṇas</s>, like <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>, would have unrestricted domains. For the preeminence of <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) and <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity) among the <s>guṇas</s> pertains only to the domain of <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic) and <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic love-in-separation). <s>Ojas</s> (vigor) pertains to the domain of <s>raudra</s> (the furious), <s>adbhuta</s> (the marvelous), and so forth. <s>Mādhurya</s> and <s>prasāda</s> pertain only to the domain of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and their semblances — thus the restriction of domain is established. But for <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>, that [restriction] breaks down. For long compounds are seen even in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, and non-compound [style] even in <s>raudra</s> etc.

children.text: tatra śṛṅgāre dīrgha-samāsā yathā-"mandāra-kusuma-reṇu-piñjaritālakā" iti / yathā vā-
children.translated_text: An example of long compounds in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>: 'with locks tinted yellow by the pollen of <s>mandāra</s> flowers.' Or as [in the following]:

children.text:
anavarata-nayana-jala-lava-
nipatana-parimuṣita-patra-lekhaṃ te /
kara-tala-niṣaṇṇam abale
vadanam idaṃ kaṃ na tāpayati //ity ādau /
children.translated_text: Your face, O delicate one, resting on the palm of your hand, its leaf-ornament effaced by the continuous falling of tear-drops from your eyes — whom does it not torment? And so forth.

children.text: tathā raudrādiṣv apy asamāsā dṛśyate / yathā-"yo yaḥ śastraṃ bibharti sva-bhuja-guru-madaḥ" ity ādau / tasmān na saṅghaṭanā-svarūpāḥ, na ca saṅghaṭanāśrayā guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, non-compound composition is also seen in <s>raudra</s> etc. As in: 'Whoever bears a weapon, intoxicated by the strength of his own arms,' and so forth. Therefore, <s>guṇas</s> are not of the nature of <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>, nor do they rest upon <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>.

children.text: nanu yadi saṅghaṭanā guṇānāṃ nāśrayas tat kim-ālambanā ete parikalpyantām ? ucyate-pratipāditam evaiṣām ālambanam /
children.translated_text: Objection: If <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> is not the foundation of <s>guṇas</s>, then what foundation should be conceived for them? Reply: Their foundation has already been established:

children.text:
tam artham avalambante ye 'ṅginaṃ te guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ /
aṅgāśritās tv alaṅkārā mantavyāḥ kaṭakādivat //iti /
children.translated_text: 'Those [qualities of style] that support that predominant meaning are called <s>guṇas</s>; but those dependent on the subordinate elements should be regarded as <s>alaṅkāras</s>, like bracelets and the like.'

children.text: athavā bhavantu śabdāśrayā eva guṇāḥ, na caiṣām anuprāsādi-tulyatvam / yasmād anuprāsādayo 'napekṣitārtha-śabda-dharmā eva pratipāditāḥ / guṇās tu vyaṅgya-viśeṣāvabhāsi-vācya-pratipādana-samartha-śabda-dharmā eva / śabda-dharmatvaṃ caiṣām anyāśrayatve 'pi śarīrāśrayatvam iva śauryādīnām /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, let <s>guṇas</s> indeed be properties of words alone — even so, they are not equivalent to <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) and the like. For <s>anuprāsa</s> and similar figures have been shown to be properties of words irrespective of meaning. But <s>guṇas</s> are properties of words that are capable of expressing a meaning through which the particular suggested sense (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) becomes manifest. And their being properties of words, even though they rest upon something else, is like the [dependence of] valor etc. upon the body.

children.text:
nanu yadi śabdāśrayā guṇās tat-saṅghaṭanā-rūpatvaṃ tad-āśrayatvaṃ vā teṣāṃ prāptam eva /
na hy asaṅghaṭitāḥ śabdā artha-viśeṣa-pratipādya-rasādy-āśritānāṃ guṇānām avācakatvād āśrayā bhavanti / naivam / varṇa-pada-vyaṅgyatvasya rasādīnāṃ pratipāditatvāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: If <s>guṇas</s> are properties of words, then it is already established that they are either of the form of <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> or based upon it. For words that are not composed [into sentences] cannot be the foundation of <s>guṇas</s> that pertain to <s>rasa</s> etc. expressed through particular meanings, since [isolated words] do not express [<s>rasa</s>]. Reply: Not so, for it has been established that <s>rasa</s> etc. can be suggested by individual phonemes and words.

children.text: abhyupagate vā vākya-vyaṅgyatve rasādīnāṃ na niyatā kācit saṅghaṭanā teṣām āśrayatvaṃ pratipadyata ity aniyata-saṅghaṭanāḥ śabdā eva guṇānāṃ vyaṅgya-viśeṣānugatā āśrayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, even if the suggestion of <s>rasa</s> etc. by sentences is accepted, no fixed <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> attains the status of their foundation. Therefore, words of unfixed composition, accompanied by the particular suggested meaning, are themselves the foundation of <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text:
nanu, mādhurye yadi nāmaivam ucyate tad ucyatām ; ojasaḥ punaḥ katham aniyata-saṅghaṭana-śabdāśrayatvam ? na hy asamāsā saṅghaṭanā kadācid ojasa āśrayatāṃ pratipadyate / ucyate-yadi na prasiddhi-mātra-graha-dūṣitaṃ cetas tad atrāpi na na brūmaḥ /
ojasaḥ katham asamāsā saṅghaṭanā nāśrayaḥ ? yato raudrādīn hi prakāśayataḥ kāvyasya dīptir oja iti prāk pratipāditam / tac caujo yady asamāsāyām api saṅghaṭanāyāṃ syāt tat ko doṣo bhavet ? na cācārutvaṃ sahṛdaya-hṛdaya-saṃvedyam asti / tasmād aniyata-saṅghaṭana-śabdāśrayatve guṇānāṃ na kācit kṣatiḥ / teṣāṃ tu cakṣur-ādīnām iva yathāsvaṃ viṣaya-niyamitasya svarūpasya na kadācid vyabhicāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: If this is said of <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), so be it; but how can <s>ojas</s> (vigor) have words of unfixed composition as its foundation? For non-compound composition never attains the status of foundation for <s>ojas</s>. Reply: If the mind is not corrupted by mere attachment to convention, then we say this here too. How can non-compound composition not be the foundation of <s>ojas</s>? For it was previously established that the brilliance of poetry that manifests <s>raudra</s> etc. is <s>ojas</s>. And if that <s>ojas</s> should exist even in non-compound composition, what fault would there be? Nor is there any unattractiveness perceptible to the hearts of the sensitive (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). Therefore, no harm comes from <s>guṇas</s> having words of unfixed composition as their foundation. Their nature, which is restricted to its own domain like the eyes etc. [to their respective objects], never deviates.

children.text: yat tūktam-"saṅghaṭanāvad guṇānām apy aniyata-viṣayatvaṃ prāpnoti / lakṣye vyabhicāradarśanāt" iti / tatrāpy etad ucyate-yatra lakṣye parikalpita-viṣaya-vyabhicāras tad virūpam evāstu / katham acārutvaṃ tādṛśe viṣaye sahṛdayānāṃ nāvabhātīti cet ? kavi-śakti-tirohitatvāt /
children.translated_text: As for what was said — '<s>Guṇas</s>, like <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>, would have unrestricted domains, since deviation is observed in examples' — to that too this is said: Where in an example there is deviation from the assigned domain, let that simply be defective. Objection: How can unattractiveness not be perceived by the sensitive in such a case? Reply: Because it is concealed by the poet's power (<s>kavi-śakti</s>).

children.text: dvividho hi doṣaḥ-kaver avyutpatti-kṛto 'śakti-kṛtaś ca / tatrāvyutpatti-kṛto doṣaḥ śakti-tiraskṛtatvāt kadācin na lakṣyate / yas tv aśakti-kṛto doṣaḥ sa jhaṭiti pratīyate / parikara-ślokaś cātra-
avyutpatti-kṛto doṣaḥ śaktyā saṃvriyate kaveḥ /
children.translated_text: A fault arising from the poet's lack of learning is concealed by [his] power;

children.text: yas tv aśakti-kṛtas tasya sa jhaṭity avabhāsate //
children.translated_text: But a fault arising from lack of power — that immediately becomes apparent.

For faults are of two kinds: those arising from the poet's lack of learning (<s>avyutpatti</s>), and those arising from lack of power (<s>aśakti</s>). Of these, a fault arising from lack of learning is sometimes not perceived, because it is concealed by [the poet's] power. But a fault arising from lack of power is immediately perceived. And the encapsulating verse here is:

children.text: tathā hi-mahā-kavīnām apy uttama-devatā-viṣaya-prasiddha-saṃbhoga-śṛṅgāra-nibandhanādy-anaucityaṃ śakti-tiraskṛtatvāt grāmyatvena na pratibhāsate / yathā kumāra-sambhave devī-sambhoga-varṇanam / evam ādau ca viṣaye yathaucitya-tyāgas tathā darśitam evāgre / śakti-kṛtatvaṃ cānvaya-vyatirekābhyām avasīyate / yathā hi śakti-rahitena kavinā evaṃ-vidhe viṣaye śṛṅgāra upanibadhyamānaḥ sphuṭam eva doṣatvena pratibhāsate /
children.translated_text: For example, even in the works of great poets, impropriety such as the well-known composition of <s>sambhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic union) with the supreme deity as subject — this does not appear as vulgar, because it is concealed by [their] power. As in the description of <s>Devī</s>'s union in the <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> [of <s>Kālidāsa</s>]. That in such and other subjects the abandonment of <s>aucitya</s> (propriety) [exists] has already been shown. And the presence of [poetic] power is ascertained by the methods of agreement and difference (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>). For when a poet lacking power composes <s>śṛṅgāra</s> in such a subject, it clearly appears as a fault.

children.text: nanv asmin pakṣe "yo yaḥ śastraṃ bibharti" ity ādau kim acārutvam ? apratīyamānam evāropayāmaḥ / tasmād guṇa-vyatiriktatve guṇa-rūpatve ca saṅghaṭanāyā anyaḥ kaścin niyama-hetur vaktavya ity ucyate /
children.translated_text: Objection: In this view, what is unattractive about 'Whoever bears a weapon' and so forth? [Reply:] We would be imposing [unattractiveness] where none is perceived. Therefore, whether <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> is different from or identical with <s>guṇas</s>, some other cause of restriction must be stated. It is said:

children.text: Dhv_3.6b:
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.6b:]

children.text: . . . . tan-niyame hetur aucityaṃ vaktṛ-vācyayoḥ // DhvK_3.6b //
children.translated_text: ... The cause of that restriction is <s>aucitya</s> (propriety) with respect to the speaker and the subject. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.6b]

children.text: tatra vaktā kaviḥ kavi-nibaddho vā, kavi-nibaddhaś cāpi rasa-bhāva-rahito rasa-bhāva-samanvito vā, raso 'pi kathā-nāyakāśrayas tad-vipakṣāśrayo vā, kathā-nāyakaś ca dhīrodāttādi-bheda-bhinnaḥ pūrvas tad-anantaro veti vikalpāḥ / vācyaṃ ca dhvany-ātma-rasāṅgaṃ rasābhāsāṅgaṃ vā, abhineyārtham anabhineyārthaṃ vā, uttama-prakṛty-āśrayaṃ tad-itarāśrayaṃ veti bahu-prakāram /
children.translated_text: Here, the 'speaker' is the poet or a character created by the poet; and a character created by the poet is either devoid of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s> or endowed with them; and the <s>rasa</s> may pertain to the hero of the story or to his adversary; and the hero is differentiated as <s>dhīrodātta</s> (lofty and steadfast) and so on, whether primary or secondary — such are the alternatives. And the 'subject' (<s>vācya</s>) is manifold: it may be a subordinate element of <s>rasa</s> that is the soul of <s>dhvani</s>, or a subordinate element of a semblance of <s>rasa</s>; it may be intended for dramatic representation or not; it may pertain to characters of high nature or otherwise — and so forth.

children.text:
tatra yadā kavir apagata-rasa-bhāvo vaktā tadā racanāyāḥ kāma-cāraḥ / yadāpi kavi-nibaddho vaktā rasa-bhāva-rahitas tadā sa eva; yadā tu kaviḥ kavi-nibaddho vā vaktā rasa-bhāva-samanvito rasaś ca pradhānāśritatvād dhvany-ātma-bhūtas tadā niyamenaiva tatrāsamāsā-madhya-samāse eva saṅghaṭane / karuṇa-vipralambha-śṛṅgārayos tv asamāsaiva saṅghaṭanā /
katham iti ced ucyate-raso yadā prādhānyena pratipādyas tadā tat-pratītau vyavadhāyakā virodhinaś ca sarvātmanaiva parihāryāḥ / evaṃ ca dīrgha-samāsā saṅghaṭanā samāsānām aneka-prakāra-sambhāvanayā kadācid rasa-pratītiṃ vyavadadhātīti tasyāṃ nātyantam abhiniveśaḥ śobhate / viśeṣato 'bhineyārthe kāvye, tato 'nyatra ca viśeṣataḥ karuṇa-vipralambha-śṛṅgārayoḥ / tayor hi sukumārataratvāt svalpāyām apy asvacchatāyāṃ śabdārthayoḥ pratītir mantharībhavati / rasāntare punaḥ pratipādye raudrādau madhyama-samāsā saṅghaṭanā kadācid dhīroddhata-nāyaka-sambandha-vyāpāreṇa dīrgha-samāsāpi vā tad-ākṣepāvinābhāvi-rasocita-vācyāpekṣayā na viguṇā bhavatīti sāpi nātyantaṃ parihāryā /
children.translated_text: Now, when the poet himself is the speaker, devoid of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>, then there is freedom in composition. Even when the speaker is a character created by the poet who is devoid of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>, the same [freedom applies]. But when the poet or a character created by the poet is the speaker endowed with <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>, and the <s>rasa</s>, being associated with the predominant [element], is the soul of <s>dhvani</s> — then the composition must invariably be either non-compound or with medium compounds. For <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic) and <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation), the composition should be non-compound alone. If asked how, it is said: When <s>rasa</s> is to be expressed as the predominant [element], all that obstructs or opposes its apprehension must be entirely avoided. And long-compound composition, through the possibility of multiple interpretations of the compounds, sometimes obstructs the apprehension of <s>rasa</s> — therefore excessive attachment to it is not becoming. Especially in poetry intended for dramatic performance, and beyond that, especially in <s>karuṇa</s> and <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s>. For these, being extremely delicate, have their apprehension retarded by even a slight lack of lucidity in word and meaning. But when another <s>rasa</s> such as <s>raudra</s> (the furious) is to be expressed, medium-compound composition [is appropriate], and sometimes, by virtue of a connection with a <s>dhīroddhata</s> (impetuous) hero, even long-compound [composition] — with regard to the expressed content appropriate to the <s>rasa</s> that is invariably drawn forth by that [hero's nature] — is not deficient in <s>guṇas</s>. Therefore, even that is not to be entirely avoided.

children.text:
sarvāsu ca saṅghaṭanāsu prasādākhyo guṇo vyāpī / sa hi sarva-rasa-sādhāraṇaḥ sarva-saṅghaṭanā-sādhāraṇaś cety uktam / prasādātikrame hy asamāsāpi saṅghaṭanā karuṇa-vipralambha-śṛṅgārau na vyanakti / tad-aparityāge ca madhyama-samāsāpi na na prakāśayati /
tasmāt sarvatra prasādo 'nusartavyaḥ / ata eva ca "yo yaḥ śastraṃ bibharti" ity ādau yady ojasaḥ sthitir neṣyate tat-prasādākhya eva guṇo na mādhuryam / na cācārutvam ; abhipreta-rasa-prakāśanāt / tasmād guṇāvyatiriktatve guṇa-vyatiriktatve vā saṅghaṭanāyā yathoktād aucityād viṣaya-niyamo 'stīti tasyā api rasa-vyañjakatvam / tasyāś ca rasābhivyakti-nimitta-bhūtāyā yo 'yam anantarokto niyama-hetuḥ sa eva guṇānāṃ niyato viṣaya iti guṇāśrayeṇa vyavasthānam apy aviruddham /
children.translated_text: And in all [types of] composition, the <s>guṇa</s> called <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity) is pervasive. For it has been said that it is common to all <s>rasas</s> and common to all compositions. When <s>prasāda</s> is transgressed, even non-compound composition does not manifest <s>karuṇa</s> and <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s>. And when it is not abandoned, even medium-compound composition does manifest [them]. Therefore, <s>prasāda</s> must be maintained everywhere. And precisely for this reason, in 'Whoever bears a weapon' and so forth, if the presence of <s>ojas</s> is not accepted, then the <s>guṇa</s> there is simply <s>prasāda</s>, not <s>mādhurya</s>. Nor is there unattractiveness, because the intended <s>rasa</s> is manifested. Therefore, whether <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> is identical with or different from <s>guṇas</s>, the restriction of domain exists through the <s>aucitya</s> (propriety) described above, and thus <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> too manifests <s>rasa</s>. And the very cause of restriction that has been stated — for <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> when it serves as the cause of the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> — that same is the fixed domain of <s>guṇas</s>. Thus, the establishment [of the domain] through the foundation of <s>guṇas</s> is also not contradicted.
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.7:]

children.text: viṣayāśrayam apy anyad aucityaṃ tāṃ niyacchati /
children.translated_text: Another <s>aucitya</s> (propriety) based on the subject and genre also governs that [<s>saṅghaṭanā</s>];

children.text: kāvya-prabhedāśrayataḥ sthitā bhedavatī hi sā // DhvK_3.7 //
children.translated_text: For it stands differentiated according to the varieties of poetic composition. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.7]

children.text: vaktṛ-vācya-gataucitye saty api viṣayāśrayam anyad aucityaṃ saṅghaṭanāṃ niyacchati / yataḥ kāvyasya prabhedā muktakaṃ saṃskṛta-prākṛtāpabhraṃśa-nibaddham, sandānitaka-viśeṣaka-kalāpaka-kulakāni, paryāya-bandhaḥ parikathā khaṇḍa-kathā sakala-kathe sarga-bandho 'bhineyārtham ākhyāyikā-kathe ity evam ādayaḥ / tad-āśrayeṇāpi saṅghaṭanā viśeṣavatī bhavati / tatra muktakeṣu rasa-bandhābhiniveśinaḥ kaves tad-āśrayam aucityam / tac ca darśitam eva / anyatra kāma-cāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when the <s>aucitya</s> pertaining to speaker and subject is present, another <s>aucitya</s> based on the subject [matter] and genre also governs <s>saṅghaṭanā</s>. For the varieties of poetry are: the independent verse (<s>muktaka</s>) — whether composed in Sanskrit, <s>Prākṛt</s>, or <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>; the <s>sandānitaka</s>, <s>viśeṣaka</s>, <s>kalāpaka</s>, and <s>kulaka</s> [types of verse-clusters]; the <s>paryāya-bandha</s> (alternating composition); the <s>parikathā</s> (tale), <s>khaṇḍa-kathā</s> (episodic narrative), <s>sakala-kathā</s> (complete narrative); the <s>sarga-bandha</s> (canto composition); the <s>abhineyārtha</s> (dramatic) [composition]; and the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> and <s>kathā</s> [prose narrative forms] — and so forth. According to each of these, <s>saṅghaṭanā</s> acquires distinctive character. Among independent verses (<s>muktaka</s>), for a poet intent on <s>rasa</s>-composition, the <s>aucitya</s> proper to them [applies]. And that has already been shown. Otherwise, there is freedom of choice.

children.text: muktakeṣu prabandheṣv iva rasa-bandhābhiniveśinaḥ kavayo dṛśyante / yathā hy amarukasya kaver muktakāḥ śṛṅgāra-rasa-syandinaḥ prabandhāyamānāḥ prasiddhā eva / sandānitakādiṣu tu vikaṭa-nibandhanaucityān madhyama-samāsā-dīrgha-samāse eva racane / prabandhāśrayeṣu yathokta-prabandhaucityam evānusartavyam / paryāya-bandhe punar asamāsā-madhyama-samāse eva saṅghaṭane / kadācid arthaucityāśrayeṇa dīrgha-samāsāyām api saṅghaṭanāyāṃ paruṣā grāmyā ca vṛttiḥ parihartavyā / parikathāyāṃ kāma-cāraḥ, tatretivṛtta-mātropanyāsena nātyantaṃ rasa-bandhābhiniveśāt / khaṇḍa-kathā-sakala-kathayos tu prākṛta-prasiddhayoḥ kulakādi-nibandhana-bhūyastvād dīrgha-samāsāyām api na virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Among independent verses, poets are seen to be intent on <s>rasa</s>-composition just as in longer works. For instance, the independent verses of the poet <s>Amaruka</s>, flowing with the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> <s>rasa</s> and extending like a continuous narrative, are well known. In <s>sandānitaka</s> and similar [verse-clusters], however, due to the propriety of intricate composition, medium-compound or long-compound constructions alone [are appropriate]. In works based on longer compositions, the <s>aucitya</s> proper to the type of composition described above must be followed. In <s>paryāya-bandha</s> (alternating composition), non-compound or medium-compound composition alone [is appropriate]. Sometimes, on the basis of propriety to the meaning, even in long-compound composition, harsh and vulgar diction must be avoided. In the <s>parikathā</s> (tale), there is freedom of choice, since there is no excessive devotion to <s>rasa</s>-composition, as only a bare narrative is presented therein. In <s>khaṇḍa-kathā</s> and <s>sakala-kathā</s>, which are well-known in <s>Prākṛt</s>, since there is a preponderance of <s>kulaka</s> and similar compositional devices, there is no contradiction even in long-compound [style].

children.text: vṛtty-aucityaṃ tu yathā-rasam anusartavyam / sarga-bandhe tu rasa-tātparye yathā-rasam aucityam anyathā tu kāma-cāraḥ / dvayor api mārgayoḥ sarga-bandha-vidhāyināṃ darśanād rasa-tātparyaṃ sādhīyaḥ / abhineyārthe tu sarvathā rasa-bandhe 'bhiniveśaḥ kāryaḥ / ākhyāyikā-kathayos tu gadya-nibandhana-bāhulyād gadye ca chando-bandha-bhinna-prasthānatvād iha niyame hetur akṛta-pūrvo 'pi manāk kriyate || DhvA_3.7 ||
children.translated_text: The propriety of diction (<s>vṛtti</s>) must be followed according to the [predominant] <s>rasa</s>. In <s>sarga-bandha</s> (canto composition), when <s>rasa</s> is the aim, propriety according to the <s>rasa</s> [applies]; otherwise, there is freedom of choice. Since poets who compose in both styles (<s>mārga</s>) of canto composition are observed, devotion to <s>rasa</s> is preferable. In dramatic poetry (<s>abhineyārtha</s>), devotion to <s>rasa</s>-composition must be maintained in all circumstances. In <s>ākhyāyikā</s> and <s>kathā</s> (prose narratives), since there is a predominance of prose composition, and since in prose the approach is different from metrical composition — here a cause of restriction, though not previously established, is briefly stated. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.7]
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.8:]

children.text: etad yathoktam aucityam eva tasyā niyāmakam /
children.translated_text: This very <s>aucitya</s> (propriety) as described is the regulator of that [<s>saṅghaṭanā</s>].

children.text: sarvatra gadya-bandhe 'pi chando-niyama-varjite // DhvK_3.8 //
children.translated_text: everywhere in prose composition as well, even though freed from metrical constraint. // DhvK_3.8 //

children.text: yad etad aucityaṃ vaktṛ-vācya-gataṃ saṅghaṭanāyā niyāmakam uktam etad eva gadye chando-niyama-varjite 'pi viṣayāpekṣaṃ niyama-hetuḥ / tathā hy atrāpi yadā kaviḥ kavi-nibaddho vā vaktā rasa-bhāva-rahitas tadā kāma-cāraḥ / rasa-bhāva-samanvite tu vaktari pūrvoktam evānusartavyam / tatrāpi ca viṣayaucityam eva / ākhyāyikāyāṃ tu bhūmnā madhyama-samāsā-dīrgha-samāse eva saṅghaṭane / gadyasya vikaṭa-bandhāśrayeṇa chāyāvattvāt / tatra ca tasya prakṛṣyamāṇatvāt / kathāyāṃ tu vikaṭa-bandha-prācurye 'pi gadyasya rasa-bandhoktam aucityam anusartavyam || DhvA_3.8 ||
children.translated_text: This propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) pertaining to the speaker and the subject matter, which has been stated as the determinant of composition, is the cause of regulation even in prose (<s>gadya</s>) freed from metrical constraint, with reference to the subject matter. For here too, when the speaker is the poet or one portrayed by the poet and is devoid of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>, there is freedom [of composition]. But when the speaker is endowed with <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>, the previously stated [principles] must be followed. And there too, propriety of subject matter [applies]. In the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> (narrative romance), however, the composition is predominantly in medium and long compounds—because prose [in that genre] naturally possesses the quality of shadow (<s>chāyāvattva</s>) through the employment of intricate (<s>vikaṭa</s>) construction, and because that [intricacy] is intensified therein. But in the <s>kathā</s> (tale), even though intricate prose construction may be abundant, the propriety stated for <s>rasa</s>-composition should be followed. // DhvA_3.8 //
DhvK 3.9:

children.text: rasa-bandhoktam aucityaṃ bhāti sarvatra saṃśritā /
children.translated_text: The propriety stated for <s>rasa</s>-composition shines forth everywhere when the composition is based upon it.

children.text: racanā viṣayāpekṣaṃ tat tu kiṃcid vibhedavat // DhvK_3.9 //
children.translated_text: That [propriety], however, is somewhat differentiated with reference to the subject matter. // DhvK_3.9 //

children.text: athavā padyavad gadya-bandhe 'pi rasa-bandhoktam aucityaṃ sarvatra saṃśritā racanā bhavati / tat tu viṣayāpekṣaṃ kiṃcid viśeṣavad bhavati, na tu sarvākāram / tathā hi gadya-bandhe 'py atidīrgha-samāsā racanā na vipralambha-śṛṅgāra-karuṇayor ākhyāyikāyām api śobhate / nāṭakādāv apy asamāsaiva na raudra-vīrādi-varṇane / viṣayāpekṣaṃ tv aucityaṃ pramāṇato 'pakṛṣyate prakṛṣyate ca / tathā hy ākhyāyikāyāṃ nātyantam asamāsā sva-viṣaye 'pi nāṭakādau nātidīrgha-samāsā ceti saṅghaṭanāyā dig-anusartavyā || DhvA_3.9 ||
children.translated_text: Or else, even in prose composition as in verse, a composition that everywhere follows the propriety stated for <s>rasa</s>-composition is [ideal]. That [propriety], however, is somewhat different with reference to the subject matter—but not in every aspect. For even in prose composition, an excessively long-compounded construction does not shine in the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> when [describing] <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (love in separation) and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos). Nor does an entirely uncompounded [construction] in <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) and the like when [describing] the <s>raudra</s> (furious) and <s>vīra</s> (heroic) [sentiments]. The propriety with reference to subject matter is, however, diminished or intensified in its application. For in the <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, even in its own subject matter, one should not use an excessively uncompounded [style]; in <s>nāṭaka</s> and the like, one should not use an excessively long-compounded [style]—this direction regarding composition should be followed. // DhvA_3.9 //

children.text: idānīm alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyo dhvaniḥ prabandhātmā rāmāyaṇa-mahābhāratādau prakāśamānaḥ prasiddha eva / tasya tu yathā prakāśanaṃ tat pratipādyate-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>dhvani</s> of the imperceptibly-sequenced (<s>alakṣyakrama</s>) suggested type, as the soul of an extended composition (<s>prabandha</s>), is well known as it shines forth in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Mahābhārata</s>, and the like. How it shines forth is now explained:

children.text: vibhāvabhāvānubhāva-sañcāry-aucitya-cāruṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The construction of the narrative body (<s>kathā-śarīra</s>)—whether actual or imagined—

children.text: vidhiḥ kathā-śarīrasya vṛttasyotprekṣitasya vā // DhvK_3.10 //
children.translated_text: made beautiful by the propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and <s>sañcārins</s> (transient emotions); // DhvK_3.10 //

children.text: itivṛtta-vaśāyātāṃ tyaktvānanuguṇāṃ sthitim /
children.translated_text: Abandoning even the historically given arrangement that does not accord [with <s>rasa</s>],

children.text: utprekṣyāpy antarābhīṣṭa-rasocita-kathonnayaḥ // DhvK_3.11 //
children.translated_text: the elevation of the narrative to suit the desired <s>rasa</s>, even by invention, at intermediate [points]; // DhvK_3.11 //

children.text: sandhi-sandhy-aṅga-ghaṭanaṃ rasābhivyakty-apekṣayā /
children.translated_text: The structuring of <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) and <s>sandhy-aṅgas</s> (subdivisions of junctures) with a view to the manifestation of <s>rasa</s>,

children.text: na tu kevalayā śāstra-sthiti-sampādanecchayā // DhvK_3.12 //
children.translated_text: and not merely out of a desire to fulfill the prescriptions of the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise); // DhvK_3.12 //

children.text: uddīpana-praśamane yathāvasaram antarā /
children.translated_text: The stimulation and calming [of <s>rasa</s>] at appropriate intervals,

children.text: rasasyārabdha-viśrānter anusandhānam aṅginaḥ // DhvK_3.13 //
children.translated_text: and the re-establishment of the principal <s>rasa</s> whose repose has been initiated; // DhvK_3.13 //

children.text: alaṅkṛtīnāṃ śaktāv apy ānurūpyeṇa yojanam /
children.translated_text: The employment of <s>alaṅkāras</s> in fitting proportion even when the poet has the capacity [for more]—

children.text: prabandhasya rasādīnāṃ vyañjakatve nibandhanam // DhvK_3.14 //
children.translated_text: [these are] the foundations for the suggestive power of an extended composition with respect to <s>rasa</s> and the like. // DhvK_3.14 //

children.text: prabandho 'pi rasādīnāṃ vyañjaka ity uktaṃ tasya vyañjakatve nibandhanam / prathamaṃ tāvad vibhāva-bhāvānubhāva-sañcāry-aucitya-cāruṇaḥ kathā-śarīrasya vidhir yathāyathaṃ pratipipādayiṣita-rasa-bhāvādy-apekṣayā ya ucito vibhāvo bhāvo 'nubhāvaḥ sañcārī vā tad-aucitya-cāruṇaḥ kathā-śarīrasya vidhir vyañjakatve nibandhanam ekam / tatra vibhāvaucityaṃ tāvat prasiddham / bhāvaucityaṃ tu prakṛty-aucityāt / prakṛtir hy uttama-madhyamādhama-bhāvena divya-mānuṣādi-bhāvena ca vibhedinī / tāṃ yathāyatham anusṛtyāsaṅkīrṇaḥ sthāyī bhāva upanibadhyamāna aucitya-bhāg bhavati / anyathā tu kevala-mānuṣāśrayeṇa divyasya kevala-divyāśrayeṇa vā kevala-mānuṣasyotsāhādaya upanibadhyamānā anucitā bhavanti / tathā ca kevala-mānuṣasya rājāder varṇane saptārṇava-laṅghanādi-lakṣaṇā vyāpārā upanibadhyamānā sauṣṭhava-bhṛto 'pi nīrasā eva niyamena bhavanti, tatra tv anaucityam eva hetuḥ /
children.translated_text: It has been stated that an extended composition (<s>prabandha</s>) too is a suggestor of <s>rasa</s> and the like; the foundations for its suggestive power [are now described]. First, the construction of the narrative body—whether actual or imagined—made beautiful by the propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>bhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>sañcārins</s>: whatever <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, or <s>sañcārin</s> is proper with reference to the <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and so forth intended to be conveyed—the beauty arising from their propriety in the construction of the narrative body is the first foundation for suggestive power. Now, the propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s> is well known. But the propriety of <s>bhāvas</s> [depends on] the propriety of nature (<s>prakṛti</s>). For nature is differentiated as superior, middling, and inferior, and as divine, human, and so forth. By following [the character's nature] as appropriate, the permanent emotion (<s>sthāyibhāva</s>) that is composed without confusion becomes characterized by propriety. Otherwise, [emotions like] enthusiasm and the like, when composed with exclusively human attributes for a divine [character], or with exclusively divine [attributes] for a merely human [character], become improper. And thus, when describing a merely human king and so forth, if activities characterized by leaping across seven oceans and the like are composed, they are invariably devoid of <s>rasa</s>, even if possessing elegance—for there, impropriety itself is the cause.

children.text: nanu nāga-loka-gamanādayaḥ sātavāhana-prabhṛtīnāṃ śrūyante, tad-aloka-sāmānya-prabhāvātiśaya-varṇane kim anaucityaṃ sarvorvī-bharaṇa-kṣamāṇāṃ kṣamā-bhujām iti / na tad asti ; na vayaṃ brūmo yat prabhāvātiśaya-varṇanam anucitaṃ rājñām, kiṃ tu kevala-mānuṣāśrayeṇa yotpādya-vastu-kathā kriyate tasyāṃ divyam aucityaṃ na yojanīyam / divya-mānuṣyāyāṃ tu kathāyām ubhayaucitya-yojanam aviruddham eva / yathā pāṇḍv-ādi-kathāyām / sātavāhanādiṣu tu yeṣu yāvad apadānaṃ śrūyate teṣu tāvan-mātram anugamyamānam anuguṇatvena pratibhāsate / vyatiriktaṃ tu teṣām evopanibadhyamānam anucitam /
children.translated_text: Objection: Journeys to the <s>Nāga</s>-world and the like are heard of in the case of <s>Sātavāhana</s> and others; so what impropriety is there in describing their extraordinary superhuman powers, since they are lords of the earth capable of bearing the entire world? [Reply:] That is not so. We are not saying that the description of extraordinary powers is improper for kings. Rather, when a narrative of imagined events is composed with exclusively human attributes, divine propriety should not be introduced. But in a narrative that is [both] divine and human, the combination of both kinds of propriety is not contradictory at all—as in the narrative of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> and others. As for <s>Sātavāhana</s> and others, whatever exploits are traditionally heard of, following only that much appears fitting. But composing anything beyond that for them is improper.

children.text: tad ayam atra paramārthaḥ-
children.translated_text: Here, this is the ultimate principle:

children.text: anaucityād ṛte nānyad rasa-bhangasya kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: There is no cause for the destruction of <s>rasa</s> other than impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>).

children.text: prasiddhaucitya-bandhas tu rasasyopaniṣat parā //
children.translated_text: And the binding together [of a composition] with well-known propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) is the supreme secret (<s>upaniṣad</s>) of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: ata eva ca bharate prakhyāta-vastu-viṣayatvaṃ prakhyātodātta-nāyakatvaṃ ca nāṭakasyāvaśya-kartavyatayopanyastam / tena hi nāyakaucityānaucitya-viṣaye kavir na vyāmuhyati / yas tūtpādya-vastu nāṭakādi kuryāt tasyāprasiddhānucita-nāyaka-svabhāva-varṇane mahān pramādaḥ /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, in <s>Bharata</s>'s [<s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s>], the requirement that a <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) have a well-known subject matter and a well-known, noble hero has been stipulated as obligatory. For thereby the poet does not err regarding the propriety and impropriety of the hero's nature. But one who would compose a <s>nāṭaka</s> and the like with imagined subject matter faces the great danger of describing the nature of an unfamiliar, improper hero.

children.text:
nanu yady utsāhādi-bhāva-varṇane kathañcid divya-mānuṣyādy-aucitya-parīkṣā kriyate tat kriyatām, raty-ādau tu kiṃ tayā prayojanam ? ratir hi bhāratavarṣocitenaiva vyavahāreṇa divyānām api varṇanīyeti sthitiḥ / naivam / tatraucityātikrameṇa sutarāṃ doṣaḥ / tathā hy adhama-prakṛtyaucityenottama-prakṛteḥ śṛṅgāropanibandhane kā bhaven nopahāsyatā /
trividhaṃ prakṛty-aucityaṃ bhārate varṣe 'py asti śṛṅgāra-viṣayam /
children.translated_text: Objection: If, in the description of emotions like enthusiasm and the like, the examination of the propriety of divine, human, and other [natures] is somehow undertaken, let it be so. But with <s>rati</s> (love) and the like, what is the purpose of that [examination]? For love, even of divine beings, should be described only in the manner proper to <s>Bhāratavarṣa</s> (the human realm)—this is the established view. [Reply:] Not so. In that [domain], transgression of propriety is even more defective. For what could not be laughable if the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> of one of superior nature were composed with the propriety befitting an inferior nature? There is a threefold propriety of nature even in <s>Bhāratavarṣa</s> with respect to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>.

children.text:
yat tu divyam aucityaṃ tat tatrānupakārakam eveti cet-na vayaṃ divyam aucityaṃ śṛṅgāra-viṣayam anyat kiṃcid brūmaḥ / kiṃ tarhi ? bhāratavarṣa-viṣaye yathottama-nāyakeṣu rājādiṣu śṛṅgāropanibandhas tathā divyāśrayo 'pi śobhate / na ca rājādiṣu prasiddha-grāmya-śṛṅgāropanibandhanaṃ prasiddhaṃ nāṭakādau, tathaiva deveṣu tat parihartavyam /
nāṭakāder abhineyārthatvād abhinayasya ca sambhoga-śṛṅgāra-viṣayasyāsabhyatvāt tatra parihāra iti cet-na; yady abhinayasyaivaṃ-viṣayasyāsabhyatā tat kāvyasyaivaṃ-viṣayasya sā kena nivāryate ? tasmād abhineyārthe 'nabhineyārthe vā kāvye yad uttama-prakṛte rājāder uttama-prakṛtibhir nāyikābhiḥ saha grāmya-sambhoga-varṇanaṃ tat pitroḥ sambhoga-varṇanam iva sutarām asabhyam / tathaivottama-devatādi-viṣayam /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But divine propriety in the domain of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is unhelpful there.
