[Reply:] We are not speaking of some other divine propriety in the domain of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. Rather, just as the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> composed for superior heroes such as kings and the like in the <s>Bhāratavarṣa</s> context shines, so too does it shine when the subject is divine. And just as in <s>nāṭaka</s> and the like, the composition of vulgar <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is not established for kings and the like, so too it should be avoided for gods. [Objection:] In <s>nāṭaka</s> and the like, the avoidance is because the subject matter is to be enacted (<s>abhineyārtha</s>), and the enactment of <s>sambhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-union) is indecent. [Reply:] No; if the enactment of such subject matter is indecent, by what [principle] is the indecency of poetry with such subject matter to be prevented? Therefore, in poetry whether meant for enactment or not, the description of vulgar love-in-union for a hero of superior nature with heroines of superior nature is supremely indecent, like describing the sexual union of one's parents. The same applies to the subject matter of superior deities and the like.

children.text: na ca sambhoga-śṛṅgārasya surata-lakṣaṇa evaikaḥ prakāraḥ, yāvad anye 'pi prabhedāḥ paraspara-prema-darśanādayaḥ sambhavanti, te kasmād uttama-prakṛti-viṣaye na varṇyante ? tasmād utsāhavad ratāv api prakṛty-aucityam anusartavyam / tathaiva vismayādiṣu / yat tv evaṃ-vidhe viṣaye mahākavīnām apy asamīkṣya-kāritā lakṣye dṛśyate sa doṣa eva / sa tu śakti-tiraskṛtatvāt teṣāṃ na lakṣyata ity uktam eva / anubhāvaucityaṃ tu bharatādau prasiddham eva /
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>sambhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (love in union) does not have only one mode, namely the erotic act. Rather, there are other varieties as well—the display of mutual love and so forth. Why should these not be described in the context of characters of superior nature? Therefore, just as with enthusiasm, propriety of nature must be followed in the case of love as well. The same applies to wonder and the other [sentiments]. As for the fact that even among great poets, unconsidered practice is seen in such matters—that is indeed a fault. But it is not noticed because it is overshadowed by [their other] powers—this has already been said. And the propriety of <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) is well known from <s>Bharata</s>'s [treatise] and the like.

children.text: iyat tūcyate-bharatādi-viracitāṃ sthitiṃ cānuvartamānena mahākavi-prabandhāṃś ca paryālocayatā sva-pratibhāṃ cānusaratā kavināvahita-cetasā bhūtvā vibhāvādy-aucitya-bhraṃśa-parityāge paraḥ prayatno vidheyaḥ / aucityavataḥ kathā-śarīrasya vṛttasyotprekṣitasya vā graho vyañjaka ity anenaitat pratipādayati-yad itihāsādiṣu kathāsu rasavatīṣu vividhāsu satīṣv api yat tatra vibhāvādy-aucityavat kathā-śarīraṃ tad eva grāhyaṃ netarat / vṛttād api ca kathā-śarīrād utprekṣite viśeṣataḥ prayatnavatā bhavitavyam / tatra hy anavadhānāt skhalataḥ kaver avyutpatti-sambhāvanā mahatī bhavati /
children.translated_text: This much is said: The poet, with attentive mind, following the prescriptions set forth by <s>Bharata</s> and others, examining the works of the great poets, and also following his own genius (<s>pratibhā</s>), should make the greatest effort to avoid lapses in the propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like. The statement 'the adoption of the narrative body, whether actual or imagined, that is characterized by propriety, is suggestive' conveys this: that among the diverse <s>rasa</s>-laden narratives available in <s>itihāsa</s> (epic history) and the like, only that narrative body which possesses propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like should be adopted—not otherwise. And when [the narrative body is] imagined, even greater care must be taken. For there, if the poet stumbles through inattention, there is a great suspicion of lack of learning.

children.text: parikara-ślokaś cātra-
children.translated_text: And the ancillary verse here is:

children.text: kathā-śarīram utpādya-vastu kāryaṃ tathā tathā /
children.translated_text: The narrative body—the imagined subject matter—should be fashioned in such a way

children.text: yathā rasa-mayaṃ sarvam eva tat pratibhāsate //
children.translated_text: that the whole of it appears as pervaded by <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: tatra cābhyupāyaḥ samyag-vibhāvādy-aucityānusaraṇam / tac ca darśitam eva / kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And the means for this is the proper following of the propriety of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like—and that has been shown. Furthermore:

children.text: santi siddha-rasa-prakhyā ye ca rāmāyaṇādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: There are [works] such as the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> and others that are renowned for their well-established <s>rasa</s>;

children.text: kathāśrayā na tair yojyā svecchā rasa-virodhinī //
children.translated_text: with their narrative frameworks, one should not combine willful [deviations] that are opposed to <s>rasa</s>.

children.text:
teṣu hi kathāśrayeṣu tāvat svecchaiva na yojyā / yad uktam-"kathā-mārge na cātikramaḥ" /
svecchāpi yadi yojyā tad-rasa-virodhinī na yojyā /
children.translated_text: In those narrative frameworks, to begin with, one's own whim should not be combined. As it has been said: 'In the path of the narrative, there should be no transgression.' And even if one's own [invention] is combined, it should not be opposed to <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: idam aparaṃ prabandhasya rasābhivyañjakatve nibandhanam / itivṛtta-vaśāyātāṃ kathañcid rasānanuguṇāṃ sthitiṃ tyaktvā punar utprekṣyāpy antarābhīṣṭa-rasocita-kathonnayo vidheyaḥ yathā kālidāsa-prabandheṣu / yathā ca sarvasena-viracite hari-vijaye / yathā ca madīya evārjuna-carite mahākāvye / kavinā kāvyam upanibadhnatā sarvātmanā rasa-paratantreṇa bhavitavyam / tatretivṛtte yadi rasānanuguṇāṃ sthitiṃ paśyet tademāṃ bhaṅktvāpi svatantratayā rasānuguṇaṃ kathāntaram utpādayet / na hi kaver itivṛtta-mātra-nirvahaṇena kiṃcit prayojanam, itihāsād eva tat-siddheḥ /
children.translated_text: This is another foundation for the suggestive power of an extended composition with respect to <s>rasa</s>: Abandoning the historically given arrangement that does not conform to [<s>rasa</s>] in any way, one should elevate the narrative to suit the desired <s>rasa</s>, even through invention at intermediate points—as in the works of <s>Kālidāsa</s>, as in the <s>Harivijaya</s> composed by <s>Sarvasena</s>, and as in my own <s>mahākāvya</s>, the <s>Arjunacarita</s>. A poet composing a <s>kāvya</s> must be entirely subservient to <s>rasa</s>. Therein, if he sees in the historical narrative an arrangement that does not accord with <s>rasa</s>, he should break it and independently produce another narrative that accords with <s>rasa</s>. For the poet has no purpose in merely carrying through the historical narrative, since that [historical information] is already available from the <s>itihāsa</s> itself.

children.text: rasādi-vyañjakatve prabandhasya cedam anyan mukhyaṃ nibandhanam, yat-sandhīnāṃ mukha-pratimukha-garbhāvamarśa-nirvahaṇākhyānāṃ tad-aṅgānāṃ copakṣepādīnāṃ ghaṭanaṃ rasābhivyakty-apekṣayā, yathā ratnāvalyām / na tu kevalaṃ śāstra-sthiti-sampādanecchayā / yathā veṇī-saṃhāre vilāsākhyasya pratimukha-sandhy-aṅgasya prakṛta-rasa-nibandhānanuguṇam api dvitīye 'ṅke bharata-matānusaraṇa-mātrecchayā ghaṭanam /
children.translated_text: And this is the other primary foundation for the suggestive power of an extended composition with respect to <s>rasa</s> and the like: the structuring of the <s>sandhis</s> (junctures)—called <s>mukha</s> (opening), <s>pratimukha</s> (progression), <s>garbha</s> (development), <s>avamarśa</s> (pause), and <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion)—and their subdivisions (<s>sandhy-aṅgas</s>) such as <s>upakṣepa</s> and the like, with a view to the manifestation of <s>rasa</s>—as in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>. Not merely out of a desire to fulfill the prescriptions of the <s>śāstra</s>—as in the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>, where the <s>sandhy-aṅga</s> called <s>vilāsa</s>, belonging to the <s>pratimukha</s> juncture, is structured in the second act merely out of a desire to follow <s>Bharata</s>'s doctrine, even though it does not accord with the composition of the principal <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: idaṃ cāparaṃ prabandhasya rasa-vyañjakatve nimittaṃ yad uddīpana-praśamane yathāvasaram antarā rasasya, yathā ratnāvalyām eva / punar ārabdha-viśrānte rasasyāṅgino 'nusandhiś ca, yathā tāpasa-vatsarāje /
children.translated_text: And this is another cause of the suggestive power of an extended composition with respect to <s>rasa</s>: the stimulation and calming of <s>rasa</s> at appropriate intervals—as in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> itself. And the re-establishment of the principal <s>rasa</s> whose repose has been initiated—as in the <s>Tāpasavatsarāja</s>.

children.text: prabandha-viśeṣasya nāṭakāde rasa-vyakti-nimittam idaṃ cāparam avagantavyaṃ yad alaṅkṛtīnāṃ śaktāv apy ānurūpyeṇa yojanam / śakto hi kaviḥ kadācid alaṅkāra-nibandhane tad ākṣiptatayaivānapekṣita-rasa-bandhaḥ prabandham ārabhate tad-upadeśārtham idam uktam / dṛśyante ca kavayo 'laṅkāra-nibandhanaika-rasā anapekṣita-rasāḥ prabandheṣu /
children.translated_text: This too should be understood as another cause of <s>rasa</s>-manifestation specific to the particular kind of extended composition such as <s>nāṭaka</s> and the like: the employment of <s>alaṅkāras</s> in fitting proportion (<s>ānurūpya</s>) even when the poet has the capacity [for more]. For a capable poet sometimes, in his attachment to the composition of <s>alaṅkāras</s>, begins an extended composition that is merely evoked and without regard for <s>rasa</s>-composition—this instruction is given for that purpose. And poets are indeed seen who, in extended compositions, are singularly devoted to the composition of <s>alaṅkāras</s> with no regard for <s>rasa</s>.
DhvK 3.15:

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Furthermore:

children.text: anusvānopamātmāpi prabhedo ya udāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The division that has been cited as resembling a reverberation (<s>anusvānopama</s>)—

children.text: dhvaner asya prabandheṣu bhāsate so 'pi keṣucit // DhvK_3.15 //
children.translated_text: Of this <s>dhvani</s>, [certain varieties] shine forth in extended works (<s>prabandha</s>) as well. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.15 //

children.text: asya vivakṣitāny apara-vācyasya dhvaner anuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgyo 'pi yaḥ prabheda udāhṛto dviprakāraḥ so 'pi prabandheṣu keṣucid dyotate / tad yathā madhumathana-vijaye pāñcajanyoktiṣu / yathā vā mamaiva kāmadevasya sahacara-samāgame viṣama-bāṇa-līlāyām /
yathā ca gṛdhra-gomāyu-saṃvādādau mahābhārate || DhvA_3.15 ||
children.translated_text: And as in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, in the dialogue of the vulture and the jackal and the like. || <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Autocommentary 3.15 ||

Of this <s>dhvani</s> whose expressed meaning is intended but another [meaning] is suggested, the variety with reverberating-echo suggestion, which was illustrated as twofold — that too shines forth in certain extended works. For example, in the <s>Madhumathana-vijaya</s>, in the speeches of <s>Pāñcajanya</s>; or as in my own [work], in the encounter of <s>Kāmadeva</s>'s companion, in the sport of <s>Viṣamabāṇa</s> (the crooked-arrowed one);
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.16:

children.text: sup-tiṅ-vacana-sambandhais tathā kāraka-śaktibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Through nominal case-endings (<s>sup</s>), verbal endings (<s>tiṅ</s>), number, syntactic relations,

children.text: kṛt-tad dhita-samāsaiś ca dyotyo 'lakṣya-kramaḥ kvacit // DhvK_3.16 //
children.translated_text: And through <s>kāraka</s> (case-role) powers, primary derivatives (<s>kṛt</s>), secondary derivatives (<s>taddhita</s>), and compounds — the imperceptible-sequence [<s>dhvani</s>] is sometimes manifested. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.16 //

children.text: alakṣya-kramo dhvaner ātmā rasādiḥ sub-viśeṣais tiṅ-viśeṣair vacana-viśeṣaiḥ sambandha-viśeṣaiḥ kāraka-śaktibhiḥ kṛd-viśeṣais tad dhita-viśeṣaiḥ samāsaiś ceti / ca-śabdān nipātopasarga-kālādibhiḥ prayuktair abhivyajyamāno dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: The imperceptible-sequence essence of <s>dhvani</s> — namely <s>rasa</s> and the like — is seen to be manifested by particular nominal endings, particular verbal endings, particular numbers, particular syntactic relations, <s>kāraka</s> powers, particular primary derivatives, particular secondary derivatives, and compounds. And by the force of the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), [it is manifested] also by particles (<s>nipāta</s>), prefixes (<s>upasarga</s>), tense (<s>kāla</s>), and the like.

children.text: yathā-
nyakkāro hy ayam eva me yad arayas tatrāpy asau tāpasaḥ
children.translated_text: 'This alone is my humiliation: that my enemies [exist] — and among them, that very ascetic;

children.text: so 'py atraiva nihanti rākṣasa-kulaṃ jīvaty aho rāvaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And he, right here, slays the <s>Rākṣasa</s> clan — and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> still lives!

children.text: dhig dhik cakra-jitaṃ prabodhitavatā kiṃ kumbhakarṇena vā
children.translated_text: Shame, shame upon the conqueror of the discus! And what of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, aroused [from sleep]?

children.text: svarga-grāmaṭikā-viluṇṭhana-vṛthocchūnaiḥ kim ebhir bhujaiḥ //[*19]
children.translated_text: What use are these arms, swollen in vain from plundering the villages of heaven?'
Note: <s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 2105. Cf. <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 1.2.

children.text: Skm 2105. Cf. Sāh.D. 1.2.

children.translated_text: For example—

children.text: atra hi śloke bhūyasā sarveṣām apy eṣāṃ sphuṭam eva vyañjakatvaṃ dṛśyate / tatra "me yad arayaḥ" ity anena sup-sambandha-vacanānām abhivyañjakatvam / "tatrāpy asau tāpasaḥ" ity atra tad dhita-nipātayoḥ / "so 'py atraiva nihanti rākṣasa-kulaṃ jīvaty aho rāvaṇaḥ" ity atra tiṅ-kāraka-śaktīnām / "dhig dhik cakra-jitam" ity ādau ślokārdhe kṛt-tad dhita-samāsopasargāṇām /
children.translated_text: In this verse, the suggestive power of nearly all of these [grammatical elements] is clearly visible. There, 'my enemies' (<s>me yad arayaḥ</s>) shows the suggestive power of nominal endings, syntactic relation, and number. 'That very ascetic there' (<s>tatrāpy asau tāpasaḥ</s>) shows [the suggestive power] of a secondary derivative and a particle. 'He, right here, slays the <s>Rākṣasa</s> clan — <s>Rāvaṇa</s> still lives!' (<s>so'py atraiva nihanti rākṣasa-kulaṃ jīvaty aho rāvaṇaḥ</s>) shows [the suggestive power] of verbal endings and <s>kāraka</s> powers. 'Shame upon the conqueror of the discus' (<s>dhig dhik cakra-jitam</s>) and the rest of the half-verse show [the suggestive power] of primary derivatives, secondary derivatives, compounds, and prefixes.

children.text: evaṃ-vidhasya vyañjaka-bhūyastve ca ghaṭamāne kāvyasya sarvātiśāyinī bandha-cchāyā samunmīlati / yatra hi vyaṅgyāvabhāsinaḥ padasyaikasyaiva tāvad āvirbhāvas tatrāpi kāvye kāpi bandha-cchāyā kim uta yatra teṣāṃ bahūnāṃ samavāyaḥ / yathātrānantarodita-śloke / atra hi rāvaṇa ity asmin pade 'rthāntara-saṃkramita-vācyena dhvani-prabhedenālaṅkṛte 'pi punar anantaroktānāṃ vyañjaka-prakārāṇām udbhāsanam / dṛśyante ca mahātmanāṃ pratibhā-viśeṣa-bhājāṃ bāhulyenaivaṃ-vidhā bandha-prakārāḥ / yathā maharṣer vyāsasya-
children.translated_text: And when such suggestors predominate, the most surpassing luster of poetic composition (<s>bandha-cchāyā</s>) unfolds. For even where a single word manifesting the suggested comes to light, there is a certain luster in the poetry — how much more so where many such [suggestors] combine? As in the verse just cited. For here, even though the word '<s>Rāvaṇa</s>' is adorned by the variety of <s>dhvani</s> whose expressed meaning is transferred to another sense, there is additionally the manifestation of the types of suggestors just mentioned. And indeed, such modes of composition are abundantly seen in the works of great souls endowed with extraordinary poetic genius. As in the great sage <s>Vyāsa</s>'s [verse]—

children.text: atikrānta-sukhāḥ kālāḥ pratyupasthita-dāruṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Times of happiness have passed; terrible [times] have arrived;

children.text: śvaḥ śvaḥ pāpīya-divasā pṛthivī gata-yauvanā //
children.translated_text: Day after day [things grow] worse — the earth has lost her youth.'

children.text: atra hi kṛt-tad dhita-vacanair alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyaḥ, "pṛthivī gata-yauvanā" ity anena cātyanta-tiraskṛta-vācyo dhvaniḥ prakāśitaḥ / eṣāṃ ca sub-ādīnām ekaikaśaḥ samuditānāṃ ca vyañjakatvaṃ mahā-kavīnāṃ prabandheṣu prāyeṇa dṛśyate / sub-antasya vyañjakatvaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, through primary derivatives, secondary derivatives, and number, <s>dhvani</s> with imperceptible-sequence suggestion is [manifested]; and by 'the earth has lost her youth' (<s>pṛthivī gata-yauvanā</s>), <s>dhvani</s> whose expressed meaning is completely set aside is revealed. And the suggestive power of these nominal endings and the like, both individually and in combination, is generally seen in the works of great poets. The suggestive power of a nominal-ending word (<s>sub-anta</s>) [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: tālaiḥ śiñjad-valaya-subhagaiḥ kāntayā nartito me /
children.translated_text: '[She] whom the beloved made dance for me with her palm-claps, lovely with jingling bracelets —'

children.text: yām adhyāste divasa-vigame nīlakaṇṭhaḥ suhṛd vaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'On that [terrace] the blue-throated [peacock], your friend, alights at the end of day.'

children.text: tiṅ-antasya yathā-
children.translated_text: The suggestive power of a verbal-ending word (<s>tiṅ-anta</s>) [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: abasara rouṃ cia ṇimmiāiṃ mā puṃsa me haacchīiṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Go away! These [eyes of mine] were created only for weeping — do not close my eyes!

children.text: daṃsaṇa-mettum bhettehiṃ jehiṃ hiaaṃ tuha ṇa ṇāaṃ //]
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] By those [eyes] that did not know your heart, even by merely seeing [you]!'

children.text: [apasara roditum eva nirmite mā puṃsaya hate akṣiṇī me /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'Go away! These [eyes of mine] were created only for weeping — do not close my eyes!

children.text: darśana-mātronmattābhyāṃ yābhyāṃ tava hṛdayam evaṃ-rūpaṃ na jñātam //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] By those [eyes] that, maddened by merely seeing [you], did not know the true nature of your heart!'

children.text: yathā vā-
children.translated_text: Or as in—

children.text: mā panthaṃ rundhīo abehi bālaa ahosi ahirīo /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Do not block the path! Go away, boy — you are bold! How shameless you are!

children.text: amhea ṇiricchāo suṇṇa-gharaṃ rakkhidabbaṃ ṇo //[*20]
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] We are dependent [on others] — an empty house of ours needs guarding!'
Note: <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> (supplement 955)

children.text: gāhā-sattasāī (supp. 955)
[mā panthānaṃ rudhaḥ apehi bālaka aprauḍha aho asi ahrīkaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'Do not block the path! Go away, boy — you are bold! How shameless!

children.text: vayaṃ para-tantrā yataḥ śūnya-gṛhaṃ māmakaṃ rakṣaṇīyaṃ vartate //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] We are dependent [on others] — since an empty house of mine needs guarding!'

children.text: sambandhasya yathā-
children.translated_text: The suggestive power of syntactic relation (<s>sambandha</s>) [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: aṇṇatta vacca bālaa hnāantīṃ kiṃ maṃ puloesi eaṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Go elsewhere, boy! Why are you gazing at me bathing?'

children.text: bho jāā-bhīruāṇaṃ taḍam bia ṇa hoi //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Alas, for those who fear their wives, there is simply no riverbank!'

children.text: [anyatra vraja bālaka snāntīṃ kiṃ māṃ pralokayasy etat /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'Go elsewhere, boy! Why are you gazing at me bathing?'

children.text: bho jāyā-bhīrukāṇāṃ taṭam eva na bhavati //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'Alas, for those who fear their wives, there is simply no riverbank!'

children.text: kṛtaka-prayogeṣu prākṛteṣu tad dhita-viṣaye vyañjakatvam āvedyata eva / avajñātiśaye kaḥ ? samāsānāṃ ca vṛtty-aucityena viniyojane / nipātānāṃ vyañjakatvaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: In Prakrit literary compositions, the suggestive power with respect to secondary derivatives is evident in itself. What [need be said] when there is a surplus of contempt? And [the same applies] to compounds when deployed with propriety of usage (<s>vṛtty-aucitya</s>). The suggestive power of particles (<s>nipāta</s>) [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: ayam eka-pade tayā viyogaḥ
children.translated_text: 'This separation from my beloved has come upon me all at once,

children.text: priyayā copanataḥ suduḥsaho me /
children.translated_text: And it is exceedingly hard to bear;

children.text: nava-vāridharodayād ahobhir
children.translated_text: And [moreover] with the rising of fresh rain-clouds,

children.text: bhavitavyaṃ ca nirātapārdha-ramyaiḥ //
children.translated_text: The days will be charming [only] in their shade-filled halves.'

children.text: ity atra ca-śabdaḥ / yathā vā-
children.translated_text: Here [the suggestor is] the particle 'and' (<s>ca</s>). Or as in—

children.text: muhur aṅguli-saṃvṛtādharauṣṭhaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Her face, with lower lip repeatedly covered by her finger,

children.text: pratiṣedhākṣara-viklavābhirāmam /
children.translated_text: Charmingly flustered by syllables of refusal,

children.text: mukham aṃsa-vivarti pakṣmalākṣyāḥ
children.translated_text: Turned aside at the shoulder, with long-lashed eyes —

children.text: katham apy unnamitaṃ na cumbitaṃ tu //
children.translated_text: Somehow it was raised upward, but (<s>tu</s>) not kissed.'

children.text: atra tu-śabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here [the suggestor is] the particle 'but' (<s>tu</s>).

children.text: nipātānāṃ prasiddham apīha dyotakatvaṃ rasāpekṣayoktam iti draṣṭavyam / upasargāṇāṃ vyañjakatvaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: Although the suggestive power of particles is well-known [in grammar], it is here stated with reference to <s>rasa</s> — this should be understood. The suggestive power of prefixes (<s>upasarga</s>) [is illustrated] as in—

children.text:
nīvārāḥ śuka-garbha-koṭara-mukha-bhraṣṭās tarūṇām adhaḥ
prasnigdhāḥ kvacid iṅgudī-phala-bhidaḥ sūcyanta evopalāḥ /
viśvāsopagamād abhinna-gatayaḥ śabdaṃ sahante mṛgās
toyādhāra-pathāś ca valkala-śikhā-niṣyanda-lekhāṅkitāḥ //ity ādau /
children.translated_text: 'Wild rice [grains], fallen from the hollows of trees that house parrots' eggs, [lie] below; here and there, smooth stones that crack open <s>iṅgudī</s> fruits are visible; deer, unhurried in their gait from trust [in the hermitage's safety], endure sounds; and the water-paths are marked with streaks of dripping from the tips of bark-garments.' And so forth.

children.text: dvitrāṇāṃ copasargāṇām ekatra pade yaḥ prayogaḥ so 'pi rasa-vyakty-anuguṇatayaiva nirdoṣaḥ / yathā-"prabhraśyaty uttarīya-tviṣi tamasi samudvīkṣya vītāvṛtīn drāg jantūn" ity ādau / yathā vā-"manuṣya-vṛttyā samupācarantam" ity ādau /
children.translated_text: And the employment of two or three prefixes together in a single word — that too is faultless precisely insofar as it accords with the manifestation of <s>rasa</s>. As in: 'When the splendor of the upper garment is falling away (<s>prabhraśyati</s>) in the darkness, having quickly looked up (<s>samudvīkṣya</s>) at the creatures that had lost their coverings...' and so forth. Or as in: 'Treating [him] according to human custom (<s>samupācarantam</s>)...' and so forth.

children.text: nipātānām api tathaiva / yathā-"aho batāsi spṛhaṇīya-vīryaḥ" ity ādau / yathā vā-
children.translated_text: The same applies to particles as well. As in: 'Aho! Alas! You are one whose prowess is enviable!' and so forth. Or as in—

children.text:
ye jīvanti na mānti ye sma vapuṣi prītyā pranṛtyanti ca
prasyandi-pramadāśravaḥ pulakitā dṛṣṭe guṇiny ūrjite /
hā dhik kaṣṭam aho kva yāmi śaraṇaṃ teṣāṃ janānāṃ kṛte
nītānāṃ pralayaṃ śaṭhena vidhinā sādhu-dviṣaḥ puṣyatā //ity ādau /
children.translated_text: 'Those who lived [for others], who did not take pride, who danced with delight on their bodies, whose tears of joy flowed freely, who bristled [with emotion] upon seeing a virtuous and mighty person — alas! Shame! How terrible! Where shall I seek refuge? For the sake of those people, brought to destruction by wicked fate that nourishes the enemies of the good!' And so forth.

children.text:
pada-paunaruktyaṃ ca vyañjakatvāpekṣayaiva kadācitprayujyamānaṃ śobhāmāvahati /
yathā-
yad vañcanāhita-matir bahu-cāṭu-garbhaṃ
kāryonmukhaḥ khala-janaḥ kṛtakaṃ bravīti /
tat sādhavo na na vidanti vidanti kintu
kartuṃ vṛthā-praṇayam asya na pārayanti //ity ādau /
children.translated_text: And the repetition of a word (<s>pada-paunaruktya</s>), when occasionally employed precisely with the intention of suggestive power, brings about beauty. As in: 'That which the wicked person, with deceitful intention, full of elaborate flattery, bent upon his purpose, speaks as a fabrication — good people do not not know it; they know it indeed — but they are unable to render his affection vain.' And so forth.

children.text: kālasya vyañjakatvaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: The suggestive power of tense (<s>kāla</s>) [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: sama-viṣama-nirviśeṣāḥ samantato manda-manda-sañcārāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The paths, without distinction of even and uneven, with slow, slow movement in every direction,

children.text: acirād bhaviṣyanti panthāno manorathānām api durlaṅghyāḥ //
children.translated_text: Will soon become impassable even for the chariots of desire.'

children.text: atra hy acirād bhaviṣyanti panthāna ity atra bhaviṣyantīty asmin pade pratyayaḥ kāla-viśeṣābhidhāyī rasa-paripoṣa-hetuḥ prakāśate / ayaṃ hi gāthārthaḥ pravāsa-vipralambha-śṛṅgāra-vibhāvatayā vibhāvyamāno rasavān / yathātra pratyayāṃśo vyañjakas tathā kvacit prakṛty-aṃśo 'pi dṛśyate / yathā-
children.translated_text: Here indeed, in 'the paths will soon become impassable,' the verbal suffix in the word 'will become' (<s>bhaviṣyanti</s>), which denotes a particular tense [future], is seen to be a cause for the nourishment of <s>rasa</s>. For the meaning of this verse, when apprehended as a <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) of the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> of separation during travel (<s>pravāsa-vipralambha</s>), is full of <s>rasa</s>. And just as here the suffix-portion is the suggestor, so in some cases the stem-portion (<s>prakṛty-aṃśa</s>) too is seen [as suggestor]. As in—

children.text: tad gehaṃ nata-bhitti mandiram idaṃ labdhāvagāhaṃ divaḥ
children.translated_text: 'That house with its bowing wall; this palace now accessible to the sky;

children.text: sā dhenur jaratī caranti kariṇām etā ghanābhā ghaṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: That cow, now old; these elephant-like dark water-pots that roam about;

children.text: sa kṣudro musala-dhvaniḥ kalam idaṃ saṅgītakaṃ yoṣitām
children.translated_text: That small pestle-sound; this singing of the women — such a melody!

children.text: āścaryaṃ divasair dvijo 'yam iyatīṃ bhūmiṃ samāropitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Marvelous — in [so few] days, this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has been raised to such heights!'

children.text: atra śloke divasair ity asmin pade prakṛty-aṃśo 'pi dyotakaḥ / sarva-nāmnāṃ ca vyañjakatvaṃ yathānantarokte śloke / atra ca sarva-nāmnām eva vyañjakatvaṃ hṛdi vyavasthāpya kavinā kvety-ādi-śabda-prayogo na kṛtaḥ / anayā diśā sahṛdayair anye 'pi vyañjaka-viśeṣāḥ svayam utprekṣaṇīyāḥ / etac ca sarvaṃ pada-vākya-racanā-dyotanoktyaiva gatārtham api vaicitryeṇa vyutpattaye punar-uktam /
children.translated_text: In this verse, in the word 'in [so few] days' (<s>divasaiḥ</s>), the stem-portion too is suggestive. And the suggestive power of all [types of] pronouns [is illustrated] as in the verse just cited. And here, having established in his heart the suggestive power of the pronouns themselves, the poet did not employ words like 'where' (<s>kva</s>) and the like. In this direction, sensitive readers (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) should themselves imagine further varieties of suggestors as well. And all of this, though already covered by the statement regarding word-, sentence-, and composition-level manifestation, has been restated with variety for the sake of [fuller] understanding.

children.text: nanu cārtha-sāmarthyākṣepyā rasādaya ity uktam, tathā ca subādīnāṃ vyañjakatva-vaicitrya-kathanam ananvitam eva / uktam atra padānāṃ vyañjakatvokty-avasare / kiṃ cārtha-viśeṣākṣepyatve 'pi rasādīnāṃ teṣām artha-viśeṣāṇāṃ vyañjaka-śabdāvinābhāvitvād yathā-pradarśitaṃ vyañjaka-svarūpa-parijñānaṃ vibhajyopayujyata eva / śabda-viśeṣāṇāṃ cānyatra ca cārutvaṃ yad vibhāgenopadarśitaṃ tad api teṣāṃ vyañjakatvenaivāvasthitam ity avagantavyam /
children.translated_text: Now, [the objection:] 'It was said that <s>rasas</s> and the like are evoked by the power of the meaning (<s>artha-sāmarthya</s>); accordingly, the discussion of the variety of suggestive power in nominal endings and the like is irrelevant.' This was addressed when the occasion arose for discussing the suggestive power of words. Moreover, even though <s>rasas</s> and the like are evoked by particular meanings, since those particular meanings are inseparable from their suggestive words, the understanding of the nature of the suggestor as demonstrated is indeed useful when applied analytically. And the charm of particular words that was shown elsewhere by analysis — that too should be understood as established precisely through their suggestive power.

children.text:
yatrāpi na tat sampratibhāsate tatrāpi vyañjake racanāntare yad adṛṣṭaṃ sauṣṭhavaṃ teṣāṃ pravāha-patitānāṃ tad evābhyāsād apoddhṛtānām apy avabhāsata ity avasātavyam / ko 'nyathā tulye vācakatve śabdānāṃ cārutva-viṣayo viśeṣaḥ syāt / anya evāsau sahṛdaya-saṃvedya iti cet, kim idaṃ sahṛdayatvaṃ nāma ? kiṃ rasa-bhāvānapekṣa-kāvyāśrita-samaya-viśeṣābhijñatvam, uta rasa-bhāvādi-maya-kāvya-svarūpa-parijñāna-naipuṇyam / pūrvasmin pakṣe tathāvidha-sahṛdaya-vyavasthāpitānāṃ śabda-viśeṣāṇāṃ cārutva-niyamo na syāt / punaḥ samayāntareṇānyathāpi vyavasthāpana-sambhavāt / dvitīyasmiṃs tu pakṣe rasajñataiva sahṛdayatvam iti / tathā-vidhaiḥ sahṛdayaiḥ saṃvedyo rasādi-samarpaṇa-sāmarthyam eva naisargikaṃ śabdānāṃ viśeṣa iti vyañjakatvāśrayy eva teṣāṃ mukhyaṃ cārutvam /
vācakatvāśrayāṇāṃ tu prasāda evārthāpekṣāyāṃ teṣāṃ viśeṣaḥ / arthānapekṣāyāṃ tv anuprāsādir eva || DhvA_3.15-16 ||
children.translated_text: Even where that [suggestive power] is not apparent, the excellence that is unseen in a particular arrangement — since [the words] are immersed in the flow [of the composition] — becomes apparent when those same [words] are extracted through repeated analysis. Otherwise, what distinction regarding charm would exist among words that have equal denotative power? If it be said that this [distinction] is something else, perceivable only by sensitive readers (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) — then what exactly is this 'sensitivity' (<s>sahṛdayatva</s>)? Is it familiarity with particular conventions residing in poetry independent of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>? Or is it expertise in the understanding of the true nature of poetry, which consists of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and the like? In the first case, the restriction of charm to particular words established by such sensitive readers would not hold, since re-establishment by a different convention is also possible. But in the second case, sensitivity is nothing other than connoisseurship of <s>rasa</s>. And the distinction of words, perceivable by such sensitive readers, is precisely the natural capacity for conveying <s>rasa</s> and the like — thus their primary charm rests on suggestive power alone. As for the distinction that resides in their denotative power — when meaning is relevant, that is merely perspicuity (<s>prasāda</s>); when meaning is not relevant, it is merely alliteration (<s>anuprāsa</s>) and the like. || <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Autocommentary 3.15-16 ||

children.text: evaṃ rasādīnāṃ vyañjaka-svarūpam abhidhāya teṣām eva virodhi-rūpaṃ lakṣayitum idam upakramyate-
children.translated_text: Having thus described the nature of the suggestors of <s>rasa</s> and the like, in order to characterize the forms that oppose them, this is now undertaken—
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.17:

children.text: prabandhe muktake vāpi rasādīn bandhum icchatā /
children.translated_text: In an extended work (<s>prabandha</s>) or in a standalone verse (<s>muktaka</s>), one who wishes to compose <s>rasas</s> and the like

children.text: yatnaḥ kāryaḥ sumatinā parihāre virodhinām // DhvK_3.17 //
children.translated_text: Should make great effort, with good judgment, to avoid what is antagonistic [to <s>rasa</s>]. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.17 //

children.text: prabandhe muktake vāpi rasa-bhāva-nibandhanaṃ pratyādṛta-manāḥ kavir virodhi-parihāre paraṃ yatnam ādadhīta / anyathā tv asya rasa-mayaḥ śloka eko 'pi samyaṅ na sampadyate // 3.17 //
children.translated_text: In an extended work or in a standalone verse, a poet whose mind is devoted to the composition of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s> should make the utmost effort to avoid what is antagonistic [to them]. Otherwise, not even a single verse pervaded by <s>rasa</s> will properly succeed for him. // 3.17 //

children.text: kāni punas tāni virodhīni yāni yatnataḥ kaveḥ parihartavyāni ? ity ucyate-
children.translated_text: Now, what are those antagonistic elements that the poet must carefully avoid? To this it is said—
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.18-19:

children.text: virodhi-rasa-sambandhi-vibhāvādi-parigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: The inclusion of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and the like that belong to an opposing <s>rasa</s>;

children.text: vistareṇānvitasyāpi vastuno 'nyasya varṇanam // DhvK_3.18 //
children.translated_text: The description at length of some other subject-matter, even if [syntactically] connected; // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.18 //

children.text: akāṇḍa eva vicchittir akāṇḍe ca prakāśanam /
children.translated_text: An abrupt interruption; and the illumination at an inopportune point;

children.text: paripoṣaṃ gatasyāpi paunaḥpunyena dīpanam /
children.translated_text: And the excessive highlighting, by repetition, even of [a <s>rasa</s>] that has reached fullness;

children.text: rasasya syād virodhāya vṛtty-anaucityam eva ca // DhvK_3.19 //
children.translated_text: And impropriety of style (<s>vṛtty-anaucitya</s>) — [all these] would be antagonistic to <s>rasa</s>. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.19 //

children.text: prastuta-rasāpekṣayā virodhī yo rasas tasya sambandhināṃ vibhāva-bhāvānubhāvānāṃ parigraho rasa-virodha-hetukaḥ sambhavanīyaḥ / tatra virodhi-rasa-vibhāva-parigraho yathā śānta-rasa-vibhāveṣu tad-vibhāvatayaiva nirūpiteṣv anantaram eva śṛṅgārādi-vibhāva-varṇane / virodhi-rasa-bhāva-parigraho yathā priyaṃ prati praṇaya-kalaha-kupitāsu kāminīṣu vairāgya-kathābhir anunaye / virodhi-rasānubhāva-parigraho yathā praṇaya-kupitāyāṃ priyāyām aprasīdantyāṃ nāyakasya kopāveśa-vivaśasya raudrānubhāva-varṇane /
children.translated_text: The adoption of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions), and <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) belonging to a <s>rasa</s> that is contradictory to the <s>rasa</s> at hand should be recognized as a cause of <s>rasa</s>-contradiction. Therein, the adoption of the <s>vibhāvas</s> of a contradictory <s>rasa</s> is [exemplified] when, after the <s>vibhāvas</s> of the <s>śānta-rasa</s> (tranquil sentiment) have been established in their capacity as such, the <s>vibhāvas</s> of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) and other [<s>rasas</s>] are described immediately afterward. The adoption of the <s>bhāvas</s> of a contradictory <s>rasa</s> is [exemplified] when, in consoling women angered by a love-quarrel toward their beloved, stories of renunciation are told. The adoption of the <s>anubhāvas</s> of a contradictory <s>rasa</s> is [exemplified] when, while the beloved is angered by love and remains displeased, the <s>anubhāvas</s> of the <s>raudra</s> (furious) [<s>rasa</s>] are described for the hero who is overcome by an onset of anger.

children.text: ayaṃ cānyo rasa-bhaṅga-hetur yat prastuta-rasāpekṣayā vastuno 'nyasya kathañcid anvitasyāpi vistareṇa kathanam / yathā vipralambha-śṛṅgāre nāyakasya kasyacid varṇayitum upakrānte kaver yamakādy-alaṅkāra-nibandhana-rasikatayā mahatā prabandhena parvatādi-varṇane / ayaṃ cāparo rasa-bhaṅga-hetur avagantavyo yad akāṇḍa eva vicchittiḥ rasasyākaṇḍa eva ca prakāśanam / tatrānavasare virāmo rasasya yathā nāyakasya kasyacit spṛhaṇīya-samāgamayā nāyikayā kayācit parāṃ paripoṣa-padavīṃ prāpte śṛṅgāre vidite ca parasparānurāge samāgamopāya-cintocitaṃ vyavahāram utsṛjya svatantratayā vyāpārāntara-varṇane / anavasare ca prakāśanaṃ rasasya yathā pravṛtte pravṛtta-vividha-vīra-saṅkṣaye kalpa-saṅkṣaya-kalpe saṅgrāme rāma-deva-prāyasyāpi tāvan nāyakasyānupakrānta-vipralambha-śṛṅgārasya nimittam ucitam antareṇaiva śṛṅgāra-kathāyām avatāra-varṇane / na caivaṃ-vidhe viṣaye daiva-vyāmohitatvaṃ kathā-puruṣasya parihāro yato rasa-bandha eva kaveḥ prādhānyena pravṛtti-nibandhanaṃ yuktam / itivṛtta-varṇanaṃ tad-upāya evety uktaṃ prāk "ālokārthi yathā dīpa-śikhāyāṃ yatnavān janaḥ" ity ādinā /
children.translated_text: And this is another cause of <s>rasa</s>-destruction (<s>rasa-bhaṅga</s>): the extended narration of some matter, however tangentially connected, that is extraneous to the <s>rasa</s> at hand. For example, when a poet has undertaken to depict a certain hero's <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation), [he causes <s>rasa</s>-destruction] by composing at great length a description of mountains and the like out of a relish for ornamental devices such as <s>yamaka</s> (alliterative repetition). And this further cause of <s>rasa</s>-destruction should be understood: the untimely interruption of a <s>rasa</s> and its untimely revelation. Therein, the interruption of a <s>rasa</s> at an inopportune moment is [exemplified] when, for a certain hero whose <s>śṛṅgāra</s> has reached the highest degree of development through a desirable union with some heroine, and whose mutual love is known, the poet abandons the narrative conduct appropriate to deliberation on the means of union and independently describes some other activity. And the revelation of a <s>rasa</s> at an inopportune moment is [exemplified] when, in an ongoing battle that is like the destruction at the end of a cosmic age, with its varied slaughter of engaged warriors, the depiction of a <s>śṛṅgāra</s>-narrative is introduced for a hero—even one as great as Lord <s>Rāma</s>—whose <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> has not yet been prepared, without any appropriate occasion. Nor in such a case is it a valid excuse that the character in the narrative was deluded by fate, since the poet's activity should be governed primarily by the arrangement of <s>rasa</s>. The narration of the story is merely a means to that [<s>rasa</s>-arrangement]—as was stated earlier with [the verse] 'Just as a person desiring light is diligent about the lamp-flame' and so forth.

children.text: ata eva cetivṛtta-mātra-varṇana-prādhānye 'ṅgāṅgi-bhāva-rahita-rasa-bhāva-nibandhena ca kavīnām evaṃ-vidhāni skhalitāni bhavantīti rasādi-rūpa-vyaṅgya-tātparyam evaiṣāṃ yuktam iti yatno 'smābhir ārabdho na dhvani-pratipādana-mātrābhiniveśena / punaś cāyam anyo rasa-bhaṅga-hetur avadhāraṇīyo yat paripoṣaṃ gatasyāpi rasasya paunaḥpunyena dīpanam / upabhukto hi rasaḥ sva-sāmagrī-labdha-paripoṣaḥ punaḥ punaḥ parāmṛśyamānaḥ parimlāna-kusuma-kalpaḥ kalpate / tathā vṛtter vyavahārasya yad anaucityaṃ tad api rasa-bhaṅga-hetur eva / yathā nāyakaṃ prati nāyikāyāḥ kasyāścid ucitāṃ bhaṅgim antareṇa svayaṃ sambhogābhilāṣa-kathane / yadi vā vṛttīnāṃ bharata-prasiddhānāṃ kaiśikyādīnāṃ kāvyālaṅkārāntara-prasiddhānām upanāgarikādyānāṃ vā yad anaucityam aviṣaye nibandhanaṃ tad api rasa-bhaṅga-hetuḥ / evam eṣāṃ rasa-virodhinām anyeṣāṃ cānayā diśā svayam utprekṣitānāṃ parihāre sat-kavibhir avahitair bhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: For this very reason—that in the predominance of mere story-narration, and in the composition of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s> devoid of the subordinate-dominant relationship (<s>aṅgāṅgi-bhāva</s>), such lapses occur among poets—the effort [shown] by us is aimed at [establishing] the primacy of the suggested content in the form of <s>rasa</s> and the rest, not out of mere insistence on demonstrating <s>dhvani</s>. And yet another cause of <s>rasa</s>-destruction must be noted: the repeated stimulation of a <s>rasa</s> that has already reached its fullness. For a <s>rasa</s> that has been savored, having attained its fullness through its proper components, when touched upon again and again becomes like a wilted flower. Similarly, impropriety of conduct or behavior is also a cause of <s>rasa</s>-destruction. For example, when a certain heroine directly expresses her desire for union to the hero without the appropriate coquetry. Or again, the impropriety of the <s>vṛttis</s> (styles) well-known from <s>Bharata</s>—<s>kaiśikī</s> and the rest—or of the <s>upanāgarika</s> and other [modes] well-known from other works on poetic ornament, when employed in an unsuitable domain, is also a cause of <s>rasa</s>-destruction. Thus, good poets should be vigilant in avoiding these and other <s>rasa</s>-contradictory [elements], as well as others that can be inferred by this method.

children.text: parikara-ślokāś cātra-
children.translated_text: And here are the supporting verses:

children.text: mukhyā vyāpāra-viṣayāḥ sukavīnāṃ rasādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For good poets, <s>rasa</s> and the rest are the primary objects of activity;

children.text: teṣām nibandhane bhāvye taiḥ sadaivāpramādibhiḥ //
children.translated_text: in their composition, [such poets] should always be vigilant.

children.text: nīrasas tu prabandho yaḥ so 'paśabdo mahān kaveḥ /
children.translated_text: A composition devoid of <s>rasa</s> is a great solecism of the poet;

children.text: sa tenākavir eva syād anyenāsmṛta-lakṣaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: by that alone he would be a non-poet, even if he has no other deficiency of definition.

children.text: pūrve viśṛṅkhala-giraḥ kavayaḥ prāpya-kīrtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Former poets of unrestrained speech [nevertheless] attained fame;

children.text: tān samāśritya na tyājyā nītir eṣā manīṣiṇā //
children.translated_text: relying on them, this principle should not be abandoned by the wise.

children.text:
vālmīki-vyāsa-mukhyāś ca ye prakhyātāḥ kavīśvarāḥ /
tad-abhiprāya-bāhyo 'yaṃ nāsmābhir darśito nayaḥ //iti// DhvA_3.19 //
children.translated_text: And the renowned lords of poets headed by <s>Vālmīki</s> and <s>Vyāsa</s>—the principle shown by us is not outside their intention. Thus [end the supporting verses].
[Verse] 3.20:

children.text: vivakṣite rase labdha-pratiṣṭhe tu virodhinām /
children.translated_text: When the intended <s>rasa</s> has been firmly established, however, the mention of contradictory [<s>rasas</s>] that are [either] suppressed

children.text: bādhyānām aṅga-bhāvaṃ vā prāptānām uktir acchalā // DhvK_3.20 //
children.translated_text: or that have attained subordinate status (<s>aṅga-bhāva</s>) is blameless.

children.text: sva-sāmagryā labdha-paripoṣe tu vivakṣite rase virodhināṃ virodhi-rasāṅgānāṃ bādhyānām aṅga-bhāvaṃ vā prāptānāṃ satām uktir adoṣā / bādhyatvaṃ hi virodhināṃ śakyābhibhavatve sati nānyathā / tathā ca teṣām uktiḥ prastuta-rasa-paripoṣāyaiva sampadyate / aṅga-bhāvaṃ prāptānāṃ ca teṣāṃ virodhitvam eva nivartate / aṅga-bhāva-prāptir hi teṣāṃ svābhāvikī samāropa-kṛtā vā / tatra yeṣāṃ naisargikī teṣāṃ tāvad uktāv avirodha eva / yathā vipralambha-śṛṅgāre tad-aṅgānāṃ vyādhy-ādīnāṃ teṣāṃ ca tad-aṅgānām evādoṣo nātad-aṅgānām / tad-aṅgatve ca sambhavaty api maraṇasyopanyāso na jyāyān / āśraya-vicchede rasasyātyanta-viccheda-prāpteḥ / karuṇasya tu tathā-vidhe viṣaye paripoṣo bhaviṣyatīti cet na ; yasyāprastutatvāt prastutasya ca vicchedāt / yatra tu karuṇa-rasasyaiva kāvyārthatvaṃ tatrāvirodhaḥ / śṛṅgāre vā maraṇasyādīrgha-kāla-pratyāpatti-sambhave kadācid upanibandho nātyanta-virodhī / dīrgha-kāla-pratyāpattau tu tasyāntarā pravāha-viccheda evety evaṃ-vidhetivṛttopanibandhanaṃ rasa-bandha-pradhānena kavinā parihartavyam /
children.translated_text: When the intended <s>rasa</s> has been firmly established through its proper components, the mention of contradictory <s>rasas</s>—whether they are in a suppressed state or have attained subordinate status—is free from fault. For the suppressibility of contradictory [<s>rasas</s>] obtains [only] when they can be overpowered, not otherwise. And thus, their mention serves precisely to enhance the <s>rasa</s> at hand. As for those that have attained subordinate status, their very contradictoriness ceases. For their attainment of subordinate status is either natural or imposed through attribution (<s>samāropa</s>). Of those whose [subordination] is innate, there is indeed no contradiction in their mention. For example, in <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation), illness and the like that are subordinate elements of that [<s>rasa</s>], and their own subordinate elements—there is no fault [in their mention], but not for elements that are not subordinate to it. Even when subordination is possible, the introduction of death is not desirable, since the complete cessation of the <s>rasa</s> results from the destruction of its locus (<s>āśraya</s>). If one objects that the <s>karuṇa-rasa</s> (pathetic sentiment) will flourish in such a domain—no; because it is not the [<s>rasa</s>] at hand, while the [<s>rasa</s>] at hand is cut off. But where the <s>karuṇa-rasa</s> itself is the subject of the poem, there is no contradiction. Or, in the case of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, the introduction of death may sometimes not be entirely contradictory when recovery after a short time is possible. But when recovery takes a long time, there is indeed an interruption of the flow in the interim—thus, a poet whose primary concern is <s>rasa</s>-arrangement should avoid such narrative construction.

children.text: tatra labdha-pratiṣṭhe tu vivakṣite rase virodhi-rasāṅgānāṃ bādhyatvenoktāv adoṣo yathā-
children.translated_text: Therein, when the intended <s>rasa</s> has been firmly established, there is no fault in mentioning the elements of a contradictory <s>rasa</s> in a suppressed state, as in—

children.text: kvākaryaṃ śaśa-lakṣmaṇaḥ kva ca kulaṃ bhūyo 'pi dṛśyeta sā
children.translated_text: 'Where [is my] dignity? Where the moon-marked one? Where my family? May she be seen once more!

children.text: doṣāṇāṃ praśamāya me śrutam aho kope 'pi kāntaṃ mukham /
children.translated_text: I have heard: for the pacification of faults—ah, even in anger, her face is lovely!

children.text: kiṃ vakṣyanty apakalmaṣāḥ kṛta-dhiyaḥ svapne 'pi sā durlabhā
children.translated_text: What will the faultless wise ones say? Even in a dream she is hard to obtain!

children.text: cetaḥ svāsthyam upaihi kaḥ khalu yuvā dhanyo 'dharaṃ pāsyati //
children.translated_text: O heart, be at peace! What fortunate youth will drink [from] her lip?'

children.text: yathā vā puṇḍarīkasya mahāśvetāṃ prati pravṛtta-nirbharānurāgasya dvitīya-muni-kumāropadeśa-varṇane / svābhāvikyām aṅga-bhāva-prāptāv adoṣo yathā-
children.translated_text: Or as in the depiction of the instruction by the second sage-youth, when <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>'s overflowing love for <s>Mahāśvetā</s> has already commenced. Where the attainment of subordinate status is natural, there is no fault, as in—

children.text:
bhramim aratim alasa-hṛdayatāṃ
pralayaṃ mūrcchāṃ tamaḥ śarīra-sādam /
maraṇaṃ ca jalada-bhujagajaṃ
prasahya kurute viṣaṃ viyoginīnām //ity ādau /
children.translated_text: 'Dizziness, restlessness, lethargy of heart, dissolution, fainting, darkness, bodily decline, and death—like [the venom of] a cloud-born serpent, the poison [of separation] forcibly inflicts [these] upon women in separation.' And so forth.

children.text: samāropitāyām apy avirodho yathā-"pāṇḍu-kṣāmam" ity ādau / iyaṃ cāṅga-bhāva-prāptir anyā yadādhikārikatvāt pradhāna ekasmin vākyārthe rasayor bhāvayor vā paraspara-virodhinor dvayor aṅga-bhāva-gamanaṃ tasyām api na doṣaḥ / yathoktaṃ "kṣipto hāstāvalagnaḥ" ity ādau / kathaṃ tatrāvirodha iti cet, dvayor api tayor anya-paratvena vyavasthānāt / anya-paratve 'pi virodhinoḥ kathaṃ virodha-nivṛttir iti cet, ucyate-vidhau viruddha-samāveśasya duṣṭatvaṃ nānuvāde / yathā-
children.translated_text: Even when [the subordination is] attributed, there is no contradiction, as in [the verse beginning] '<s>pāṇḍu-kṣāmam</s>' (pale and emaciated) and so forth. And there is another kind of attainment of subordinate status: when, due to the narrative requirement, two mutually contradictory <s>rasas</s> or <s>bhāvas</s> attain subordinate status while one sentence-meaning is primary—even in that case there is no fault. As stated in [the verse beginning] 'Thrown [aside yet] clinging to the hand' and so forth. If one asks how there is no contradiction there—it is because both are established as having another [meaning] as their purpose. If one further asks how the contradiction ceases when both [<s>rasas</s>], though having another purpose, are contradictory—the answer is: the co-presence of contradictories is faulty in an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) but not in a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>). As in—

children.text:
ehi gaccha patottiṣṭha vada maunaṃ samācara /
evam āśā-graha-grastaiḥ krīḍanti dhanino 'rthibhiḥ //ity ādau /
children.translated_text: 'Come! Go! Fall! Get up! Speak! Observe silence!'—thus do the wealthy sport with supplicants seized by the demon of hope.' And so forth.

children.text: atra hi vidhi-pratiṣedhayor anūdyamānatvena samāveśe na virodhas tathehāpi bhaviṣyati / śloke hy asminn īrṣyā-vipralambha-śṛṅgāra-karuṇa-vastunor na vidhīyamānatvam / tripura-ripu-prabhāvātiśayasya vākyārthatvāt tad-aṅgatvena ca tayor vyavasthānāt /
children.translated_text: For here, since the injunction and prohibition are [merely] being restated, there is no contradiction in their co-presence; so too it will be in this [verse under discussion]. For in this verse, the subject-matter of <s>īrṣyā</s> (jealousy), <s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-separation), and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos) is not being enjoined. Since the surpassing power of the enemy of <s>Tripura</s> [i.e., <s>Śiva</s>] is the sentence-meaning, and since those [<s>rasas</s>] are established as subordinate to that—

children.text:
na ca raseṣu vidhy-anuvāda-vyavahāro nāstīti śakyaṃ vaktum, teṣāṃ vākyārthatvenābhyupagamāt / vākyārthasya vācyasya ca yau vidhy-anuvādau tau tad-ākṣiptānāṃ rasānāṃ kena vāryate / yair vā sākṣāt-kāvyārthatā rasādīnāṃ nābhyupagamyate, tais teṣāṃ tan-nimittatā tāvad avaśyam abhyupagantavyā / tathāpy atra śloke na virodhaḥ /
yasmād anūdyamānāṅga-nimittobhaya-rasa-vastu-sahakāriṇo vidhīyamānāṃśād bhāva-viśeṣa-pratītir utpadyate tataś ca na kaścid virodhaḥ / dṛśyate hi viruddhobhaya-sahakāriṇaḥ kāraṇāt kārya-viśeṣotpattiḥ / viruddha-phalotpādana-hetutvaṃ hi yugapad ekasya kāraṇasya viruddhaṃ na tu viruddhobhaya-sahakāritvam / evaṃ-vidha-viruddha-padārtha-viṣayaḥ katham abhinayaḥ prayoktavya iti cet, anūdyamānaivaṃ-vidha-vācya-viṣaye yā vārtā sātrāpi bhaviṣyati / evaṃ-vidhy-anuvādanayāśrayeṇātra śloke parihṛtas tāvad virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor can it be said that the usage of injunction and restatement does not apply to <s>rasas</s>, since they are accepted as sentence-meanings. Whatever injunction and restatement pertain to the expressed sentence-meaning, who can prevent [these from applying to] the <s>rasas</s> implied by that [meaning]? Or for those who do not accept that <s>rasa</s> and the rest are directly the meaning of poetry, they must at least accept that [<s>rasas</s>] are occasioned by [the expressed meaning]. Even so, there is no contradiction in this verse. For from the element being restated—the subordinate occasion for both <s>rasa</s>-subjects—taken together with the element being enjoined, a specific apprehension of emotion arises, and hence there is no contradiction. For it is observed that from a cause aided by both contradictory [factors], a specific effect arises. For it is contradictory for a single cause to simultaneously produce contradictory results, but not for it to be aided by both contradictory [factors]. If one asks how enactment (<s>abhinaya</s>) should be performed in such a domain of contradictory elements—whatever applies in such a domain of restated expressed meaning will apply here too. Thus, by resort to the method of injunction-and-restatement, the contradiction has been resolved in this verse.

children.text: kiṃ ca nāyakasyābhinandanīyodayasya kasyacit prabhāvātiśaya-varṇane tat-pratipakṣāṇāṃ yaḥ karuṇo rasaḥ sa parīkṣakāṇāṃ na vaiklavyam ādadhāti pratyuta prīty-atiśaya-nimittatāṃ pratipadyata ity atas tasya kuṇṭha-śaktikatvāt tad-virodha-vidhāyino na kaścid doṣaḥ / tasmād vākyārthī-bhūtasya rasasya bhāvasya vā virodhī rasa-virodhīti vaktuṃ nyāyyaḥ, na tv aṅga-bhūtasya kasyacit /
children.translated_text: Moreover, when the surpassing power of a certain hero whose rise is to be celebrated is being described, the <s>karuṇa-rasa</s> concerning his adversaries does not produce distress in discerning [audiences]; rather, it comes to serve as a cause of heightened delight. Therefore, since the power of that [contradictory <s>rasa</s>] is blunted, there is no fault in that which occasions its contradiction. Hence it is proper to call a <s>rasa</s> or <s>bhāva</s> contradictory to a <s>rasa</s> [only] when it is the sentence-meaning, but not when it is subordinate.

children.text: athavā vākyārthī-bhūtasyāpi kasyacit karuṇa-rasa-viṣayasya tādṛśena śṛṅgāra-vastunā bhaṅgi-viśeṣāśrayeṇa saṃyojanaṃ rasa-paripoṣāyaiva jāyate / yataḥ prakṛti-madhurāḥ padārthāḥ śocanīyatāṃ prāptāḥ prāg-avasthā-bhāvibhiḥ saṃsmaryamāṇair vilāsair adhikataraṃ śokāveśam upajanayanti / yathā-
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, even for some [<s>rasa</s>] that has become the sentence-meaning—a subject of <s>karuṇa-rasa</s>—its combination with such <s>śṛṅgāra</s>-material, through a particular mode of presentation, serves precisely to enhance the <s>rasa</s>. For objects that are naturally sweet, when they have come to a pitiable state, evoke a still greater rush of grief when one remembers the graces [they displayed] in their former condition. As in—

children.text:
ayaṃ sa raśanotkarṣī pīna-stana-vimardanaḥ /
nābhyūru-jaghana-sparśī nīvī-visraṃsanaḥ karaḥ //ity ādau /
children.translated_text: 'This is that very hand—the one that pulled at the girdle, that pressed the full breasts, that touched the navel, thigh, and hips, that loosened the waist-band.' And so forth.

children.text: tad atra tripura-yuvatīnāṃ śāmbhavaḥ śarāgnir ārdrāparādhaḥ kāmī yathā vyavaharati sma / tathā vyavahṛtavān ity anenāpi prakāreṇāsty eva nirvirodhatvam / tasmād yathā yathā nirūpyate tathā tathātra doṣābhāvaḥ / itthaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Therefore, in this [verse about the <s>Tripura</s> maidens], <s>Śambhu</s>'s arrow-fire behaved toward them as a lover guilty of a tender offense. [Since] he acted in that manner—by this mode too there is indeed no contradiction. Therefore, the more closely one examines, the more one finds the absence of fault here. And thus—

children.text: krāmantyaḥ kṣata-komalāṅguli-galad-raktaiḥ sadarbhāḥ sthalīḥ
children.translated_text: Walking over ground strewn with <s>darbha</s> grass, with feet [dripping blood] from wounded tender toes

children.text: pādaiḥ pātita-yāvakair iva patad-bāṣpāmbu-dhautānanāḥ /
children.translated_text: as if [stained with] fallen lac-dye, their faces washed by falling tears,

children.text: bhītā bhartṛ-karāvalambita-karās tvad-vairi-nātho 'dhunā
children.translated_text: frightened, with hands held by their husbands' hands—your enemy's lord's [wives] now

children.text: dāvāgniṃ parito bhramanti punar apy udyad-vivāhā iva //
children.translated_text: wander around the forest fire, looking once again as if [performing] a wedding [circumambulation].

children.text: ity evam ādīnāṃ sarveṣām eva nirvirodhatvam avagantavyam / evaṃ tāvad rasādīnāṃ virodhi-rasādibhiḥ samāveśāsamāveśayor viṣaya-vibhāgo darśitaḥ || DhvA_3.20 ||
children.translated_text: The freedom from contradiction in all [verses] such as this and the like should be understood [in the same way]. Thus, the division of domains regarding the co-presence and non-co-presence of <s>rasa</s> and the rest with contradictory <s>rasas</s> and the rest has been shown.

children.text: idānīṃ teṣām eka-prabandha-viniveśane nyāyyo yaḥ kramas taṃ pratipādayitum ucyate-
children.translated_text: Now, to establish the proper sequence for arranging these [<s>rasas</s>] in a single composition, this is said—
[Verse] 3.21:

children.text: prasiddhe 'pi prabandhānāṃ nānā-rasa-nibandhane /
children.translated_text: Even though it is well-known that compositions employ multiple <s>rasas</s>,

children.text: eko raso 'ṅgīkartavyas teṣām utkarṣam icchatā // DhvK_3.21 //
children.translated_text: one who desires their excellence should adopt one [dominant] <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: prabandheṣu mahākāvyādiṣu nāṭakādiṣu vā viprakīrṇatayāṅgāṅgi-bhāvena bahavo rasā upanibadhyanta ity atra prasiddhau satyām api yaḥ prabandhānāṃ chāyātiśaya-yogam icchati tena teṣāṃ rasānām anyatamaḥ kaścid vivakṣito raso 'ṅgitvena viniveśayitavya ity ayaṃ yuktataro mārgaḥ || DhvA_3.21 ||
children.translated_text: In extended compositions — whether <s>mahākāvyas</s> (great poems) or <s>nāṭakas</s> (dramas) — it is well known that many <s>rasas</s> are composed in a scattered manner through the relationship of subordinate and predominant. Nevertheless, whoever wishes for excellence of aesthetic quality in compositions should arrange one particular intended <s>rasa</s> as predominant — this is the more appropriate path. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.21]

children.text: nanu rasāntareṣu bahuṣu prāpta-paripoṣeṣu satsu katham ekasyāṅgitā na virudhyata ity āśaṅkyedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Objection: When many other <s>rasas</s> have been fully developed, how is the predominance of one not contradicted? Anticipating this doubt, it is said:
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.22:]

children.text: rasāntara-samāveśaḥ prastutasya rasasya yaḥ /
children.translated_text: The inclusion of other <s>rasas</s> alongside the principal <s>rasa</s>

children.text: nopahanty aṅgitāṃ so 'sya sthāyitvenāvabhāsinaḥ // DhvK_3.22 //
children.translated_text: Does not impair the predominance of that [<s>rasa</s>] which shines forth as the permanent [emotional state]. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.22]

children.text: prabandheṣu prathamataraṃ prastutaḥ san punaḥ punar anusandhīyamānatvena sthāyī yo rasas tasya sakala-bandha-vyāpino rasāntarair antarāla-vartibhiḥ samāveśo yaḥ sa nāṅgitām upahanti || DhvA_3.22 ||
children.translated_text: In compositions, the <s>rasa</s> that was introduced first and is permanent by virtue of being repeatedly traced throughout — the inclusion of other <s>rasas</s> occurring in the intervals alongside that [<s>rasa</s>] which pervades the entire work does not impair its predominance. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.22]

children.text: etad evopapādayitum ucyate-
children.translated_text: To establish this very point, it is said:
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.23:]

children.text: kāryam ekaṃ yathā vyāpi prabandhasya vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Just as one pervasive plot-purpose is ordained for a composition,

children.text: tathā rasasyāpi vidhau virodho naiva vidyate // DhvK_3.23 //
children.translated_text: So too in the arrangement of a [single] <s>rasa</s>, there is indeed no contradiction. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.23]

children.text: sandhyādi-mayasya prabandha-śarīrasya yathā kāryam ekam anuyāyi vyāpakaṃ kalpyate na ca tat-kāryāntarair na saṅkīryate, na ca taiḥ saṅkīryamāṇasyāpi tasya prādhānyam apacīyate, tathaiva rasasyāpy ekasya sanniveśe kriyamāṇe virodho na kaścit / pratyuta pratyudita-vivekānām anusandhānavatāṃ sa-cetasāṃ tathā-vidhe viṣaye prahlādātiśayaḥ pravartate || DhvA_3.23 ||
children.translated_text: Just as for the body of a composition consisting of junctures (<s>sandhi</s>) etc., one pervasive plot-purpose is conceived as accompanying [the whole], and it is not confused by other sub-plots, and even when intermingled with them its predominance is not diminished — in exactly the same way, when one <s>rasa</s> is arranged [as predominant], there is no contradiction whatsoever. On the contrary, for sensitive persons (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) of awakened discernment who maintain continuous attention, an excess of delight arises in such a subject. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.23]

children.text: nanu yeṣāṃ rasānāṃ parasparāvirodhaḥ yathā-vīra-śṛṅgārayoḥ śṛṅgāra-hāsyayo raudra-śṛṅgārayor vīrādbhutayor vīra-raudrayo raudra-karuṇayoḥ śṛṅgārādbhutayor vā tatra bhavatv aṅgāṅgi-bhāvaḥ / teṣāṃ tu sa kathaṃ bhaved yeṣāṃ parasparaṃ bādhya-bādhaka-bhāvaḥ ? yathā-śṛṅgāra-bībhatsayor vīra-bhayānakayoḥ śānta-raudrayoḥ śanta-śṛṅgārayor vā ity āśaṅkyedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Objection: For those <s>rasas</s> that are mutually compatible — such as the heroic (<s>vīra</s>) and erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>), the erotic and comic (<s>hāsya</s>), the furious (<s>raudra</s>) and erotic, the heroic and marvelous (<s>adbhuta</s>), the heroic and furious, the furious and pathetic (<s>karuṇa</s>), or the erotic and marvelous — let there be a subordinate-predominant relationship. But how can that exist for those that mutually obstruct each other? Such as the erotic and disgusting (<s>bībhatsa</s>), the heroic and fearful (<s>bhayānaka</s>), the tranquil (<s>śānta</s>) and furious, or the tranquil and erotic? Anticipating this doubt, it is said:
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.24:]

children.text: avirodhī virodhī vā raso 'ṅgini rasāntare /
children.translated_text: Whether compatible or incompatible, a <s>rasa</s> alongside the predominant <s>rasa</s>

children.text: paripoṣaṃ na netavyas tathā syād avirodhitā // DhvK_3.24 //
children.translated_text: Should not be brought to full development — thus there will be no conflict. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.24]

children.text: aṅgini rasāntare śṛṅgārādau prabandha-vyaṅgye sati avirodhī virodhī vā rasaḥ paripoṣaṃ na netavyaḥ / tatrāvirodhino rasasyāṅgi-rasāpekṣayāty antam ādhikyaṃ na kartavyam ity ayaṃ prathamaḥ paripoṣa-parihāraḥ / utkarṣa-sāmye 'pi tayor virodhāsambhavāt / yathā-
children.translated_text: When another <s>rasa</s> such as <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is the predominant [<s>rasa</s>] suggested by the composition, a compatible or incompatible <s>rasa</s> should not be brought to full development. The first way of avoiding full development is this: a compatible <s>rasa</s> should not be made excessively [prominent] relative to the predominant <s>rasa</s>. For when both are equal in intensity, conflict does not arise since they are compatible. As in:

children.text:
ekato roditi priyā anyataḥ samara-tūrya-nirghoṣaḥ /
snehena raṇa-rasena ca bhaṭasya dolāyitaṃ hṛdayam /
children.translated_text: On one side weeps the beloved, on the other resounds the battle-drum; with love and with the relish of battle, the warrior's heart swings like a pendulum.

children.text: yathā vā-
children.translated_text: Or as [in the following]:

children.text:
kaṇṭhāc chitvākṣamālāvalayam iva kare hāram āvartayantī
kṛtvā paryaṅka-bandhaṃ viṣadhara-patinā mekhalāyā guṇena /
mithyā-mantrābhijāpasphurad-adhara-puṭa-vyañjitāvyakta-hāsā
devī sandhyābhyasūyā hasita-paśupatis tatra dṛṣṭā tu vo 'vyāt //ity atra /
children.translated_text: Cutting from her neck the rosary and winding it around her hand like a bracelet, having fashioned a cross-legged posture with the cord of her girdle — [the cord] of the lord of serpents — with lip-folds quivering as she mutters feigned mantras, revealing an indistinct smile, <s>Devī</s> was seen there while <s>Paśupati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) laughed, suspecting the jealousy of twilight — may she protect you!

children.text: aṅgirasa-viruddhānāṃ vyabhicāriṇāṃ prācuryeṇāniveśanam, niveśane vā kṣipram evāṅgirasa-vyabhicāry-anuvṛttir iti dvitīyaḥ / aṅgatvena punaḥ punaḥ pratyavekṣā paripoṣaṃ nīyamānasyāpy aṅga-bhūtasya rasasyeti tṛtīyaḥ / anayā diśānye 'pi prakārā utprekṣaṇīyāḥ / virodhinas tu rasasyāṅgirasāpekṣayā kasyacin nyūnatā sampādanīyā / yathā śānte 'ṅgini śṛṅgārasya śṛṅgāre vā śāntasya / paripoṣa-rahitasya rasasya kathaṃ rasatvam iti cet-uktam atrāṅgirasāpekṣayeti / aṅgino hi rasasya yāvān paripoṣas tāvāṃs tasya na kartavyaḥ, svatas tu sambhavī paripoṣaḥ kena vāryate / etac cāpekṣikaṃ prakarṣa-yogitvam ekasya rasasya bahu-raseṣu prabandheṣu rasānām aṅgāṅgi-bhāvam anabhyupagacchatāpy aśakya-pratikṣepam ity anena prakāreṇāvirodhināṃ virodhināṃ ca rasānām aṅgāṅgi-bhāvena samāveśe prabandheṣu syād avirodhaḥ / etac ca sarvaṃ yeṣāṃ raso rasāntarasya vyabhicārī bhavati iti darśanaṃ tan-matenocyate / matāntare 'pi rasānāṃ sthāyino bhāvā upacārād rasa-śabdenoktās teṣām aṅgatvaṃ nirvirodham eva || DhvA_3.24 ||
children.translated_text: The second [method] is: the transitory emotions (<s>vyabhicārin</s>) that conflict with the predominant <s>rasa</s> should not be abundantly employed; or, if employed, the transitory emotions belonging to the predominant <s>rasa</s> should quickly follow. The third is: even when a subordinate <s>rasa</s> is being fully developed, repeated reversion to the predominant <s>rasa</s>, [viewing the subordinate] as subordinate. Other methods too may be imagined along these lines. For an incompatible <s>rasa</s>, however, some inferiority relative to the predominant <s>rasa</s> must be arranged — as for the tranquil (<s>śānta</s>) when <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is predominant, or for <s>śṛṅgāra</s> when the tranquil is predominant. If asked how an undeveloped <s>rasa</s> can be a <s>rasa</s> at all: the answer has been given — 'relative to the predominant <s>rasa</s>.' The development of the predominant <s>rasa</s> is not to be matched [by the subordinate]; but spontaneous development cannot be prevented by anyone. And this relative superiority of one <s>rasa</s> in multi-<s>rasa</s> compositions cannot be rejected even by those who do not accept the subordinate-predominant relationship among <s>rasas</s>. In this way, the co-existence of both compatible and incompatible <s>rasas</s> in compositions through the subordinate-predominant relationship is without conflict. All this is stated according to those who hold that a <s>rasa</s> can become the <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) of another <s>rasa</s>. In another view too, the permanent emotional states (<s>sthāyin</s>) of <s>rasas</s>, metaphorically called <s>rasas</s>, can unproblematically be subordinate. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.24]

children.text: evam avirodhināṃ virodhināṃ ca prabandha-sthenāṅginā rasena samāveśe sādhāraṇam avirodhopāyaṃ pratipādyedānīṃ virodhi-viṣayam eva taṃ pratipādayitum idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Having thus set forth the general method of resolving conflict in the co-existence of compatible and incompatible [<s>rasas</s>] with a predominant <s>rasa</s> pervading the composition, now, to set forth that [method] specifically for incompatible [<s>rasas</s>], this is said:
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.25:]

children.text: viruddhaikāśrayo yas tu virodhī sthāyino bhavet /
children.translated_text: An incompatible [<s>rasa</s>] that, sharing one locus with the permanent [<s>rasa</s>], would be in conflict —

children.text: sa vibhinnāśrayaḥ kāryas tasya poṣe 'py adoṣatā // DhvK_3.25 //
children.translated_text: That should be assigned a different locus; even in its full development, there is no fault. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.25]

children.text: ekādhikaraṇy avirodhī nairantarya-virodhī ceti dvividho virodhī / tatra prabandha-sthena sthāyināṅginā rasenaucityāpekṣayā viruddhaikāśrayo yo virodhī yathā vīreṇa bhayānakaḥ sa vibhinnāśrayaḥ kāryaḥ / tasya vīrasya ya āśrayaḥ kathānāyakas tad-vipakṣa-viṣaye sanniveśayitavyaḥ / tathā sati ca tasya virodhino 'pi yaḥ paripoṣaḥ sa nirdoṣaḥ / vipakṣa-viṣaye hi bhayātiśaya-varṇane nāyakasya naya-parākramādi-sampat sutarām uddyotitā bhavati / etac ca madīye 'rjuna-carite 'rjunasya pātālāvataraṇa-prasaṅge vaiśadyena pradarśitam /
children.translated_text: The incompatible [<s>rasa</s>] is of two kinds: one sharing the same locus (<s>ekādhikaraṇya</s>), and one conflicting in contiguity (<s>nairantarya</s>). Of these, the incompatible [<s>rasa</s>] that shares one locus with the permanent, predominant <s>rasa</s> pervading the composition — in view of propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) — such as <s>bhayānaka</s> (the fearful) alongside <s>vīra</s> (the heroic): that should be assigned a different locus. That is, it should be placed in the adversary of the hero who is the locus of the heroic <s>rasa</s>. When this is done, even the full development of that incompatible [<s>rasa</s>] is without fault. For the portrayal of extreme fear in the adversary makes the hero's own qualities of strategy and valor shine forth all the more. This has been shown in detail in my own <s>Arjunacarita</s>, in the episode of <s>Arjuna</s>'s descent to the netherworld.

children.text: evam aikādhikaraṇya-virodhinaḥ prabandha-sthena sthāyinā rasenāṅga-bhāva-gamane nirvirodhatvaṃ yathā tathā tad darśitam / dvitīyasya tu tat pratipādayitum ucyate-
children.translated_text: Thus it has been shown how the incompatible [<s>rasa</s>] that conflicts through sharing one locus can, without conflict, assume subordinate status alongside the permanent <s>rasa</s> pervading the composition. To set forth [the resolution for] the second type, it is said:
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.26:]

children.text: ekāśrayatve nirdoṣo nairantarye virodhavān /
children.translated_text: That which is faultless when sharing one locus but conflicts in contiguity —

children.text: rasāntara-vyavadhinā raso vyaṅgyaḥ sumedhasā // DhvK_3.26 //
children.translated_text: Such a <s>rasa</s>, if suggested, should be [placed with] an intervening other <s>rasa</s>, by the wise poet. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.26]

children.text: yaḥ punar ekādhikaraṇatve nirvirodho nairantarye tu virodhī sa rasāntara-vyavadhānena prabandhe niveśayitavyaḥ / yathā śānta-śṛṅgārau nāgānande niveśitau / śāntaś ca tṛṣṇā-kṣaya-sukhasya yaḥ paripoṣas tal-lakṣaṇo rasaḥ pratīyata eva / tathā coktam-
children.translated_text: That which is without conflict when sharing one locus but conflicts in contiguity — that should be placed in the composition with another <s>rasa</s> intervening. As the tranquil (<s>śānta</s>) and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> have been placed in the <s>Nāgānanda</s> [of <s>Harṣadeva</s>]. And the <s>śānta rasa</s>, whose defining feature is the full development of the joy of the extinction of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā-kṣaya-sukha</s>), is indeed perceived as a <s>rasa</s>. As it is said:

children.text: yac ca kāma-sukhaṃ loke yac ca divyaṃ mahat sukham /
children.translated_text: Whatever is the pleasure of desire in the world, and whatever is the great celestial pleasure —

children.text: tṛṣṇākṣaya-sukhasyaite nārhataḥ ṣoḍaśīṃ kalām //
children.translated_text: These are not worth a sixteenth part of the happiness of the extinction of craving.

children.text:
yadi nāma sarva-janānubhava-gocaratā tasya nāsti naitāvatāsāv aloka-sāmānya-mahānubhāva-citta-vṛtti-viśeṣaḥ pratikṣeptuṃ śakyaḥ / na ca vīre tasyāntar-bhāvaḥ kartuṃ yuktaḥ / tasyābhimāna-mayatvena vyavasthāpanāt / asya cāhaṅkāra-praśamaika-rūpatayā sthiteḥ / tayoś caivaṃ-vidha-viśeṣa-sadbhāve 'pi yady aikyaṃ parikalpyate tad vīra-raudrayor api tathā prasaṅgaḥ / dayā-vīrādīnāṃ ca citta-vṛtti-viśeṣāṇāṃ sarvākāram ahaṅkāra-rahitatvena śānta-rasa-prabhedatvam, itarathā tu vīra-prabhedatvam iti vyavasthāpyamāne na kaścid virodhaḥ /
tad evam asti śānto rasaḥ / tasya cāviruddha-rasa-vyavadhānena prabandhe virodhi-rasa-samāveśe saty api nirvirodhatvam / yathā pradarśite viṣaye || DhvA_3.26 ||
children.translated_text: Even if that [happiness] is not within the experience of all people, this much cannot be rejected: that it is a special mental state of great persons who are not of ordinary [worldly] nature. Nor is it proper to subsume it under the heroic (<s>vīra</s>), since that [heroic <s>rasa</s>] has been established as consisting of pride (<s>abhimāna</s>), while this [tranquil <s>rasa</s>] abides in the very form of the subsidence of ego (<s>ahaṅkāra-praśama</s>). And even though such specific differences exist between them, if their identity is imagined, then the same [problem] would arise for the heroic and the furious (<s>raudra</s>) as well. When it is established that mental states such as compassion-based heroism (<s>dayā-vīra</s>) etc. are varieties of the <s>śānta rasa</s> insofar as they are entirely devoid of ego, and varieties of the heroic otherwise — there is no contradiction whatsoever. Thus, the <s>śānta rasa</s> exists. And its co-existence with an incompatible <s>rasa</s> in a composition, when separated by a compatible <s>rasa</s> intervening, is without conflict — as shown in the example given. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.26]

children.text: etad eva sthirī-kartum idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: To confirm this very point, it is said:
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.27:]

children.text: rasāntarāntaritayor eka-vākya-sthayor api /
children.translated_text: Even when two [<s>rasas</s>] separated by another <s>rasa</s> are within the same sentence,

children.text: nivartate hi rasayoḥ samāveśe virodhitā // DhvK_3.27 //
children.translated_text: The conflict between them ceases when they are [thus] combined. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.27]

children.text:
rasāntara-vyavahitayor eka-prabandha-sthayor virodhitā nivartata ity atra na kācid bhrāntiḥ /
yasmād eka-vākya-sthayor api rasayor uktayā nītyā viruddhatā nivartate / yathā-
children.translated_text: That the conflict of two [<s>rasas</s>] separated by another <s>rasa</s> within the same composition ceases — in this there is no doubt. For even when they are within the same sentence, their conflict ceases by the method described. As in:

children.text: bhū-reṇu-digdhān nava-pārijāta-
children.translated_text: Their bodies smeared with the dust of the earth, their waists perfumed

children.text: mālā-rajo-vāsita-bāhu-madhyāḥ /
children.translated_text: By the pollen of garlands of fresh <s>pārijāta</s> flowers,

children.text: gāḍhaṃ śivābhiḥ parirabhyamāṇān
children.translated_text: Tightly embraced by their consorts (<s>śivā</s>),

children.text: surāṅganāśliṣṭa-bhujān tarālāḥ //
children.translated_text: Their arms clasped by celestial women — glittering [warriors]!

children.text: sa-śoṇitaiḥ kravya-bhujāṃ sphuradbhiḥ
children.translated_text: Fanned by the blood-stained, quivering wings

children.text: pakṣaiḥ khagānām u pavījyamānān /
children.translated_text: Of the birds that feast on flesh,

children.text: saṃvījitāś candana-vāri-sekaiḥ
children.translated_text: And [also] fanned with sprinklings of sandalwood water

children.text: sugandhibhiḥ kalpa-latā-dukūlaiḥ //
children.translated_text: And fragrant garments of wish-fulfilling creepers —

children.text:
vimāna-paryaṅka-tale niṣaṇṇāḥ
kutūhalāviṣṭatayā tadānīm /
nirdiśyamānāṃ lalanāṅgulībhir
vīrāḥ sva-dehān patitān apaśyan //ity ādau /
children.translated_text: Seated on the couches of celestial chariots, filled with wonder at that moment, as their fallen bodies were being pointed out by the fingers of women — [such] heroes beheld [their own bodies]! And so forth.

children.text: atra hi śṛṅgāra-bībhatsayos tad-aṅgayor vā vīra-rasa-vyavadhānena samāveśo na virodhī /
children.translated_text: Here, the co-existence of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) and <s>bībhatsa</s> (the disgusting), or of their subordinate components, separated by the <s>vīra rasa</s> (the heroic), is without conflict.
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.28:]

children.text: virodham avirodhaṃ ca sarvatretthaṃ nirūpayet /
children.translated_text: One should examine conflict and non-conflict in this manner everywhere;

children.text: viśeṣatas tu śṛṅgāre sukumāratamā hy asau // DhvK_3.28 //
children.translated_text: But especially in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, for it is the most delicate of all. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.28]

children.text: yathokta-lakṣaṇānusāreṇa virodhāvirodhau sarveṣu raseṣu prabandhe 'nyatra ca nirūpayet sahṛdayaḥ; viśeṣatas tu śṛṅgāre / sa hi rati-paripoṣātmakatvād rateś ca svalpenāpi nimittena bhaṅga-sambhavāt sukumāratamaḥ sarvebhyo rasebhyo manāg api virodhi-samāveśaṃ na sahate /
children.translated_text: The sensitive person should examine conflict and non-conflict following the criteria described, in all <s>rasas</s>, whether in compositions or elsewhere; but especially in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. For since it consists in the full development of <s>rati</s> (love), and since <s>rati</s> is susceptible to disruption by even the slightest cause, it is the most delicate of all <s>rasas</s> and does not tolerate even a slight admixture of a conflicting [<s>rasa</s>].
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.29:]

children.text: avadhānātiśayavān rase tatraiva sat-kaviḥ /
children.translated_text: The good poet should be exceedingly attentive to that very <s>rasa</s> [<s>śṛṅgāra</s>];

children.text: bhavet tasmin pramādo hi jhaṭity evopalakṣyate // DhvK_3.29 //
children.translated_text: For negligence in it is immediately perceived. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.29]

children.text: tatraiva ca rase sarvebhyo 'pi rasebhyaḥ saukumāryātiśaya-yogini kavir avadhānavān prayatnavān syāt / tatra hi pramādyatas tasya sahṛdaya-madhye kṣipram evāvajñāna-viṣayatā bhavati / śṛṅgāra-raso hi saṃsāriṇāṃ niyamenānubhava-viṣayatvāt sarva-rasebhyaḥ kamanīyatayā pradhāna-bhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The poet should be attentive and careful regarding that very <s>rasa</s> which, among all <s>rasas</s>, possesses the greatest delicacy. For when he is negligent in it, he quickly becomes an object of contempt among the sensitive (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). For the <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s>, being invariably within the experience of worldly beings, is the most preeminent among all <s>rasas</s> by virtue of its loveliness.

children.text: evaṃ ca sati-
children.translated_text: This being so:
[<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.30:]

children.text: vineyān unmukhī-kartuṃ kāvya-śobhārtham eva vā /
children.translated_text: To make the audience receptive, or for the sake of the beauty of the poem itself,

children.text: tad-viruddha-rasa-sparśas tad-aṅgānāṃ na duṣyati // DhvK_3.30 //
children.translated_text: The touch of a <s>rasa</s> opposed to it upon its subordinate elements is not a fault. [End of <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.30]

children.text:
śṛṅgāra-viruddha-rasa-sparśaḥ śṛṅgārāṅgānāṃ yaḥ sa na kevalam avirodha-lakṣaṇa-yoge sati na duṣyati yāvad vineyān unmukhīkartuṃ kāvya-śobhārtham eva vā kriyamāṇo na duṣyati /
śṛṅgāra-rasāṅgair unmukhī-kṛtāḥ santo hi vineyāḥ sukhaṃ vinayopadeśān gṛhṇanti /
sad-ācāropadeśa-rūpā hi nāṭakādi-goṣṭhī vineya-jana-hitārtham eva munibhir avatāritā /
kiṃ ca śṛṅgārasya sakala-jana-mano-harābhirāmatvāt tad-aṅga-samāveśaḥ kāvye śobhātiśayaṃ puṣyatīty anenāpi prakāreṇa virodhini rase śṛṅgārāṅga-samāveśo na virodhī /
tataś ca-
children.translated_text: The touch of a <s>rasa</s> opposed to <s>śṛṅgāra</s> upon the subordinate elements of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> — that is not only faultless when the conditions for non-conflict described above are met, but even when done to make the audience receptive, or for the sake of the beauty of the poem, it is not a fault.
