children.text: patyuḥ śiraś-candra-kalām anena
children.translated_text: 'Touch the crescent moon on your lord's head with this [garland]'—

children.text: spṛśeti sakhyā parihāsa-pūrvam /
children.translated_text: So said her friend playfully;

children.text: sā rañjayitvā caraṇau kṛtāśīr
children.translated_text: She, having reddened [<s>Śiva</s>'s] feet [with the lac-dye on her hands], offered a blessing,

children.text: mālyena tāṃ nirvacanaṃ jaghāna //
children.translated_text: And silently struck her [friend] with the garland.

children.text: yathā ca-
prayacchatoccaiḥ kusumāni māninī
children.translated_text: The proud woman, addressed with the name of her rival's family by her beloved,

children.text: vipakṣa-gotraṃ dayitena lambhitā /
children.translated_text: Offered flowers aloft [to the deity];

children.text: na kiṃcid ūce caraṇena kevalaṃ
children.translated_text: She said nothing at all, but with her foot alone,

children.text: lilekha bāṣpākula-locanā bhuvam //
children.translated_text: Eyes brimming with tears, she traced [lines] upon the ground.
And as in:

children.text: ity atra "nirvacanaṃ jaghāna" "na kiṃcid ūce" iti pratiṣedha-mukhena vyaṅgyasyārthasyoktyā kiṃcid viṣayī-kṛtatvād guṇībhāva eva śobhate / yadā vakroktiṃ vinā vyaṅgyo 'rthas tātparyeṇa pratīyate tadā tasya prādhānyam / yathā "evaṃ vādini devarṣau" ity ādau / iha punaruktir bhaṅgyāstīti vācyasyāpi prādhānyam / tasmān nātrānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgya-dhvani-vyapadeśo vidheyaḥ || DhvA_3.39 ||
children.translated_text: Here, since the suggested meaning is somewhat made an object [of expression] through the statement via negation—'it killed the utterance,' 'she said nothing'—its subordinate status (<s>guṇībhāva</s>) is precisely what is beautiful. When the suggested meaning is apprehended as primary without <s>vakrokti</s> (indirect expression), then it has primacy—as in [the verse beginning] 'When the divine sage spoke thus' and so forth. But here, since there is an oblique expression, the expressed meaning also has primacy. Therefore, the designation of <s>dhvani</s> of the <s>anuraṇana</s> (resonance) type should not be applied here.
[Verse] 3.40:

children.text: prakāro 'yaṃ guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyo 'pi dhvani-rūpatām /
children.translated_text: This type, though belonging to <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> (suggestion in subordinate role), assumes the nature of <s>dhvani</s>

children.text: dhatte rasādi-tātparya-paryālocanayā punaḥ // DhvK_3.40 //
children.translated_text: again, when examined from the perspective of its aim toward <s>rasa</s> and the rest.

children.text: guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyo 'pi kāvya-prakāro rasa-bhāvādi-tātparyālocane punar dhvanir eva sampadyate / yathātraivānantarodāhṛte śloka-dvaye / yathā ca-
children.translated_text: Even the type of poetry belonging to <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>, when examined from the perspective of its aim toward <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and the rest, becomes nothing but <s>dhvani</s>. As in the very pair of verses just cited above. And as in—

children.text: durārādhā rādhā subhaga yad anenāpi mṛjatas
children.translated_text: '<s>Rādhā</s> is hard to please (<s>durārādhā</s>), O fortunate one; even as you rub [her feet]

children.text: tavaitat-prāṇeśājaghana-vasanenāśru patitam /
children.translated_text: this tear has fallen, O lord of her life, from this hip-garment of yours.

children.text: kaṭhoraṃ strī-cetas tad alam upacārair virama he
children.translated_text: The heart of a woman is hard; enough of these entreaties—desist!'

children.text: kriyāt kalyāṇaṃ vo harir anunayeṣv evam uditaḥ //
children.translated_text: May <s>Hari</s>, thus addressed during [his] attempts at reconciliation, bring you welfare!

children.text:
evaṃ sthite ca "nyakkāro hy ayam eva" ity ādi-śloka-nirdiṣṭānāṃ padānāṃ vyaṅgya-viśiṣṭa-vācya-pratipādane 'py etad-vākyārthībhūta-rasāpekṣayā vyañjakatvam uktam / ne teṣāṃ padānām arthāntara-saṃkramita-vācya-dhvani-bhramo vidhātavyaḥ, vivakṣita-vācyatvāt teṣām / teṣu hi vyaṅgya-viśiṣṭatvaṃ vācyasya pratīyate na tu vyaṅgya-rūpa-pariṇatatvam /
tasmād vākyaṃ tatra dhvaniḥ, padāni tu guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyāni / na ca kevalaṃ guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyāny eva padāny alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgya-dhvaner vyañjakāni yāvad-arthāntara-saṃkramita-vācyāni dhvani-prabheda-rūpāṇy api / yathātraiva śloke rāvaṇa ity asya prabhedāntara-rūpa-vyañjakatvam / yatra tu vākye rasādi-tātparyaṃ nāsti guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyaiḥ padair udbhāsite 'pi tatra guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyataiva samudāya-dharmaḥ / yathā-
children.translated_text: This being so, even though the words indicated in the verse beginning 'This is indeed humiliation' establish an expressed meaning qualified by suggestion, their suggestive function has been stated with reference to the <s>rasa</s> that has become the sentence-meaning. One should not mistakenly assign them to the <s>arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācya-dhvani</s> (meaning-transferred <s>dhvani</s>) type, since their expressed meaning is intended (<s>vivakṣita</s>). For in their case, what is apprehended is the expressed meaning qualified by suggestion, not the expressed meaning transformed into the form of the suggested. Therefore, the sentence there is <s>dhvani</s>, while the words are <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>. And it is not the case that only <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> words serve as suggestors of imperceptible-sequence <s>dhvani</s>; even words of the <s>arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācya</s> type, being varieties of <s>dhvani</s>, also [serve as suggestors]. As in this very verse, the word '<s>Rāvaṇa</s>' functions as a suggestor of another variety [of <s>dhvani</s>]. But where the sentence has no aim toward <s>rasa</s> and the rest, even when highlighted by <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> words, the <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> character is the property of the whole. As in—

children.text:
rājānam api sevante viṣamam apy upayuñjate /
ramante ca saha strībhiḥ kuśalāḥ khalu mānavāḥ //ity ādau /
children.translated_text: 'They serve even the king, they employ even poison, and they sport with women—skillful indeed are men!' And so forth.

children.text: vācya-vyaṅgyayoḥ prādhānyāprādhānya-viveke paraḥ prayatno vidhātavyaḥ, yena dhvani-guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyayor alaṅkārāṇāṃ cāsaṅkīrṇo viṣayaḥ sujñāto bhavati / anyathā tu prasiddhālaṅkāra-viṣaya eva vyāmohaḥ pravartate / yathā-
children.translated_text: The utmost effort should be made in distinguishing the primacy and subordination of the expressed and suggested [meanings], whereby the distinct domains of <s>dhvani</s>, <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>, and the [poetic] ornaments (<s>alaṅkāras</s>) become clearly understood. Otherwise, confusion arises even in the well-established domain of ornaments. As in—

children.text: lāvaṇya-draviṇa-vyayo na gaṇitaḥ kleśo mahān svīkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The expenditure of the wealth of grace was not considered; great suffering was undertaken;

children.text: svacchandasya sukhaṃ janasya vasataś cintānalo dīpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: the fire of anxiety was kindled for a freely-living, comfortable public;

children.text: eṣāpi svayam eva tulya-ramaṇābhāvād varākī hatā
children.translated_text: she too, the wretched one, is ruined of herself due to the absence of an equal lover—

children.text: ko 'rthaś cetasi vedhasā vinihitas tanvyās tanuṃ tanvatā //[*21]
children.translated_text: what purpose was placed in the mind of <s>Brahman</s> (the Creator) when fashioning the body of this slender woman?
Reference note: Attributed to <s>Dharmakīrti</s> (<s>Kuvalayāvalī</s> 100, <s>Aucitya-vicāra-carcā</s> 11, <s>Sad-ukti-karṇāmṛta</s> 814).

children.text: Dharma-kīrteḥ (kuvalayāvalī 100, aucitya-vicāra-carcā 11, sa.u.ka. 814

ity atra vyāja-stutir alaṅkāra iti vyākhyāyi kenacit tan na caturasram, yato 'syābhidheyasyaitad-alaṅkāra-svarūpa-mātra-paryavasāyitve na suśliṣṭā / yato na tāvad ayaṃ rāgiṇaḥ kasyacid vikalpaḥ / tasya "eṣāpi svayam eva tulya-ramaṇābhāvād varākī hatā" ity evaṃ-vidhokty-anupapatteḥ / nāpi nīrāgasya; tasyaivaṃ-vidha-vikalpa-parihāraika-vyāpāratvāt / na cāyaṃ ślokaḥ kvacit prabandha iti śrūyate, yena tat-prakaraṇānugatārthatāsya parikalpyate / tasmād aprastuta-praśaṃseyam / yasmād anena vācyena guṇībhūtātmanā niḥsāmānya-guṇāvalopādhmātasya nija-mahimotkarṣa-janita-samatsara-jana-jvarasya viśeṣa-jñam ātmano na kañcid evāparaṃ paśyataḥ paridevitam etad iti prakāśyate / tathā cāyaṃ dharmakīrteḥ śloka iti prasiddhiḥ / sambhāvyate ca tasyaiva /
children.translated_text: Here, someone has explained [this as containing] the ornament of <s>vyāja-stuti</s> (ironic praise). That is not astute, because the expressed meaning does not rest merely in the form of that ornament, since it is not well-connected [on that interpretation]. For this is not the reflection of some lover—since the utterance 'she too, the wretched one, is ruined of herself due to the absence of an equal lover' would be impossible for him. Nor is it [the reflection] of one free from passion, since his sole activity would be the dismissal of such reflections. Nor is this verse known [to occur] in any literary composition, whereby its meaning might be construed as following a narrative context. Therefore this is <s>aprastuta-praśaṃsā</s> (allegorical praise). For by this expressed meaning, which is itself subordinate, what is revealed is the lamentation of someone who, puffed up by the admiration of his extraordinary, unmatched qualities and by the fervor of jealousy born from the surpassing excellence of his own greatness, sees no one at all equal to himself as a connoisseur. And accordingly, the tradition is that this verse is by <s>Dharmakīrti</s>. And it is indeed plausible for him.

children.text: yasmāt-
anadhyavasitāvagāhanam analpa-dhī-śaktināpy
children.translated_text: Unfathomed in its depth even by those of considerable intellectual power,

children.text: adṛṣṭa-paramārtha-tattvam adhikābhiyogair api /
children.translated_text: its ultimate truth unseen even by those of the greatest effort,

children.text: mataṃ mama jagaty alabdha-sadṛśa-pratigrāhakaṃ
children.translated_text: my doctrine, finding no worthy recipient in the world,

children.text: prayāsyati payonidheḥ paya iva sva-dehe jarām //
children.translated_text: will age in its own body, like the water of the ocean.
Because—

children.text: ity anenāpi ślokenaivaṃ-vidho 'bhiprāyaḥ prakāśita eva / aprastuta-praśaṃsāyāṃ ca yad vācyaṃ tasya kadācid vivakṣitatvaṃ, kadācid avivakṣitatvaṃ, kadācid vivakṣitāvivakṣitatvam iti trayī bandha-cchāyā /
children.translated_text: By this verse too, the same kind of intention is revealed. And in <s>aprastuta-praśaṃsā</s>, the expressed meaning has three compositional modes: sometimes it is intended (<s>vivakṣita</s>), sometimes unintended (<s>avivakṣita</s>), and sometimes partially intended and partially unintended (<s>vivakṣitāvivakṣita</s>).

children.text: tatra vivakṣitatvaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: Therein, the [mode where the expressed meaning is] intended [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: parārthe yaḥ pīḍām anubhavati bhaṅge 'pi madhuro
children.translated_text: He who experiences suffering for the sake of others, who is sweet even when broken,

children.text: yadīyaḥ sarveṣām iha khalu vikāro 'py abhimataḥ /
children.translated_text: whose transformation is indeed desired by all here—

children.text: na samprāpto vṛddhiṃ yadi sa bhṛśam akṣetra-patitaḥ
children.translated_text: if he has not attained growth, being fallen on barren soil,

children.text: kim ikṣor doṣo 'sau na punar aguṇāyā maru-bhuvaḥ //[*22]
children.translated_text: is that the fault of sugarcane, or rather of the unmeritorious desert land?
Reference note: <s>Subhāṣita-padya-dīpikā</s> 1052.

children.text: Spd 1052
yathā vā mamaiva-
children.translated_text: Or as in my own [verse]—

children.text: amī ye dṛśyante nanu subhaga-rūpāḥ saphalatā
children.translated_text: These [things] that are seen—are they not of beautiful form? Their fruitfulness

children.text: bhavaty eṣāṃ yasya kṣaṇam upagatānāṃ viṣayatām /
children.translated_text: belongs to whoever has even for a moment come to experience them.

children.text: nirāloke loke katham idam aho cakṣur adhunā
children.translated_text: In this world devoid of discernment, how is it that this eye now

children.text: samaṃ jātaṃ sarvair na samam athavānyair avayavaiḥ //
children.translated_text: has come to be equal to all [other eyes], yet unequal to [them] in its other faculties?

children.text: anayor hi dvayoḥ ślokayor ikṣu-cakṣuṣī vivakṣita-svarūpe eva na ca prastute / mahā-guṇasyāviṣaya-patitatvād aprāpta-para-bhāgasya kasyacit svarūpam upavarṇayituṃ dvayor api ślokayos tātparyeṇa prastutatvāt / avivakṣitatvaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: For in both of these verses, sugarcane and the eye are intended in their own nature as expressed meanings, and yet they are not the subject at hand (<s>prastuta</s>). Since both verses have as their primary aim the description of the nature of someone whose great qualities have fallen on unsuitable ground and who has not attained his due, [they employ] the intended mode. The [mode where the expressed meaning is] unintended [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: kas tvaṃ bhoḥ kathayāmi daiva-hatakaṃ māṃ viddhi śākhoṭakaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Who are you, sir?' 'I tell you: know me as a wretched <s>Śākhoṭaka</s> tree, struck by fate.'

children.text: vairāgyād iva vakṣi, sādhu viditaṃ kasmād idaṃ kathyate /
children.translated_text: 'You speak as if with detachment.' 'Well understood; why is this said?

children.text: vāmenātra vaṭas tam adhvaga-janaḥ sarvātmanā sevate
children.translated_text: The banyan tree nearby—travelers serve it with their whole being,

children.text: na cchāyāpi paropakāra-kariṇī mārga-sthitasyāpi me //
children.translated_text: but not even my shade, though I stand on the road, serves as a benefit to others.'

children.text: na hi vṛkṣa-viśeṣeṇa sahokti-pratyuktī sambhavata ity avivakṣitābhidheyenaivānena ślokena samṛddhāsat-puruṣa-samīpa-vartino nirdhanasya kasyacin manasvinaḥ paridevitaṃ tātparyeṇa vākyārthīkṛtam iti pratīyate / vivakṣitatvāvivakṣitatvaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: For a conversation with a particular tree is impossible; therefore, by this verse, whose expressed meaning is entirely unintended (<s>avivakṣitābhidheya</s>), what is apprehended as the primary sentence-meaning is the lamentation of a poor but noble-minded person residing near a prosperous but undeserving man. The [mode where the expressed meaning is] both intended and unintended [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: utpatha-jātāyā aśobhanāyā phala-kusuma-patra-rahitāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: '[You who give] sustenance to a jujube tree born on a bypath, ugly, devoid of fruit, flowers, and leaves—

children.text: badaryā vṛttiṃ dadat-pāmāraḥ bhoḥ hasiṣyase //
children.translated_text: O wretch, you will be laughed at!'

children.text: atra hi vācyārtho nātyantaṃ sambhavī na cāsambhavī / tasmād vācya-vyaṅgyayoḥ prādhānyāprādhānye yatnato nirūpaṇīye || DhvA_3.40 ||
children.translated_text: For here, the expressed meaning is neither entirely possible nor entirely impossible. Therefore, the primacy and subordination of the expressed and suggested [meanings] must be carefully examined.

children.text: pradhāna-guṇa-bhāvābhyāṃ vyaṅgyasyaivaṃ vyavasthite /
children.translated_text: Thus, the domain of poetry being established through the primary and subordinate status of the suggested [meaning],

children.text: kāvye ubhe tato 'nyad yat tac citram abhidhīyate // DhvK_3.41 //
children.translated_text: that which is other than both [of these types] is called <s>citra</s> (pictorial).

children.text: citraṃ śabdārtha-bhedena dvividhaṃ ca vyavasthitam /
children.translated_text: <s>Citra</s> is established as twofold, based on the distinction of word and meaning:

children.text: tatra kiṃcic chabda-citraṃ vācya-citram ataḥ param // DhvK_3.42 //
children.translated_text: one is <s>śabda-citra</s> (word-pictorial), and the other, beyond that, is <s>vācya-citra</s> (meaning-pictorial).

children.text: vyaṅgyasyārthasya prādhānye dhvani-saṃjñita-kāvya-prakāraḥ guṇa-bhāve tu guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyatā / tato 'nyad rasa-bhāvādi-tātparya-rahitaṃ vyaṅgyārtha-viśeṣa-prakāśana-śakti-śūnyaṃ ca kāvyaṃ kevala-vācya-vācaka-vaicitrya-mātrāśrayeṇopanibaddham ālekhya-prakhyaṃ yad ābhāsate tac citram / na tan-mukhyaṃ kāvyam / kāvyānukāro hy asau / tatra kiṃcic chabda-citraṃ yathā duṣkara-yamakādi / vācya-citraṃ tataḥ śabda-citrād anyad vyaṅgyārtha-saṃsparśa-rahitaṃ prādhānyena vākyārthatayā sthitaṃ rasādi-tātparya-rahitam utprekṣādi /
children.translated_text: When the suggested meaning is primary, it is the type of poetry designated as <s>dhvani</s>; when [suggestion is] subordinate, it is <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>. That which is other than both—poetry devoid of the aim toward <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and the rest, lacking the power to reveal any special suggested meaning, composed solely on the basis of mere variety in the expressed meaning and its expression, appearing like a painting—that is <s>citra</s>. It is not true (<s>mukhya</s>) poetry; rather, it is an imitation of poetry. Therein, some [<s>citra</s>] is <s>śabda-citra</s> (word-pictorial), such as difficult <s>yamaka</s> (alliterative repetition) and the like. <s>Vācya-citra</s> (meaning-pictorial) is what is other than <s>śabda-citra</s>—devoid of contact with suggested meaning, established primarily as sentence-meaning, lacking the aim toward <s>rasa</s> and the rest—such as <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) and the like.

children.text: atha kim idaṃ citraṃ nāma ? yatra na pratīyamānārtha-saṃsparśaḥ / pratīyamāno hy arthas tribhedaḥ prāk pradarśitaḥ / tatra yatra vastv-alaṅkārāntaraṃ vā vyaṅgyaṃ nāsti sa nāma citrasya kalpyatāṃ viṣayaḥ / yatra tu rasādīnām aviṣayatvaṃ sa kāvya-prakāro na sambhavaty eva / yasmād avastu-saṃsparśitā kāvyasya nopapadyate / vastu ca sarvam eva jagad gatam avaśyaṃ kasyacid rasasya bhāvasya vāṅgatvaṃ pratipadyate antato vibhāvatvena / citta-vṛtti-viśeṣā hi rasādayaḥ, na ca tad asti vastu kiṃcid yan na citta-vṛtti-viśeṣam upajanayati tad-anutpādane vā kavi-viṣayataiva tasya na syāt kavi-viṣayaś ca citratayā kaścin nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: Now, what is this <s>citra</s> exactly? That in which there is no contact with a cognized [suggested] meaning. For the cognized meaning has been shown earlier to be of three types. Where there is no <s>vastu</s> (content) or other ornament as the suggested meaning—let that be established as the domain of <s>citra</s>. But a type of poetry that has no connection with <s>rasa</s> and the rest is simply impossible. For poetry cannot be devoid of contact with reality (<s>vastu</s>). And all reality in the entire world necessarily attains subordination to some <s>rasa</s> or <s>bhāva</s>—at the very least as a <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant). For <s>rasa</s> and the rest are specific states of the mind, and there is no thing that does not generate a specific mental state; and if it did not generate one, it would not even be an object for the poet—and whatever is an object for the poet is classified as belonging to <s>citra</s> [by the opponents].

children.text: atrocyate-satyaṃ na tādṛk-kāvya-prakāro 'sti yatra rasādīnām apratītiḥ / kiṃ tu yadā rasa-bhāvādi-vivakṣā-śūnyaḥ kaviḥ śabdālaṅkāram arthālaṅkāraṃ vopanibadhnāti tadā tad-vivakṣāpekṣayā rasādi-śūnyatārthasya parikalpyate / vivakṣopārūḍha eva hi kāvye śabdānām arthaḥ / vācya-sāmarthya-vaśena vā kavi-vivakṣā-virahe 'pi tathā-vidhe viṣaye rasādi-pratītir bhavantī paridurbalā bhavatīty anenāpi prakāreṇa nīrasatvaṃ parikalpya citra-viṣayo vyavasthāpyate / tad idam uktam-
children.translated_text: To this it is replied: True, there is no such type of poetry in which <s>rasa</s> and the rest are not apprehended. However, when a poet, devoid of any intention regarding <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and the rest, composes a word-ornament or meaning-ornament, then with reference to that intention, the absence of <s>rasa</s> and the rest is postulated. For it is the meaning of words as mounted upon the poet's intention that constitutes the meaning of poetry. Or, even in the absence of the poet's intention, when the apprehension of <s>rasa</s> and the rest occurs in such a domain merely by the power of the expressed meaning, it occurs in an extremely feeble form—and by this mode too, the absence of <s>rasa</s> is postulated and the domain of <s>citra</s> is established. Thus it has been said—

children.text: rasa-bhāvādi-viṣaya-vivakṣā-virahe sati /
children.translated_text: When there is absence of intention regarding <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and the rest as subject-matter,

children.text: alaṅkāra-nibandho yaḥ sa citra-viṣayo mataḥ //
children.translated_text: the composition of ornaments [alone] is considered the domain of <s>citra</s>.

children.text: rasādiṣu vivakṣā tu syāt tātparyavatī yadā /
children.translated_text: But when the intention regarding <s>rasa</s> and the rest is fully purposive,

children.text: tadā nāsty eva tat kāvyaṃ dhvaner yatra na gocaraḥ //
children.translated_text: then there is simply no poetry at all that is not the domain of <s>dhvani</s>.

children.text: etac ca citraṃ kavīnāṃ viśṛṅkhala-girāṃ rasādi-tātparyam anapekṣyaiva kāvya-pravṛtti-darśanād asmābhiḥ parikalpitam / idānīntanānāṃ tu nyāyye kāvya-naya-vyavasthāpane kriyamāṇe nāsty eva dhvani-vyatiriktaḥ kāvya-prakāraḥ / yataḥ paripākavatāṃ kavīnāṃ rasādi-tātparya-virahe vyāpāra eva na śobhate / rasādi-tātparye ca nāsty eva tad vastu yad abhimata-rasāṅgatāṃ nīyamānaṃ na praguṇībhavati / acetanā pi hi bhāvā yathāyatham ucita-rasa-vibhāvatayā cetana-vṛttānta-yojanayā vā na santy eva te ye yānti na rasāṅgatām / tathā cedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: And this [category of] <s>citra</s> has been postulated by us because we observe the poetic activity of undisciplined poets who compose without regard for the aim toward <s>rasa</s> and the rest. But for poets of our time, when the proper principles of poetics are being established, there is simply no type of poetry other than <s>dhvani</s>. For the activity of mature poets does not shine without the aim toward <s>rasa</s> and the rest. And when there is the aim toward <s>rasa</s> and the rest, there is simply no subject-matter that does not become excellent when led to subordination to the desired <s>rasa</s>. For even inanimate entities, when made into <s>vibhāvas</s> of the appropriate <s>rasa</s> in their proper manner, or when conjoined with the narrative of conscious beings, are such that none fails to attain subordination to <s>rasa</s>. And thus it is said—

children.text: apāre kāvya-saṃsāre kavir ekaḥ prajāpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: In the boundless world of poetry, the poet alone is <s>Prajāpati</s> (the Creator);

children.text: yathāsmai rocate viśvaṃ tathedaṃ parivartate //
children.translated_text: as it pleases him, so does this universe turn.

children.text: śṛṅgārī cet kaviḥ kāvye jātaṃ rasa-mayaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: If the poet is amorous, the world [in his poem] is born full of <s>rasa</s>;

children.text: sa eva vīta-rāgaś cen nīrasaṃ sarvam eva tat //
children.translated_text: if that same [poet] is free from passion, all of that becomes devoid of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: bhāvān acetanān api cetanavac cetanānacetanavat /
children.translated_text: The good poet, by his own sovereignty in poetry, treats inanimate things as if animate

children.text: vyavahārayati yatheṣṭaṃ sukaviḥ kāvye svatantratayā //
children.translated_text: and animate things as if inanimate—as he wishes.

children.text: tasmān nāsty eva tad vastu yat sarvātmanā rasa-tātparyavataḥ kaves tad-icchayā tad-abhimata-rasāṅgatāṃ na dhatte / tathopanibadhyamānaṃ vā na cārutvātiśayaṃ puṣṇāti / sarvam etac ca mahā-kavīnāṃ kāvyeṣu dṛśyate / asmābhir api sveṣu kāvya-prabandheṣu yathāyathaṃ darśitam eva / sthite caivaṃ sarva eva kāvya-prakāro na dhvani-dharmatām atipatati rasādy-apekṣāyāṃ kaver guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya-lakṣaṇo 'pi prakāras tad-aṅgatām avalambata ity uktaṃ prāk / yadā tu cāṭuṣu devatā-stutiṣu vā rasādīnām aṅgatayā vyavasthānaṃ hṛdayavatīṣu ca suprajñaka-gāthāsu kāsucid vyaṅgya-viśiṣṭa-vācye prādhānyaṃ tad api guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyasya dhvani-niṣpanda-bhūtatvam evety uktaṃ prāk / tad evam idānīṃtana-kavi-kāvya-nayopadeśe kriyamāṇe prāthamikānām abhyāsārthināṃ yadi paraṃ citreṇa vyavahāraḥ, prāpta-pariṇatīnāṃ tu dhvanir eva kāvyam iti sthitam etat /
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is simply no subject-matter that, by the will of a poet whose purport is <s>rasa</s>, does not assume the status of a subordinate element of his intended <s>rasa</s>, or that, when composed accordingly, does not nourish a surpassing charm. And all this is seen in the works of the great poets. It has also been shown by us, as appropriate, in our own poetic compositions. And this being so, every variety of poetry does not transcend the nature of <s>dhvani</s>. With respect to <s>rasa</s> and the like, even the variety characterized by suggested-as-subordinate (<s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>) depends on <s>dhvani</s> as its subsidiary — as was stated before. And when in eulogies (<s>cāṭu</s>) or in hymns to deities, <s>rasas</s> and the like are established as subordinate elements, and when in certain witty sayings (<s>suprajñaka-gāthā</s>) spoken by intelligent [persons], the expressed meaning distinguished by the suggested holds primacy — even that is but a ripple of <s>dhvani</s>, belonging to the category of suggested-as-subordinate — as was stated before. Thus, in the present instruction on the method of poets' poetry, if beginners who desire practice [deal] only with <s>citra</s> (the pictorial/figurative), [that is acceptable]; but for those who have attained maturity, it is established that <s>dhvani</s> alone is poetry.

children.text: tad ayam atra saṅgrahaḥ-
children.translated_text: Here is the summary of this:

children.text: yasmin raso vā bhāvo vā tātparyeṇa prakāśate /
children.translated_text: Where <s>rasa</s> or <s>bhāva</s> is manifested as the purport,

children.text: saṃvṛttyābhihitau vastu yatrālaṅkāra eva vā //
children.translated_text: Or where, [though] expressed indirectly (<s>saṃvṛttyā</s>), the subject-matter or indeed a figure of speech [is the suggested] —

children.text: kāvyādhvani dhvanir vyaṅgya-prādhānyaika-nibandhanaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the domain of poetry, <s>dhvani</s>, which is grounded solely in the primacy of the suggested,

children.text: sarvatra tatra viṣayī jñeyaḥ sahṛdayair janaiḥ || DhvA_3.42 ||
children.translated_text: Should be recognized as the ruling [principle] everywhere, by sensitive persons (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). || <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Autocommentary 3.42 ||
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.43:

children.text: saguṇībhūta-vyaṅgyaiḥ sālaṅkāraiḥ saha prabhedaiḥ svaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Together with [the variety of] suggested-as-subordinate (<s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>), together with figures, and together with its own sub-varieties,

children.text: saṅkara-saṃsṛṣṭibhyāṃ punar apy uddyotate bahudhā // DhvK_3.43 //
children.translated_text: Through conflation (<s>saṅkara</s>) and combination (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>), [<s>dhvani</s>] shines forth again in manifold [forms]. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.43 //

children.text: tasya ca dhvaneḥ sva-prabhedair guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyena vācyālaṅkāraiś ca saṅkara-saṃsṛṣṭi-vyavasthāyāṃ kriyamāṇāyāṃ bahu-prabhedatā lakṣye dṛśyate / tathā hi sva-prabheda-saṅkīrṇaḥ, sva-prabheda-saṃsṛṣṭo guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya-saṅkīrṇo guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya-saṃsṛṣṭo vācyālaṅkārāntara-saṅkīrṇo vācyālaṅkārāntara-saṃsṛṣṭaḥ saṃsṛṣṭālaṅkāra-saṅkīrṇaḥ saṃsṛṣṭālaṅkāra-saṃsṛṣṭaś ceti bahudhā dhvaniḥ prakāśate /
children.translated_text: When the arrangement of <s>dhvani</s> through conflation and combination with its own sub-varieties, with suggested-as-subordinate, and with figures of expressed meaning is undertaken, a multiplicity of sub-varieties is seen in actual literary examples. Namely: conflated with its own sub-variety, combined with its own sub-variety, conflated with suggested-as-subordinate, combined with suggested-as-subordinate, conflated with a different figure of expressed meaning, combined with a different figure of expressed meaning, conflated with a combined figure, and combined with a combined figure — thus <s>dhvani</s> shines forth in manifold ways.

children.text: tatra sva-prabheda-saṅkīrṇatvaṃ kadācid anugrāhyānugrāhaka-bhāvena / yathā-"evaṃ-vādini devarṣau" ity ādau / atra hy artha-śakty-udbhavānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgya-dhvani-prabhedenālakṣya-krama-vyaṅgya-dhvani-prabhedo 'nugṛhyamāṇaḥ pratīyate / evaṃ kadācit prabheda-dvaya-sampāta-sandehena / yathā-
children.translated_text: There, conflation with its own sub-variety sometimes occurs in the relation of supported and supporter. As in 'When the divine sage spoke thus...' and so forth. For here, the <s>dhvani</s> sub-variety of imperceptible-sequence suggestion is perceived as being supported by the <s>dhvani</s> sub-variety of reverberating-echo suggestion arising from the power of the meaning. And sometimes [it occurs] through the doubt of coincidence of two sub-varieties. As in—

children.text: khaṇa-pāhuṇiā deara esā jāāeṃ kiṃ pi de bhaṇidā /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'She is but a guest for a moment, O brother-in-law — your wife has said something to her;

children.text: rua{i} paḍohara-valahī-gharammi aṇuṇijja{u} barāī //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] She weeps in the empty upper-story room — let the poor thing be consoled!'

children.text: [kṣaṇa-prāghuṇikā devara eṣā jāyayā kim api te bhaṇitā /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'She is but a guest for a moment, O brother-in-law — your wife has said something to her;

children.text: roditi śūnya-valabhī-gṛhe 'nunīyatāṃ varākī //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] She weeps in the empty upper-story room — let the poor thing be consoled!'

children.text: atra hy anunīyatām ity etat-padam arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācyatvena vivakṣitāny apara-vācyatvena ca sambhāvyate / na cānyatara-pakṣa-nirṇaye pramāṇam asti / eka-vyañjakānupraveśena tu vyaṅgyatvam alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyasya sva-prabhedāntarāpekṣayā bāhulyena sambhavati / yathā-"snigdha-śyāmala" ity ādau / sva-prabheda-saṃsṛṣṭatvaṃ ca yathā pūrvodāharaṇa eva / atra hy arthāntara-saṃkramita-vācyasyātyanta-tiraskṛta-vācyasya ca saṃsargaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the word 'let her be consoled' (<s>anunīyatām</s>) can be construed as having its expressed meaning transferred to another sense (<s>arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācya</s>) or as [belonging to <s>dhvani</s>] whose expressed meaning is intended but directed toward another (<s>vivakṣitānya-para-vācya</s>). And there is no evidence to decide between the two alternatives. When the entry of a single suggestor [allows for] suggestion of the imperceptible-sequence type, [conflation] with reference to another of its own sub-varieties is abundantly possible. As in 'dark and smooth...' and so forth. And combination with its own sub-variety [is illustrated] as in the very example just cited. For here there is a combination of [<s>dhvani</s> with] expressed meaning transferred to another sense and [<s>dhvani</s> with] expressed meaning completely set aside.

children.text: guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgya-saṅkīrṇatvaṃ yathā-"nyak-kāro hy ayam eva me yad arayaḥ" ity ādau /
children.translated_text: Conflation with suggested-as-subordinate [is illustrated] as in 'This alone is my humiliation: that my enemies [exist]...' and so forth.

children.text: yathā vā-
kartā dyūta-cchalānāṃ jatu-maya-śaraṇoddīpanaḥ so 'bhimānī
children.translated_text: 'The contriver of the stratagem of dice, the incendiary of the house of lac, that proud one,

children.text: kṛṣṇā-keśottarīya-vyapanayana-paṭuḥ pāṇḍavā yasya dāsāḥ /
children.translated_text: Expert at stripping the garment from <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s (Draupadī's) hair — he whose slaves are the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>;

children.text: rājā duḥśāsanāder gurur anuja-śatasyāṅga-rājasya mitraṃ
children.translated_text: King, master of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> and the rest, lord of a hundred younger brothers, friend of the king of <s>Aṅga</s> —

children.text: kvāste duryodhano 'sau kathayata na ruṣā draṣṭum abhyāgatau svaḥ //
children.translated_text: Where is that <s>Duryodhana</s>? Tell [him]! Not in anger — we have come to see [him]!'
Or as in—

children.text:
atra hy alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyasya vākyārthī-bhūtasya vyaṅgya-viśiṣṭa-vācyābhidhāyibhiḥ padaiḥ sammiśratā / ata eva ca padārthāśrayatve guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgyasya vākyārthāśrayatve ca dhvaneḥ saṅkīrṇatāyām api na virodhaḥ sva-prabhedāntaravat / yathā hi dhvani-prabhedāntarāṇi parasparaṃ saṅkīryante padārtha-vākyārthāśrayatvena ca na viruddhāni /
kiṃ caika-vyaṅgyāśrayatve tu pradhāna-guṇa-bhāvo virudhyate na tu vyaṅgya-bhedāpekṣayā, tato 'py asya na virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>dhvani</s> of imperceptible-sequence suggestion, having become sentence-meaning, is mixed with words that express subject-matter distinguished by suggestion as subordinate. And precisely for this reason, even when suggested-as-subordinate rests on word-meaning and <s>dhvani</s> rests on sentence-meaning, the conflation is not contradictory — just as with other of its own sub-varieties. For just as the sub-varieties of <s>dhvani</s> are conflated with one another, [resting] on word-meaning and sentence-meaning, and are not contradictory — [the same applies here]. Moreover, when [resting on] a single suggested [meaning], the principal-subsidiary relation would be contradictory; but with respect to different suggested [meanings], it is not. Hence there is no contradiction here either.

children.text: ayaṃ ca saṅkara-saṃsṛṣṭi-vyavahāro bahūnām ekatra vācya-vācaka-bhāva iva vyaṅgya-vyañjaka-bhāve 'pi nirvirodha eva mantavyaḥ / yatra tu padāni kānicid avivakṣita-vācyāny anuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgya-vācyāni vā tatra dhvani-guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgyayoḥ saṃsṛṣṭatvam / yathā-"teṣāṃ gopa-vadhū-vilāsa-suhṛdām" ity ādau /
children.translated_text: And this practice of conflation and combination should be understood as perfectly non-contradictory in the suggested-suggestor relation, just as in the expressed-expressor relation where many [elements] coexist in a single [locus]. But where certain words have unintended expressed meaning or have expressed meaning belonging to reverberating-echo suggestion, there is combination of <s>dhvani</s> and suggested-as-subordinate. As in 'Of those who were the companions of the amorous sports of the cowherd women...' and so forth.

children.text: atra hi "vilāsa-suhṛdām" "rādhā-rahaḥ-sākṣiṇām" ity ete pade dhvani-prabheda-rūpe "te" "jāne" ity ete ca pade guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgya-rūpe / vācyālaṅkāra-saṅkīrṇatvam alakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyāpekṣayā rasavati sālaṅkāre kāvye sarvatra suvyavasthitam / prabhedāntarāṇām api kadācit saṅkīrṇatvaṃ bhavaty eva / yathā mamaiva-
children.translated_text: Here, the words 'companions of amorous sports' (<s>vilāsa-suhṛdām</s>) and 'witnesses of <s>Rādhā</s>'s secret' (<s>rādhā-rahaḥ-sākṣiṇām</s>) belong to the <s>dhvani</s> sub-variety, while the words 'those' (<s>te</s>) and 'I know' (<s>jāne</s>) belong to the suggested-as-subordinate variety. Conflation with figures of expressed meaning, with respect to imperceptible-sequence suggestion, is well-established everywhere in <s>rasa</s>-ful poetry adorned with figures. Conflation of other sub-varieties also sometimes occurs. As in my own [verse]—

children.text: yā vyāpāravatī rasān rasayituṃ kācit kavīnāṃ navā
children.translated_text: 'That fresh vision of certain poets which is engaged in savoring <s>rasas</s>,

children.text: dṛṣṭir yā pariniṣṭhitārtha-viṣayonmeṣā ca vaipaścitī /
children.translated_text: And that philosophical insight whose illumination has perfected truths as its object —

children.text: te dve apy avalambya viśvam aniśaṃ nirvarṇayanto vayaṃ
children.translated_text: Resting on both of these, we ceaselessly contemplate the universe,

children.text: śrāntā naiva ca labdham abdhi-śayana ! tvad-bhakti-tulyaṃ sukham //
children.translated_text: Yet we are not wearied — nor, O Sleeper-on-the-Ocean, have we found a happiness equal to devotion to You!'

children.text:
ity atra virodhālaṅkāreṇārthāntara-saṃkramita-vācyasya dhvani-prabhedasya saṅkīrṇatvam /
vācyālaṅkāra-saṃsṛṣṭatvaṃ ca padāpekṣayaiva / yatra hi kānicit padāni vācyālaṅkāra-bhāñji kānicic ca dhvani-prabheda-yuktāni / yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>dhvani</s> sub-variety whose expressed meaning is transferred to another sense is conflated with the figure of contradiction (<s>virodha</s>). Combination with figures of expressed meaning occurs at the word-level. Where certain words embody figures of expressed meaning while others are endowed with a <s>dhvani</s> sub-variety — as in—

children.text: dīrghīkurvan paṭu mada-kalaṃ kūjitaṃ sārasānāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Prolonging skillfully the passionate cooing of the <s>sārasa</s> cranes,

children.text: pratyūṣeṣu sphuṭita-kamalāmoda-maitrī-kaṣāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Astringent with the fragrance of friendship (<s>maitrī</s>) with the scent of blooming lotuses at dawn,

children.text: yatra strīṇāṃ harati surata-glānim aṅgānukūlaḥ
children.translated_text: The breeze of the <s>Siprā</s> [river], conforming to the limbs, removing the languor of love-making in women,

children.text: siprāvātaḥ priyatama iva prārthanā-cāṭu-kāraḥ //
children.translated_text: Like a dearest one making flattering entreaties —'

children.text: atra hi maitrī-padam avivakṣita-vācyo dhvaniḥ / padāntareṣv alaṅkārāntarāṇi /
children.translated_text: Here, the word 'friendship' (<s>maitrī</s>) constitutes <s>dhvani</s> whose expressed meaning is unintended. In the other words, [there are] other figures.

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭālaṅkārāntara-saṅkīrṇo dhvanir, yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Dhvani</s> conflated with a different combined figure [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: danta-kṣatāni karajaiś ca vipāṭitāni
children.translated_text: 'The tooth-marks and the scratches made by nails

children.text: prodbhinna-sāndra-pulake bhavataḥ śarīre /
children.translated_text: On your body, where dense goose-bumps have arisen —

children.text: dattāni rakta-manasā mṛga-rāja-vadhvā
children.translated_text: Bestowed by the lioness with a passionate heart —

children.text: jāta-spṛhair munibhir apy avalokitāni //
children.translated_text: Were gazed upon with longing even by the sages.'

children.text: atra hi samāsokti-saṃsṛṣṭena virodhālaṅkāreṇa saṅkīrṇasyālakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyasya dhvaneḥ prakāśanam / dayā-vīrasya paramārthato vākyārthībhūtatvāt / saṃsṛṣṭālaṅkāra-saṃsṛṣṭatvaṃ ca dhvaner yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, <s>dhvani</s> of imperceptible-sequence suggestion is manifested conflated with the figure of contradiction (<s>virodha</s>) that is itself combined with condensed expression (<s>samāsokti</s>). [This is] because compassionate heroism (<s>dayā-vīra</s>) is the ultimate sentence-meaning [here]. And <s>dhvani</s> combined with a combined figure [is illustrated] as in—

children.text: abhinava-payodhara-rasiteṣu pathika-śyāmāyiteṣu divaseṣu /
children.translated_text: 'In those days when the fresh rain-clouds resound, when [the sky] darkens like a traveler,

children.text: śobhate prasārita-grīvāṇāṃ nṛttaṃ mayūra-vṛndānām //
children.translated_text: The dance of the flocks of peacocks with outstretched necks is resplendent.'

children.text: atra hy upamā-rūpakābhyāṃ śabda-śakty-udbhavānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgyasya dhvaneḥ saṃsṛṣṭatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>dhvani</s> of reverberating-echo suggestion arising from the power of the word is combined with simile (<s>upamā</s>) and metaphor (<s>rūpaka</s>).
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.44:

children.text: evaṃ dhvaneḥ prabhedāḥ prabheda-bhedāś ca kena śakyante /
children.translated_text: Thus, the sub-varieties of <s>dhvani</s> and the divisions of those sub-varieties — who can

children.text: saṅkhyātuṃ diṅ-mātraṃ teṣām idam uktam asmābhiḥ // DhvK_3.44 //
children.translated_text: Enumerate them? Only a fraction of them has been stated by us. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.44 //

children.text: anantā hi dhvaneḥ prakārāḥ sahṛdayānāṃ vyutpattaye teṣāṃ diṅ-mātraṃ kathitam //
children.translated_text: For the varieties of <s>dhvani</s> are infinite; only a fraction of them has been described for the education of sensitive readers (<s>sahṛdaya</s>).
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.45:

children.text: ity ukta-lakṣaṇo yo dhvanir vivecyaḥ prayatnataḥ sadbhiḥ
sat-kāvyaṃ kartuṃ vā jñātuṃ vā samyag abhiyuktaiḥ // DhvK_3.45 //
children.translated_text: By those who are diligently engaged either in composing or in truly understanding excellent poetry. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.45 //
This <s>dhvani</s>, whose characteristics have thus been described, should be carefully discerned by the good —

children.text: ukta-svarūpa-dhvani-nirūpaṇa-nipuṇā hi sat-kavayaḥ sahṛdayāś ca niyatam eva kāvya-viṣaye parāṃ prakarṣa-padavīm āsādayanti //
children.translated_text: For good poets and sensitive readers who are skilled in discerning <s>dhvani</s> of the nature described assuredly attain the highest level of excellence in the domain of poetry.
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.46:

children.text: asphuṭa-sphuritaṃ kāvya-tattvam etad yathoditam /
children.translated_text: This essence of poetry, which had dimly flickered [in awareness], as now expounded —

children.text: aśaknuvadbhir vyākartuṃ rītayaḥ sampravartitāḥ // DhvK_3.46 //
children.translated_text: By those unable to fully articulate it, the [doctrines of] <s>rītis</s> (styles) were set forth. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.46 //

children.text: etad-dhvani-pravartanena nirṇītaṃ kāvya-tattvam asphuṭa-sphuritaṃ sad aśaknuvadbhiḥ pratipādayituṃ vaidarbhī gauḍī pāñcālī ceti rītayaḥ pravartitāḥ / rīti-lakṣaṇa-vidhāyināṃ hi kāvya-tattvam etad asphuṭatayā manāk-sphuritam āsīd iti lakṣyate tad atra sphuṭatayā sampradarśitenānyena rīti-lakṣaṇena na kiṃcit || DhvA_3.46 ||
children.translated_text: The essence of poetry that has now been determined through this exposition of <s>dhvani</s> — while it existed [before], dimly flickering — by those unable to articulate it, the <s>rītis</s> (styles) called <s>Vaidarbhī</s>, <s>Gauḍī</s>, and <s>Pāñcālī</s> were set forth. For it is observed that this essence of poetry had faintly flickered before the formulators of the <s>rīti</s> definitions. Now that it has been clearly demonstrated here, those [previous] <s>rīti</s> definitions serve no further purpose. || <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Autocommentary 3.46 ||
<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.47:

children.text: śabda-tattvāśrayāḥ kāścid artha-tattva-yujo 'parāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some <s>vṛttis</s> (modes) that rest on the essence of words, and others endowed with the essence of meaning —

children.text: vṛttayo 'pi prakāśante jñāte 'smin kāvya-lakṣaṇe // DhvK_3.47 //
children.translated_text: These too become clearly manifest when this characteristic of poetry [<s>dhvani</s>] is understood. // <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> Kārikā 3.47 //

children.text: asmin vyaṅgya-vyañjakabhāvavivecanamaye kāvya-lakṣaṇe jñāte sati yāḥ kāścitprasiddhā upanāgarikādyāḥ śabdatattvāśrayāḥ vṛttayo yāścārthatattvasambaddhāḥ kaiśikyādayastāḥ samyagrītipadavīmavataranti / anyathā tu tāsāmadṛṣṭārthānām iva vṛttīnāmaśraddheyatvam eva syānnānubhavasiddhatvam / evaṃ sphuṭatayaiva lakṣaṇīyaṃ svarūpamasya dhvaneḥ / yatra śabdānām arthānāṃ ca keṣāñcitpratipattṛviśeṣasaṃvedyaṃ jātyatvam iva ratnaviśeṣāṇāṃ cārutvamanākhyeyamavabhāsate kāvye tatra dhvanivyavahāra iti yallakṣaṇaṃ dhvaner ucyate kenacittadayuktam iti nābhidheyatāmarhati / yataḥ śabdānāṃ svarūpāśrayas tāvad akliṣṭatve satyaprayuktaprayogaḥ / vācakāśrayas tu prasādo vyañjakatvaṃ ceti viśeṣaḥ / arthānāṃ ca sphuṭatvenāvabhāsanaṃ vyaṅgyaparatvaṃ vyaṅgyāṃśaviśiṣṭatvam ceti viśeṣaḥ / tau ca viśeṣau vyākhyātuṃ śakyete vyākhyātau ca bahuprakāram / tadvyatiriktānākhyeyaviśeṣasambhāvanā tu vivekāvasādabhāvamūlaiva / yasmādanākhyeyatvaṃ sarva-śabdāgocaratvena na kasyacitsambhavati / antato 'nākhyeyaśabdena tasyābhidhānasambhavāt / sāmānyasaṃsparśivikalpaśabdāgocaratve sati, prakāśamānatvaṃ tu yadanākhyeyatvam ucyate kvacit tad api kāvyaviśeṣāṇāṃ ratnaviśeṣāṇām iva na sambhavati / teṣāṃ lakṣaṇakāraivyākṛta-rūpatvāt / ratnaviśeṣāṇāṃ ca sāmānyasambhāvanayaiva mūlyasthitiparikalpanādarśanācca / ubhayeṣām api teṣāṃ pratipattṛviśeṣasaṃvedyatvamasty eva / vaikaṭikā eva hi ratnatattvavidaḥ, sahṛdayā eva hi kāvyānāṃ rasajñā iti kasyātra vipratipattiḥ / yat tv anirdeśyatvaṃ sarva-lakṣaṇa-viṣayaṃ bauddhānāṃ prasiddhaṃ tattanmataparīkṣāyāṃ granthāntare nirūpayiṣyāmaḥ / iha tu granthāntaraśravaṇalavaprakāśanaṃ sahṛdayavaimanasyapradāyīti na prakriyate / bauddhamatena vā yathā pratyakṣādilakṣaṇaṃ tathāsmākaṃ dhvanilakṣaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / tasmāllakṣaṇāntarasyāghaṭanādaśabdārthatvācca tasyoktam eva dhvanilakṣaṇaṃ sādhīyaḥ / tad idam uktam-
children.translated_text: When this definition of poetry, which consists in the discrimination of the suggested-suggestor relationship, is understood, then whatever well-known styles (<s>vṛttis</s>) based on the nature of words — such as <s>upanāgarikā</s> and the like — and those connected with the nature of meaning — such as <s>kaiśikī</s> and the like — properly descend into the path of poetic tradition (<s>rīti</s>). Otherwise, those styles, as if their purpose were unseen, would be simply untrustworthy rather than established through experience. Thus the essential nature of this <s>dhvani</s> is to be defined with this much clarity. As for the definition of <s>dhvani</s> stated by someone — that 'in poetry where a certain inexpressible (<s>anākhyeya</s>) charm of particular words and meanings shines forth, perceivable only by a particular type of perceiver, like the essential quality (<s>jātyatva</s>) of particular gems, there the designation dhvani applies' — that is improper and does not merit being stated. For the charm of words based on their own form, when there is absence of harshness, is [merely] an uncommon usage (<s>aprayuktaprayoga</s>). But the distinction based on the expressor is perspicuity (<s>prasāda</s>) and suggestive power (<s>vyañjakatva</s>). And the distinction of meanings is: manifestation with clarity, primacy of the suggested, and being qualified by the suggested element. These two distinctions can be explained and have been explained in many ways. But the supposition of some other inexpressible distinction is rooted solely in the decline of discriminative faculty. For inexpressibility in the sense of being beyond the range of all words is impossible for anything whatsoever — since even that [inexpressibility] can be denoted by the word 'inexpressible' itself. And if the inexpressibility spoken of is that [the charm], while being manifest, is beyond the range of conceptual words that partake of generality — even that is impossible for particular poems, just as for particular gems. For the former have had their nature analyzed by the makers of definitions. And for the latter [gems], one sees that the determination of value is made on the basis of general estimation alone. For both of them, perceivability by a particular type of perceiver certainly exists — for only skilled jewelers (<s>vaikaṭika</s>) are experts in the true nature of gems, and only sensitive readers (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) are connoisseurs of <s>rasa</s> in poems — who would dispute this? As for the inexpressibility that is well-known among the Buddhists as applying to all objects of definition — that we shall examine in another treatise devoted to the examination of their doctrine. Here, however, the illumination of even a fragment of another treatise's teaching would cause displeasure to sensitive readers, so it is not undertaken. Or else, just as under the Buddhist system the definition of direct perception and the like [is valid], so too will our definition of <s>dhvani</s> [be valid under those same terms]. Therefore, since no other definition is feasible and since that [alternative] is not a [real] verbal-meaning entity, the definition of <s>dhvani</s> as already stated is superior. This is what has been said—

children.text: anākhyeyāṃśa-bhāsitvaṃ nirvācyārthatayā dhvaneḥ /
children.translated_text: The shining forth of an inexpressible element, as constituting an inexpressible meaning of <s>dhvani</s>,

children.text: na lakṣaṇaṃ, lakṣaṇaṃ tu sādhīyo 'sya yathoditam //
children.translated_text: is not the definition [of <s>dhvani</s>]; rather, the definition stated [earlier] is superior for it.

children.text: // iti śrī-rājānakānandavardhanācārya-viracite dhvany-āloke tṛtīya uddyotaḥ //
children.translated_text: // Thus ends the third <s>uddyota</s> in the <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> composed by the revered master <s>Rājānaka Ānandavardhana</s> //

children.text: // caturthoddyotaḥ //
children.translated_text: // The Fourth <s>Uddyota</s> //

children.text: evaṃ dhvaniṃ sa-prapañcaṃ vipratipatti-nirāsārthaṃ vyutpādya tad-vyutpādane prayojanāntaram ucyate-
children.translated_text: Having thus taught <s>dhvani</s> in detail for the purpose of refuting objections, another purpose of that teaching is now stated—
DhvK 4.1:

children.text: dhvaner yaḥ saguṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgyasyādhvā pradarśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this [teaching], the path of <s>dhvani</s> and of the suggested-become-subordinate (<s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>) that has been shown—

children.text: anenānantyam āyāti kavīnāṃ pratibhā-guṇaḥ // DhvK_4.1 //
children.translated_text: through it, the quality of creative intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) of poets attains infinity. // DhvK_4.1 //

children.text: ya eṣa dhvaner guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgyasya ca mārgaḥ prakāśitas tasya phalāntaraṃ kavi-pratibhānantyam /
children.translated_text: This path of <s>dhvani</s> and <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> that has been illuminated — a further result of it is the infinity of poetic creative intuition.

children.text: katham iti cet-
children.translated_text: How so?
DhvK 4.2:

children.text: ato hy anyatamenāpi prakāreṇa vibhūṣitā /
children.translated_text: For by being adorned through even one of these modes,

children.text: vāṇī navatvam āyāti pūrvārthānvayavaty api // DhvK_4.2 //
children.translated_text: speech attains novelty even when dealing with previously [treated] subject matter. // DhvK_4.2 //

children.text: ato dhvaner ukta-prabheda-madhyād anyatamenāpi prakāreṇa vibhūṣitā satī vāṇī purātana-kavi-nibaddhārtha-saṃsparśavaty api navatvam āyāti / tathā hy avivakṣita-vācyasya dhvaneḥ prakāra-dvaya-samāśrayeṇa navatvaṃ pūrvārthānugame 'pi, yathā-
children.translated_text: For this reason, when speech is adorned through even one of the stated sub-divisions of <s>dhvani</s>, it attains novelty even when dealing with subject matter composed by ancient poets. Thus, through recourse to the two modes of <s>dhvani</s> with unintended expressed meaning (<s>avivakṣita-vācya</s>), there is novelty even when following a prior subject matter. For example—

children.text: smitaṃ kiṃcin mugdhaṃ tarala-madhuro dṛṣṭi-vibhavaḥ
children.translated_text: A slightly innocent smile; the splendor of a glance, tremulous and sweet;

children.text: parispando vācām abhinava-vilāsormi-sarasaḥ /
children.translated_text: The play of her speech, flowing with waves of fresh coquetry;

children.text: gatānām ārambhaḥ kisalayita-līlā-parimalaḥ
children.translated_text: The commencement of her movements, fragrant with the charm of tender-sprouting playfulness—

children.text: spṛśantyās tāruṇyaṃ kim iva hi na ramyaṃ mṛgadṛśaḥ //
children.translated_text: Of the doe-eyed one touching youth, what indeed is not enchanting?

children.text: ity asya,
children.translated_text: Of this [verse],

children.text: sa-vibhrama-smitodbhedā lolākṣyaḥ praskhalad-giraḥ /
children.translated_text: With the breaking forth of a smile accompanied by flirtatious gestures, with rolling eyes and stumbling speech,

children.text: nitambālasa-gāminyaḥ kāminyaḥ kasya na priyāḥ //
children.translated_text: With slow gait at the hips — what amorous women are not dear to anyone?

children.text: ity evam ādiṣu ślokeṣu satsv api tiraskṛta-vācya-dhvani-samāśrayeṇāpūrvatvam eva pratibhāsate / tathā-
children.translated_text: Even though such verses as these exist, through recourse to <s>dhvani</s> with obscured expressed meaning (<s>tiraskṛta-vācya</s>), absolute novelty shines forth. Likewise—

children.text: yaḥ prathamaḥ prathamaḥ sa tu tathā hi hata-hasti-bahala-palalāśī /
children.translated_text: He who is foremost is truly the foremost, for he who has slain the elephant feeds on the abundant flesh;

children.text: śvāpada-gaṇeṣu siṃhaḥ siṃhaḥ kenādharī-kriyate //ity asya,
children.translated_text: Among the packs of wild beasts, the lion — the lion — by whom can he be surpassed?

children.text: sva-tejaḥ-krīta-mahimā kenānyenātiśayyate /
children.translated_text: One whose greatness is purchased by his own splendor — by what other can he be exceeded?

children.text: mahadbhir api mātaṅgaiḥ siṃhaḥ kim abhibhūyate //
children.translated_text: Can the lion be overpowered even by great elephants?

children.text:
ity evam ādiṣu ślokeṣu satsv apy arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācya-dhvani-samāśrayeṇa navatvam /
vivakṣitāny apara-vācyasyāpy ukta-prakāra-samāśrayeṇa navatvaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: Even though such verses as these exist, through recourse to <s>dhvani</s> with expressed meaning transferred to another sense (<s>arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācya</s>), there is novelty. And for <s>dhvani</s> with intended expressed meaning (<s>vivakṣitānyapara-vācya</s>) too, through recourse to the stated modes, there is novelty. For example—

children.text: nidrā-kaitavinaḥ priyasya vadane vinyasya vaktraṃ vadhūr
children.translated_text: The bride, placing her face upon the face of her sleeping beloved who feigns sleep,

children.text: bodha-trāsa-niruddha-cumbana-rasāpy ābhoga-lolaṃ sthitā /
children.translated_text: Remains poised, eager for the fullness [of the kiss], though the savoring of the kiss is arrested by fear of his awakening;

children.text: vailakṣyād vimukhībhaved iti punas tasyāpy anārambhiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: 'She will turn away in embarrassment' — and so he too does not initiate;

children.text: sākāṅkṣa-pratipatti nāma hṛdayaṃ yātaṃ tu pāraṃ rateḥ //
children.translated_text: This expectant mutual awareness — the heart has truly crossed to the far shore of love.

children.text: ity ādeḥ ślokasya,
children.translated_text: Of such a verse,

children.text: śūnyaṃ vāsa-gṛhaṃ vilokya śayanād utthāya kiṃcic chanair
children.translated_text: Seeing the bedchamber empty, rising slowly from the bed,

children.text: nidrā-vyājam upāgatasya suciraṃ nirvarṇya patyur mukham /
children.translated_text: Long gazing at the face of her husband who had come feigning sleep;

children.text: visrabdhaṃ paricumbya jāta-pulakām ālokya gaṇḍa-sthalīṃ
children.translated_text: Having kissed him trustingly and then seeing his cheek bristling with horripilation,

children.text: lajjā-namra-mukhī priyeṇa hasatā bālā ciraṃ cumbitā //
children.translated_text: The young woman, her face bowed with shame, was long kissed by her laughing beloved.

children.text: ity ādiṣu ślokeṣu satsv api navatvam /
children.translated_text: Even though such verses exist, there is novelty.

children.text: yathā vā-"taraṅgabhrūbhaṅgā" ity ādiślokasya "nānābhaṅgibhramadbhrūḥ" ity ādiślokāpekṣayānyatvam || DhvA_4.2 ||
children.translated_text: Or again, the verse beginning 'with wave-like brow-arching' (<s>taraṅgabhrūbhaṅgā</s>) has its distinctness relative to the verse beginning 'with brows roaming in varied bends' (<s>nānābhaṅgibhramadbhrūḥ</s>). // DhvA_4.2 //
DhvK 4.3:

children.text: yuktyānayānusartavyo rasādir bahu-vistaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> and the like, of vast extent, should be pursued by this method;

children.text: mitho 'py anantatāṃ prāptaḥ kāvya-mārgo yadāśrayāt // DhvK_4.3 //
children.translated_text: The path of poetry, depending on which, attains infinity even among its own [practitioners] mutually. // DhvK_4.3 //

children.text: bahu-vistāro 'yaṃ rasa-bhāva-tad-ābhāsa-tat-praśama-lakṣaṇo mārgo yathāsvaṃ vibhāvānubhāva-prabheda-kalanayā yathoktaṃ prāk / sa sarva evānayā yuktyānusartavyaḥ / yasya rasāder āśrayād ayaṃ kāvya-mārgaḥ purātanaiḥ kavibhiḥ sahasra-saṃkhyair asaṃkhyair vā bahu-prakāraṃ kṣuṇṇatvān mito 'py anantatām eti / rasa-bhāvādīnāṃ hi pratyekaṃ vibhāvānubhāva-vyabhicāri-samāśrayād aparimitatvam / teṣāṃ caikaika-prabhedāpekṣayāpi tāvaj jagad-vṛttam upanibadhyamānaṃ sukavibhis tad-icchā-vaśād anyathā sthitam apy anyathaiva vivartate / pratipāditaṃ caitac citra-vicārāvasare / gāthā cātra kṛtaiva mahā-kavinā-
children.translated_text: This path, characterized by <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, their semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>), and their quiescence (<s>praśama</s>), is of vast extent through the elaboration of varieties of <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and so on, as stated before. All of this should be pursued by this method. The path of poetry, depending on which <s>rasa</s> and the like, even though trodden in manifold ways by ancient poets numbering in the thousands or innumerable — even when exhausted, attains infinity. For each <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s> individually possesses limitlessness through its recourse to [different] <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s>. And with reference to each sub-type of these, the affairs of the world, when composed by good poets, are transformed into something different from their actual state, according to the poet's will. And this was demonstrated on the occasion of discussing <s>citra</s> (pictorial poetry). And here, a <s>gāthā</s> has already been composed by the great poet—

children.text: atathā-sthitān api tathā-saṃsthitān iva hṛdaye yā niveśayati /
children.translated_text: That speech which implants in the heart particular meanings as if established [in a certain way],

children.text: artha-viśeṣān sā jayati vikaṭa-kavi-gocarā vāṇī //
children.translated_text: even though they are actually not so established — that [speech], the domain of the extraordinary poet, is victorious!

children.text: tad itthaṃ rasa-bhāvādy-āśrayeṇa kāvyārthānām ānantyaṃ supratipāditam / etad evopapādayitum ucyate-
children.translated_text: Thus, through the dependence on <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and the like, the infinity of poetic meanings has been well demonstrated. To further substantiate this, it is said—
DhvK 4.4:

children.text: dṛṣṭa-pūrvā api hy arthāḥ kāvye rasa-parigrahāt /
children.translated_text: For even meanings that have been seen before, in poetry, through the embrace of <s>rasa</s>,

children.text: sarve navā ivābhānti madhu-māsa iva drumāḥ // DhvK_4.4 //
children.translated_text: all appear as if new — like trees in the spring month (<s>madhu-māsa</s>). // DhvK_4.4 //

children.text: tathā hi vivakṣitāny apara-vācyasyaiva śabda-śakty-udbhavānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgya-prakāra-samāśrayeṇa navatvam / yathā-"dharaṇī-dhāraṇāyādhunā tvaṃ śeṣaḥ" ity ādeḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, for <s>dhvani</s> with intended expressed meaning (<s>vivakṣitānyapara-vācya</s>) itself, through recourse to the mode of suggested meaning of the reverberation type (<s>anuranana-rūpa-vyaṅgya</s>) born from the power of the word (<s>śabda-śakti</s>), there is novelty. For example, of [the verse beginning] 'For bearing the earth, you are now <s>Śeṣa</s>' and the like—

children.text: śeṣo hima-giris tvaṃ ca mahānto guravaḥ sthirāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śeṣa</s>, the <s>Himālaya</s>, and you — [all are] great, weighty, and steadfast;

children.text: yad alaṅghita-maryādāś calantīṃ bibhrate bhuvam //
children.translated_text: For, with boundaries unviolated, you bear the earth that trembles.

children.text: ity ādiṣu satsv api /
children.translated_text: Even though such [verses] exist.

children.text: tasyaivārtha-śakty-udbhavānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgya-samāśrayeṇa navatvam / yathā-"evaṃ-vādini devarṣau" ity ādi ślokasya /
children.translated_text: Of that same [type], through recourse to the suggested of the reverberation type born from the power of meaning (<s>artha-śakti</s>), there is novelty. For example, of the verse beginning '<s>evaṃ-vādini devarṣau</s>' ('When the divine sage spoke thus')—

children.text: kṛte vara-kathālāpe kumāryaḥ pulakodgamaiḥ /
children.translated_text: When the speech about the bridegroom had been made, the maidens, with horripilation arising,

children.text: sūcayanti spṛhām antar-lajjayāvanatānanāḥ //
children.translated_text: indicated their desire within, their faces bowed with modesty.

children.text: ity ādiṣu satsv artha-śakty-udbhavānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgyasya kavi-prauḍhokti-nirmita-śarīratvena navatvam / yathā-"sajjayati surabhi-māso" ity ādeḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though such [verses] exist, the suggested of the reverberation type born from the power of meaning has novelty through having a body fashioned by the mature utterance (<s>prauḍhokti</s>) of the poet. For example, of [the verse beginning] '<s>sajjayati surabhi-māso</s>' ('The fragrant month makes ready')—

children.text: surabhi-samaye pravṛtte sahasā prādurbhavanti ramaṇīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: When the fragrant season has commenced, suddenly there arise, delightful,

children.text: rāgavatām utkalikāḥ sahaiva sahakāra-kalikābhiḥ //
children.translated_text: the longings of the passionate — together with the buds of the mango tree.

children.text: ity ādiṣu satsv apy apūrvatvam eva /
children.translated_text: Even though such [verses] exist, there is absolute novelty.

children.text: artha-śakty-udbhavānuraṇana-rūpa-vyaṅgyasya kavi-nibaddha-vaktṛ-prauḍhokti-mātra-niṣpanna-śarīratvena navatvam / yathā "'vāṇijya hasti-dantāḥ" ity ādi-gāthārthasya /
children.translated_text: The suggested of the reverberation type born from the power of meaning has novelty through having a body accomplished solely by the mature utterance of a speaker composed by the poet. For example, of the meaning of the <s>gāthā</s> beginning '<s>vāṇijya hasti-dantāḥ</s>' ('Ivory for trade')—

children.text: kariṇī-behabbaaro maha putto ekka-kāṇḍa-vinibāī /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'He who causes the widowhood of she-elephants — my son, felled by a single shaft!

children.text: haa soṇhāeṃ taha kaho jaha kaṇḍa-karaṇḍaaṃ baha{i} //
children.translated_text: Alas, by the daughter-in-law thus bereaved, he is made to carry a basket of arrows!'

children.text: [kariṇī-vaidhavya-karo mama putra eka-kāṇḍa-vinipātī /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>:] 'He who causes the widowhood of she-elephants — my son, felled by a single shaft!

children.text: hata-snuṣayā tathā kṛto yathā kāṇḍa-karaṇḍakaṃ vahati //]
children.translated_text: Alas, by the bereaved daughter-in-law he is made to carry a basket of arrows!'

children.text: evam ādiṣv artheṣu satsv apy anālīḍhataiva || DhvA_4.4 ||
children.translated_text: Even in such meanings, when they exist, there is sheer untouchedness [of the poetic treatment]. // DhvA_4.4 //

children.text: yathā vyaṅgya-bheda-samāśrayeṇa dhvaneḥ kāvyārthānāṃ navatvam utpadyate, tathā vyañjaka-bheda-samāśrayeṇāpi / tat tu grantha-vistara-bhayān na likhyate, svayam eva sahṛdayair abhyūhyam / atra ca punaḥ punar uktam api sāratayedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Just as novelty of poetic meanings arises through recourse to different types of the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), so too it arises through recourse to different types of the suggestor (<s>vyañjaka</s>). But that [aspect] is not written out, for fear of extending the treatise, and should be inferred by sensitive readers themselves. And here, though stated again and again, this is said once more as the essence—
DhvK 4.5:

children.text: vyaṅgya-vyañjaka-bhāve 'smin vividhe sambhavaty api /
children.translated_text: Even when this diverse suggested-suggestor relationship is possible,

children.text: rasādi-maya ekasmin kaviḥ syād avadhānavān // DhvK_4.5 //
children.translated_text: a poet should be attentive to the single one that is pervaded by <s>rasa</s> and the like. // DhvK_4.5 //

children.text: asminn arthānantya-hetau vyaṅgya-vyañjaka-bhāve vicitre śabdānāṃ sambhavaty api kavir apūrvārtha-lābhārthī rasādi-maya ekasmin vyaṅgya-vyañjaka-bhāve yatnād avadadhīta / rasa-bhāva-tad-ābhāsa-rūpe hi vyaṅgye tad-vyañjakeṣu ca yathā-nirdiṣṭeṣu varṇa-pada-vākya-racanā-prabandheṣv avahita-manasaḥ kaveḥ sarvam apūrvaṃ kāvyaṃ sampadyate /
children.translated_text: In this suggested-suggestor relationship, which is the cause of the infinity of meanings, even when its variety among words is possible, a poet seeking to obtain novel meaning should with effort devote himself to the single suggested-suggestor relationship that is pervaded by <s>rasa</s> and the like. For when the suggested is of the form of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and their semblances, and when [the poet] is attentive to the suggestors as specified — the syllable-, word-, sentence-, and composition-level constructions — all of the poet's poetry becomes entirely novel.

children.text: tathā ca rāmāyaṇa-mahābhāratādiṣu saṅgrāmādayaḥ punaḥ punar abhihitā api nava-navāḥ prakāśante / prabandhe cāṅgī rasa eka evopanibadhyamāno 'rtha-viśeṣa-lābhaṃ chāyātiśayaṃ ca puṣṇāti / kasminn iveti cet-yathā rāmāyaṇe yathā vā mahābhārate / rāmāyaṇe hi karuṇo rasaḥ svayam ādi-kavinā sūtritaḥ "śokaḥ ślokatvam āgataḥ" ity evaṃ-vādinā / nirvyūḍhaś ca sa eva sītātyanta-viyoga-paryantam eva sva-prabandham uparacayatā / mahābhārate 'pi śāstra-kāvya-rūpa-cchāyānvayini vṛṣṇi-pāṇḍava-virasāvasāna-vaimanasya-dāyinīṃ samāptim upanibadhnatā mahā-muninā vairāgya-janana-tātparyaṃ prādhānyena sva-prabandhasya darśayatā mokṣa-lakṣaṇaḥ puruṣārthaḥ śānto rasaś ca mukhyatayā vivakṣā-viṣayatvena sūcitaḥ / etac cāṃśena vivṛtam evānyair vyākhyā-vidhāyibhiḥ / svayam eva caitad udgīrṇaṃ tenodīrṇa-mahā-moha-magnam ujjihīrṣatā lokam ativimala-jñānāloka-dāyinā loka-nāthena-
children.translated_text: And thus, in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Mahābhārata</s>, and the like, battles and such events, though described again and again, appear ever new. And in an extended composition (<s>prabandha</s>), the single principal <s>rasa</s> (<s>aṅgī rasa</s>), when composed [throughout], nourishes the acquisition of particular meanings and the surpassing quality of its 'shadow' (<s>chāyā</s>). In which [work], one might ask? As in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, or as in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>. In the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, the <s>karuṇa rasa</s> (pathos) was announced by the <s>Ādi-kavi</s> (first poet, <s>Vālmīki</s>) himself, who declared: 'Grief (<s>śoka</s>) has turned into verse (<s>śloka</s>).' And that same [<s>karuṇa</s>] was carried through by him as he brought his own composition to its culmination in the final and absolute separation from <s>Sītā</s>. In the <s>Mahābhārata</s> too, the great sage (<s>Vyāsa</s>), who made the concluding portion engender distress through the calamitous end of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> — in a work whose 'shadow' partakes of both the form of treatise (<s>śāstra</s>) and poetry (<s>kāvya</s>) — and who thereby showed the purport of his own composition to be primarily the generation of dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), indicated <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) as the [supreme] human goal and the <s>śānta rasa</s> (tranquility) as the primary object of his poetic intention. And this has been explained in part by other commentators. And this was proclaimed by that Lord of the world himself — who sought to raise up the world submerged in the swelling of great delusion and who bestowed the light of supremely pure knowledge—

children.text: yathā yathā viparyeti loka-tantram asāravat /
children.translated_text: The more the worldly order, devoid of essence, goes awry,

children.text: tathā tathā virāgo 'tra jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: the more does dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) arise therein — of this there is no doubt.

children.text: ity ādi bahuśaḥ kathayatā / tataś ca śānto raso rasāntarair mokṣa-lakṣaṇaḥ puruṣārthaḥ puruṣārthāntarais tad-upasarjanatvenānugamyamāno 'ṅgitvena vivakṣā-viṣaya iti mahābhārata-tātparyaṃ suvyaktam evāvabhāsate /
children.translated_text: And so forth, as stated repeatedly [in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>]. Accordingly, <s>śānta rasa</s> (the tranquil sentiment), [expressing] the <s>puruṣārtha</s> (human goal) characterized as <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), [with] other <s>rasas</s> and <s>puruṣārthas</s> following it in subordinate relationship — is clearly seen to be the object of [the poet's] intention as the predominant [element], and thus the purport of the <s>Mahābhārata</s> is quite evident.

children.text: aṅgāṅgi-bhāvaś ca yathā rasānāṃ tathā pratipāditam eva /
children.translated_text: And the subordinate-predominant relationship (<s>aṅgāṅgi-bhāva</s>) among the <s>rasas</s> has been established as described.

children.text: pāramārthikāntas tattvānapekṣayā śarīrasyevāṅga-bhūtasya rasasya puruṣārthasya ca sva-prādhānyena cārutvam apy aviruddham /
children.translated_text: Without regard to the ultimate truth, the charm of a <s>rasa</s> or <s>puruṣārtha</s> that is subordinate — like a limb of the body — through its own [relative] predominance, is also not contradicted.

children.text: nanu mahābhārate yāvān vivakṣā-viṣayaḥ so 'nukramaṇyāṃ sarva evānukrānto na caitat tatra dṛśyate, pratyuta sarva-puruṣārtha-prabodha-hetutvaṃ sarva-rasa-garbhatvaṃ ca mahābhāratasya tasminn uddeśe sva-śabda-niveditatvena pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Objection: Whatever is the intended content of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, all of it is enumerated in the <s>Anukramaṇī</s> (table of contents), and this [predominance of <s>śānta rasa</s>] is not seen there. On the contrary, what is conveyed by the text's own words in that introductory section is that the <s>Mahābhārata</s> is the cause of awakening to all human goals and is pregnant with all <s>rasas</s>.

children.text: atrocyate-satyaṃ śāntasyaiva rasasyāṅgitvaṃ mahābhārate mokṣasya ca sarva-puruṣārthebhyaḥ prādhānyam ity etan na sva-śabdābhidheya-tvenānukramaṇyā darśitam, darśitaṃ tu vyaṅgyatvena-"bhagavān vāsudevaś ca kīrtyate 'tra sanātanaḥ" ity asmin vākye / anena hy ayam artho vyaṅgyatvena vivakṣito yad atra mahābhārate pāṇḍavādi-caritaṃ yat kīrtyate tat sarvam avasāna-virasam avidyā-prapañca-rūpaṃ ca, paramārtha-satya-svarūpas tu bhagavān vāsudevo 'tra kīrtyate / tasmāt tasminn eva parameśvare bhagavati bhavata bhāvita-cetaso, mā bhūta vibhūtiṣu niḥsārāsu rāgiṇo guṇeṣu vā naya-vinaya-parākramādiṣv amīṣu kevaleṣu keṣucit sarvātmanā pratiniviṣṭa-dhiyaḥ / tathā cāgre-paśyata niḥsāratāṃ saṃsārasyety amum evārthaṃ dyotayan sphuṭam evāvabhāsate vyañjaka-śakty-anugṛhītaś ca śabdaḥ / evaṃ-vidham evārthaṃ garbhīkṛtaṃ sandarśayanto 'nantara-ślokā lakṣyante-"sa hi satyam" ity ādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: To this we say: True, the predominance of <s>śānta rasa</s> alone in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, and the supremacy of <s>mokṣa</s> among all <s>puruṣārthas</s> — this is not shown in the <s>Anukramaṇī</s> as something expressed by the text's own words, but is shown as suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) — in the sentence 'And the eternal Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s> is glorified herein.' For by this [sentence], the following meaning is intended as suggested: that in this <s>Mahābhārata</s>, the narrative of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> and others that is glorified — all of it is insipid at its conclusion and of the nature of the display of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), while the Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, whose nature is ultimate truth, is glorified herein. Therefore, let your minds be devoted to that Supreme Lord alone; do not be attached to insubstantial splendors, nor be utterly absorbed in mere [worldly] qualities such as statecraft, modesty, valor, and the like. And thus, as one who sees ahead, illuminating the insubstantiality of <s>saṃsāra</s> — the text, graced by its suggestive power, appears as clearly revealing this very meaning. And the verses that follow — beginning with '<s>sa hi satyam</s>' ('for He is truth') and so forth — are observed to display this very kind of meaning imbedded [within them].

children.text: ayaṃ ca nigūḍha-ramaṇīyo 'rtho mahābhāratāvasāne harivaṃśa-varṇanena samāptiṃ vidadhatā tenaiva kavi-vedhasā kṛṣṇa-dvaipāyanena samyak-sphuṭī-kṛtaḥ / anena cārthena saṃsārātīte tattvāntare bhakty-atiśayaṃ pravartayatā sakala eva sāṃsāriko vyavahāraḥ pūrva-pakṣīkṛto nyakṣeṇa prakāśate / devatā-tīrtha-tapaḥ-prabhṛtīnāṃ ca prabhāvātiśaya-varṇanaṃ tasyaiva para-brahmaṇaḥ prāpty-upāyatvena tad-vibhūtitvenaiva devatā-viśeṣāṇām anyeṣāṃ ca / pāṇḍavādi-carita-varṇanasyāpi vairāgya-janana-tātparyād vairāgyasya ca mokṣa-mūlatvān mokṣasya ca bhagavat-prāpty-upāyatvena mukhyatayā gītādiṣu pradarśitatvāt para-brahma-prāpty-upāyatvam eva paramparayā / vāsudevādi-saṃjñābhidheyatvena cāparimita-śakty-āspadaṃ paraṃ brahma gītādi-pradeśāntareṣu tad-abhidhānatvena labdha-prasiddhi māthura-prādurbhāvānukṛta-sakala-svarūpaṃ vivakṣitaṃ na tu māthura-prādurbhāvāṃśa eva, sanātana-śabda-viśeṣitatvāt / rāmāyaṇādiṣu cānayā saṃjñayā bhagavan-mūrty-antare vyavahāra-darśanāt / nirṇītaś cāyam arthaḥ śabda-tattva-vidbhir eva /
children.translated_text: And this meaning, of deeply hidden beauty, was perfectly clarified by that very poet-creator <s>Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>), who concluded [the <s>Mahābhārata</s>] with the description of the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>. And by this meaning — which directs an excess of devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) toward the ultimate reality beyond <s>saṃsāra</s> — the entire worldly enterprise is seen to have been implicitly presented as the opponent's position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>). And the portrayal of the extraordinary powers of deities, sacred sites, austerities, and the like — [serves] as means for attaining that Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, and specific deities and others are [presented] simply as manifestations of it. Even the narration of the deeds of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> and others, since its purpose is the generation of dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), and since <s>vairāgya</s> is the root of <s>mokṣa</s>, and since <s>mokṣa</s> is shown principally in the <s>Gītā</s> and elsewhere as a means of attaining the Lord — its ultimate purpose is indirectly the attainment of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. And the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the repository of immeasurable powers, denoted by the names <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the like, having gained renown through being so designated in the <s>Gītā</s> and other passages — is intended in its complete essence as imitated by the <s>Mathurā</s> manifestation, not as confined to the <s>Mathurā</s> incarnation alone, since it is qualified by the word 'eternal' (<s>sanātana</s>). For in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> and elsewhere, usage of this name is seen with reference to another divine form of the Lord. And this meaning has been determined by those who know the true nature of language.

children.text: tad evam anukramaṇī-nirdiṣṭena vākyena bhagavad-vyatirekiṇaḥ sarvasyānyasyānityatāṃ prakāśayatā mokṣa-lakṣaṇa evaikaḥ paraḥ puruṣārthaḥ śāstranaye, kāvya-naye ca tṛṣṇākṣaya-sukha-paripoṣa-lakṣaṇaḥ śānto raso mahābhāratasyāṅgitvena vivakṣita iti supratipāditam / atyanta-sāra-bhūtatvāc cāyam artho vyaṅgyatvenaiva darśito na tu vācyatvena / sāra-bhūto hy arthaḥ sva-śabdānabhidheyatvena prakāśitaḥ sutarām eva śobhām āvahati / prasiddhiś ceyam asty eva vidagdha-vidvat-pariṣatsu yad abhimatataraṃ vastu vyaṅgyatvena prakāśyate na sākṣāc-chabda-vācyatvena / tasmāt sthitam etat-aṅgibhūta-rasādy-āśrayeṇa kāvye kriyamāṇe navārtha-lābho bhavati bandha-cchāyā ca mahatī sampadyata iti / ata eva ca rasānuguṇārtha-viśeṣopanibandham alaṅkārāntara-virahe 'pi chāyātiśaya-yogi lakṣye dṛśyate / yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, through the sentence indicated in the <s>Anukramaṇī</s> — which reveals the impermanence of everything other than the Lord — the single supreme <s>puruṣārtha</s>, which in the doctrinal system is characterized as <s>mokṣa</s>, and in the poetic system is the <s>śānta rasa</s> characterized by the full development of the happiness of the extinction of craving — is well-established as the intended predominant [element] of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>. And because this meaning is of the utmost essence, it is shown by way of suggestion (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) rather than explicit expression (<s>vācya</s>). For the essential meaning, when illuminated without being directly denoted by its own words, brings about beauty all the more. And this is indeed the well-known [practice] in assemblies of the refined and learned: that the most cherished thing is revealed through suggestion, not through direct verbal expression. Therefore, it stands established: when poetry is composed with the predominant <s>rasa</s> etc. as its basis, novelty of meaning arises and a magnificent quality of composition comes about. And precisely for this reason, a poetic instance is seen to possess a surpassing quality of composition even in the absence of any other figure, when particular meanings conforming to the [predominant] <s>rasa</s> are composed. For example:

children.text:
munir jayati yogīndro mahātmā kumbha-sambhavaḥ /
yenaika-culake dṛṣṭau tau divyau matsya-kacchapau //ity ādau /
children.translated_text: Victorious is the sage, the supreme yogin, the great-souled <s>Kumbhasaṃbhava</s> (<s>Agastya</s>), by whom in a single water-pot were seen those two divine beings — the Fish and the Tortoise.

children.text: atra hy adbhuta-rasānuguṇam eka-culake matsya-kacchapa-darśanaṃ chāyātiśayaṃ puṣṇāti / tatra hy eka-culake sakala-jaladhi-sannidhānād api divya-matsya-kacchapa-darśanam akṣuṇṇatvād adbhuta-rasānuguṇataram / kṣuṇṇaṃ hi vastu loka-prasiddhyādbhutam api nāścaryakāri bhavati / na cākṣuṇṇaṃ vastūpanibadhyamānam adbhuta-rasasyaivānuguṇaṃ yāvad rasāntarasyāpi / tad yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, the seeing of the Fish and the Tortoise in a single water-pot, which conforms to the <s>adbhuta rasa</s> (the marvelous), nourishes the surpassing quality [of the composition]. For the seeing of the divine Fish and Tortoise in a single water-pot, even in the presence of the entire ocean, being unprecedented, is all the more conformable to the <s>adbhuta rasa</s>. For a thing that is commonplace, even if marvelous, does not produce wonder due to familiarity. Nor is the composition of an unprecedented thing conformable only to the <s>adbhuta rasa</s> — it serves other <s>rasas</s> as well. For example:

children.text: svidyati romāñcate vepate rathyāyāṃ tulāgreṇa /
children.translated_text: It sweats, it bristles with goosebumps, it trembles — in the street, at the mere tip of a [balance-]beam —

children.text: sa pārśvo 'dyāpi subhaga tasyā yenāsyatikrāntaḥ //
children.translated_text: That side [of my body], O lovely one, even today, by which yours was once passed.

children.text: [svidyati romāñcate vepate rathyāyāṃ tulāgreṇa /
children.translated_text: [It sweats, it bristles with goosebumps, it trembles — in the street, at the mere tip of a [balance-]beam —

children.text: sa pārśvo 'dyāpi subhaga tasyā yenāsyatikrāntaḥ //]
children.translated_text: That side [of my body], O lovely one, even today, by which yours was once passed.]

children.text: etad gāthārthād bhāvyamānād yā rasa-pratītir bhavati, sā tvāṃ spṛṣṭvā svidyati romāñcate vepate ity evaṃ-vidhād arthāt pratīyamānān manāg api no jāyate / tad evaṃ dhvani-prabheda-samāśrayeṇa yathā kāvyārthānāṃ navatvaṃ jāyate tathā pratipāditam / guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyasyāpi tribheda-vyaṅgyāpekṣayā ye prakārās tat-samāśrayeṇāpi kāvya-vastūnāṃ navatvaṃ bhavaty eva / tat tv ativistāra-kārīti nodāhṛtaṃ sahṛdayaiḥ svayam utprekṣaṇīyam || DhvA_4.5 ||
